source_quote: Promote community stewardship and management of neighborhood public lands to ensure higher levels of care and maintenance. Establish Neighborhood Stewardship Councils or Ambassadors.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific governance and stewardship program for public natural lands; climate relevance is through sustained management of natural systems.

parent_statement: By 2030, include all City-owned lands under a management plan that results in neutral or negative carbon emissions and maximizes community co-benefits.
policy_statement: Explore low-carbon and carbon farming practices in food forests and community gardens on public lands.
source_quote: Explore the ability of food forests and community gardens on public lands to use low-carbon and carbon farming practices. This agricultural practice can improve carbon sequestration rates in agricultural systems, aid in plant growth, reduce fertilizer use, and improve soil water retention.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific public-land agriculture strategy explicitly linked to carbon sequestration and reduced inputs.

policy_statement: Implement Bahrain Economic Vision 2030 to diversify the economy, including diversified energy sources, under sustainability principles.
source_quote: In recognition of the necessity of economic reform, in 2008 the government launched its Economic Vision 2030 initiative, with a goal of a diversified and dynamic economy, including diversified energy sources. The vision has three guiding principles: sustainability, competitiveness, and fairness.
extraction_rationale: This is a named national vision with a defined economic and energy-diversification objective. Its climate relevance is indirect because the quote frames diversification and sustainability rather than a specific GHG or resilience target.

policy_statement: Implement the 2016-2021 National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan to reverse biodiversity loss through restoration, reforestation, and public awareness programs.
source_quote: Today, the 2016-2021 NBSAP is recognized as the principal element for CBD implementation in Bahrain, aiming to reverse '… the loss of biodiversity within Bahraini terrestrial, marine and freshwater ecosystems.' Various activities such as restoration, reforestation and public awareness raising programs are ongoing in support of this central aim.
extraction_rationale: This is a named action plan with specific ecosystem interventions. It is climate-relevant through ecosystem restoration and reforestation, though the cited objective is biodiversity rather than climate.

policy_statement: Implement the National Renewable Energy Action Plan to reach renewable energy targets of 5% of peak capacity by 2025 and 10% by 2035.
source_quote: NREAP has two primary targets: having 5% of energy (255 MW of installed capacity) from renewable sources by 2025, and 10% (710 MW of installed capacity) by 2035 (SEU, 2017a). The plan seeks to realize these targets by a mixture of solar, wind, and waste-toenergy technologies and involves a mixture of public and private investment.
extraction_rationale: This is a named national action plan with quantified renewable energy targets and technology pathways. It has sub-policies listed immediately after it.

parent_statement: National Renewable Energy Action Plan (NREAP)
policy_statement: Establish net metering to allow consumers to generate on-site grid-connected renewable energy.
source_quote: Three main policies have been established to realize the targets, as follows: Net metering: This will enable consumers to generate on-site, grid-connected, renewable energy, for example via the installation of solar panels on roofs; Feed-in tariffs: This is a tender-based mechanism to support renewable energy characterized by long-term power purchase agreements; and Mandates: This refers to renewable energy mandates for new buildings.
extraction_rationale: Net metering is a specific regulatory/economic mechanism to expand renewable generation under NREAP.

parent_statement: National Renewable Energy Action Plan (NREAP)
policy_statement: Use tender-based feed-in tariffs with long-term power purchase agreements to support renewable energy.
source_quote: Three main policies have been established to realize the targets, as follows: Net metering: This will enable consumers to generate on-site, grid-connected, renewable energy, for example via the installation of solar panels on roofs; Feed-in tariffs: This is a tender-based mechanism to support renewable energy characterized by long-term power purchase agreements; and Mandates: This refers to renewable energy mandates for new buildings.
extraction_rationale: Feed-in tariffs are a named policy mechanism and qualify as a financial instrument supporting renewable electricity.

parent_statement: National Renewable Energy Action Plan (NREAP)
policy_statement: Introduce renewable energy mandates for new buildings.
source_quote: Three main policies have been established to realize the targets, as follows: Net metering: This will enable consumers to generate on-site, grid-connected, renewable energy, for example via the installation of solar panels on roofs; Feed-in tariffs: This is a tender-based mechanism to support renewable energy characterized by long-term power purchase agreements; and Mandates: This refers to renewable energy mandates for new buildings.
extraction_rationale: This is a binding-style mandate for new buildings to deploy renewable energy.

parent_statement: National Renewable Energy Action Plan (NREAP)
policy_statement: Deploy solar PV through rooftop, government-building, urban, utility-scale, industrial, and new-town applications.
source_quote: Solar PV systems will be deployed as decentralized renewable energy applications in urban areas as well as large-scale installations on available land. Decentralized applications include the following: Solar systems for new housing units; Solar systems for government buildings; Decentralized solar in urban developments (solar lighting, solar parking); and Decentralized rooftop solar on existing residential and commercial buildings.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific renewable technology deployment pathway under the renewable energy plan.

parent_statement: National Renewable Energy Action Plan (NREAP)
policy_statement: Deploy onshore wind systems, including utility-scale wind farms by large industry groups and wind farms on other available land.
source_quote: Aside from some micro wind opportunities in urban areas, onshore wind systems will be mostly deployed as large-scale installations on available land. These opportunities on available land include the following: Utility-scale wind farms by large industry groups; and Wind farms on other available land.
extraction_rationale: This is a named renewable energy deployment initiative with specified project types.

parent_statement: National Renewable Energy Action Plan (NREAP)
policy_statement: Deploy offshore wind systems through near-shore/offshore wind farms and renewable integration in major infrastructure projects.
source_quote: Offshore wind systems will be mostly deployed as large-scale installations on available land. These opportunities on available land include the following: Near shore or offshore wind farms; and Integrating renewable energy technologies in large infrastructure projects (causeways and railway systems).
extraction_rationale: This is a specific renewable technology initiative with identified deployment channels.

parent_statement: National Renewable Energy Action Plan (NREAP)
policy_statement: Deploy biogas systems through landfill gas capture at Askar landfill and waste-to-energy at Tubli wastewater treatment plant.
source_quote: Biogas systems will be deployed as large-scale installations on available land. Opportunities include landfill gas capture at the Askar landfill site and a waste-to-energy plant at the Tubli wastewater treatment plant.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific renewable energy and waste-to-energy intervention. The policy primarily reduces fossil generation emissions through renewable biogas.

policy_statement: Implement the National Energy Efficiency Action Plan to reduce energy use by 6% by 2025 relative to 2009-2013 average energy use.
source_quote: NEEAP identifies specific programs and new initiatives across various sectors to achieve a national target for energy savings. In all, 22 initiatives have been established that together will contribute to a reduction in energy use of 6% by 2025 relative to average energy use over the period 2009-2013.
extraction_rationale: This is a named national action plan with a quantified energy savings target and multiple sub-initiatives.

parent_statement: National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP)
policy_statement: Adopt building energy efficiency codes with mandatory specifications for new construction and renovation.
source_quote: Building energy efficiency codes: This initiative aims to reduce energy demand in buildings by putting in place comprehensive mandatory energy efficiency specifications for the construction of new buildings and renovation of existing buildings. Minimum energy performance standards and labeling for lighting, air conditioning, appliances: This initiative implements minimum energy performance standards (MEPS) for household and commercial lamps, small and large air conditioning units, and appliances.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific regulatory code intervention to reduce building energy demand.

parent_statement: National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP)
policy_statement: Implement minimum energy performance standards and labeling for lighting, air conditioning, and appliances.
source_quote: Minimum energy performance standards and labeling for lighting, air conditioning, appliances: This initiative implements minimum energy performance standards (MEPS) for household and commercial lamps, small and large air conditioning units, and appliances. It also makes energy performance an explicit part of the purchase decision through energy labeling.
extraction_rationale: MEPS and labeling are specific regulatory and information instruments for efficient end-use equipment.

parent_statement: National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP)
policy_statement: Introduce building energy labeling to disclose building energy performance.
source_quote: Building energy labeling: This initiative aims to reduce energy consumption in buildings through making energy performance of buildings explicit through the use of building energy labels. Green building certification: This initiative aims to promote the construction of more resourceefficient buildings by establishing a green building certification program.
extraction_rationale: Building energy labeling is a named policy tool to reduce energy consumption by information disclosure.

parent_statement: National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP)
policy_statement: Establish a green building certification program to promote resource-efficient buildings.
source_quote: Green building certification: This initiative aims to promote the construction of more resourceefficient buildings by establishing a green building certification program. District cooling: This initiative aims to revitalize and expand the existing capacity of district cooling in Bahrain, by establishing a regulatory framework.
extraction_rationale: This is a named building-sector certification program to improve resource efficiency.

parent_statement: National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP)
policy_statement: Revitalize and expand district cooling capacity through a regulatory framework.
source_quote: Green building certification: This initiative aims to promote the construction of more resourceefficient buildings by establishing a green building certification program. District cooling: This initiative aims to revitalize and expand the existing capacity of district cooling in Bahrain, by establishing a regulatory framework.
extraction_rationale: District cooling is a specific energy-efficient cooling intervention and includes a regulatory framework.

parent_statement: National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP)
policy_statement: Establish energy management systems for government buildings.
source_quote: Government Buildings Energy Management: This initiative aims to pursue energy efficiency on a continuous basis in government buildings by establishing an energy management system for government buildings. Government Buildings Lighting Replacement: This initiative aims to improve the energy efficiency of lighting in all government premises.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific operational energy management intervention for public buildings.

parent_statement: National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP)
policy_statement: Replace lighting in government buildings to improve lighting energy efficiency.
source_quote: Government Buildings Energy Management: This initiative aims to pursue energy efficiency on a continuous basis in government buildings by establishing an energy management system for government buildings. Government Buildings Lighting Replacement: This initiative aims to improve the energy efficiency of lighting in all government premises.
extraction_rationale: This is a named public-sector lighting efficiency retrofit initiative.

parent_statement: National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP)
policy_statement: Refurbish street lighting by replacing high-pressure sodium lamps with LED lamps.
source_quote: Street Lighting Refurbishment: This initiative aims to improve energy efficiency in street lighting through the replacement of existing high-pressure sodium lamps with LED lamps. Green Public Procurement: This initiative aims to improve energy efficiency in government operations through requiring all public institutions to give preference to energy efficient and sustainable products when purchasing products, equipment and services.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific technology replacement program for energy-efficient public lighting.

parent_statement: National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP)
policy_statement: Require public institutions to prefer energy-efficient and sustainable products, equipment, and services in procurement.
source_quote: Green Public Procurement: This initiative aims to improve energy efficiency in government operations through requiring all public institutions to give preference to energy efficient and sustainable products when purchasing products, equipment and services. Figure 4-3 (top) summarizes projected target energy savings over the 2015-2030 period for the government sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a procurement requirement that changes public purchasing to favor efficient products and services.

parent_statement: National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP)
policy_statement: Implement an industry program to improve annual industrial energy consumption by 1% and reach a 4% efficiency improvement by 2020.
source_quote: Industry Program: This initiative aims to drive a 1% improvement in annual energy consumption to reach a 4% energy efficiency improvement by 2020. The Industry Program initiative has a three-fold purpose: to coordinate the energy efficiency activities of the major industry players and large energy consumers; to share best practice between the companies through workshops and other knowledge-sharing activities; and to facilitate the collection of energy saving data between the companies and SEU, in order to demonstrate that each party is making progress towards meeting its target (SEU, 2017a).
extraction_rationale: This is a sectoral energy efficiency program with quantified improvement targets and named implementation mechanisms.

parent_statement: National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP)
policy_statement: Improve electricity production efficiency by 1% by 2025 through operational measures and demand-side alternatives.
source_quote: Electricity Production Efficiency: This initiative aims for a 1% improvement by 2025 in combustion. It will accomplish this through a number of complementary measures including reducing reliance on least efficient plants; using aggregated demand reduction/response as an alternative to new capacity; using demand side frequency response as an alternative to spinning reserve; and using real-time tariffs to better utilize existing capacity.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific power-sector efficiency initiative with a quantified improvement target.

parent_statement: National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP)
policy_statement: Improve electricity transmission and distribution efficiency and reduce system losses through line rating, storage, and equipment upgrades.
source_quote: Electricity T&D Efficiency: This initiative aims to improve the efficiency of the electricity delivery system and reduce current system losses of 9.8%. It will involve conducting dynamic line rating trials; using capacity banks and battery storage to better manage the system; and upgrading conductors, transformers and cables.
extraction_rationale: This is a grid efficiency intervention with specific technical measures and an identified system-loss baseline.

parent_statement: National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP)
policy_statement: Improve electricity power factor to 0.9 or greater to reduce inefficient electricity consumption.
source_quote: Power Factor Correction: This initiative aims to improve the power factor to be 0.9 or greater. A low power factor can result in overall higher electricity consumption due to overheating of equipment; low efficiency of connected devices; and high voltage drops in alternators and transformers.
extraction_rationale: This is a technical electricity-efficiency standard with a quantified power-factor target.

parent_statement: National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP)
policy_statement: Introduce smart meters for high electricity consumers and new developments.
source_quote: Smart Metering Program: This initiative aims to introduce smart meters to high electricity consumers and new developments. Smart meters record electricity use and communicates the information to the electricity supplier for monitoring.
extraction_rationale: This is a named metering program to enable better electricity demand management.

parent_statement: National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP)
policy_statement: Reform transport fuel subsidies to reduce annual light-duty vehicle fuel use by 4%.
source_quote: Transport Subsidy Reform: This initiative aims for a 4% reduction in annual fuel use in the light duty vehicle fleet. It will accomplish this through modification to the retail price of gasoline and diesel fuel, a reform process that has been underway since 2016.
extraction_rationale: This is a fiscal pricing reform with a quantified transport fuel-use reduction target.

parent_statement: National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP)
policy_statement: Set and label minimum fuel economy standards for light-duty vehicles.
source_quote: Vehicle Efficiency Standards & Labeling: This initiative aims to improve efficiency in the transport sector by setting minimum fuel economy standards for light duty vehicles; and by making vehicle fuel economy an explicit part of the purchase decision by ensuring that labels are appropriately displayed thereby increasing consumer awareness. The fuel economy labels for light duty vehicles were implemented on all new vehicles of model 2018.
extraction_rationale: This is a vehicle efficiency standard and labeling policy, with implementation already begun for model-year 2018 vehicles.

parent_statement: National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP)
policy_statement: Reform electricity subsidies by increasing tariffs to reflect power generation costs and reduce electricity use by 14% relative to the 2009-2013 baseline.
source_quote: Electricity Subsidy Reform: This initiative aims to gradually increase electricity tariffs to reflect the actual costs of power generation and promote more efficient electricity consumption. When the effects of these new tariffs are fully realized, they are projected to result in a 14% reduction in electricity use compared to the 2009 - 2013 baseline.
extraction_rationale: This is an explicit tariff/subsidy reform with a quantified electricity-use reduction effect, so it is a financial instrument.

parent_statement: National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP)
policy_statement: Run awareness and information campaigns on energy-saving habits and equipment replacement.
source_quote: Raising Awareness & Information Dissemination: This initiative aims to augment information campaigns that focus on ways to reduce energy use, including habits and behaviors that should be modified and energy-consuming equipment and appliances that should be replaced. Training for Market Actors: This initiative aims to build and increase capacity in the energy services market, including energy efficiency training, accreditation and certification programmes.
extraction_rationale: This is a named energy-use information campaign supporting energy efficiency; its effects are behavioral and indirect but embedded in the NEEAP mitigation package.

parent_statement: National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP)
policy_statement: Provide energy efficiency training, accreditation, and certification for energy market actors.
source_quote: Training for Market Actors: This initiative aims to build and increase capacity in the energy services market, including energy efficiency training, accreditation and certification programmes tailored to energy auditors, energy managers and energy service providers. Institutional Infrastructure: This initiative aims strengthen institutional capacity to implement the various initiatives for achieving the national energy efficiency target.
extraction_rationale: This is a capacity-building program for energy efficiency service delivery. It is operational rather than regulatory.

parent_statement: National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP)
policy_statement: Strengthen institutional infrastructure, centered on the Sustainable Energy Unit, to implement the national energy efficiency target.
source_quote: Institutional Infrastructure: This initiative aims strengthen institutional capacity to implement the various initiatives for achieving the national energy efficiency target. Its focus will be on the SEU as the designated agency to coordinate implementation of the NEEAP.
extraction_rationale: This is a governance and implementation capacity initiative tied to a national efficiency target.

policy_statement: Operate BAPCO’s carbon recovery plan to find industrial applications for waste CO2 from oil extraction.
source_quote: Project-level initiatives: Two projects have been launched. The first is BAPCO's carbon recovery plan, which finds industrial applications for the waste CO 2 associated with its oil extraction activities.
extraction_rationale: This is a launched project-level mitigation initiative for CO2 recovery and utilization.

policy_statement: Operate GPIC’s carbon dioxide recovery unit, launched in 2009, for petrochemical-sector CO2 recovery.
source_quote: Project-level initiatives: Two projects have been launched. The first is BAPCO's carbon recovery plan, which finds industrial applications for the waste CO 2 associated with its oil extraction activities. The other is a carbon dioxide recovery unit launched by Gulf Petrochemicals Industries Company (GPIC) in 2009, a first for a petrochemicals company in the Middle East.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific operational CO2 recovery project in industry.

policy_statement: Introduce climate change education and awareness through primary-school curriculum changes and educational reforms.
source_quote: Education-based initiatives: This involves improving education and awareness on climate change primarily by introducing changes in educational curricula in primary schools. In addition, specific proposals for educational reforms were delivered to the Ministry of Education on the basis of studies of how other countries have introduced climate change into educational curricula.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific education-based climate initiative. It does not directly reduce emissions or hazards, so its climate mechanism is behavioral and classified as peripheral mitigation/adaptation support.

policy_statement: Protect Tubli Bay as a protected area, natural reserve, and Ramsar site to conserve mangrove habitats.
source_quote: These factors have led to the loss of about a third of total mangrove area in Tubli Bay; from 150 hectares in 1980 to about 100 hectares in 1992 (FAO, 2005) In response, Tubli Bay was declared nationally as a protected area in 1995 and Law 2006/53 designated Tubli Bay as a natural reserve. In 1997, it was designated internationally as a RAMSAR Site (Public Commission for the Protection of Marine Resources, Environment and Wildlife, 2006).
extraction_rationale: This is a legally designated protected area/natural reserve. It is climate-relevant because the section discusses mangrove vulnerability to sea level rise, although the original designation was for conservation.

policy_statement: Establish a Tubli Bay observatory to strengthen ecological monitoring, species mapping, documentation, and policy dissemination for mangrove services.
source_quote: Tubli Bay observatory: This aims to strengthen existing observation systems to better understand the ecological services provided by mangrove habitats in Tubli Bay. Activities include monitoring, species mapping, systematic documentation, and dissemination of collected information to policymakers.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific proposed adaptation-support intervention for mangrove ecosystem management. The document states it is under consideration, so commitment strength is somewhat weaker.

policy_statement: Develop a blue carbon inventory for Tubli Bay to estimate and document carbon pools and fluxes.
source_quote: Blue carbon inventory: This aims to augment Bahrain's existing GHG emission tracking system to estimate and document carbon pools/fluxes in Tubli Bay consistent with international methodological guidance. This will involve data sharing across institutions, database development, information management, documentation, and dissemination of the levels and rates of carbon pool storage.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific carbon accounting intervention for mangrove blue carbon. It is a planned/considered measure rather than an already implemented program.

policy_statement: Introduce ecosystem services valuation for Tubli Bay mangrove habitats to support financial planning frameworks.
source_quote: Ecosystem services valuation: This aims to introduce economic valuation as a basis to account for the value of the market (i.e., tourism) and non-market (i.e., regulating, provisioning, supporting) services that, Tubli Bay mangrove habitats provide. It will leverage information developed by the Tubli Bay observatory and apply state-of-the art ecological valuation methods to in support of financial planning frameworks.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific planning and valuation intervention for nature-based adaptation planning. It is not itself a financial instrument because it is an analytical framework, not a fund or subsidy.

policy_statement: Maintain building code requirements that new buildings’ ground floors be 1.5 meters above pavement level, increasing resilience to sea level rise.
source_quote: Some adaptation measures have already taken place in certain sectors. For example, while not explicitly in reference to sea level rise, Bahrain's building codes enacted in 2009 call for the height of the ground floor of a new building being 1.5 meters above the level of the pavement surface (KoB, 2009).
extraction_rationale: This is a binding building code requirement with a quantified elevation standard. The document notes it was not explicitly enacted for sea level rise, so climate relevance is indirect but adaptation-relevant.

policy_statement: Develop a national adaptation framework for sea level rise using protection, accommodation, retreat, and avoidance strategies.
source_quote: Going forward, it is recommended that systematic adaptation planning efforts be organized within an adaptation framework that address strategies for protection, accommodation, retreat, and avoidance. In the near-term, the focus should be on the following elements, with the aim of increasing institutional capacity to incorporate sea level rise risks within development planning:
extraction_rationale: This is a recommended planning framework with specific sub-tools. It is framed as a recommendation rather than an enacted commitment.

parent_statement: National adaptation framework for sea level rise
policy_statement: Use planning tools for coastal hazard assessment, coastal risk modeling and management, and emergency preparedness strategies.
source_quote: Planning tools: Planning tools include activities of setting an overall policy to mitigate the effect of sea level rise. At minimum, it should incorporate assessment of coastal hazards, coastal risk modeling/management, and development of emergency preparedness strategies.
extraction_rationale: This sub-policy names specific planning interventions to manage sea level rise risk.

parent_statement: National adaptation framework for sea level rise
policy_statement: Use regulatory tools such as coastal zoning offsets, stronger building codes, and real-estate permit requirements accounting for sea level rise.
source_quote: Regulatory tools: These include tools such as enacting land use regulations (e.g., zoning offsets from the coastline), adjusting building codes (e.g., increasing the distance from pavement to ground floor) and accounting for sea level rise in real estate development permits (e.g., identification of nobuild zones). Land use tools: These refer to tools in support of strategic adaptation and include such as land acquisition (i.e., purchase/transfer of development rights), reclamation (e.g., adding more restrictions on top of basic zoning requirements for certain highrisk areas), zoning (i.e., reclassifying highly vulnerable land for low risk uses) and subdivision regulation (e.g., minimum conservation requirements)
extraction_rationale: This is a set of concrete regulatory adaptation instruments for sea level rise risk.

parent_statement: National adaptation framework for sea level rise
policy_statement: Use land use tools including land acquisition, restricted reclamation, zoning, and subdivision regulation for strategic adaptation.
source_quote: Land use tools: These refer to tools in support of strategic adaptation and include such as land acquisition (i.e., purchase/transfer of development rights), reclamation (e.g., adding more restrictions on top of basic zoning requirements for certain highrisk areas), zoning (i.e., reclassifying highly vulnerable land for low risk uses) and subdivision regulation (e.g., minimum conservation requirements) Hard and soft structural tools: Structural tools include assessment frameworks by which to assess the optimality of coastal protection with either hard measures (e.g., dikes, breakwaters) or soft measures (e.g., mangrove plantations, beach nourishment).
extraction_rationale: This is a set of specific land-use adaptation interventions for sea level rise exposure.

parent_statement: National adaptation framework for sea level rise
policy_statement: Assess and deploy hard and soft coastal protection measures, including dikes, breakwaters, mangrove plantations, and beach nourishment.
source_quote: Hard and soft structural tools: Structural tools include assessment frameworks by which to assess the optimality of coastal protection with either hard measures (e.g., dikes, breakwaters) or soft measures (e.g., mangrove plantations, beach nourishment). Regardless of specific tools or combination of tools applied, a framework for adaptation to sea level rise is an urgent need in Bahrain.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete set of structural adaptation options, including nature-based measures. It is recommended rather than currently committed.

policy_statement: Expand reuse of treated wastewater in irrigation, with free delivery to farmers, to protect groundwater and satisfy irrigation and landscaping demands.
source_quote: At present, Bahrain is pursuing a policy of expansion in the re-use of treated wastewater in irrigation. The primary objectives are to protect groundwater from further lowering of the groundwater table, deterioration in water quality, and satisfying demands for irrigation and landscaping.
extraction_rationale: This is an active water reuse policy with stated groundwater protection and irrigation objectives. It is climate-relevant because it reduces water stress and improves resilience in an arid, climate-vulnerable water system.

policy_statement: Reduce per capita municipal water demand by 33%, from 183 to 122 m3 per person per year by 2035.
source_quote: The first intervention aims to achieve a 33% reduction in per capita municipal water demand, from the current level of 183 to 122 m 3 per person per year by 2035, with a policy start year of 2016. To achieve this target, three complementary demand side management policies would be advanced, as outlined in the bullets below.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified water demand reduction intervention designed for climate-resilient municipal water management. It has three listed sub-policies.

parent_statement: 33% per capita municipal water demand reduction intervention
policy_statement: Run social campaigns and government incentives to promote water efficiency and conservation.
source_quote: Awareness raising : This would involve social campaigns and government incentives to emphasize the importance of water efficiency and conservation among the general population. Strengthened block tariffs: Up until recently water tariffs were heavily subsidized and did not recover minimum production and distribution costs.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific demand-side water conservation intervention under the quantified per-capita reduction target.

parent_statement: 33% per capita municipal water demand reduction intervention
policy_statement: Strengthen block water tariffs for commercial, industrial, touristic, and other non-household users.
source_quote: Strengthened block tariffs: Up until recently water tariffs were heavily subsidized and did not recover minimum production and distribution costs. Effective 1 March 2016, water tariffs for commercial, industrial, touristic, and other nonhousehold users are being gradually strengthened in accordance with the new tariff schedule established by EWA.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific water tariff reform used to encourage efficient municipal water use. It is a financial instrument.

parent_statement: 33% per capita municipal water demand reduction intervention
policy_statement: Strengthen building codes and require or promote water-saving devices, including low-flow shower heads, faucet aerators, and automatic shut-off nozzles.
source_quote: New legislation: To promote water use efficiency and conservation, new legislation would be needed to strengthen existing building codes, promote water saving devices such as low-flow shower heads, faucet aerators, automatic shut-off nozzles and others for new buildings while existing buildings would be retrofitted. Such devices can reduce water consumption by 20% to 40% (Ababa and Alhaji, 2001; Al-Rumikhani, 2001).
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory/building-code intervention using specific water-saving technologies.

policy_statement: Reduce leakage in the municipal water distribution network to cut per capita municipal water demand by 22%, from 183 to 142 m3 per person per year by 2035.
source_quote: The second intervention aims to reduce leakage in the water distribution network. Through investments in detection and repair, this second intervention aims to achieve a 22% reduction in per capita municipal water demand, from the current level of 183 to 142 m 3 per person per year by 2035, with a policy start year of 2016.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified water network loss-reduction intervention for climate-resilient water management. It has two sub-policies.

parent_statement: 22% municipal water leakage reduction intervention
policy_statement: Strengthen EWA’s leak detection programme and expand leak detection technologies.
source_quote: Leak detection: This would involve the strengthening of the leak detection programme within EWA's Leakage Detection and Control Group to perform more frequent leak detection surveys and expand the use of leak detection technologies (e.g., leak noise correlators, thermography free-floating inline leak detectors, etc). Leak control: This would involve several available currently technologies including Active Leakage Control, Pressure Management, Networks Rehabilitations and Speed & Quality of Repair (Lambert, 2003).
extraction_rationale: This is a specific operational water-loss reduction program using named technologies.

parent_statement: 22% municipal water leakage reduction intervention
policy_statement: Implement leak control technologies including active leakage control, pressure management, network rehabilitation, and faster higher-quality repair.
source_quote: Leak control: This would involve several available currently technologies including Active Leakage Control, Pressure Management, Networks Rehabilitations and Speed & Quality of Repair (Lambert, 2003). Reference and policy scenarios were constructed to reflect plausible potential futures of water supply and demand in Bahrain.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific set of technologies and management practices to reduce water losses.

policy_statement: Formulate a clear, comprehensive, integrated national water resources policy and strategy based on IWRM principles.
source_quote: The results of the assessment make clear that significant water demand reductions are possible and therefore it is imperative for Bahrain to formulate a clear comprehensive national water policy and strategy based on integrated water resource management (IWRM) principles. A clear, comprehensive, and integrated water resources policy will be required to achieve the above benefits.
extraction_rationale: This is a strategic policy recommendation rather than a fully adopted policy, but it is concrete in requiring an integrated national water policy and strategy.

policy_statement: Establish a Bahrain-Saudi cooperation mechanism for transboundary groundwater management, including artificial recharge/storage enhancement using surplus tertiary treated wastewater.
source_quote: Further deterioration of groundwater resources should be addressed by establishing a cooperation mechanism between Bahrain and Saudi Arabia in the development and management of transboundary groundwater resources, including groundwater artificial recharge/storage enhancement using surplus tertiary treated wastewater. Going forward, it will be important to expand water sector coverage beyond the municipal sector, in order to capture opportunities for efficiency and conservation in the agricultural and industrial sectors.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific institutional and technical adaptation recommendation for groundwater resilience.

policy_statement: Implement the climate change public awareness plan specifying activities, target groups, input requirements, and institutional roles.
source_quote: Other major findings include the need to make better use of social media to build awareness, as well as print and televised media, including the use of slogans. Based on these findings, a climate change awareness plan was developed that specified activities, target groups, input requirements, and institutional roles.
extraction_rationale: This is a named climate awareness plan with concrete sub-activities. It supports climate action indirectly through awareness rather than by directly changing emissions or exposure.

parent_statement: Climate change public awareness plan
policy_statement: Hold three climate awareness workshops for media organizations, Shura Council and Parliament members, civil society organizations, and educators.

policy_statement: Lebanon is establishing the Lebanon Green Investment Facility to provide accessible and affordable climate and green finance instruments and technical assistance for public and private sector bankable projects.
source_quote: Therefore, Lebanon  is  working  towards    the establishment of the Lebanon Green Investment  Facility  (LGIF) as  stipulated  in  the Government's Financial Recovery Plan, to provide climate and green finance through accessible  and  affordable  finance  instruments for both the public and private sectors, as well as to provide needed technical assistance to various entities to create bankable projects. The LGIF  is  foreseen  to  substantially  contribute  to the  implementation  of  the  NDC  by  increasing investments to climate-friendly projects, through strong donor and investor coordination mechanism and capitalization strategy.

policy_statement: Lebanon is developing a climate-proofing methodology to assess and reduce impacts of climate-negative projects and guide investment evaluation through a climate lens.

policy_statement: Ensure each new City Council contract is geared towards a zero-waste policy.
source_quote:  The City Council is committed to ensuring that each new City Council contract is geared towards a Zero Waste policy.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 1. Consuming differently by reducing the quantity of waste
extraction_rationale: Procurement-related waste commitment applying to all new contracts.

policy_statement: Set up a waste recovery and reconditioning method at one city market.
source_quote:  The City Council undertakes to set up a waste recovery and reconditioning method at one of the city's markets.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 2. Reusing the resources around us
extraction_rationale: Specific reuse/reconditioning intervention at a market.

policy_statement: Recycle, upgrade or directly recover 70% of waste collected during bulky goods collections, especially through social-economy actors.
source_quote:  Increase the recycling and reuse of waste collected during bulky goods collections, in particular by parties interested in the social economy: 70% of the waste collected during bulky goods collections is recycled, upgraded or recovered directly by parties interested in the social economy.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 3. Recycling through better organisation of waste sorting
extraction_rationale: Quantified recycling and reuse target for bulky waste.

policy_statement: Sort 90% of waste collected during bulky goods collections.
source_quote:  Increase the sorting of waste collected during bulky goods collections: 90% of the waste collected during bulky goods collections is sorted.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 3. Recycling through better organisation of waste sorting
extraction_rationale: Quantified waste-sorting target.

policy_statement: Make 60% of household waste by weight ready for reuse and recycling.
source_quote:  Improved sorting of household waste: 60% of the weight of household waste is ready for re-use and recycling 1 .
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 3. Recycling through better organisation of waste sorting
extraction_rationale: Quantified household-waste reuse and recycling readiness target.

policy_statement: Make 70% of non-household waste excluding construction waste ready for reuse and recycling.
source_quote:  Increase in the proportion of non-household waste (excluding construction waste) ready for re-use and recycling: 70% of the weight of non-household waste (excluding construction waste) is suitable for re-use and recycling.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 3. Recycling through better organisation of waste sorting
extraction_rationale: Quantified non-household waste reuse and recycling readiness target.

policy_statement: Make 95% of construction waste ready for reuse and recycling.
source_quote:  Increase in the proportion of construction waste ready for re-use and recycling: 95% of construction waste is ready for re-use and recycling.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 3. Recycling through better organisation of waste sorting
extraction_rationale: Quantified construction-waste circularity target.

policy_statement: Recover 100% of bio-waste produced by the city.
source_quote:  Increase the recovery of bio-waste produced by the city: Recover 100% of the biowaste produced by the city.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 4. Composting bio-waste from the city and third parties
extraction_rationale: Quantified bio-waste recovery target.

policy_statement: Set up community composting facilities accessible to all Brussels residents and encourage individual composting facilities wherever possible.
source_quote:  Set up individual and collective composting facilities wherever possible: As part of the 10-Minute City initiative, the City Council aims to set up community composting facilities accessible to all Brussels residents, and to encourage the development of individual composting facilities.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 4. Composting bio-waste from the city and third parties
extraction_rationale: Specific composting infrastructure intervention; conditional on feasibility.

policy_statement: Reduce mains-water consumption by 40% in building use and outdoor-area maintenance by treating leaks and equipping public buildings with storage where technically possible.
source_quote:  Reduce our consumption of mains water by 40% in the use of buildings and in the maintenance of outdoor areas: The City Council has set itself the target of identifying and treating every leak in all of its buildings, as well as equipping all public buildings, where technically possible, with a water storage capacity equivalent to their needs for watering plants, sanitary facilities, road cleaning, vehicles or vegetable gardens (rainwater tank, water from lowering the water table, swimming pools, canal, grey water).
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 1. Water, a precious resource to be consumed sustainably
extraction_rationale: Quantified water-efficiency target with specific interventions.

policy_statement: Equip the municipality with rainwater storage capacity covering the equivalent of 20 days of green-space watering and cleaning use.
source_quote:  Equip the municipality with a rainwater storage capacity. Together, these installations will cover the equivalent of 20 days' use (watering green spaces and cleaning).
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 1. Water, a precious resource to be consumed sustainably
extraction_rationale: Specific water-storage target quantified by days of use.

policy_statement: Equip public buildings under renovation with rainwater storage capacity equivalent to 20 days of use where conditions allow.
source_quote:  During renovation, equip public buildings with rainwater storage capacity equivalent to 20 days' use, if conditions allow.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 1. Water, a precious resource to be consumed sustainably
extraction_rationale: Specific building-retrofit requirement, conditional on site conditions.

policy_statement: Increase access to drinking water by ensuring public drinking fountains are easily accessible in dense areas and near every sports ground and children's play area.
source_quote:  Increase access to drinking water: Public drinking fountains will be easily accessible in densely built-up areas and in the immediate vicinity of every sports ground and children's play area.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 1. Water, a precious resource to be consumed sustainably
extraction_rationale: Specific water-access infrastructure commitment; climate link is partly heat adaptation and reduced bottled-water use.

policy_statement: Ensure 100% of roadworks in priority intervention zones and upstream of flood-prone areas incorporate integrated rainwater management.
source_quote:  Generalise Integrated Stormwater Management (ISWM) during public works in priority areas and upstream of them: The City Council is committed to ensuring that 100% of roadworks in priority intervention zones and upstream of flood-prone areas incorporate integrated rainwater management.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 2. Combatting the growing risk of flooding
extraction_rationale: Quantified flood-adaptation requirement for roadworks.

policy_statement: Permeabilise or disconnect from sewers at least 250,000 m² of impermeable surfaces in the Molenbeek catchment priority intervention zone.
source_quote:  The City Council is committed to permeabilising or disconnecting from the sewers at least 250,000m² of impermeable surfaces in the priority intervention zone of the Molenbeek catchment area. This objective can be achieved with a strategy that gives priority to action on the Heysel plateau, and includes action by the City Council and local interested parties.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 2. Combatting the growing risk of flooding
extraction_rationale: Quantified flood-risk reduction and stormwater management target.

policy_statement: Ensure 100% of City Council projects in priority flood-control zones incorporate integrated rainwater management system measures.
source_quote:  The City Council's projects in priority flood control zones include integrated rainwater management system projects: The City Council is committed to ensuring that 100% of its projects incorporate integrated rainwater management system measures.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 2. Combatting the growing risk of flooding
extraction_rationale: Quantified adaptation requirement for municipal projects in flood-control zones.

policy_statement: Support at least 50 voluntary integrated rainwater management projects by local interested parties in priority intervention zones, using awareness campaigns and municipal and regional grants.
source_quote:  The City Council will encourage the integration of integrated rainwater management system intervention for all projects by local interested parties located in priority intervention zones: At least 50 integrated rainwater management system projects by local interested parties in priority intervention zones are carried out on a voluntary basis (excluding permit obligations) via the City Council's flood control awareness campaign, with the help of municipal and regional grants.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 2. Combatting the growing risk of flooding
extraction_rationale: Quantified voluntary adaptation project target with grant support.

policy_statement: Implement the blue network as a network of permeable, infiltrating water surfaces linked to the green network.
source_quote:  The blue network will be implemented, creating a network of permeable, infiltrating water surfaces throughout the area, linked to the green network.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 3. Blue mesh: Using water as a source of freshness in the face of global warming
extraction_rationale: Named adaptation infrastructure commitment using water and green networks.

policy_statement: Increase cool areas or recreational access to water in every neighbourhood so they are accessible within 10 minutes from any point in the city.
source_quote:  Increase the number of cool areas or recreational access to water in every City of Brussels neighbourhood, accessible in less than 10 minutes from any point in the city.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 3. Blue mesh: Using water as a source of freshness in the face of global warming
extraction_rationale: Heat-adaptation target with spatial access standard.

policy_statement: Create a natural open-air bathing area accessible in the City of Brussels region.
source_quote:  A natural open-air bathing area will be accessible in the City of Brussels region.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 3. Blue mesh: Using water as a source of freshness in the face of global warming
extraction_rationale: Specific cooling and recreational water-access intervention.

policy_statement: Maintain good water quality in all ponds and semi-natural water areas through constant monitoring and an intervention procedure.
source_quote:  Good water quality (in accordance with the European Water Framework Directive) will be maintained in all the ponds and (semi-) natural water areas: constant monitoring will be carried out and an intervention procedure will be defined and applied.
extraction_rationale: Specific monitoring and intervention commitment for water quality; climate relevance is indirect via ecosystem and resilience functions.

policy_statement: Reduce sewage discharge into the canal and Seine river in cooperation with regional and catchment-area authorities.
source_quote:  The City Council undertakes to do its utmost, in cooperation with the Regional Council and the municipalities in the same catchment area, to reduce the discharge of sewage into the canal and the Seine river.
extraction_rationale: Specific water-quality intervention, though the phrase 'do its utmost' makes the commitment less binding.

policy_statement: Promote use of roofs, green spaces, agricultural land and gardens for agro-ecology on city properties and in the surrounding region.
source_quote:  The City Council promotes the use of surfaces such as roofs, green spaces, existing agricultural land, gardens, etc. to encourage agro-ecology on city properties and in the surrounding region:
extraction_rationale: Umbrella agro-ecology commitment with specific quantified sub-targets.

parent_statement: Promote agro-ecology on city properties and in the surrounding region
policy_statement: Set aside 10 new hectares for agro-ecological, open-ground professional farming on city land and/or property.
source_quote: o 10 new hectares have been set aside for agro-ecological, open-ground professional farming on city land and/or property.
extraction_rationale: Quantified land-allocation target for agro-ecology.

parent_statement: Promote agro-ecology on city properties and in the surrounding region
policy_statement: Set up four pilot agro-ecology projects in the city's green spaces.
source_quote: o 4 pilot projects will be set up in the city's green spaces.
extraction_rationale: Quantified pilot-project commitment in green spaces.

policy_statement: Double the number of professionals working in urban agriculture and explore qualifying training in horticulture and market gardening.
source_quote:  Increase the number of professionals working in the field of urban agriculture: The City Council is proposing to double the number of professionals working in the field of urban agriculture. The city will look into the possibility of developing the provision of training leading to qualifications in horticulture and market gardening.
extraction_rationale: Quantified workforce-development target for sustainable urban agriculture; training element is exploratory.

policy_statement: End the use of synthetic pesticides in the city.
source_quote:  Synthetic pesticides are no longer used in the city.
extraction_rationale: Clear regulatory/operational commitment protecting ecosystems.

policy_statement: Ensure at least 50% of fruit and vegetables purchased by the City of Brussels come from local production channels, if procurement rules allow.
source_quote:  With a view to reterritorialization, and if current European regulations on public procurement allow, at least 50% of the fruit and vegetables purchased by the City of Brussels come from local production channels and contribute to the objectives of the European Farm To Fork strategy.
extraction_rationale: Quantified sustainable procurement target, conditional on EU procurement rules.

policy_statement: Double the number of local producers and artisans at city markets and prioritise permits for them.
source_quote:  Develop local sources for the city's markets: Double the number of local producers and artisans at the city's markets. The town gives priority to providing permits to local producers and artisans.
extraction_rationale: Quantified local-sourcing target with permitting preference.

policy_statement: Propose that the region reach 50 Good Food shops.
source_quote:  Increase the number of Good Food and bulk products on offer in the city: The city is proposing that the region should have 50 Good Food shops.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 2. A city that meets the demand for sustainable, accessible food
extraction_rationale: Quantified sustainable-food retail target, framed as a regional proposal.

policy_statement: Propose that the region reach 100 restaurants with the Good Food label.
source_quote:  Increase the number of Good Food restaurants: The city is proposing that the region reach 100 restaurants with the Good Food label.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 2. A city that meets the demand for sustainable, accessible food
extraction_rationale: Quantified sustainable-restaurant certification target.

policy_statement: Launch at least five neighbourhood kitchens in the city.
source_quote:  Encourage "neighbourhood kitchens" throughout the city: The City Council is proposing to the region to launch at least 5 "neighbourhood kitchens" in the city.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 2. A city that meets the demand for sustainable, accessible food
extraction_rationale: Specific community food-system intervention with a quantified target.

policy_statement: Set up logistics hubs in the city for pooled deliveries and/or waste management and sustainable food logistics.
source_quote:  Setting up logistics hubs in the city:
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 2. A city that meets the demand for sustainable, accessible food
extraction_rationale: Named food logistics initiative with two sub-actions.

parent_statement: Setting up logistics hubs in the city
policy_statement: Establish at least one city logistics hub for pooling deliveries and/or waste management.
source_quote: o At least one logistics hub within the city, with the aim of pooling deliveries and/or waste management.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 2. A city that meets the demand for sustainable, accessible food
extraction_rationale: Specific quantified logistics infrastructure target.

parent_statement: Setting up logistics hubs in the city
policy_statement: Support logistical resources or tools for pooling sustainable food operators in shopping districts.
source_quote: o The City Council undertakes to support logistical resources or tools dedicated to the pooling of sustainable food operators in shopping districts.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 2. A city that meets the demand for sustainable, accessible food
extraction_rationale: Specific support commitment for pooled sustainable food logistics.

policy_statement: Double citizen initiatives for sustainable food procurement groups.
source_quote:  Increase the number of citizen initiatives for sustainable food procurement groups: The City Council is inviting the region to increase by a factor of 2 the number of citizen initiatives for sustainable procurement groups.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 2. A city that meets the demand for sustainable, accessible food
extraction_rationale: Quantified target for sustainable food procurement initiatives.

policy_statement: Promote flexitarian diets so 50% of Brussels residents eat meat four days a week or less.
source_quote:  Promoting the flexitarian diet to the people of Brussels: 50% of Brussels residents eat meat 4 days a week or less (36% in 2020).
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 2. A city that meets the demand for sustainable, accessible food
extraction_rationale: Quantified dietary-shift target with baseline.

policy_statement: Ensure food served in city facilities complies with Good Food criteria: 100% organic meals, reduced meat, no increase in red meat, and vegetarian menus three days out of five.
source_quote:  The food served in the city's facilities fully complies with Good Food criteria: In line with ONE's nutritional recommendations and the Federal Plan for Nutrition and Health, the meals served by the Cuisines Bruxelloises to the City (schools, crèches, etc.) are 100% organic, have reduced the amount of meat to 60% (previously 50%), without increasing the proportion of red meat, and the menus are vegetarian 3 days out of 5.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 2. A city that meets the demand for sustainable, accessible food
extraction_rationale: Specific and quantified sustainable-food procurement/menu commitment.

policy_statement: Host three zero-waste markets in the region by 2030 and conduct awareness campaigns.
source_quote:  Encourage the development of "bulk" and "organic" products in the city's markets: The city is committed to hosting three zero-waste markets in its region by 2030, and to conducting awareness-raising campaigns.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 2. A city that meets the demand for sustainable, accessible food
extraction_rationale: Quantified zero-waste market commitment with deadline.

policy_statement: Reduce food waste in city infrastructure by 50% by 2030 and encourage Cuisines Bruxelloises clients in the city region to do the same.
source_quote:  Reduce food waste within the city's infrastructure: Reduce food waste by 50% by 2030, starting with the City of Brussels' infrastructure, and encourage the clients of the Cuisines Bruxelloises located in the city's region to do the same.
extraction_rationale: Quantified food-waste reduction target with deadline.

policy_statement: Call on the region to reduce food waste by 50% by 2030.
source_quote:  Operate a business within the City of Brussels. The city is calling on the region to reduce food waste by 50% by 2030.
extraction_rationale: Quantified territorial food-waste target, though the first sentence appears mistranslated and the commitment is framed as a call to the region.

policy_statement: Recover at least 100 tons of surplus food every year.
source_quote:  Increased food recovery from food surpluses/unsold food: At least 100 tons of surplus food are recovered every year.
extraction_rationale: Quantified annual surplus-food recovery target.

policy_statement: Develop differentiated management of green spaces meeting Réseau Nature criteria.
source_quote:  Develop a differentiated management system for green spaces, meeting the criteria of the "Réseau Nature" label, i.e. absence of synthetic pesticides, preservation of natural environments, diversity of wildlife, priority given to indigenous plants and combatting invasive exotic species.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 1. Protecting and developing local and urban biodiversity
extraction_rationale: Named ecological management programme with specific sub-targets.

parent_statement: Develop a differentiated management system for green spaces meeting Réseau Nature criteria
policy_statement: Label 100% of the city's green spaces as Réseau Nature by 2030.
source_quote: o 100% of the city's green spaces to be labelled Réseau Nature by 2030.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 1. Protecting and developing local and urban biodiversity
extraction_rationale: Quantified ecological certification target.

parent_statement: Develop a differentiated management system for green spaces meeting Réseau Nature criteria
policy_statement: Propose that local operators manage private green spaces according to the same Réseau Nature criteria.
source_quote: o The city is proposing that local operators join in the objectives by respecting the same criteria in the management of private green spaces.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 1. Protecting and developing local and urban biodiversity
extraction_rationale: Voluntary extension of ecological management criteria to private operators.

policy_statement: Develop the City of Brussels green network connected to the regional green network and integrating flora and fauna.
source_quote:  Develop the City of Brussels' green network - connected to the regional green network, integrating flora and fauna. Creation of a green network will be carried out in conjunction with local operators, while respecting third party rights:
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 1. Protecting and developing local and urban biodiversity
extraction_rationale: Named ecological infrastructure initiative with a specific mapped-development sub-action.

parent_statement: Develop the City of Brussels green network connected to the regional green network
policy_statement: Map and develop the city green network by 2030, create green spaces and greening where possible, and identify priority migration corridors.
source_quote: o By 2030, the city's green network will be mapped and developed to complement the regional network, for example by creating new green spaces and greening wherever possible with trees and shrubs in public spaces, climbing plants and green roofs. Priority migration corridors will have been identified, giving rise to new measures to promote biodiversity and species migration.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 1. Protecting and developing local and urban biodiversity
extraction_rationale: Specific mapped green-infrastructure and biodiversity corridor target with deadline.

policy_statement: Complete the green network so every resident has access to a local green space or park within 10 minutes.
source_quote:  Complete the green network so that every resident has access to a local green space or park within 10 minutes.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 1. Protecting and developing local and urban biodiversity
extraction_rationale: Spatial access target for green infrastructure.

policy_statement: Develop two pilot projects to protect nocturnal biodiversity while maintaining a sense of security.
source_quote:  Preserving biodiversity: developing 2 pilot projects aimed at protecting nocturnal biodiversity while guaranteeing a sense of security.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 1. Protecting and developing local and urban biodiversity
extraction_rationale: Quantified biodiversity pilot-project commitment.

policy_statement: Continue the Neder-Over-Hembeek Urban Forest project to create an extensive biodiversity conservatory.
source_quote:  Continuing the Neder-Over-Hembeek Urban Forest project to create an extensive biodiversity conservatory.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 1. Protecting and developing local and urban biodiversity
extraction_rationale: Named urban forest project functioning as ecosystem-based climate infrastructure.

policy_statement: Adopt and enforce a tree charter for local operators to guide species selection, planting and management.
source_quote:  Adopt and ensure compliance with a tree charter aimed at all local operators, so that the right species can be planted in the right places and in the right way, and these trees can be managed with respect. Integrate these principles as early as possible in the project and throughout the life of the trees to maximise all the possible benefits of the plantations.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 1. Protecting and developing local and urban biodiversity
extraction_rationale: Specific governance/regulatory-style instrument for urban trees.

parent_statement: Adopt and ensure compliance with a tree charter aimed at all local operators
policy_statement: Invite local operators to apply the same tree-management criteria to private trees.
source_quote: o Suggest to local operators that they join in the city's objectives by respecting the same criteria in the management of private trees.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 1. Protecting and developing local and urban biodiversity
extraction_rationale: Voluntary extension of tree charter criteria to private tree management.

policy_statement: Plant eight trees for each newborn child registered in the population registers in deforestation-sensitive areas in developing countries.
source_quote:  To increase carbon sinks, the City of Brussels is committed to planting 8 trees for each new-born child registered in its population registers in deforestation-sensitive areas in countries recognised by the UN as "Developing Countries".
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 2. Preserving biodiversity on a global scale
extraction_rationale: Quantified tree-planting commitment explicitly aimed at increasing carbon sinks.

policy_statement: Include biodiversity criteria in the city's sustainable procurement strategy for goods and services and in Cuisines Bruxelloises food contracts.
source_quote:  The city is helping to combat the erosion of ecosystems on a global scale by incorporating biodiversity criteria into its sustainable procurement strategy for goods and services, and into the Cuisines Bruxelloises food contracts.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 2. Preserving biodiversity on a global scale
extraction_rationale: Procurement policy with explicit biodiversity criteria.

policy_statement: Combat heat islands in public spaces and buildings, prioritising vegetation.
source_quote:  The city is combatting heat islands in public spaces and buildings.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 3. Using nature as a solution to combat heat islands
extraction_rationale: Umbrella heat-adaptation commitment with specific sub-actions.

parent_statement: The city is combatting heat islands in public spaces and buildings
policy_statement: Carry out three pilot projects to reduce the urban heat island phenomenon.
source_quote: o The city is committed to carrying out 3 pilot projects to reduce the urban heat island phenomenon.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 3. Using nature as a solution to combat heat islands
extraction_rationale: Quantified urban-heat adaptation pilot commitment.

parent_statement: The city is combatting heat islands in public spaces and buildings
policy_statement: Use vegetation as the first solution to combat heat.
source_quote: o The city is committed to using vegetation as the first solution to combat heat.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 3. Using nature as a solution to combat heat islands
extraction_rationale: Explicit nature-based heat-adaptation mechanism.

policy_statement: Require all City-funded and directly dependent cultural venues to implement climate action plans, and raise awareness among other cultural venues.
source_quote:  The city undertakes to ensure that all cultural venues (museums, theatres and cultural centres) that are funded and directly dependent on the City Council have put in place an action plan designed to meet the area's climate objectives, and to make all other cultural venues in the area aware of the need to have an action plan. This action plan includes the following objectives:
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 1. An environmentally-responsible cultural policy
extraction_rationale: Named cultural action-plan requirement with listed sub-objectives.

parent_statement: Cultural venues action plan designed to meet the area's climate objectives
policy_statement: Routinely propose low-carbon transport solutions for travel linked to cultural activities.
source_quote: o Routinely proposing transport solutions so that travel linked to cultural activities is carried out using low-carbon transport.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 1. An environmentally-responsible cultural policy
extraction_rationale: Specific low-carbon mobility action for cultural activities.

parent_statement: Cultural venues action plan designed to meet the area's climate objectives
policy_statement: Increase catering offers in cultural venues that meet Good Food criteria.
source_quote: o An increase in the catering offering that meets the "Good Food" criteria.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 1. An environmentally-responsible cultural policy
extraction_rationale: Specific sustainable-food action in cultural venues.

parent_statement: Cultural venues action plan designed to meet the area's climate objectives
policy_statement: Promote local sourcing among cultural operators directly dependent on the City Council, including through a local Brussels currency.
source_quote: o Promoting local sourcing among cultural operators directly dependent on the City of Brussels Council, in particular through the use of a local Brussels currency.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 1. An environmentally-responsible cultural policy
extraction_rationale: Specific local-sourcing intervention; climate link is indirect.

parent_statement: Cultural venues action plan designed to meet the area's climate objectives
policy_statement: Reduce energy consumption in cultural venues.
source_quote: o Reduced energy consumption.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 1. An environmentally-responsible cultural policy
extraction_rationale: Energy-efficiency objective, though not quantified within this sub-bullet.

policy_statement: Ensure all City Council events comply with the BME sustainability action plan and require events on city territory to meet the sustainable event charter's mandatory criteria.
source_quote:  The City Council undertakes to ensure that 100% of the events organised by the City Council comply with the BME's sustainability action plan, and that the events organised on the City's territory comply with the mandatory criteria of the sustainable event charter and 50% propose to go further via non-mandatory recommendations. These action plans focus in particular on:
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 2. An environmentally-responsible events policy
extraction_rationale: Quantified events sustainability requirement with sub-actions.

parent_statement: Environmentally-responsible events policy action plans
policy_statement: Increase the proportion of event visitors travelling with low-carbon solutions through promotion and facilitation measures.
source_quote: o Transport: using promotion and facilitation measures to increase the proportion of visitors travelling with a low-carbon solution.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 2. An environmentally-responsible events policy
extraction_rationale: Specific low-carbon transport measure for events.

parent_statement: Environmentally-responsible events policy action plans
policy_statement: Make vegetarian formulas routine for event Horeca offerings.
source_quote: o Food: a routine vegetarian formula for Horeca offerings.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 2. An environmentally-responsible events policy
extraction_rationale: Specific sustainable catering requirement.

parent_statement: Environmentally-responsible events policy action plans
policy_statement: Increase routine sorting of organic, plastic/PMC, cardboard and residual waste and make reusable crockery widely available at events.
source_quote: o Waste: increased routine sorting of organic, plastic/PMC, cardboard and residual waste; widespread availability of reusable crockery.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 2. An environmentally-responsible events policy
extraction_rationale: Specific waste sorting and reuse requirement for events.

parent_statement: Environmentally-responsible events policy action plans
policy_statement: Reduce energy consumption at events.
source_quote: o Reduced energy consumption.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 2. An environmentally-responsible events policy
extraction_rationale: Energy-efficiency measure within events policy, though not quantified in this sub-bullet.

policy_statement: Double the number of tourists coming to Brussels by train and double the number of cycle tourists through promotion and facilitation of low-carbon tourist travel.
source_quote: Transport: while maintaining its attractiveness to tourists from all over the world, increase, through promotion and facilitation measures, the proportion of tourist travel using a low-carbon solution to reach twice as many tourists who come to Brussels by train and twice as many cycle tourists.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 3. An environmentally-responsible tourism policy
extraction_rationale: Quantified low-carbon tourism transport target.

policy_statement: Double the number of tourist accommodations with Green Key certification.
source_quote:  Double the number of tourist accommodations with "Green Key" certification.
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 3. An environmentally-responsible tourism policy
extraction_rationale: Quantified sustainable-accommodation certification target.

policy_statement: Develop and support user-saving services throughout the city as part of the 10-Minute City approach.
source_quote:  The City Council is developing and supporting the development of user-saving services throughout its region, in particular for as many neighbourhoods as possible, as part of the "10-Minute City" approach:
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 1. Supporting economy of use, the circular economy and shared services
extraction_rationale: Umbrella circular-economy and sharing-services initiative with listed sub-services.

parent_statement: Developing and supporting user-saving services as part of the 10-Minute City approach
policy_statement: Provide at least one carsharing or pooling station.
source_quote: o At least one carsharing/pooling station;
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 1. Supporting economy of use, the circular economy and shared services
extraction_rationale: Specific shared-mobility infrastructure target, though geographic scope is implied by the parent.

parent_statement: Developing and supporting user-saving services as part of the 10-Minute City approach
policy_statement: Develop equipment-loan services such as loan centres and fablabs.
source_quote: o Equipment loans: loan centres, fablabs, etc. (see waste chapter);
section_header: 2030 Strategic objectives / 1. Supporting economy of use, the circular economy and shared services
extraction_rationale: Specific sharing-economy intervention reducing material consumption.

parent_statement: Developing and supporting user-saving services as part of the 10-Minute City approach
policy_statement: Pool municipal public buildings for complementary functions when not in use by 2030, after a feasibility study, and routinely consider pooling in new projects.
source_quote:  Between now and 2030, the City Council is committed to developing the pooling of municipal public buildings for other complementary functions during the periods when they are not in use, following a feasibility study on all of its assets. In addition, new (construction/renovation) projects will routinely take into account the options for pooling.

policy_statement: Reduce Budapest's greenhouse gas emissions by 40% by 2030 compared with 2015.
source_quote: Accordingly, the Municipality of Budapest has set the target to reduce its emissions by 40% by 2030 compared to the base year of 2015. Chart 2: The decarbonisation target of Budapest
section_header: 4.1.   REDUCTION OF THE EMISSION OF GREENHOUSE GASES (MITIGATION)
extraction_rationale: This is a quantifiable citywide emissions-reduction target with a deadline and baseline year; it is the central mitigation commitment of the SECAP.
