parent_statement: Enable Interconnection and Storage
policy_statement: Encourage 1,000 megawatts of new energy demand reduction by 2030 and 3,000 megawatts by 2040.
source_quote: Encourage 1,000 megawattsofnewenergydemand reduction by 2030, and 3,000 megawatts by 2040. Energy demand surges occur when many energy customers use significant amounts of energy at the same time (for example: using air conditioning during heat waves).
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified demand reduction target with deadlines. It qualifies as resource efficiency because it reduces peak electricity demand, with explicit climate resilience relevance during heat waves.

policy_statement: Collect neighborhood-level energy burden, water, soil, and air quality data to guide equitable climate action.
source_quote: Energy burden, water quality, soil quality, and air quality data can be used to measure the equity of climate action across Chicago neighborhoods. Data will be collected by community area, where possible, to show decision-makers where and how their decisions most affect residents.
extraction_rationale: This is a named strategy with three data-collection actions. It qualifies because it commits to collecting and reporting climate-relevant data for policy decisions.

parent_statement: Collect Relevant Data
policy_statement: Report energy burden by community area by 2023.
source_quote: Report energy burden by community area by 2023. The City will analyze energy reports and other data sources to identify where building retrofits or energy subsidies are most needed.
extraction_rationale: This is a time-bound data reporting commitment. It qualifies because it supports targeting climate and energy interventions to reduce energy burden.

parent_statement: Collect Relevant Data
policy_statement: Develop a water and soil quality measurement and mitigation strategy by 2023.
source_quote: Develop a water and soil quality measurement and mitigation strategy by 2023. A commitment to advancing environmental justice recognizes the difference in exposure to contaminants based on proximity to sources of pollution.
extraction_rationale: This is a time-bound measurement and mitigation strategy for environmental quality. It is climate-relevant through the CAP's climate justice framework, though the climate link is less direct than emissions policies.

parent_statement: Collect Relevant Data
policy_statement: Establish a robust outdoor air quality monitoring network by 2025.
source_quote: Establish a robust outdoor air quality monitoring network by 2025. Fossil-fuel combustion has a negative impact on climate change and air quality, both indoors and outdoors.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific monitoring network commitment with a deadline. It qualifies because it supports tracking pollution from fossil-fuel combustion and climate investments.

policy_statement: Enable data-driven decision-making by integrating climate resilience, justice, health, and equity criteria into planning, budgeting, and reporting.
source_quote: Achieving equity across neighborhoods will require that City policymakers and implementers have relevant and accurate data when making decisions. By integrating decision-making with equity criteria, City decisions can be made to objectively prioritize health outcomes.
extraction_rationale: This is a named strategy with five sub-actions. It qualifies because it commits to specific planning, reporting, and climate risk decision-making tools.

parent_statement: Enable Data-Driven Decision-Making
policy_statement: Publish clean energy just transition metrics by 2022.
source_quote: Publish clean energy just transition metrics by 2022. The transition from fossil fuels to a clean-energy economy will certainly bring significant health and environmental benefits.
extraction_rationale: This is a time-bound metric publication commitment. It qualifies because it creates accountability metrics for the clean-energy transition.

parent_statement: Enable Data-Driven Decision-Making
policy_statement: Integrate community resilience and climate justice criteria into department-level strategic planning and annual budget setting by 2023.
source_quote: Integrate community resilience and climate justice criteria into department-level strategic planning and annual budget setting by 2023. The City will work with stakeholders to identify key health, resilience, climate, and equity criteria to assess.
extraction_rationale: This is a time-bound institutional planning and budgeting commitment. It qualifies because it embeds climate resilience and justice criteria into City decision-making.

parent_statement: Enable Data-Driven Decision-Making
policy_statement: Develop a Heat Vulnerability Index and integrate it into planning, community safety, and public health processes beginning in 2023.
source_quote: Develop a Heat Vulnerability Index and integrate into planning and development, community safety, and public health planning processes beginning in 2023. Climate science indicates that Chicagoland will continue to experience more days of extreme heat and increased precipitation.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific climate-risk tool and integration commitment with a start date. It qualifies as adaptation because it addresses extreme heat vulnerability.

parent_statement: Enable Data-Driven Decision-Making
policy_statement: Publish citywide and community-level quality-of-life metrics on equity and sustainability by 2023.
source_quote: Publish citywide and community-level qualityof-life metrics on equity and sustainability by 2023. The City will work with community groups and frontline leaders to identify metrics that meaningfully reflect community needs, aspirations, and well-being.
extraction_rationale: This is a time-bound public reporting commitment. It qualifies because it creates accountability metrics for equity and sustainability outcomes linked to climate action.

parent_statement: Enable Data-Driven Decision-Making
policy_statement: Assess and optimize community-level emergency management strategies related to climate preparedness by 2024.
source_quote: Assess and optimize community-level emergency management strategies related to climate preparedness by 2024. While a climate hazard may affect the greater city or region, its impact may be unequally felt due to communities' underlying physical, socioeconomic, and health conditions.
extraction_rationale: This is a time-bound emergency management and climate preparedness commitment. It qualifies as adaptation because it directly addresses climate hazards and preparedness.

policy_statement: Enable community resiliency through community-designed climate infrastructure projects and integration with hazard mitigation planning.
source_quote: As the City strives to reduce emission levels, there must also be an effort to enable greater community resilience to withstand the impacts that are underway. By co-designing resiliency projects with community members, local civic leaders, and businesses, initiatives can stem from a shared understanding of historic events, community needs, and other critical insights unique to that community.
extraction_rationale: This is a named strategy with two sub-actions. It qualifies because it commits the City to community resilience projects and hazard mitigation integration.

parent_statement: Enable Community Resiliency
policy_statement: Resource community-led climate infrastructure projects by 2022.
source_quote: Resource community-led climate infrastructure projects by 2022. Pairing citywide infrastructure investments with community-designed resiliency projects creates more effective and relevant projects to those living within a community.
extraction_rationale: This is a time-bound resource allocation commitment for climate infrastructure projects. It qualifies as a financial instrument because it explicitly commits resources to community-led climate infrastructure.

parent_statement: Enable Community Resiliency
policy_statement: Integrate community resiliency strategies with the City's hazard mitigation planning by 2023.
source_quote: Integrate community resiliency strategies with the City's hazard mitigation planning by 2023. As part of the City's regular hazard mitigation planning process, senior residents, people with disabilities, and residents living in high-risk geographic areas are recognized as most vulnerable to the negative impacts of hazards and natural disasters.
extraction_rationale: This is a time-bound planning integration commitment. It qualifies as adaptation because it embeds community resilience into hazard mitigation planning.

policy_statement: Chile will close all coal-fired power generation plants nationwide no later than 2040, with interim closures by 2024.
source_quote: Their commitment is materializing itself in specific results, such as the closure of coal-fired power generation plants. The process has already started in 3 plants, will continue with 7 more by 2024, and will conclude no later than 2040 with the closure of all coal plants nationwide.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete mitigation commitment with a named intervention, interim milestone, and final deadline. It is stated in the foreword rather than the formal contribution section, but it is described as an ongoing national commitment.

policy_statement: Chile will seek to reach greenhouse gas neutrality by 2050.
source_quote: The quantitative goals presented in this NDC are part of a wider analysis, in which Chile will seek to reach GHG neutrality by 2050, 19 as established in the Draft Framework Law on Climate Change that is currently under discussion in the National Congress. As such, this contribution and its consecutive iterations will be intermediate milestones to achieve the 2050 neutrality goal, conforming in design with the necessary measures to reach this.
section_header: 4.2 Long-term vision on mitigation: GHG neutrality by 2050
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified long-term mitigation target with a 2050 deadline and linkage to proposed national climate legislation.

policy_statement: Chile will ensure application of the NDC social-pillar criteria in updating, elaborating, and implementing the NDC.
source_quote: SP1) Ensure the application of the criteria mentioned in Section 3.2 in the processes of update, elaboration and implementation of the NDC. SP2) Establish a mechanism to measure, report and verify the application of the criteria mentioned in section 3.2.
section_header: 3.3 Commitments in the application of the social pillar for updating and implementing the NDC
extraction_rationale: This is a governance commitment tied to implementation of NDC criteria. It is broad and procedural but qualifies because it is a stated commitment under the NDC social pillar.

policy_statement: Chile will establish a mechanism to measure, report, and verify application of the NDC social-pillar criteria.
source_quote: SP2) Establish a mechanism to measure, report and verify the application of the criteria mentioned in section 3.2. SP3) Develop by 2021 a 'Strategy for Just Transition' that protects the rights of the most vulnerable in the process of decarbonizing the energy matrix, ensuring active participation of citizens in its design and implementation.
section_header: 3.3 Commitments in the application of the social pillar for updating and implementing the NDC
extraction_rationale: This is a specific monitoring and verification mechanism for NDC implementation. It is procedural but has a concrete institutional function.

policy_statement: Chile will develop by 2021 a Strategy for Just Transition for the decarbonization of the energy matrix.
source_quote: SP3) Develop by 2021 a 'Strategy for Just Transition' that protects the rights of the most vulnerable in the process of decarbonizing the energy matrix, ensuring active participation of citizens in its design and implementation.
section_header: 3.3 Commitments in the application of the social pillar for updating and implementing the NDC
extraction_rationale: This is a named strategy with a deadline, linked to energy-sector decarbonization. The social-protection aspects are central, but the climate mechanism is mitigation through decarbonization.

policy_statement: Chile commits to a 2020-2030 GHG emissions budget not exceeding 1,100 MtCO2eq, peaking by 2025, and reaching 95 MtCO2eq by 2030.
source_quote: M1) Chile commits to a GHG emission budget not exceeding 1,100 MtCO 2eq between 2020 and 2030, with a GHG emissions maximum (peak) by 2025, and a GHG emissions level of 95 MtCO 2eq by 2030.
extraction_rationale: This is the principal quantified economy-wide mitigation target, with budget, peak year, and 2030 emissions level.

policy_statement: Chile will establish in 2020 a public-private dialogue roundtable to define specific policy for the use of carbon markets under Article 6.
source_quote: Therefore, at the national level, in 2020 we will establish a public-private dialogue roundtable to define specific policy for the use of markets, taking into account clear guidelines that preserve environmental integrity, avoid double-counting and promote sustainable development.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific institutional action to develop carbon-market policy. It is preparatory rather than a final market instrument, so it is not classified as a financial instrument.

policy_statement: Chile will reduce total black carbon emissions by at least 25% by 2030 relative to 2016 levels.
source_quote: M2) Reduce total black carbon emissions by at least 25% by 2030, with respect to 2016 levels. This commitment will be implemented primarily through national policies focused on air quality.
section_header: 4.4 Chile ' s work in short-lived pollutants
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified short-lived climate pollutant reduction target with a baseline and deadline. Air quality is a co-benefit and implementation channel, but the climate relevance is explicit.

policy_statement: By 2021, Chile will define the objective, scope, goals, and elements of the adaptation component in its Long-Term Climate Strategy through a participatory process.
source_quote: A1) By 2021, Chile will define the objective, scope, goals and elements structuring the adaptation component in its Long Term Climate Strategy, based on a participatory process involving different actors at various regional/local scales.
section_header: 5.2.1 Climate change policies, strategies and plans
extraction_rationale: This is a specific adaptation-planning commitment with a deadline and named strategy.

policy_statement: Chile will strengthen national adaptation coordination through the national adaptation plan and 11 priority-sector adaptation plans.
source_quote: A2) The coordination of climate action on adaptation at national level will be strengthened through the national adaptation plan, and the adaptation plans for 11 priority sectors, incorporating lessons learned from the implementation of earlier plans. Those documents will be used as inputs for the Adaptation Communication that will be sent to the UNFCCC in 2022 at the latest.
section_header: 5.2.1 Climate change policies, strategies and plans
extraction_rationale: This is a named umbrella adaptation-planning initiative with scheduled sub-actions listed beneath it.

parent_statement: Strengthen national adaptation coordination through the national adaptation plan and 11 priority-sector adaptation plans.
policy_statement: By 2022, Chile will update and begin implementing the National Adaptation Plan.
source_quote: The plans will be developed according to the following schedule: a) 2022: The National Adaptation Plan shall be updated and in the first stages of implementation.
section_header: 5.2.1 Climate change policies, strategies and plans
extraction_rationale: This is a specific scheduled sub-action under the adaptation-plan umbrella commitment.

parent_statement: Strengthen national adaptation coordination through the national adaptation plan and 11 priority-sector adaptation plans.
policy_statement: By 2022, Chile will develop and begin implementing first adaptation plans for water resources, coastal areas, and mining.
source_quote: b) 2022: The first Adaptation Plans on water resources, coastal areas and the mining sector shall be developed and in the first stages of implementation.
section_header: 5.2.1 Climate change policies, strategies and plans
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete sectoral adaptation-planning commitment with a deadline.

parent_statement: Strengthen national adaptation coordination through the national adaptation plan and 11 priority-sector adaptation plans.
policy_statement: Between 2021 and 2028, Chile will update and implement adaptation plans across priority sectors including agriculture, forestry, biodiversity, fisheries, health, infrastructure, energy, cities, tourism, water, coastal areas, and mining.
source_quote: c) 2021-2028: The Adaptation Plans for sectors in Agriculture and Forestry (Updates: 2021 and 2026), Biodiversity (Updates: 2022 and 2027), Fisheries and Aquaculture (Updates: 2022 and 2027), Health (Updates: 2022 and 2027), Facilities (Updates: 2023 and 2028), Energy (Updates: 2023 and 2028) Cities (Updates: 2023 and 2028), Tourism (Update: 2026), Water Resources (Update: 2027), Coastal Areas (Update: 2027), and Mining (Update 2027) shall be updated and implemented.
section_header: 5.2.1 Climate change policies, strategies and plans
extraction_rationale: This sub-action provides a detailed schedule for sector adaptation-plan updates and implementation.

policy_statement: By 2025, Chile will strengthen subnational climate capacities and begin implementing adaptation and mitigation actions through Regional Climate Change Action Plans in 10 regions, expanding to 16 regions by 2030.
source_quote: A3) By 2025, Climate Change capacities and institutionality at the subnational level will be strengthened and the implementation of necessary adaptation and mitigation actions will have begun through the delivery of Regional Climate Change Action Plans in 10 administrative regions. By 2030, 16 administrative regions will have their own climate change action plans.
section_header: 5.2.1 Climate change policies, strategies and plans
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified regional climate-planning and implementation commitment with 2025 and 2030 milestones.

policy_statement: During NDC implementation, Chile will update and expand climate vulnerability and risk studies to inform adaptation measures.
source_quote: A4) During the implementation phase of this NDC, existing studies and analysis on climate vulnerability and risk in Chile will be updated and expanded to address relevant threats, considering gender in the approach. Those studies wills serve as key inputs for the design of adaptation measures.
section_header: 5.2.1 Climate change policies, strategies and plans
extraction_rationale: This is an adaptation risk-assessment initiative with specific sub-actions listed beneath it.

parent_statement: Update and expand climate vulnerability and risk studies to inform adaptation measures.
policy_statement: By 2021, Chile will develop a communal-level climate risk map platform for continental Chile.
source_quote: Specifically, the following climate actions will be developed: a) By 2021, a climate risk map platform for Chile's continental territory, at a communal level.
section_header: 5.2.1 Climate change policies, strategies and plans
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete adaptation information tool with a deadline and geographic scope.

parent_statement: Update and expand climate vulnerability and risk studies to inform adaptation measures.
policy_statement: By 2021, Chile will estimate costs of climate inaction, and by 2025 estimate costs associated with historical losses and damage.
source_quote: b) By 2021, an estimation of the costs of inaction on climate change, and by 2025 an estimation of costs associated with historic by losses and damage as part of this.
section_header: 5.2.1 Climate change policies, strategies and plans
extraction_rationale: This is a specific analytical commitment supporting adaptation planning and loss-and-damage assessment.

parent_statement: Update and expand climate vulnerability and risk studies to inform adaptation measures.
policy_statement: By 2025, Chile will assess climate change risk to vulnerable groups nationwide, focusing on indigenous peoples, poverty, and gender.
source_quote: c) By 2025, assessments of climate change risk to vulnerable groups nation-wide, with a special focus on indigenous peoples, poverty and gender.
section_header: 5.2.1 Climate change policies, strategies and plans
extraction_rationale: This is a specific adaptation-risk assessment commitment for vulnerable groups with a deadline.

policy_statement: By 2026, Chile will strengthen its monitoring and evaluation system for adaptation instruments with progress and impact indicators.
source_quote: A5) By 2026, the current monitoring and evaluation system will have been strengthened, with indicators on progress and impact for all climate change adaptation instruments to assess the progress and compliance of established goals.
section_header: 5.2.1 Climate change policies, strategies and plans
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete monitoring and evaluation commitment for adaptation policy instruments.

policy_statement: During NDC implementation, Chile will strengthen inclusion of non-governmental actors in adaptation planning and implementation.
source_quote: A6) During the implementation period of this NDC, the inclusion of non-governmental actors in the planning and implementation of adaptation measures will be strengthened.
section_header: 5.2.1 Climate change policies, strategies and plans
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella adaptation-governance commitment with two specific sub-actions listed beneath it.

parent_statement: Strengthen inclusion of non-governmental actors in adaptation planning and implementation.
policy_statement: By 2025, Chile will implement and update a record of adaptation actions by non-governmental actors.
source_quote: Specifically, the following climate actions will be developed: a) By 2025, an implemented and updated record of actions on adaptation by non-governmental actors.
section_header: 5.2.1 Climate change policies, strategies and plans
extraction_rationale: This is a specific adaptation-tracking action with a deadline.

parent_statement: Strengthen inclusion of non-governmental actors in adaptation planning and implementation.
policy_statement: By 2030, Chile will establish public-private cooperation mechanisms for adaptation actions at national and local scales.
source_quote: b) By 2030, public-private cooperation mechanisms for the execution of adaptation actions, at national and local scale.
section_header: 5.2.1 Climate change policies, strategies and plans
extraction_rationale: This is a specific cooperation mechanism for adaptation implementation with a deadline.

policy_statement: Chile will enhance information mechanisms for managing climate-change impacts on water resources to improve resilience.
source_quote: A7) Information mechanisms for managing the impacts of climate change on water resources will be enhanced in order to improve resilience.
section_header: 5.2.2 Areas of greatest urgency in climate action to adaptation
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella water-resilience adaptation commitment with multiple quantified sub-actions.

parent_statement: Enhance information mechanisms for managing climate-change impacts on water resources.
policy_statement: By 2025, Chile will establish a national hydrological-watershed indicator to track water shortages and risk and promote water security.
source_quote: a) By 2025, a national indicator for hydrological watersheds will be established to track water shortages and risk, helping to promote water security nationwide.
section_header: 5.2.2 Areas of greatest urgency in climate action to adaptation
extraction_rationale: This is a specific water-security adaptation indicator with a deadline. The named hazard is water shortages.

parent_statement: Enhance information mechanisms for managing climate-change impacts on water resources.
policy_statement: By 2025, Chile will create a HuellaChile certification system for organizational water-consumption management.
source_quote: b) By 2025, a system to certify levels of water consumption management at an organizational level will be created, through the HuellaChile Program.
section_header: 5.2.2 Areas of greatest urgency in climate action to adaptation
extraction_rationale: This is a specific water-management certification system. It primarily optimizes water use, with adaptation context from the parent water-resilience commitment.

parent_statement: Enhance information mechanisms for managing climate-change impacts on water resources.
policy_statement: By 2030, Chile will establish Watershed Strategic Plans for Water Resources Management in 101 hydrological basins, incorporating climate adaptation.
source_quote: c) By 2030, Watershed Strategic Plans for the Management of Water Resources will be established, taking into account climate change adaptation in the country's 101 hydrological basins.
section_header: 5.2.2 Areas of greatest urgency in climate action to adaptation
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified basin-level adaptation planning commitment covering all 101 hydrological basins.

parent_statement: Enhance information mechanisms for managing climate-change impacts on water resources.
policy_statement: By 2030, Chile will inspect and register 95% of Rural Health Systems to ensure rural drinking-water quality standards.
source_quote: d) By 2030, 95% of Rural Health Systems will be inspected and registered, ensuring the quality standards of rural drinking water.
section_header: 5.2.2 Areas of greatest urgency in climate action to adaptation
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified water-security action under climate adaptation. The climate link comes from the water-resilience parent commitment.

parent_statement: Enhance information mechanisms for managing climate-change impacts on water resources.
policy_statement: By 2030, all health-sector companies will implement disaster risk management plans that consider climate-change risks.
source_quote: e) By 2030, 100% of companies in the health sector will have implemented disaster risk management plans, including consideration of risks resulting from climate change.
section_header: 5.2.2 Areas of greatest urgency in climate action to adaptation
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified disaster-risk and climate-risk planning requirement for the health sector.

parent_statement: Enhance information mechanisms for managing climate-change impacts on water resources.
policy_statement: By 2030, Chile will implement 100% of the 2030 Agenda goals for the health sector.
source_quote: f) By 2030, 100% of the 2030 Agenda Goals 22 for the health sector will be implemented.
section_header: 5.2.2 Areas of greatest urgency in climate action to adaptation
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified implementation commitment in the health sector. Its climate specificity is weaker than other sub-actions but it is listed as a climate action under the water-resource adaptation contribution.

parent_statement: Enhance information mechanisms for managing climate-change impacts on water resources.
policy_statement: By 2030, all water-related public infrastructure projects will evaluate protection of population and land and support human water-consumption demands.
source_quote: g) By 2030, all water-related public infrastructure projects will consider in their evaluation, the ability to protect the population and land (through river works) and/or support as a priority the demands of urban and/or rural human water consumption in their areas of influence.
section_header: 5.2.2 Areas of greatest urgency in climate action to adaptation
extraction_rationale: This is a binding evaluation requirement for all water-related public infrastructure projects under climate adaptation.

parent_statement: Enhance information mechanisms for managing climate-change impacts on water resources.
policy_statement: By 2030, Chile will reduce non-treated sewage by at least 25%.
source_quote: h) By  2030, non-treated sewage will be reduced by at least 25%.
section_header: 5.2.2 Areas of greatest urgency in climate action to adaptation
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified sanitation and water-quality commitment under the water-resilience adaptation contribution. The climate link is contextual rather than intrinsic.

policy_statement: Chile will strengthen nationwide capacity to adapt to climate-related risks and manage socio-natural disasters.
source_quote: A8) The capacity to adapt to climate-related risks and the capacity to manage the adverse effects of socio-natural disasters will be strenghtened throughout the country.
section_header: 5.2.2 Areas of greatest urgency in climate action to adaptation
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella disaster-risk adaptation commitment with listed sub-actions.

parent_statement: Strengthen nationwide capacity to adapt to climate-related risks and manage socio-natural disasters.
policy_statement: By 2021, Chile will develop guidelines on the effect of climate change on human mobility.
source_quote: a) By 2021, guidelines on the effect of climate change in the phenomenon of human mobility in Chile will be developed, in line with related international instruments.
section_header: 5.2.2 Areas of greatest urgency in climate action to adaptation
extraction_rationale: This is a specific adaptation-governance output addressing climate-related human mobility.

parent_statement: Strengthen nationwide capacity to adapt to climate-related risks and manage socio-natural disasters.
policy_statement: By 2022, Chile will develop a national plan for risk variables associated with heat waves.
source_quote: b) By 2022, a specific national plan for risk variables associated with heat wave will be developed, through the cross-sectoral work of the Meteorological Risk Variables Working Group.
section_header: 5.2.2 Areas of greatest urgency in climate action to adaptation
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete adaptation policy addressing the named climate hazard of heat waves.

parent_statement: Strengthen nationwide capacity to adapt to climate-related risks and manage socio-natural disasters.
policy_statement: By 2025, all Chilean regions will incorporate climate adaptation actions in Regional Plans for Disaster Risk Reduction.
source_quote: c) By 2025, all Regions in Chile will incorporate climate change adaptation actions in the Regional Plans for Disaster Risk Reduction, in coordination with the Regional Committees for Climate Change (CORECC).
section_header: 5.2.2 Areas of greatest urgency in climate action to adaptation
extraction_rationale: This is a nationwide regional disaster-risk planning requirement for climate adaptation.

parent_statement: Strengthen nationwide capacity to adapt to climate-related risks and manage socio-natural disasters.
policy_statement: By 2030, Chile will fully implement and harmonize the National Policy for Disaster Risk Reduction 2019-2030, with review by 2023.
source_quote: d) By 2030, the National Policy for Disaster Risk Reduction 2019-2030 will be fully implemented, and its content will be harmonized with the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction, the Paris Agreement and the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. This policy instrument will also be reviewed by 2023.
section_header: 5.2.2 Areas of greatest urgency in climate action to adaptation
extraction_rationale: This is a named national disaster-risk policy implementation commitment aligned with the Paris Agreement.

policy_statement: In 2020, Chile will develop a national Circular Economy Roadmap for 2020-2040 with short-, medium-, and long-term measures.
source_quote: I1) In 2020, develop a Circular Economy Roadmap for the years 2020 to 2040, agreed at a national level, which will focus on the transition towards a circular economy with short, medium and long-term measures established to 2040.
extraction_rationale: This is a named resource-efficiency roadmap with a defined time horizon and measures through 2040.

policy_statement: In 2020, Chile will develop a National Organic Waste Strategy to increase municipal organic-waste recovery.
source_quote: I2) In 2020, develop a National Organic Waste Strategy, aimed at increasing the recovery of organic waste generated at municipal level by recovering nutrients, organic materials or substrates into the productive process and, thereby, contributing to climate change adaptation and mitigation.
extraction_rationale: This is a named strategy for organic-waste recovery. It is primarily resource efficiency; climate adaptation and mitigation are explicitly recognized but no separate GHG target or named hazard is stated.

policy_statement: By 2022, Chile will establish and implement circularity metrics and indicators to monitor circular-economy progress and climate contributions.
source_quote: I3) By 2022, establish and implement, metrics and indicators on circularity to monitor the country's progress in circular economy and identify its contribution to climate change mitigation and adaptation.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete monitoring commitment for circular economy, linked explicitly to climate mitigation and adaptation contributions.

policy_statement: Chile will sustainably manage and recover 200,000 hectares of native forests, capturing around 0.9 to 1.2 MtCO2eq annually by 2030.
source_quote: I4) Chile commits to the sustainable management 25 and recovery 26 of 200,000 hectares of native forests, representing GHG captures of around 0.9 to 1.2 MtCO 2eq annually by 2030. The management plan to be implemented shall consider the following sustainability criteria:
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified forest-management and recovery commitment with a carbon-capture estimate and listed management criteria.

parent_statement: Sustainably manage and recover 200,000 hectares of native forests.
policy_statement: Chile will plan long-term activities to ensure forest conservation and permanence under the native-forest management commitment.
source_quote: The management plan to be implemented shall consider the following sustainability criteria: a) Planning of long-term activities to ensure forest conservation (permanence).
extraction_rationale: This is a required sustainability criterion under the forest management plan. It supports permanence of the nature-based carbon sink.

parent_statement: Sustainably manage and recover 200,000 hectares of native forests.
policy_statement: Chile will apply sustainable yield parameters so forest extractions do not exceed forest growth.
source_quote: b) Sustainable yield parameters guaranteeing that extractions do not exceed forest growth will be applied.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete forest-management rule that sustains forest carbon and ecosystem functions.

policy_statement: Chile will afforest 200,000 hectares by 2030, including at least 100,000 hectares of permanent forest cover and 70,000 hectares of native species, capturing 3.0 to 3.4 MtCO2eq annually.
source_quote: I5) Chile commits to afforest 200,000 hectares, of which at least 100,000 hectares will comprise permanent forest cover, with at least 70,000 hectares of native species. Recovery and afforestation 27 will be undertaken primarily in land suitable for forest growth and/or priority areas for conservation and will represent captures of between 3.0 and 3.4 MtCO 2eq annually by 2030.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified afforestation commitment with composition requirements and explicit carbon-capture estimates. It has conditions listed beneath it.

parent_statement: Afforest 200,000 hectares by 2030 with permanent cover and native-species requirements.
policy_statement: Chile will promote use of native species in afforestation, selected and managed according to appropriate environmental conditions.
source_quote: To deliver benefits in climate change adaptation, these afforestation measures must meet the following conditions: 28 a) Promote the use of native species, having into consideration for their selection and management the appropriate environmental conditions.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific ecological condition for the afforestation commitment, explicitly intended to deliver adaptation benefits.

parent_statement: Afforest 200,000 hectares by 2030 with permanent cover and native-species requirements.
policy_statement: Chile will not count substitution of native forests as afforestation under the native-forest recovery and forest-promotion law.
source_quote: b) As per Law Nº20.283 on Native Forest Recovery and Forest Promotion, and under the consideration that afforestation is undertaken in lands without vegetation, the substitution of native forests is not considered.
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory safeguard for the afforestation commitment, preventing replacement of native forests.

parent_statement: Afforest 200,000 hectares by 2030 with permanent cover and native-species requirements.
policy_statement: Chile will prioritize afforestation on forestry land and conservation-priority areas, including degraded soils and areas with erosion-related mass-movement risks.
source_quote: c) Preference for forestry land 29 and/or conservation priority areas, 30 considering degraded soils with active erosive processes, mass movement risks resulting from erosion and those not suitable for crop cultivation.
extraction_rationale: This is a spatial-prioritization rule for afforestation, explicitly naming degraded soils and mass-movement risks, so it has an adaptation mechanism.

policy_statement: By 2030, Chile will reduce forestry-sector emissions associated with degradation and deforestation of native forest by 25% relative to 2001-2013 average emissions.
source_quote: I6) By 2030, reduce emissions in the forestry sector associated with degradation and deforestation of the native forest by 25%, with respect to average emissions in the period 2001-2013. 31 In order to fulfill this commitment, the following  actions proposed in the ENCCRV (National Strategy on Climate Change and Vegetation Resources), will be considered:
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified land-sector mitigation target with a baseline and deadline, using forest conservation and management actions.

parent_statement: Reduce forestry-sector emissions associated with native-forest degradation and deforestation by 25% by 2030.
policy_statement: Chile will strengthen management models for forest-wildfire prevention and restoration of burned areas.
source_quote: In order to fulfill this commitment, the following  actions proposed in the ENCCRV (National Strategy on Climate Change and Vegetation Resources), will be considered: a) Strengthen management models in forest wildfire prevention and restoration of burned areas.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific forest-management action addressing wildfire, a named climate-exacerbated hazard, while supporting emissions reduction.

parent_statement: Reduce forestry-sector emissions associated with native-forest degradation and deforestation by 25% by 2030.
policy_statement: Chile will strengthen sustainable management models for the use of natural resources.
source_quote: b) Strengthen sustainable management models on the use of natural resources.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific management action under the ENCCRV forest-emissions commitment, though the wording is broad.

parent_statement: Reduce forestry-sector emissions associated with native-forest degradation and deforestation by 25% by 2030.
policy_statement: Chile will apply management models to reconcile livestock activity with forest conservation.
source_quote: c) Apply management models to reconcile livestock with conservation forest.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific land-use management action under the forest-emissions reduction commitment.

parent_statement: Reduce forestry-sector emissions associated with native-forest degradation and deforestation by 25% by 2030.
policy_statement: Chile will strengthen phytosanitary protection in native plant resources.
source_quote: d) Strengthen phytosanitary protection in native plant resources.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific ecosystem-protection action under the ENCCRV commitment.

parent_statement: Reduce forestry-sector emissions associated with native-forest degradation and deforestation by 25% by 2030.
policy_statement: Chile will implement adaptive vegetation-resource management for climate change, desertification, land degradation, and drought.
source_quote: e) Adaptive vegetation resource management to climate change, desertification, land degradation and drought.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific nature-based adaptation measure addressing named hazards and degradation processes.

parent_statement: Reduce forestry-sector emissions associated with native-forest degradation and deforestation by 25% by 2030.
policy_statement: Chile will adjust regulations and agricultural development to be compatible with plant resources.
source_quote: f) Regulatory adjustment and agricultural development compatible with plant resources.
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory and land-use compatibility action under the ENCCRV forest commitment.

parent_statement: Reduce forestry-sector emissions associated with native-forest degradation and deforestation by 25% by 2030.
policy_statement: Chile will provide support to the forestry sector under the ENCCRV forest-emissions reduction commitment.
source_quote: g) Support to the forestry sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a listed implementation action, but it is vague and does not specify the type of support.

policy_statement: By 2025, Chile will identify peatland areas and other wetlands through a national inventory.
source_quote: I7) By 2025, peatland areas and any other types of wetland will be identified under a national inventory.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific ecosystem inventory commitment with a deadline, supporting wetland climate mitigation and adaptation functions.

policy_statement: By 2030, Chile will develop wetland adaptation and mitigation metrics and implement actions in five pilot protected-area sites to enhance climate co-benefits.
source_quote: I8) By 2030, standardized metrics will be developed to evaluate the capacity of wetlands (especially peatlands) for climate change adaptation or mitigation, implementing actions to enhance these co-benefits in five pilot sites in public or private protected areas in the country.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete wetland-climate metrics and pilot-action commitment. It is ecosystem-based and explicitly references adaptation and mitigation.

policy_statement: By 2021, Chile will develop a National Plan for the Restoration of Landscapes, considering restoration of 1,000,000 hectares of vulnerable ecosystems.
source_quote: I9) By 2021, a National Plan for the Restoration of Landscapes will be developed, which will consider restoration of 1,000,000 hectares of ecosystems, prioritizing those facing greatest social, economic and environmental vulnerabilities.
extraction_rationale: This is a named landscape-restoration plan with a quantified ecosystem-restoration target and vulnerability prioritization.

policy_statement: Chile will establish new protected areas in under-represented marine ecoregions and coastal ecosystems, using climate-change criteria.
source_quote: I10) New protected areas will be established in under-represented marine ecoregions. The identification of such areas shall take into account criteria related to the effects of the climate change and the construction of a network of protected marine areas, among others.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella marine protected-area commitment with specific protection targets listed beneath it.

parent_statement: Establish new protected areas in under-represented marine ecoregions and coastal ecosystems.
policy_statement: By 2030, Chile will protect at least 10% of under-represented marine ecoregions through participatory, science-based marine spatial planning with climate-change criteria.
source_quote: a) By 2030, protect at least 10% of under-represented marine eco-regions (Humboldt, Central Chile, Araucanía and Chiloe), in the framework of a participatory marine spatial planning, based on science and holding criteria to deal with the effects of climate change.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified marine protection target with a deadline and explicit climate-change criteria.

parent_statement: Establish new protected areas in under-represented marine ecoregions and coastal ecosystems.
policy_statement: By 2025, Chile will protect at least 20 coastal wetlands as new protected areas.
source_quote: b) By 2025, protect at least 20 coastal wetlands as new protected areas.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified coastal wetland protection commitment with a deadline.

parent_statement: Establish new protected areas in under-represented marine ecoregions and coastal ecosystems.
policy_statement: By 2030, Chile will protect at least 10 additional coastal wetlands as protected areas.
source_quote: c) By 2030, protect at least 10 additional coastal wetlands as protected areas.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified additional coastal wetland protection target with a deadline.

policy_statement: All Chilean marine protected areas created up to 2020 will have management or administration plans under implementation that include climate adaptation actions.
source_quote: I11) All marine protected areas of Chile created up to 2020 will have a management or administration plan under implementation, taking into account actions for adaptation to climate change.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella marine protected-area management commitment with quantified implementation sub-actions.

parent_statement: Implement climate-adaptation management or administration plans for marine protected areas.
policy_statement: By 2025, all marine protected areas created up to 2020 will have management or administration plans including climate adaptation actions.
source_quote: a) By 2025: 100% of marine protected areas created up to 2020 will hold management or administration plans including actions for adaptation to climate change.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified MPA planning target with a deadline and explicit adaptation actions.

parent_statement: Implement climate-adaptation management or administration plans for marine protected areas.
policy_statement: By 2025, at least 40% of pre-2020 marine protected-area plans will be implemented through monitoring, control, community involvement, and threat-control programs.
source_quote: b) By 2025: Management or administration plans of at least 40% of the marine protected areas created before 2020 will be implemented at least through monitoring, control, community involvement and threat control programs.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified implementation milestone for MPA management plans.

parent_statement: Implement climate-adaptation management or administration plans for marine protected areas.
policy_statement: By 2030, all marine protected areas created between 2020 and 2025 will have management or administration plans including climate adaptation actions.
source_quote: c) By 2030: 100% of marine protected areas created between 2020 and 2025 will have management or administration plans including actions for adaptation to climate change.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified future MPA planning requirement with adaptation content.

parent_statement: Implement climate-adaptation management or administration plans for marine protected areas.
policy_statement: By 2030, Chile will implement management or administration plans for 100% of marine protected areas created up to 2020.
source_quote: d) By 2030: Management or administration plans for 100% of the marine protected areas created up to 2020 will be implemented, through monitoring, control, community links and threat control programs.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified full-implementation target for pre-2020 MPAs.

parent_statement: Implement climate-adaptation management or administration plans for marine protected areas.
policy_statement: By 2030, Chile will implement a methodology to evaluate management effectiveness of all marine protected-area plans for mitigation and adaptation targets.
source_quote: e) By 2030: Implementation of a methodology for the evaluation of management effectiveness of 100% management or administration plans of marine protected areas in order to know the progress of targets proposed in said plans for mitigation and adaptation to climate change.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified monitoring and evaluation methodology commitment for MPA climate targets.

policy_statement: Chile will assess and strengthen mitigation and adaptation co-benefits of ecosystems in marine protected areas.
source_quote: I12) The co-benefits of different ecosystems in marine protected areas will be assessed with respect to climate change mitigation and adaptation. Actions will also be implemented to strengthen these co-benefits.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella MPA ecosystem-climate co-benefits commitment with specific metrics sub-actions.

parent_statement: Assess and strengthen mitigation and adaptation co-benefits of ecosystems in marine protected areas.
policy_statement: By 2025, three Chilean marine protected areas will have standardized metrics for evaluating adaptation or mitigation capacities.
source_quote: a) By 2025: Three marine protected areas of Chile will have standardized metrics for the evaluation of their capacities for adaptation or mitigation to climate change.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified metrics-development commitment for MPA climate capacities.

parent_statement: Assess and strengthen mitigation and adaptation co-benefits of ecosystems in marine protected areas.
policy_statement: By 2030, Chile will apply adaptation or mitigation monitoring and verification metrics in at least five marine protected areas and strengthen co-benefits in their management plans.
source_quote: b) By 2030: metrics for monitoring and verification of adaptation or mitigation capacities will be applied in at least five marine protected areas, while strengthening co-benefits in their management plans.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified application and management-plan enhancement commitment for MPAs.

policy_statement: Chile will develop in 2020 and begin implementing in 2021 a Strategy for Capacity Development and Climate Empowerment to strengthen capacities for mitigation and adaptation targets.
source_quote: IM1) In 2020, Chile will develop 'Strategy for 'Capacity Development and Climate Empowerment' and will begin its implementation in 2021, with the aim of strengthening the sectoral, national and subnational capacities of citizens and organizations (public and private, from academia and civil society), to achieve national mitigation and adaptation targets.
section_header: 7.3 Contribution in capacity building and strengthening
extraction_rationale: This is a named implementation strategy with development and implementation dates, directly supporting climate targets. Sub-elements are listed beneath it.

parent_statement: Strategy for Capacity Development and Climate Empowerment.
policy_statement: Chile will strengthen institutionality and governance for climate action.
source_quote: The elaboration and implementation of 'Capacity Development and Climate Empowerment Strategy' will consider at least the following elements: a) Strengthening institutionality and governance of climate action.
section_header: 7.3 Contribution in capacity building and strengthening
extraction_rationale: This is a listed implementation element under the capacity strategy. It is broad but policy-relevant because it is required in the strategy.

parent_statement: Strategy for Capacity Development and Climate Empowerment.
policy_statement: Chile will generate sectoral, national, and subnational capacities to strengthen resilience and promote a just transition toward resilient, low-emissions development.
source_quote: b) Promoting the generation of capacities at sectoral, national and subnational levels for climate action in order to strengthen resilience to face the effects of climate change and promote the just transition towards resilient and low-emissions development.
section_header: 7.3 Contribution in capacity building and strengthening
extraction_rationale: This is a capacity-building action explicitly tied to resilience and low-emissions development.

parent_statement: Strategy for Capacity Development and Climate Empowerment.
policy_statement: Chile will promote research and science for climate action.
source_quote: c) Research and science for climate action. - Promote research in climate change related areas in the different fields of science and knowledge.
section_header: 7.3 Contribution in capacity building and strengthening
extraction_rationale: This is a listed research-support commitment under the capacity strategy. It is enabling rather than a direct emissions or resilience measure.

parent_statement: Strategy for Capacity Development and Climate Empowerment.
policy_statement: Chile will develop awareness and education processes for climate action.
source_quote: d) Awareness and education for climate action. - Develop formal and informal climate change environmental education processes, to empower the citizenship for climate action.
section_header: 7.3 Contribution in capacity building and strengthening
extraction_rationale: This is a specific education and empowerment commitment under the capacity strategy.

parent_statement: Strategy for Capacity Development and Climate Empowerment.
policy_statement: Chile will promote cooperation and exchange of experience on mitigation, adaptation, and implementation tools among local actors domestically and abroad.
source_quote: e) Cooperation and exchange of experiences. - Cooperation and exchange among local actors in country and overseas, regarding the development and implementation of climate change mitigation and adaptation actions, about implementation tools (capacity building, technology transfer, financing).
section_header: 7.3 Contribution in capacity building and strengthening
extraction_rationale: This is an enabling cooperation action directly linked to climate-action implementation.

policy_statement: In 2020, Chile will present and initiate implementation of its Climate Change Technology Transfer and Development Strategy to support resilient and carbon-neutral development by 2050.
source_quote: IM2) In 2020, Chile will present its 'Climate Change Technology Transfer and Development Strategy' (EDTTCC) and it will initiate the implementation of this strategy to encourage and strengthen technology transfer and development and transfer to support and promote the cultural, social, environmental and economic transformations necessary to achieve sustainable, resilient and carbon neutral development by 2050.
section_header: 7.4 Contribution in terms of Technology development and transfer
extraction_rationale: This is a named technology strategy with a start date, directly supporting climate resilience and carbon neutrality.

parent_statement: Climate Change Technology Transfer and Development Strategy.
policy_statement: By 2020, Chile will establish governance and an institutional framework for EDTTCC implementation supporting mitigation, adaptation, and long-term climate response.
source_quote: By 2020, Chile will have established a governance and institutional  framework for the implementation of the EDTTCC and will support the national contribution in mitigation and adaptation, as well as the global long-term response to climate change.
section_header: 7.4 Contribution in terms of Technology development and transfer
extraction_rationale: This is a specific institutional setup commitment under the technology strategy.

parent_statement: Climate Change Technology Transfer and Development Strategy.
policy_statement: Between 2020 and 2025, Chile will implement the first cycle of the EDTTCC Technological Needs Action Plan for at least three prioritized areas or sectors.
source_quote: Between 2020 and 2025, Chile shall implement the first cycle of the EDTTCC Technological Needs Action Plan for at least three prioritized areas and/or sectors.
section_header: 7.4 Contribution in terms of Technology development and transfer
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete implementation commitment with time frame and minimum number of priority areas or sectors.

parent_statement: Climate Change Technology Transfer and Development Strategy.
policy_statement: By 2021, Chile will establish a Climate Technology Inventory System covering locally generated and globally existing technologies.
source_quote: By 2021, Chile will have a Climate Technology Inventory System to be transferred that includes the local generation, such as also, the adoption of existing technologies worldwide.
section_header: 7.4 Contribution in terms of Technology development and transfer
extraction_rationale: This is a specific climate technology information-system commitment with a deadline.

parent_statement: Climate Change Technology Transfer and Development Strategy.
policy_statement: By 2022, Chile will inventory research centers, R&D+i initiatives, and projects related to mitigation and adaptation for climate technology transfer coordination.
source_quote: By 2022, Chile will have an inventory of Research Centers, R&D+i initiatives and projects related with mitigation and adaptation, and skills to coordinate Technology Development and Transfer for climate change.
section_header: 7.4 Contribution in terms of Technology development and transfer
extraction_rationale: This is a specific inventory and coordination commitment supporting climate technology development and transfer.

policy_statement: Chile will begin implementing the Financial Strategy on Climate Change in 2020 and update it every five years, with first revision in 2021.
source_quote: IM3) Implementation of the EFCC will commence in 2020 and it will be updated every 5 years, 44 with the first revision taking place in 2021. This will take into account the emissions neutrality target presented in Chile's Long-Term Climate Strategy (LTCS) and, where appropriate, the guidelines defined in this strategy.
extraction_rationale: This is a named climate-finance strategy implementation and update commitment. Although finance-related, it is a strategy rather than a direct grant, loan, tax, or budget line.

parent_statement: Financial Strategy on Climate Change implementation and five-year update cycle.
policy_statement: Chile will generate information, data, and analysis to mobilize capital flows under a policy framework consistent with national climate objectives.
source_quote: a) Generate information, data and analysis to mobilize capital flows under an institutional framework of policies and measures consistent with the national climate objectives, economic growth priorities, fiscal responsibility and sustainable development with a long-term vision.
extraction_rationale: This is a finance-enabling information commitment under the climate-finance strategy.

parent_statement: Financial Strategy on Climate Change implementation and five-year update cycle.
policy_statement: Chile will promote design and implementation of green financial instruments and market momentum for climate-resilient, low-carbon sectors.
source_quote: b) Promote the design and implementation of financial green instruments and market momentum to contribute to the development of climate-resilient and low carbon-emission economic sectors.
extraction_rationale: This is a commitment to develop green finance instruments, but no specific instrument type or funding allocation is defined.

parent_statement: Financial Strategy on Climate Change implementation and five-year update cycle.
policy_statement: Chile will promote long-term public-private cooperation to manage climate-related risks and opportunities in financial-sector decision-making.
source_quote: c) Promote long-term public-private cooperation for a better understanding and management of risks and opportunities related to climate change, for decision-making of actors from the local financial sector.
extraction_rationale: This is an institutional cooperation commitment for climate-related financial risk management.

parent_statement: Financial Strategy on Climate Change implementation and five-year update cycle.
policy_statement: During 2020, Chile will establish a work plan for a public framework to determine direct and indirect climate expenditure, subject to budget approval and resource availability.
source_quote: d) Establish a work plan during 2020 to advance in a public framework for the determination of direct and indirect climate expenditure, in line with the efforts to improve efficiency and quality of public expenditure. The implementation of this plan is subject to resources availability as per the corresponding approval to the Budget Law.
extraction_rationale: This is a public climate-expenditure tracking framework commitment. It is finance-related but not itself a funding allocation.

parent_statement: Financial Strategy on Climate Change implementation and five-year update cycle.
policy_statement: Chile will improve its Green Climate Fund institutionality, including project evaluation, prioritization, and calls aligned with the NDC and 2050 neutrality goal.
source_quote: e) Improve Chile's institutionality for the Green Climate Fund (GCF), including: - Improving the evaluation methodology 45 and prioritization of projects to be submitted to the GCF, in the light of the current and future national priorities, ensuring the alignment of prioritized projects with the Long-Term Climate Strategy, and with the objectives and commitments of the NDC. - Standardize calls for public and private projects in order to identify a project portfolio compatible with the GHG emissions neutrality goal by 2050.
extraction_rationale: This is a climate-finance governance commitment linked to GCF project pipelines and alignment with national climate targets.

policy_statement: Develop and support unique places and centers as models of resilience and sustainability.
source_quote:
GOAL UP-5

Develop and support unique places and centers as models of resilience and sustainability. Policy UP-5.A: Actively evaluate plans for existing, new, and redeveloping urban places and corridors from the perspective of fiscal and environmental sustainability.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella goal with listed policies and strategies addressing environmental sustainability, energy and water efficiency, zero-waste standards, and redevelopment of a power plant. It is broad but qualifies because it is tied to concrete sub-actions.

parent_statement: GOAL UP-5: Develop and support unique places and centers as models of resilience and sustainability.
policy_statement: Incorporate fiscal and environmental sustainability into small area and corridor planning.
source_quote: Policy UP-5.A: Actively evaluate plans for existing, new, and redeveloping urban places and corridors from the perspective of fiscal and environmental sustainability. Strategy UP-5.A-1: Consider fiscal and environmental sustainability in the preparation of small area and corridor plans.
extraction_rationale: This is a planning commitment requiring sustainability evaluation in specific plan types. It is climate-relevant through environmental sustainability, although the mechanism is planning rather than a direct project.

parent_statement: GOAL UP-5: Develop and support unique places and centers as models of resilience and sustainability.
policy_statement: Plan for closure, repurposing, and redevelopment of the Martin Drake Power Plant.
source_quote: Strategy UP-5.A-2: Proactively plan for the closure, repurposing, and redevelopment of the Martin Drake Power Plant. Strategy UP-5.A-3: Encourage creation of a City recognition program for excellence in sustainable and resilient urban development and local business practice.
extraction_rationale: The closure and redevelopment of a power plant is a specific named intervention with likely emissions and land-use implications. The quote also includes a related recognition program; the power plant action is the extracted policy.

parent_statement: GOAL UP-5: Develop and support unique places and centers as models of resilience and sustainability.
policy_statement: Revise codes, criteria, procedures, and development flexibility to promote energy- and water-efficient development.
source_quote: Policy UP-5.B: Encourage cost-effective development that promotes the wise use of resources. Strategy UP-5.B-1: Promote development that results in the efficient use of energy and water through the revision and adaptation of codes, criteria, and procedures. Strategy UP-5.B-4: Provide City, Pikes Peak Regional Building Department, and other code flexibility to allow projects that incorporate elements of energy and water efficient building and development.
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory and procedural commitment to change codes and allow flexibility for energy and water efficient projects. It has a concrete mechanism and directly targets resource consumption.

parent_statement: GOAL UP-5: Develop and support unique places and centers as models of resilience and sustainability.
policy_statement: Consider zero-waste standards, policies, and practices for City projects and incentivized private development.
source_quote: Strategy UP-5.B-2: Examine and consider zero-waste standards, policies, and practices for City projects as well as private development receiving special City incentives. Strategy UP-5.B-3: Revise, adapt, and apply codes and requirements to encourage landscape design and maintenance that uses water efficiently and effectively.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific standards-development commitment for zero-waste practices. It is somewhat exploratory because it says 'examine and consider,' but it is concrete enough because it names the standards and applicable project types.

parent_statement: GOAL UP-5: Develop and support unique places and centers as models of resilience and sustainability.
policy_statement: Revise and apply codes to require or encourage water-efficient landscape design and maintenance.
source_quote: Strategy UP-5.B-3: Revise, adapt, and apply codes and requirements to encourage landscape design and maintenance that uses water efficiently and effectively. Strategy UP-5.B-4: Provide City, Pikes Peak Regional Building Department, and other code flexibility to allow projects that incorporate elements of energy and water efficient building and development.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific code and requirements change focused on water-efficient landscapes. It qualifies as a policy through a regulatory mechanism and named resource-efficiency outcome.

policy_statement: Promote cleaner, energy-efficient industrial districts through cost-effective technologies and environmentally sensitive building and site design.
source_quote: Strategy TE-2.A-3: Promote improvements that make industrial districts cleaner, energy efficient, and safer for integration with surrounding neighborhoods, including the implementation of cost-effective technologies and environmentally sensitive building and site design. Strategy TE-2.A-4: Ensure screening or other mitigation around high impact industrial districts to reduce impacts on nearby residential areas.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific intervention for industrial districts, naming energy efficiency, technologies, and environmentally sensitive design. Climate benefits are significant but embedded in an economic development section.

policy_statement: Focus development and redevelopment inside or near the city to preserve open space, maximize existing infrastructure, limit maintenance costs, and reduce blight impacts.
source_quote:
GOAL TE-4

Focus on productively developing and redeveloping areas already in, nearby, or surrounded by the city in order to preserve open spaces, maximize investments in existing infrastructure, limit future maintenance costs, and reduce the impacts of disinvestment in blighted areas. Policy TE-4.A: Prioritize development within the existing City boundaries and built environment (not in the periphery).
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella land-use sustainability policy with concrete sub-strategies on infill, density, greenfield development, and fiscal impact requirements. Climate relevance is indirect through reduced infrastructure expansion and open-space preservation.

parent_statement: GOAL TE-4: Focus on productively developing and redeveloping areas already in, nearby, or surrounded by the city.
policy_statement: Encourage infill, density in identified areas, mixed-use higher-density greenfield clusters, and longer fiscal-impact forecasting.
source_quote: Strategy TE-4.A-1: Encourage revitalization and infill in underutilized urban places, as detailed in Chapter 3. Strategy TE-4.A-2: Ensure land use regulations allow for increased density in areas identified for this, including Downtown, activity centers, and urban corridors. Strategy TE-4.A-3: Support greenfield development that includes mixeduse, higher-density clusters, and quality design.
extraction_rationale: This groups directly related land-use strategies under the sustainability goal. The commitment is concrete because it names infill, density regulation, and mixed-use higher-density clusters; climate relevance is mainly through efficient land and infrastructure use.

parent_statement: GOAL TE-4: Focus on productively developing and redeveloping areas already in, nearby, or surrounded by the city.
policy_statement: Integrate sustainable and cost-effective best practices and technologies into public infrastructure investments.
source_quote: Policy TE-4.C: Promote sustainable efforts and initiatives in the public and private sector. Strategy TE-4.C-1: Encourage the integration of sustainable and cost effective best practices and technology into public infrastructure investments. Strategy TE-4.C-2: Promote the development of businesses, jobs, and programs focused on renewable energy, clean technology, waste reduction, and recycling.
extraction_rationale: This is a public investment and operational commitment to incorporate sustainable practices and technology into infrastructure. It is broad but anchored in public infrastructure investments.

parent_statement: GOAL TE-4: Focus on productively developing and redeveloping areas already in, nearby, or surrounded by the city.
policy_statement: Promote renewable energy, clean technology, waste reduction, recycling, and green-economy jobs.
source_quote: Strategy TE-4.C-2: Promote the development of businesses, jobs, and programs focused on renewable energy, clean technology, waste reduction, and recycling. Strategy TE-4.C-3: Promote the city's natural assets, infrastructure, and supportive policies to expand our green economy and attract additional green jobs.
extraction_rationale: This is a programmatic economic-development commitment with named climate-relevant sectors. Renewable energy and clean technology make it directly relevant to mitigation, while waste reduction and recycling add resource-efficiency mechanisms.

policy_statement: Create and implement a Smart Cities plan using innovative technology to manage facilities and services and improve quality of life.
source_quote:
GOAL TE-5

Become a Smart Cities leader in applying innovative technology in ways that enhance the City's ability to better manage our facilities and services and improve our overall quality of life. Policy TE-5.A: Create a plan for a Smart City future.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella technology initiative with listed sub-actions. Climate relevance comes from the document's Smart City definition, which includes energy, utilities, buildings, sustainability, transportation, and resilience.

parent_statement: GOAL TE-5: Become a Smart Cities leader in applying innovative technology.
policy_statement: Regularly refine and execute the SmartCOS implementation plan and incorporate SmartCOS technologies into City initiatives.
source_quote: Policy TE-5.A: Create a plan for a Smart City future. Strategy TE-5.A-1: Regularly adapt, refine, and execute a SmartCOS implementation plan in coordination with private sector partners. Strategy TE-5.A-2: In all City initiatives and decisions consider ways to implement innovative technology from SmartCOS.
extraction_rationale: This is a named implementation plan commitment and applies to City initiatives and decisions. The climate link is indirect unless implemented technologies target energy, mobility, or resilience.

parent_statement: GOAL TE-5: Become a Smart Cities leader in applying innovative technology.
policy_statement: Test, implement, and incorporate proven Smart Cities applications and adaptive technology in facilities, infrastructure, and services.
source_quote: Policy TE-5.B: Implement Smart City innovations and technology. Strategy TE-5.B-1: Test prioritized Smart Cities ideas beginning with pilot projects. Strategy TE-5.B-2: Implement proven and cost-effective Smart Cities applications and technology.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete technology implementation pathway using pilots and cost-effective applications. Climate relevance depends on application area, but the Smart City pillar list explicitly includes energy, transportation, buildings, and sustainability.

policy_statement: Multimodally connect people and land uses throughout the city and region.
source_quote:
GOAL SC-1

Multimodally connect people and land uses throughout the city and region. Policy SC-1.A: Plan for and implement transportation projects for the overall mobility of people and to manage the impacts of cars on our built environment.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella transportation policy with many specific modal-shift strategies. The climate link is indirect through transportation efficiency, reduced car dependence, and reduced land and pavement needs.

parent_statement: GOAL SC-1: Multimodally connect people and land uses throughout the city and region.
policy_statement: Update the Intermodal Transportation Plan as an Intermodal Mobility Plan focused on maximizing multimodal capacity and reducing land and pavement needs.
source_quote: Strategy SC-1.A-1: Approach the Intermodal Transportation Plan update as an overall mobility plan, with a focus on maximizing the multimodal capacity of the current and future transportation system, thereby reducing the overall need for land and pavement. Focus and brand this effort as an intermodal mobility plan (IMP).
extraction_rationale: This is a specific named plan update with a resource-efficiency objective: reducing land and pavement. It is climate-relevant through lower infrastructure footprint and multimodal capacity.

parent_statement: GOAL SC-1: Multimodally connect people and land uses throughout the city and region.
policy_statement: Build complete streets and design first- and last-mile trips with safe non-motorized options.
source_quote: Strategy SC-1.A-5: Build 'complete streets' by safely and reasonably incorporating multiple modes in the design of new and redeveloped transportation corridors. Strategy SC-1.A-8: Design land uses and transportation improvements with an emphasis on 'first and last mile' trips having desirable and safe options for non-motorized travel.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific transportation design commitment to incorporate multiple modes and non-motorized travel. It is indirectly climate-relevant by enabling mode shift and reducing motor vehicle dependence.

parent_statement: GOAL SC-1: Multimodally connect people and land uses throughout the city and region.
policy_statement: Reduce emphasis on designing transportation facilities around peak-hour traffic forecasts in higher-density multimodal areas.
source_quote: Strategy SC-1.A-9: Reduce the emphasis on requiring transportation facilities to be designed to fully address peak hour traffic demand forecasts, especially in Downtown and other identified higher density multimodal corridors and centers. Strategy SC-1.A-10: When applicable, use a multistreet corridor in the planning and implementation of transit routes in order to manage impacts while maintaining a high level of service (Typology 1: Urban Core Streets).
extraction_rationale: This is a transportation standard/planning policy that reduces overbuilding for peak car demand and supports multimodal corridors. It qualifies through a specific change in transportation design assumptions.

parent_statement: GOAL SC-1: Multimodally connect people and land uses throughout the city and region.
policy_statement: Create multimodal neighborhood connections through sidewalks, bike facilities, trails, bike-plan implementation, and coordinated pedestrian and bicycle planning.
source_quote: Policy SC-1.D: Establish and maintain convenient multimodal connections between neighborhoods, local destinations, employment and activity centers, and Downtown. Strategy SC-1.D-1: Encourage well-connected system of streets, sidewalks, bike facilities, and off-system trails in areas defined by Recent Suburban (Typology 3) and by Future Streets (Typology 4) typologies for new developments and redevelopments areas. Strategy SC-1.D-7: Implement and if necessary adapt key priorities of the Bicycle Master Plan.
extraction_rationale: This policy names specific infrastructure types and a Bicycle Master Plan implementation commitment. It is indirectly climate-relevant through active transportation and reduced car dependence.

parent_statement: GOAL SC-1: Multimodally connect people and land uses throughout the city and region.
policy_statement: Fund and implement sidewalk additions, replacements, and maintenance through PPRTA and related programs.
source_quote: Strategy SC-1.D-4: Continue to fund Pikes Peak Rural Transportation Authority (PPRTA) program and other programs for adding, replacing, and maintaining sidewalks in neighborhoods with missing or substandard sidewalk connections. Strategy SC 1.D-5: Pay particular planning attention to addressing and reasonably mitigating the impacts multimodal transportation decisions have on traditional, historic, and established neighborhoods, and apply a multistreet corridor planning approach where appropriate and feasible.
extraction_rationale: This is a financial and infrastructure commitment for sidewalks. It is climate-relevant indirectly by enabling walking and multimodal transportation.

parent_statement: GOAL SC-1: Multimodally connect people and land uses throughout the city and region.
policy_statement: Create an Electric Vehicle Plan and smart roadway corridors for connected, autonomous, and intelligent transportation systems.
source_quote: Strategy SC-1.E-5: Create and implement a long-term Electric Vehicle (EV) Plan in collaboration with Colorado Springs Utilities and other stakeholders. Strategy SC-1.E-6: Develop priority Smart Roadway corridors to be developed for smart cars, communications, and Intelligent Transportation System applications.
