policy_statement: Require ministries to prepare annual reports on progress toward NCCS goals, policy implementation status and needed new policies.
source_quote: It is proposed that each ministry, on an annual basis, will prepare an overview report covering where the ministry stands against achieving the specified goals and objectives, what was helpful and what are the main challenges encountered. To ensure systematic and consistent reporting between the ministries, each ministry shall report on the status of implementing the policies, tools and directions that were covered in section 5 of the NCCS, and shall also propose new ones if needed.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete annual monitoring and evaluation reporting mechanism for climate strategy implementation.

policy_statement: Require biennial ministry reporting on implementation of mitigation and adaptation actions.
source_quote: On a biennial basis, ministries will be responsible for reporting on the status of implementing the identified mitigation and adaptation actions and providing update for the new ones. To ensure the consistency and quality control of the calculated GHG emission reduction, Table 7-1 contains a quantitative reporting template on mitigation actions tailored from Egypt's first Biennial Update Report (BUR).
extraction_rationale: This is a recurring monitoring policy for mitigation and adaptation implementation.

To ensure consistency among the different ministries, Table 7-2 contains a proposed standardized quantitative reporting template on adaptation actions.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific MRV standardization policy for climate actions.

policy_statement: Fiji declares a climate emergency and commits to achieving net zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050.

extraction_rationale: This is a statutory declaration with a quantifiable national emissions target and deadline. It is a direct mitigation commitment, although it also frames broader resilience policy.

policy_statement: The Minister must review implementation of the Act every 5 years and report annually to Parliament on climate obligations and progress toward net zero and climate-resilient development.
source_quote: The Minister must review the implementation of this Act every 5 years, including with regard to progress made towards achieving the objectives and principles of this Act, and report to Parliament on the findings of the review. The Minister must report annually to Parliament on the status of implementation of international and national obligations to respond to climate change and progress towards the attainment of net zero emissions and climate resilient development.
section_header: Obligation to report on and review the implementation of this Act
extraction_rationale: This establishes binding review and reporting cycles for national climate governance.

policy_statement: The Director must maintain climate data platforms, assess emissions reduction projects and units, prevent double counting, and establish the Fijian Registry.
source_quote: The Director has the following functions- (c) to develop and maintain the Information Platform and the Adaptation Registry; (d) to assess and determine applications for- (i) approval to carry out emissions reduction projects, programmes and activities developed in accordance with emissions reduction methodologies; (ii) the issuance of Fijian Mitigation Outcome Units generated by approved projects, programmes and activities; and (iii) the international transfer of Fijian Mitigation Outcome Units in accordance with the Paris Agreement and other market mechanisms; (f) to develop standards to ensure there is no double counting of emissions reductions achieved by approved projects, programmes and activities; and (g) to establish and maintain the Registry, including establishing and maintaining accounts and ensuring emissions reduction projects, programmes and activities and the issuance, holding, transfer, surrender or cancellation of emissions reduction units are accurately and transparently recorded in the Registry.
section_header: Director of the Climate Change and International Cooperation Division
extraction_rationale: This assigns concrete operational responsibilities for emissions reduction approvals, mitigation units and registries.

policy_statement: The National Climate Change Coordination Committee must mainstream climate change across national and local government and advise on policies for net zero emissions and climate-resilient development.
source_quote: The Committee has the following functions- (f) to ensure the mainstreaming of the consideration of and action on climate change by the national and local governments including the provincial administrations; (g) to advise the national and local governments including the provincial administrations on policy and other measures necessary for responding to climate change and promoting net zero emissions and climate resilient development;
extraction_rationale: This is a named institutional mechanism with statutory functions for mitigation and adaptation mainstreaming.

policy_statement: Each ministry must appoint a climate focal point who promotes the Act's objectives and principles and reports bi-annually to the Director.

extraction_rationale: This creates a specific institutional climate mainstreaming mechanism with a reporting frequency.

policy_statement: State entities must ensure decisions, policies, programmes and processes are consistent with ministerial climate guidelines and must review prior policies for consistency with the Act.
source_quote: All State entities must ensure that any decision made and any policy, programme or process developed or implemented by the State entity after the commencement of this section is consistent with the guidelines published by the Minister in accordance with subsection (4), to the extent that the guidelines are applicable to the decision, policy, programme or process. All State entities must review and update relevant decisions made and policies, programmes and processes developed by the State entity prior to the commencement of this section for the purpose of ensuring that the decision, policy, programme or process is consistent with achieving the objectives and the principles of this Act if relevant to the decision, policy, programme or process.

policy_statement: The Minister must issue guidelines within 12 months on how State entities ensure consistency with the Act's objectives and principles.

policy_statement: Decision-makers under prescribed laws must promote and ensure consistency with climate objectives, including mitigation, adaptation, vulnerability and emissions impacts.

section_header: Decision-makers must promote and ensure consistency with climate objectives
extraction_rationale: This is a binding decision-making standard across listed laws, explicitly covering emissions and climate vulnerability.

policy_statement: Environmental impact assessments must assess material greenhouse gas emissions, increased climate vulnerability and climate impacts, and measures to address them.

extraction_rationale: This creates a binding EIA requirement for emissions and climate risk assessment.

policy_statement: Government procurement policies must align with Fiji's climate instruments and, where possible, set minimum standards for adaptation, resilience, and zero- or low-emission products, vehicles and energy sources.
source_quote: The Fijian Procurement Office established by the Procurement Regulations 2010 must formulate procurement policies that are consistent with, or review and update existing procurement policies to ensure they are consistent with, the objectives and principles of this Act and the implementation of Fiji's NDC, NCCP, LEDS, NAP and National Ocean Policy and where possible, these procurement policies are to set minimum standards for- (a) promoting adaptation and climate resilience; and (b) sourcing zero or low emissions products, vehicles or energy sources.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete public procurement mandate with climate standards.

policy_statement: Ministers must annually review portfolios and adjust performance indicators to address climate risks, and revise civil-service job descriptions to support implementation of the Act.
source_quote: All ministers must, where relevant, annually review and assess ministerial portfolios and functions in relation to climate risks and make adjustments and changes to key performance indicators with the aim of ensuring climate change considerations are able to be adequately addressed. All ministers must, where relevant, review and revise key performance indicators and job descriptions for civil servants within their ministry with the aim of ensuring that civil servants are increasingly equipped with relevant specialist skills to support the implementation of this Act.
section_header: Ministerial portfolios, functions and human resourcing
extraction_rationale: This is a specific annual institutional capacity and accountability measure for climate implementation.

policy_statement: Climate change learning must be integrated into the Fiji National Curriculum Framework at all levels.
source_quote: In accordance with section 31(4) of the Constitution, the minister responsible for education must, in consultation with the Minister, integrate evidence-based learning about climate change into a variety of subjects of the Fiji National Curriculum Framework at all levels of the curriculum. The Minister may advise State entities responsible for universities and tertiary institutions on the integration of evidence-based learning about climate change into their curricula.
section_header: Integration of climate change into curricula
extraction_rationale: This is a specific education policy mandate for climate literacy.

policy_statement: State entities must include climate-relevant expenditure, climate financial impacts and support needs in budget submissions, and the finance minister must report economic implications of climate change in the national budget supplement.
source_quote: The minister responsible for finance must provide information on the economic implications of climate change in the supplement to the national budget. All State entities must include in their budget submissions- (a) actual and estimated details of climate-relevant expenditure for the purposes of the national budget and budget estimates document along with the financial impacts of climate change on the State entity; and (b) information on support needed and received in relation to finance, technology transfer and capacity-building under Articles 9, 10 and 11 of the Paris Agreement.
extraction_rationale: This is a mandatory climate budget reporting and tracking requirement. It is not itself an appropriation or grant.

policy_statement: The Minister must develop and implement a National Climate Change Policy through 2030 and successive 10-year periods.
source_quote: The Minister must, with the assistance of the Committee, develop and implement a NCCP for the period until 2030 and for successive periods of 10 years. The Minister must publish the NCCP online prior to the commencement of each successive period.
section_header: Development of the National Climate Change Policy
extraction_rationale: This is a named national policy framework with set duration and renewal periods.

policy_statement: The NCCP must state clear objectives and targets, provide strategic actions, cover all sectors, mainstream climate policy, and include monitoring and evaluation systems.
source_quote: The NCCP must- (a) state clear objectives and appropriate targets to achieve those objectives; (b) be explicitly in line with this Act and the Paris Agreement, and enhance synergies with other relevant national, regional and international policies, strategies and frameworks; (c) provide clear policy guidelines, and related strategic actions, to meet the overall objectives of the policy; and (d) embed gender, human-rights, and social and cultural issues. The NCCP must address all sectors of the economy and provide mechanisms for the mainstreaming of the NCCP into those sectors.
section_header: Development of the National Climate Change Policy
extraction_rationale: This specifies required content and mechanisms for the national climate policy, including targets and strategic actions.

policy_statement: The Minister must develop and publicly provide the Fijian GHG Inventory using accepted international methodologies.
source_quote: The Minister must develop the Fijian GHG Inventory in accordance with the good practice guidelines and methodologies established under the Convention, accepted by the IPCC and agreed upon by the CMA. The Minister must make the Fijian GHG Inventory publicly available online on the Information Platform.
extraction_rationale: This creates a formal national emissions inventory system, central to mitigation MRV.

policy_statement: Permanent secretaries for energy, transport, industry, agriculture, forestry, land use and waste must biennially estimate and submit emissions and emissions-reduction data.
source_quote: The following permanent secretaries must biennially estimate and compile data related to emissions and emissions reductions activities from within their portfolio and submit it to the Committe- (a) the permanent secretary or permanent secretaries responsible for energy and transport in relation to the energy and transport sectors; (b) the permanent secretary or permanent secretaries responsible for industrial processes and product use in relation to the industrial processes and product use sector; (c) the permanent secretary or permanent secretaries responsible for agriculture, forestry and other land use in relation to the agriculture, forestry and other land use sector; and (d) the permanent secretary or permanent secretaries responsible for waste in relation to the waste sector.
section_header: Sector-based collection of data and information needed to estimate emissions and emissions reduction data
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete recurring emissions-data collection requirement across key sectors.

policy_statement: Fuel importers distributing or selling fuel must keep and biennially report the amount of fuel sold.
source_quote: A person who imports fuels into Fiji for the purposes of distributing or selling fuel to companies or individuals must keep and biennially provide information to the permanent secretary responsible for transport on the amount of fuel sold for the financial year. The Minister must develop and publish guidelines on the content and form of the information that is to be kept and provided to the relevant permanent secretary for transport, including with respect to the type of fuels that must be reported on.
section_header: Mandatory reporting on bulk sale of fuels
extraction_rationale: This is a mandatory sectoral reporting requirement supporting transport and fuel-emissions accounting.

policy_statement: Facilities above a prescribed emissions threshold may biennially report net GHG emissions, removals and internationally transferred emissions reductions.
source_quote: A person who operates a facility in Fiji that collectively emits in excess of a quantity of carbon dioxide equivalent as specified by regulations per financial year may keep and biennially provide information to the relevant permanent secretary as prescribed by regulations made under this Act on their net greenhouse gas emissions for the financial year, including emissions by sources and anthropogenic removals by sinks of greenhouse gases and any emission reductions transferred internationally under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement or for any other purpose. The Minister must consult with relevant stakeholders to determine the quantity prescribed in accordance with subsection (1).
section_header: Voluntary facility-level reporting on emissions and emissions reduction data
extraction_rationale: This establishes a voluntary facility-level emissions reporting system with regulatory thresholds.

policy_statement: The Director must prepare a national inventory report every two years using the Fijian GHG Inventory and make it publicly available.
source_quote: The Director must prepare a national inventory report biennially and in accordance with the Paris Agreement, using the emissions data contained in the Fijian GHG Inventory. The Director must make national inventory reports publicly available online as soon as practicable after they are submitted in accordance with the Paris Agreement, including on the Information Platform.
extraction_rationale: This is a recurring reporting commitment under the Paris Agreement transparency framework.

policy_statement: The Director may develop, review and update a national climate change communications strategy to improve public awareness, risk reduction and preparedness.
source_quote: The Minister may direct the Director to develop, review and update a national climate change communications strategy to guide the dissemination of climate change related information through a variety of formats, media-types, languages and other communications channels for the purpose of increasing the consistency of State entities' communications on climate change and improving public awareness, risk-reduction and preparedness.
extraction_rationale: This is a named strategy for climate communications and preparedness. It is discretionary but specific.

policy_statement: The Director must establish within 12 months a public online Information Platform containing climate data, policies, reports, carbon budgets, risk scenarios, vulnerability information and finance activities.
source_quote: Within 12 months of the commencement of this section, the Director must develop a publicly accessible Information Platform online for the purpose of increasing the availability and accessibility of comprehensive data, information and government policies related to climate change. The Director must maintain the Information Platform and ensure that it contains all data and policies relevant to this purpose, including--
extraction_rationale: This is a time-bound data infrastructure commitment supporting climate governance and transparency.

policy_statement: Fiji's long-term emissions reduction target is net zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050, pursued through carbon budgets, LEDS, NCCP and NDC.
source_quote: The long term emissions reduction target for Fiji is net zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050. The Minister must, with the assistance of the Committee, take all reasonable steps to promote the achievement of the long term emissions reduction target through the development and implementation of carbon budgets, the LEDS, NCCP and NDC.
extraction_rationale: This is a statutory economy-wide mitigation target with a deadline and implementation mechanisms.

policy_statement: The Minister must determine 5-year carbon budgets for 2026-2050, publish them, and ensure each budget represents greater emissions reductions than the previous budget.
source_quote: This section establishes the process for the development of 5-year carbon budgets for the purposes of planning whole of economy emissions reductions as part of a cumulative effort to achieve net zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050. The Minister must ensure that each carbon budget constitutes a greater reduction in greenhouse gas emissions than any previous carbon budget as part of the cumulative effort to achieve net zero greenhouse gas emissions by the year 2050.
extraction_rationale: This creates a statutory carbon budgeting regime with defined periods and progressive ambition.

policy_statement: The Minister may introduce and implement regulations, measures and actions to limit or reduce greenhouse gas emissions across the economy.
source_quote: The Minister has the power to introduce and implement regulations, measures and actions with the purpose of limiting or reducing Fiji's greenhouse gas emissions across the economy including the energy, transport, industry, agriculture, forestry, fisheries, waste, tourism, aviation and shipping sectors. Without limiting subsection (1), the Minister may-
section_header: Minister has the power to introduce and implement regulations, measures and actions
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella statutory mitigation authority followed by listed regulatory, fiscal and operational sub-actions.

parent_statement: Ministerial mitigation regulations, measures and actions
policy_statement: Introduce and implement a carbon pricing mechanism, including an emissions trading scheme.
source_quote: Without limiting subsection (1), the Minister may- (a) introduce and implement a carbon pricing mechanism, including an emissions trading scheme; (b) prescribe fees and other charges due to the State paid on the volume of greenhouse gas emissions above a prescribed level;
section_header: Minister has the power to introduce and implement regulations, measures and actions
extraction_rationale: This is a specific market-based emissions pricing instrument.

parent_statement: Ministerial mitigation regulations, measures and actions
policy_statement: Prescribe fees and charges payable to the State for greenhouse gas emissions above a prescribed level.
source_quote: Without limiting subsection (1), the Minister may- (a) introduce and implement a carbon pricing mechanism, including an emissions trading scheme; (b) prescribe fees and other charges due to the State paid on the volume of greenhouse gas emissions above a prescribed level;
section_header: Minister has the power to introduce and implement regulations, measures and actions
extraction_rationale: This is a specific emissions fee or charge mechanism.

parent_statement: Ministerial mitigation regulations, measures and actions
policy_statement: Introduce fiscal incentives and national levies to reduce emissions, conserve natural sinks, and encourage investment in renewable energy, efficient cogeneration, energy-efficient infrastructure and zero-waste infrastructure.
source_quote: Without limiting subsection (1), the Minister may- (c) introduce and implement fiscal incentives and national levies with the purpose of- (i) limiting or reducing Fiji's greenhouse gas emissions, including in relation to particular sectors or industries; (ii) enhancing the conservation of natural sinks, particularly within natural protected areas and ecological conservation zones; and (iii) encouraging public and private investment in renewable energy and efficient cogeneration technologies, energy efficient infrastructure and zero-waste infrastructure and processes;
section_header: Minister has the power to introduce and implement regulations, measures and actions
extraction_rationale: This is a broad fiscal instrument for mitigation and resource-efficient infrastructure investment.

parent_statement: Ministerial mitigation regulations, measures and actions
policy_statement: Enhance environmental protection of land and ocean carbon sinks, including halting and reversing deforestation, afforestation, REDD+, reef and fisheries conservation, mangrove protection and nature-based coastal protection.
source_quote: Without limiting subsection (1), the Minister may- (d) enhance environmental protection of land and ocean carbon sinks in consultation with the ministers responsible for forests, fisheries, agriculture and environment, including with respect to halting and reversing deforestation and degradation of forests, afforestation initiatives, Fiji's REDD+ initiative, reef and fisheries conservation, mangrove protection and planting initiatives, nature-based coastal protection applications and sustainable agricultural practices;
section_header: Minister has the power to introduce and implement regulations, measures and actions
extraction_rationale: This is a specific sink-enhancement and ecosystem-based mitigation measure. It explicitly names natural sinks and nature-based coastal protection.

parent_statement: Ministerial mitigation regulations, measures and actions
policy_statement: Make regulations and policies for sustainable, low-emissions, energy-efficient and climate-resilient buildings and infrastructure.
source_quote: Without limiting subsection (1), the Minister may- (e) make regulations and develop policies for the construction of sustainable, low-emissions, energy efficient and climate resilient infrastructure and buildings; and (f) implement programmes that raise awareness of the impact of patterns of production and consumption in the generation of greenhouse gas emissions and compounds and promote patterns of sustainable production and consumption in the civil, social and private sectors.
section_header: Minister has the power to introduce and implement regulations, measures and actions
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete regulatory building and infrastructure policy combining emissions, efficiency and resilience.

parent_statement: Ministerial mitigation regulations, measures and actions
policy_statement: Implement programmes to raise awareness of production and consumption emissions and promote sustainable production and consumption.
source_quote: Without limiting subsection (1), the Minister may- (e) make regulations and develop policies for the construction of sustainable, low-emissions, energy efficient and climate resilient infrastructure and buildings; and (f) implement programmes that raise awareness of the impact of patterns of production and consumption in the generation of greenhouse gas emissions and compounds and promote patterns of sustainable production and consumption in the civil, social and private sectors.
section_header: Minister has the power to introduce and implement regulations, measures and actions
extraction_rationale: This is a specific awareness and behavior-change programme targeting emissions from consumption and production.

policy_statement: The Minister must develop and implement a Transport Decarbonisation Implementation Strategy within 2 years, and review it every 5 years, to decarbonise transport by 2050.
source_quote: The Minister must, in consultation with the Minister responsible for transport, develop and implement a detailed Transport Decarbonisation Implementation Strategy within 2 years from the commencement of this section, that builds upon the LEDS to decarbonise the transport sector by 2050. The Minister must review and update the Transport Decarbonisation Implementation Strategy every 5 years.
extraction_rationale: This is a named, time-bound sectoral mitigation strategy with a 2050 decarbonisation objective.

policy_statement: Fiji establishes registrable carbon sequestration property rights as separate legal rights to carbon sequestration and carbon stocks.
source_quote: In this Act, carbon sequestration property right means the exclusive and distinct legal right to carbon sequestration and carbon stocks. A carbon sequestration property right- (a) must be registered in accordance with this Part with the office of the Registrar of Titles who, for the purposes of this Act, is the Registrar of Carbon Sequestration Property Rights ( the Registrar );
extraction_rationale: This creates a legal mechanism enabling carbon sequestration and emissions reduction projects.

policy_statement: Mining, logging, exploration, exploitation or extractive activity may not be approved on land with registered carbon sequestration rights and approved REDD+ or qualifying emissions reduction projects.
source_quote: No mining, logging, exploration, exploitation or extractive activity is to be approved on lands over which- (a) a carbon sequestration property right has been registered; and (b) an international REDD+ program or emissions reduction project, programme or activity involving forests, blue carbon or other project, programme or activity type prescribed by regulations made under this Act has been approved.
section_header: Land over which a carbon sequestration property right is registered
extraction_rationale: This is a binding land-use restriction protecting carbon sequestration projects.

policy_statement: The forests minister is responsible for Fiji's national REDD+ policy framework, safeguards, international participation and benefit sharing.
source_quote: The Minister responsible for forests is responsible for- (a) developing and updating Fiji's national REDD+ policy and strategy including the development of any national or sub-national REDD+ programme; (b) developing the national forest reference emissions level; (c) developing policies, procedures and safeguards for the implementation of REDD+ and forest emission reduction projects, programmes and activities, with all safeguards to be developed in accordance with the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples;
extraction_rationale: This is a named REDD+ umbrella policy with listed subcomponents for forest emissions reductions.

parent_statement: REDD+ Policy
policy_statement: Develop and update Fiji's national REDD+ policy and strategy, including national or sub-national REDD+ programmes.
source_quote: The Minister responsible for forests is responsible for- (a) developing and updating Fiji's national REDD+ policy and strategy including the development of any national or sub-national REDD+ programme; (b) developing the national forest reference emissions level;
extraction_rationale: This is a specific forest-based mitigation programme commitment.

parent_statement: REDD+ Policy
policy_statement: Develop the national forest reference emissions level.
source_quote: The Minister responsible for forests is responsible for- (a) developing and updating Fiji's national REDD+ policy and strategy including the development of any national or sub-national REDD+ programme; (b) developing the national forest reference emissions level;
extraction_rationale: This establishes a technical benchmark needed to quantify forest-sector emissions reductions.

parent_statement: REDD+ Policy
policy_statement: Develop policies, procedures and safeguards for REDD+ and forest emission reduction projects, programmes and activities.
source_quote: The Minister responsible for forests is responsible for- (c) developing policies, procedures and safeguards for the implementation of REDD+ and forest emission reduction projects, programmes and activities, with all safeguards to be developed in accordance with the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples; (d) Fiji's participation in international REDD+ programmes; and
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete governance safeguard commitment for forest emissions reduction projects.

parent_statement: REDD+ Policy
policy_statement: Participate in international REDD+ programmes and develop benefit-sharing arrangements for forest emission reduction projects.
source_quote: The Minister responsible for forests is responsible for- (d) Fiji's participation in international REDD+ programmes; and (e) developing a benefit sharing arrangement for forest emission reduction projects, programmes and activities.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific REDD+ market and benefit-sharing arrangement. The benefit-sharing component is financial but within a broader REDD+ policy.

policy_statement: The Director may develop emissions reduction methodologies and the Minister may approve them as Fijian Emissions Reduction Methodologies.
source_quote: The Director may develop emissions reduction methodologies. The Minister may by notice in the Gazette approve as a Fijian Emissions Reduction Methodology- (a) an emissions reduction methodology developed by the Director; or (b) an emissions reduction methodology that is approved under an approved international emissions reduction standard or a foreign emissions trading scheme and for which it has obtained consent to use.
extraction_rationale: This creates the methodological framework for credited emissions reduction activities.

policy_statement: Persons may apply for emissions reduction projects, programmes or activities to be declared as Fijian Emissions Reduction Projects, Programmes or Activities.
source_quote: A person may apply to the Director for the declaration of an emissions reduction project, programme or activity as a Fijian Emissions Reduction Project, Programme or Activity. The Director must determine, in writing, an application made in accordance with subsection (1) within 60 days of receiving the application by either- (a) declaring the emissions reduction project, programme or activity to be a Fijian Emissions Reduction Project, Programme or Activity, with or without conditions; or (b) refusing the application.
section_header: Fijian Emissions Reduction Projects, Programmes or Activities
extraction_rationale: This establishes a formal approval process for domestic emissions reduction projects.

policy_statement: Verified Fijian emissions reductions may receive Fijian Emissions Reduction Statements and equivalent Fijian Mitigation Outcome Units.
source_quote: The Director must issue a Fijian Emissions Reduction Statement within 30 days of receiving the application if he or she is satisfied that- (b) the verification report is true and correct and the emissions reductions generated by the project, programme or activity have been verified in accordance with the applicable methodology, regulations, rules or standards; (c) the grant of the statement will not result in any double counting of emission reductions from the project, programme or activity; and (d) any preconditions specified in the regulations have been met. The Fijian Emissions Reduction Statement must state that a specified number of emissions reductions have been achieved by the Fijian Emissions Reduction Project, Programme or Activity for the relevant reporting period and that an equivalent number of Fijian Mitigation Outcome Units may be issued to the nominated Registry account.
extraction_rationale: This creates a verified crediting pathway for emissions reductions.

policy_statement: The Director must issue Fijian Mitigation Outcome Units equal to the verified unit entitlement in a Fijian Emissions Reduction Statement.
source_quote: If a Fijian Emissions Reduction Statement has been issued in respect of a Fijian Emissions Reduction Project, Programme or Activity for a reporting period, the Director must, as soon as practicable after the day on which the Fijian Emissions Reduction Statement was issued, issue to the Registry account nominated on the statement a number of Fijian Mitigation Outcome Units equal to the number specified in the statement as the unit entitlement for that statement. Upon the issuance of a Fijian Mitigation Outcome Unit to a person, that person will be the legal owner of the Fijian Mitigation Outcome Unit.
section_header: Issue of Fijian Mitigation Outcome Units in respect of Fijian Emissions Reduction Projects, Programmes and Activities
extraction_rationale: This creates tradable mitigation outcome units, functioning as a carbon market instrument.

policy_statement: Where sequestration reversals or carbon stock losses occur in forest, blue carbon or prescribed projects, proponents must report and remedy the reversal or cancel equivalent units.
source_quote: If Fijian Mitigation Outcome Units have been issued in respect of a Fijian Emissions Reduction Programme, Project or Activity involving forests, blue carbon, or other project, programme or activity type prescribed by regulations, and there has been a material reversal or loss of carbon stocks within the permanence period of that programme, project or activity, the proponent must report the reversal or loss of carbon stocks to the Director as soon as practicable after becoming aware of the reversal or loss of carbon stocks. A proponent may satisfy a requirement under subsection (2) to remedy the reversal or loss of carbon stocks by, within 90 days after the requirement was issued- (a) submitting a remediation plan to the Director; or (b) purchasing and cancelling a number of Fijian Mitigation Outcome Units or other emissions reduction units approved by the Director as equivalent to the reversal or loss of carbon stocks.
section_header: Requirement to cancel Fijian Mitigation Outcome Units where there has been a reversal of sequestration
extraction_rationale: This is a permanence and reversal management mechanism for carbon sequestration projects.

policy_statement: Emissions reduction projects under approved international standards in Fiji require the Director's consent for registration, conduct, use, sale or transfer of units.
source_quote: A person who registers and conducts an emissions reduction project, programme or activity in Fiji under an approved international emissions reduction standard or uses, sells or transfers emission reduction units under the relevant standard without the consent of the Director commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $750,000. A person may apply to the Director for the Director's consent for the proponent to- (a) register or conduct an emissions reduction project, programme or activity in Fiji under an approved international emissions reduction standard for a designated crediting period; or (b) use, sell and transfer domestically and/or internationally emissions reduction units issued under an approved international emissions reduction standard for an emissions reduction project, programme or activity during the designated crediting period.
section_header: Registration and conduct of emissions reduction projects, programmes and activities under approved international emissions reduction standards
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory approval system for international carbon market projects and units in Fiji.

policy_statement: Emission reduction units generated in Fiji under international standards may be converted to Fijian Mitigation Outcome Units with Director consent and cancellation of the foreign units.
source_quote: The proponent of an emissions reduction project, programme or activity in Fiji that is registered under an approved international emissions reduction standard may apply to the Director for the Director's consent for the proponent to convert any or all of the emission reduction units issued in relation to the project, programme or activity to Fijian Mitigation Outcome Units. As soon as practicable after the Director receives evidence of the cancellation of the number of emission reduction units set out in the conversion statement from a foreign account, the Director must issue the number of Fijian Mitigation Outcomes Units set out in the conversion statement to the nominated Registry account.
section_header: Conversion of emission reduction units generated in Fiji under international emissions reduction standards to Fijian Mitigation Outcome Units
extraction_rationale: This establishes conversion between international and domestic carbon units while preventing double counting.

policy_statement: Article 6 emissions reduction projects in Fiji require the Director's consent and must align with Fiji's NDC, carbon budget and long-term emissions target.
source_quote: A person who registers, conducts or otherwise operates an emissions reduction project, programme or activity in Fiji for the purposes of Article 6 of the Paris Agreement without the consent of the Director commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $750,000. The Director may only grant consent to the application if he or she is satisfied that the project, programme or activity- (b) is consistent with Fiji's NDC, current carbon budget and the long term emissions reduction target; (c) is consistent with and will be accounted for in accordance with any rules, modalities and guidance developed by the CMA for the purposes of Articles 6 and 13 of the Paris Agreement;
section_header: Emissions reduction projects, programmes and activities for the purposes of Article 6 of the Paris Agreement
extraction_rationale: This is a binding regulatory framework for Article 6 mitigation projects.

policy_statement: International transfer of Fijian Mitigation Outcome Units requires Director consent and must be consistent with Fiji's NDC, ITMO policies and Paris Agreement accounting rules.
source_quote: A person who, without the consent of the Director- (a) transfers Fijian Mitigation Outcome Units to a foreign account; or (b) transfers Fijian Mitigation Outcome Units internationally and for the purposes of Article 6 of the Paris Agreement, commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $750,000. The Director may only grant consent to an application if it is satisfied that the international transfer- (a) complies with this Act and any regulations made under this Act; (b) is consistent with Fiji's NDC; (c) is consistent with any policy, guidelines, standards or procedures adopted by the Government for the transfer and use of ITMOs and the international transfer of Fijian Mitigation Outcome Units in accordance with the Paris Agreement or any other international agreements to which Fiji is a Party including with respect to avoiding double counting; and
section_header: International transfer of Fijian Mitigation Outcome Units
extraction_rationale: This regulates international carbon-unit transfers and Article 6 mitigation outcomes.

policy_statement: Government transactions under international REDD+ programmes must obtain required consent, compensate landowners or right holders through benefit-sharing plans, and record transactions in the Registry.
source_quote: Where the Government participates in any transaction under an international REDD + programme, the Minister is to be taken to have the authority of the person who owns the registered carbon sequestration property right under section 45(2) to sell and transfer all carbon sequestered by the forest including in the form of emissions reductions, Fijian Mitigation Outcome Units or carbon sequestration resulting from that programme provided that- (c) the Government compensates the iTaukei Land Trust Board, if applicable, and any other landowner with forest carbon or person who owns a registered carbon sequestration property right included in the transaction under an approved benefits sharing plan; (d) the Minister has considered the market value of the emissions reductions or Fijian Mitigation Outcome Units at the time of evaluating the proposed transaction and the impact such a transaction will have on Fiji's NDC;
extraction_rationale: This is a REDD+ transaction and benefit-sharing framework involving carbon assets and compensation.

policy_statement: The Fijian Registry is established as an online public registry for emissions reduction projects, Fijian Mitigation Outcome Units, international-standard units and ITMOs.
source_quote: This section establishes the Fijian Registry. The purposes of the Registry are as follows- (a) to be a registry for emissions reduction projects, programmes and activities; (b) to be a registry for Fijian Mitigation Outcome Units; (c) to be a registry for emissions reduction units issued under an approved international emissions reduction standard in relation to an emissions reduction project, programme or activity in Fiji; and (d) to be Fiji's national registry for any incoming ITMOs from another country or outgoing Fijian Mitigation Outcome Units to another country.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific institutional mechanism for tracking mitigation projects and carbon units.

policy_statement: The National Adaptation Plan Steering Committee must prepare successive National Adaptation Plans addressing climate risk management, sectors, ecosystems, infrastructure, resource mobilisation and integration of climate risk.
source_quote: The NAP Steering Committee must prepare successive NAPs, that may address- (a) comprehensive risk management; (b) water resources; (c) agriculture, forestry, fishing and aquaculture; (d) ecosystems and biodiversity; (e) transportation and communication infrastructure; (f) land-use planning and urban development; (g) health and public health infrastructure; (h) marine and terrestrial pollution reduction objectives; (i) adaptation and mitigation co-benefits resulting from environmental conservation activities;
extraction_rationale: This is a named national adaptation planning instrument covering multiple sectors and risk-management measures.

policy_statement: The Minister may introduce and implement regulations, policies, measures, adaptation planning processes and actions to increase Fiji's climate resilience and adaptive capacity.
source_quote: The Minister has the power to introduce and implement regulations, policies, measures, adaptation planning processes and actions with the purpose of increasing Fiji's resilience to climate change and ability to adapt to climate change. The Director must record any regulations, policies, measures, adaptation planning processes and actions implemented in accordance with this section on the Adaptation Registry.
section_header: Minister has the power to introduce and implement regulations, policies, measures, adptation planning processes and actions
extraction_rationale: This grants a broad but explicit statutory authority for adaptation measures and requires registry recording.

policy_statement: The Director may build or commission integrated risk scenarios that model physical climate impacts, socioeconomic interactions and adaptation options.
source_quote: The Director, in consultation with the Fiji Meteorological Service and other relevant stakeholders, may build or commission work to consider, analyse and consult upon interdisciplinary information, data, trends and projections that can be integrated to produce intelligence on potential future risk scenarios. These integrated risk scenarios must- (a) model the potential and projected physical impacts of climate change as well as the way these impacts interact with other projected risks and socioeconomic factors and considerations over different time horizons; (b) support national, sub-national and localised vulnerability, exposure and sensitivity assessments as required; and (c) assist efforts to assess adaptive management options, conduct thresholds analysis and improve capacity for system-based approaches to achieving resilient development objectives.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific adaptation planning tool for vulnerability, risk and resilience decision-making.

policy_statement: The Minister may audit public infrastructure and physical assets at risk from climate change and maintain a resilience register.
source_quote: The Minister may, in close co-ordination with relevant ministries and State entities, conduct an audit of existing public infrastructure and physical assets that are at risk from climate change, including- (d) the extent to which infrastructure and physical assets are climate resilient, including physical, social and environmental resilience to the impacts of climate change, with reference to any integrated risk scenarios developed in accordance with this Act. The Minister may maintain a register of all existing public infrastructure and physical assets which records the data collected by the audit conducted in accordance with subsection (1) and any repairs carried out on public infrastructure and physical assets for the purpose of increasing resilience to the impacts of climate change.
section_header: Audit of public infrastructure and physical assets
extraction_rationale: This is a specific adaptation intervention for climate risk assessment and asset resilience tracking.

policy_statement: New infrastructure proposals must undergo climate risk and resilience assessment, and approvals must be consistent with that assessment.
source_quote: In addition to sections 19, 22 and 23, all ministers, State entities and other persons making decisions relating to proposals for new infrastructure must-- (a) direct that a climate risk and resilience assessment be conducted on the proposal with reference to any integrated risk scenarios developed in accordance with this Act and other relevant risk scenarios; (b) consider the climate risk and resilience assessment prepared in accordance with paragraph (a) when deciding whether or not to approve the proposal; and (c) make a decision to approve or not approve the proposal that promotes and is consistent with the climate risk and resilience assessment prepared in accordance with paragraph (a).
extraction_rationale: This is a binding climate-resilience assessment requirement for new infrastructure.

policy_statement: The National Building Code must be reviewed immediately and every 5 years to increase building resilience and align with the Act.
source_quote: The Minister responsible for health, with the assistance of the Director and the Minister responsible for infrastructure as required, must review and if necessary amend the content, expand the scope and scale up the implementation and enforcement of the National Building Code immediately upon the commencement of this section and every 5 years thereafter for the purpose of increasing the climate resilience of Fiji's buildings and the alignment of the National Building Code with the objectives and principles of this Act. The Minister responsible for health, in reviewing and amending the National Building Code, must take into consideration-
extraction_rationale: This is a recurring regulatory building-code reform mandate for climate resilience.

policy_statement: The Fijian Adaptation Registry is established as an online public registry for adaptation projects in Fiji.
source_quote: This section establishes the Fijian Adaptation Registry. The Adaptation Registry is to be maintained by electronic means and publicly accessible online. The purpose of the Adaptation Registry is to be a registry for adaptation projects in Fiji.
extraction_rationale: This creates a specific institutional registry for adaptation projects.

policy_statement: Adaptation project implementers may submit reports for registration and publication on the Adaptation Registry.
source_quote: A person who implements an adaptation project in Fiji may provide reports to the Director. If the Director considers that the report is in relation to an adaptation project in Fiji, the Director must register the Project and publish the report on the Adaptation Registry.
extraction_rationale: This is a voluntary reporting and transparency mechanism for adaptation projects.

policy_statement: Fiji establishes the Taskforce on the Relocation and Displacement of Communities Vulnerable to the Impacts of Climate Change.
source_quote: This section establishes the Fijian Taskforce on the Relocation and Displacement of Communities Vulnerable to the Impacts of Climate Change. The governance, membership, operation, frequency of meetings and reporting procedures of the Fijian Taskforce on Relocation and Displacement must be in accordance with the Fijian Taskforce on Relocation and Displacement's Terms of Reference.
section_header: Fijian Taskforce on the Relocation and Displacement of Communities Vulnerable to the Impacts of Climate Change
extraction_rationale: This creates a named institutional mechanism for climate displacement and relocation.

policy_statement: The Minister must prepare successive Fijian Planned Relocation Guidelines and operationalise them through standard operating procedures for climate- and disaster-driven displacement.
source_quote: The Minister, with the assistance of the Fijian Taskforce on Relocation and Displacement, must prepare successive Fijian Planned Relocation Guidelines. The Minister, with the assistance of the Fijian Taskforce on Relocation and Displacement, must operationalise the Fijian Planned Relocation Guidelines through developing standard operating procedures which enable pro-active processes for addressing the risk of climate and disaster driven displacement.
extraction_rationale: This is a named adaptation policy and operational procedure for displacement risk.

policy_statement: The Minister is responsible for relocating and supporting at-risk communities under rights-based objectives, only after other NAP adaptation measures are exhausted and with free, prior and informed consent.
source_quote: The Minister, with the support of the Fijian Taskforce on Relocation and Displacement, is responsible for relocating and supporting at-risk communities in accordance with the following objectives- (d) to relocate at-risk communities only when other adaptation measures as set out in the NAP have been exhausted; (e) to relocate at-risk communities only with the full free and prior informed consent of the communities, following inclusive and gender responsive consultation and participatory processes; (f) to ensure that relocation sites- (i) are on land that is least vulnerable to climate change impacts and capable of supporting the current and future needs of the at-risk community and any existing or host communities;
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete climate adaptation and relocation policy with safeguards and decision criteria.

policy_statement: The Minister may use the Climate Relocation of Communities Trust Fund for planned relocation of communities adversely affected by climate change.
source_quote: The Minister may use monies in the Climate Relocation of Communities Trust Fund established under section 3 of the Climate Relocation of Communities Trust Fund Act 2019 for the purposes of this Part.
section_header: Trust Fund for the Planned Relocation of Communities in Fiji that are adversely affected by climate change
extraction_rationale: This is a named financial instrument for climate relocation and adaptation.

policy_statement: Fiji maintains the permanence of its maritime boundaries and maritime zones notwithstanding climate change and sea-level rise.
source_quote: This Act recognises the permanence of Fiji's maritime boundaries and maritime zones and maintains the rights and entitlements that flow from Fiji's maritime zones under Articles 3, 8, 33, 49, 57 and 76 of UNCLOS notwithstanding the effects of climate change and sea level rise. For the purposes of subsection (1), the list of geographical coordinates submitted to the Secretary-General of the United Nations pursuant to UNCLOS are, without reduction, to be maintained as Fiji's permanent maritime boundaries, notwithstanding the effects of climate change and sea level rise.
section_header: Permanence of Fiji's maritime boundaries and maritime zones
extraction_rationale: This is a legal adaptation response to sea-level rise and sovereignty risk.

policy_statement: Fiji sets a long-term ocean sustainability target of 100% sustainable and effective management of its maritime waters and a 2030 target to designate 30% as marine protected areas.
source_quote: This section sets Fiji's long term ocean sustainability target, which is for Fiji's internal waters, archipelagic waters, territorial seas, contiguous zone and exclusive economic zone to be 100% sustainably and effectively managed. This section sets Fiji's 2030 marine protected area target, which is for 30% of Fiji's internal waters, archipelagic waters, territorial seas, contiguous zone and exclusive economic zone to be designated as a marine protected area by 2030.
extraction_rationale: This establishes quantifiable ocean conservation targets with a 2030 deadline for marine protected areas.

policy_statement: The National Ocean Policy Steering Committee must prepare successive National Ocean Policies to guide government policy on fisheries, marine resources, maritime issues, marine research and conservation.
source_quote: The National Ocean Policy Steering Committee must prepare successive National Ocean Policies. The purpose of the National Ocean Policy is to guide all government policies in relation to fisheries, marine resources, maritime issues, marine scientific research and any other issues related to the use, management and conservation of Fiji's maritime waters.
extraction_rationale: This is a named ocean governance policy with recurring preparation and review requirements.

policy_statement: The Minister may implement regulations, policies, measures and actions for evidence-based conservation and restoration of Fiji's maritime waters and coastal environments.
source_quote: The Minister may make and implement regulations, policies, measures and actions that promote an evidence-based approach to the conservation and restoration of Fiji's internal waters, archipelagic waters, territorial seas, contiguous zone and exclusive economic zone and coastal environments, including- (a) protecting stores of blue carbon; (b) sustainable management of oceans and reducing anthropogenic stresses on marine and coastal ecosystems;
section_header: Minister has the power to introduce and implement regulations, policies, measures and actions
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella ocean and coastal ecosystem policy followed by specific sub-actions.

parent_statement: Ocean and coastal conservation and restoration regulations, policies, measures and actions
policy_statement: Protect stores of blue carbon in Fiji's maritime waters and coastal environments.
source_quote: The Minister may make and implement regulations, policies, measures and actions that promote an evidence-based approach to the conservation and restoration of Fiji's internal waters, archipelagic waters, territorial seas, contiguous zone and exclusive economic zone and coastal environments, including- (a) protecting stores of blue carbon; (b) sustainable management of oceans and reducing anthropogenic stresses on marine and coastal ecosystems;
section_header: Minister has the power to introduce and implement regulations, policies, measures and actions
extraction_rationale: This is an ecosystem-based carbon storage policy explicitly focused on blue carbon.

parent_statement: Ocean and coastal conservation and restoration regulations, policies, measures and actions
policy_statement: Sustainably manage oceans and reduce anthropogenic stresses on marine and coastal ecosystems.
source_quote: The Minister may make and implement regulations, policies, measures and actions that promote an evidence-based approach to the conservation and restoration of Fiji's internal waters, archipelagic waters, territorial seas, contiguous zone and exclusive economic zone and coastal environments, including- (b) sustainable management of oceans and reducing anthropogenic stresses on marine and coastal ecosystems; (c) putting in place measures to maintain and reinforce Fiji's maritime boundaries pursuant to section 80; and
section_header: Minister has the power to introduce and implement regulations, policies, measures and actions
extraction_rationale: This is a specific ecosystem management and stress-reduction intervention.

parent_statement: Ocean and coastal conservation and restoration regulations, policies, measures and actions
policy_statement: Implement measures to maintain and reinforce Fiji's maritime boundaries in response to sea-level rise.
source_quote: The Minister may make and implement regulations, policies, measures and actions that promote an evidence-based approach to the conservation and restoration of Fiji's internal waters, archipelagic waters, territorial seas, contiguous zone and exclusive economic zone and coastal environments, including- (c) putting in place measures to maintain and reinforce Fiji's maritime boundaries pursuant to section 80; and (d) fiscal incentives and education campaigns supporting alternatives to nonbiodegradable and non-ecofriendly materials.
section_header: Minister has the power to introduce and implement regulations, policies, measures and actions
extraction_rationale: This is a legal and policy adaptation measure for maritime boundary permanence under climate-driven sea-level rise.

parent_statement: Ocean and coastal conservation and restoration regulations, policies, measures and actions
policy_statement: Use fiscal incentives and education campaigns to support alternatives to non-biodegradable and non-eco-friendly materials.
source_quote: The Minister may make and implement regulations, policies, measures and actions that promote an evidence-based approach to the conservation and restoration of Fiji's internal waters, archipelagic waters, territorial seas, contiguous zone and exclusive economic zone and coastal environments, including- (c) putting in place measures to maintain and reinforce Fiji's maritime boundaries pursuant to section 80; and (d) fiscal incentives and education campaigns supporting alternatives to nonbiodegradable and non-ecofriendly materials.
section_header: Minister has the power to introduce and implement regulations, policies, measures and actions
extraction_rationale: This is a financial and behavioral resource-efficiency measure to reduce harmful materials affecting marine environments.

policy_statement: The Minister may implement regulations, policies, measures and actions to enhance the mitigation potential of oceans.
source_quote: The Minister may make regulations and policies and implement measures and actions to enhance the mitigation potential of oceans, including- (a) enhancing blue carbon; (b) developing offshore renewable energy generation; and (c) increasing energy efficiency in maritime services.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella ocean-mitigation policy with listed sub-actions.

parent_statement: Enhancing the mitigation potential of oceans
policy_statement: Enhance blue carbon.
source_quote: The Minister may make regulations and policies and implement measures and actions to enhance the mitigation potential of oceans, including- (a) enhancing blue carbon; (b) developing offshore renewable energy generation; and (c) increasing energy efficiency in maritime services.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific ecosystem-based carbon sequestration measure.

parent_statement: Enhancing the mitigation potential of oceans
policy_statement: Develop offshore renewable energy generation.
source_quote: The Minister may make regulations and policies and implement measures and actions to enhance the mitigation potential of oceans, including- (a) enhancing blue carbon; (b) developing offshore renewable energy generation; and (c) increasing energy efficiency in maritime services.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific renewable energy mitigation intervention.

parent_statement: Enhancing the mitigation potential of oceans
policy_statement: Increase energy efficiency in maritime services.
source_quote: The Minister may make regulations and policies and implement measures and actions to enhance the mitigation potential of oceans, including- (a) enhancing blue carbon; (b) developing offshore renewable energy generation; and (c) increasing energy efficiency in maritime services.
extraction_rationale: This is a named efficiency action for maritime services, explicitly tied to ocean mitigation potential.

policy_statement: The Minister may direct Fiji Meteorological Service or a State entity to prepare and update studies on climate impacts on oceans and sustainable ocean resource provision.
source_quote: The Minister may direct the Fiji Meteorological Service or any State entity to prepare and regularly update studies on the impact of climate change on oceans and the ability of oceans to sustainably provide resources for Fijians for commercial, subsistence and other purposes.
section_header: Minister may direct Fiji Meteorological Service or any State entity to prepare studies
extraction_rationale: This is a specific climate research and planning measure for ocean adaptation and resource sustainability.

policy_statement: The finance minister may implement climate budget coding and tracking systems within the public financial management system.
source_quote: The Minister responsible for finance may- (b) work closely with the national budget process and relevant offices within the ministry responsible for finance to implement climate budget coding and tracking systems and the incorporation of such systems in to the Government's overall public financial management system; (c) carry out the reporting, monitoring and evaluation of domestic climate finance sources including ECAL, private sector sources, and insurance initiatives and make any such reports publicly available on the Information Platform;
section_header: Powers of the Minister responsible for finance
extraction_rationale: This is a specific climate public-finance management and tracking mechanism, but not itself a funding instrument.

policy_statement: The finance minister may oversee access to climate funds and multilateral development banks to enhance sustainable climate finance flows.
source_quote: The Minister responsible for finance may- (d) actively oversee Fiji's engagement with the Green Climate Fund, Adaptation Fund and multilateral development banks to facilitate and enhance Fiji's access to sustainable climate finance flows; and (e) review donor engagement and coordination arrangements to enhance efficiency, complementarity, and the leveraging of co-benefits in alignment with the NCCP.
section_header: Powers of the Minister responsible for finance
extraction_rationale: This is a climate finance access and coordination policy. It concerns finance but is a governance role rather than a specific grant or levy.

policy_statement: The finance minister may grant incentives for measures that mitigate climate change, reduce GHG emissions, use renewable energy, improve energy efficiency, adapt to climate change, improve resilience, or provide climate training.
source_quote: The Minister responsible for finance may, in accordance with the Financial Management Act 2004, grant to persons that- (a) encourage and put in place measures for the mitigation of climate change including reduction of greenhouse emissions, use of renewable energy and energy efficiency; (b) put in place measures to adapt and improve Fiji's resilience to climate change; or (c) are involved in the conduct of accredited training in programmes that are aimed at mitigating and adapting to climate change, such incentives as may be necessary for the advancement of such measures and activities designed for the mitigation of and adaptation to climate change.
section_header: Incentives for the promotion of climate change initiatives
extraction_rationale: This is an explicit incentive instrument for mitigation, adaptation, renewable energy and energy efficiency.

policy_statement: Accredited State entities or private organisations may receive and administer public or private contributions for mitigation and adaptation measures with ministerial approval.
source_quote: State entities or private organisations accredited to climate funds, including the Green Climate Fund, can be recipients and administrators of public or private contributions designated to be used for the implementation of measures for mitigation and adaptation to climate change with the approval of the Minister. Administrators of the State entities or private organisations in subsection (1) must monitor, evaluate, publish and communicate to the Minister and the Minister responsible for finance the results of their actions to address climate change and demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of their expenditure.
extraction_rationale: This creates an institutional climate finance channel for mitigation and adaptation funding.

policy_statement: The finance minister may institute financial instruments and mechanisms to implement the Act and climate mitigation and adaptation actions.
source_quote: The Minister responsible for finance, subject to and in accordance with all written laws, may institute financial instruments and mechanisms with the purpose of implementing this Act and climate change mitigation and adaptation actions pursuant to the objectives and principles of this Act.
extraction_rationale: This is a broad financial instrument authority for climate action.

policy_statement: The finance minister, in consultation with the Reserve Bank, must develop national climate finance strategies, frameworks and approaches and review them every 5 years.
source_quote: The Minister responsible for finance, in consultation with the Reserve Bank, must develop national climate finance strategies, frameworks and approaches to support and coordinate Fiji's ongoing access to climate finance. The Minister, in consultation with the Reserve Bank, must review the national climate finance strategies and frameworks every 5 years.
extraction_rationale: This is a mandatory climate finance planning commitment with a recurring review cycle.

policy_statement: The Minister may establish a private sector advisory committee to support private-sector implementation, knowledge sharing, compliance resources and climate-aligned public-private partnerships.
source_quote: The Minister may establish a private sector advisory committee for the following purposes- (a) promoting dialogue with the private sector on the implementation of this Act; (b) promoting the sharing of knowledge and experience between the private and public sectors; (c) developing and disseminating resources to assist the private sector in complying with this Act; and (d) promoting and creating an enabling environment for public private partnerships that are consistent with achieving the objectives and principles of this Act.
extraction_rationale: This is a named engagement mechanism for climate implementation by the private sector.

policy_statement: Within 12 months, the Minister must publish guidance to help companies, investment schemes, financial institutions and the Reserve Bank meet climate-risk obligations, using best practice including TCFD recommendations.
source_quote: Within 12 months of the commencement of this section, the Minister must develop and publish guidance materials for the purpose of assisting directors or other officers of a company, managed investment schemes, the Fiji National Provident Fund Board, licensed financial institutions and the Reserve Bank to fulfil their obligations under this Part. In developing such guidance materials, the Minister must have regard to industry best practice including the recommendations of the Financial Stability Board's Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures.
extraction_rationale: This is a time-bound guidance policy for climate-related financial disclosure and risk governance.

policy_statement: Company directors and officers must consider and evaluate foreseeable climate change risks and opportunities that intersect with company interests.
source_quote: In exercising reasonable care and diligence under section 106(1) of the Companies Act 2015, directors or other officers of a company must consider and evaluate climate change risks and opportunities to the extent they are foreseeable and intersect with the interests of the company. For the purposes of this Part, climate change risks include- (a) the physical risks associated with climate change, including both acute risks (for example extreme weather events) and chronic risks (for example rising temperatures, rising sea levels and changes in water availability, sourcing and quality) that may affect, for example, a company's premises and other assets, operations, supply chains, transport needs and employee safety;
section_header: Directors must consider and evaluate climate change risks and opportunities
extraction_rationale: This creates a binding private-sector climate-risk governance duty.

policy_statement: The Fiji National Provident Fund Board must consider and evaluate foreseeable climate change risks and opportunities affecting each fund and the Board.
source_quote: In exercising its duties under section 9 of the Fiji National Provident Fund Act 2011, the Fiji National Provident Fund Board must consider and evaluate climate change risks and opportunities to the extent they are foreseeable and intersect with the interests of each fund and the Board.
section_header: Fiji National Provident Fund Board must consider and evaluate climate change risks and opportunities
extraction_rationale: This imposes a climate-risk governance obligation on a major public provident fund.

policy_statement: Companies and managed investment schemes must disclose material financial climate risks, measures to reduce them, integration of climate risks into policies and decision-making, and climate impacts and Paris alignment.
source_quote: All companies and managed investment schemes that are required to prepare financial statements and a directors' report under section 388 of the Companies Act 2015 must disclose, in their financial statements and directors' report- (a) any material financial risks to the company or managed investment scheme arising from climate change risks and climate change opportunities; (b) measures adopted by the company or managed investment scheme to reduce its exposure to these material financial risks; (c) how consideration of climate change risks are integrated into investment policies, risk management policies and investment decision-making processes; and (d) the climate change impacts of the activities of the company or managed investment scheme activities and of the use of goods and services it produces and the extent to which the company or managed investment scheme complies with the long-term temperature goal in Article 2 of the Paris Agreement.
section_header: Disclosure of financial risks of climate change and measures adopted to reduce them by companies and managed investment schemes
extraction_rationale: This is a binding climate-related financial disclosure requirement for companies and investment schemes.

policy_statement: The Fiji National Provident Fund Board must disclose material climate financial risks, risk-reduction measures, integration into investment policies, climate impacts and Paris alignment in financial reports.
source_quote: The Fiji National Provident Fund Board, when preparing financial reports in accordance with section 25 of the Fiji National Provident Fund Act 2011, must disclose in their financial reports- (a) any material financial risks to each fund and the Board arising from climate change risks and climate change opportunities; (b) measures adopted by each fund and the Board to reduce its exposure to these material financial risks; (c) how consideration of climate change risks are integrated into investment policies, risk management policies and investment decision-making processes; and (d) the climate change impacts of each fund and the Board's activities and of the use of goods and services it produces and the extent to which each fund and the Board complies with the long-term temperature goal in Article 2 of the Paris Agreement.
section_header: Disclosure of financial risks of climate change and measures adopted to reduce them by the Fiji National Provident Fund Board
extraction_rationale: This is a binding climate disclosure rule for the national provident fund.

policy_statement: Licensed financial institutions must disclose material climate financial risks, risk-reduction measures, integration into investment and risk policies, climate impacts and Paris alignment.
source_quote: Every licensed financial institution that is required to submit statements and returns under section 26(1) of the Banking Act 1995 must disclose in their submission- (a) any material financial risks to the licensed financial institution arising from climate change risks and climate change opportunities; (b) measures adopted by the licensed financial institution to reduce its exposure to these material financial risks; (c) how consideration of climate change risks are integrated into investment policies, risk management policies and investment decision-making processes; and (d) the climate change impacts of the licensed financial institution's activities and of the use of goods and services it produces and the extent to which the licensed financial institution complies with the long-term temperature goal in Article 2 of the Paris Agreement.
section_header: Disclosure of financial risks of climate change and measures adopted to reduce them by licensed financial institutions
extraction_rationale: This is a mandatory climate-risk and climate-impact disclosure rule for banks and licensed financial institutions.

policy_statement: The Reserve Bank must disclose material climate financial risks, risk-reduction measures, integration into investment and risk policies, climate impacts and Paris alignment in annual accounts and reports.
source_quote: The Reserve Bank must disclose in its annual accounts and reports of its operations transmitted to the Minister in accordance with section 56(1) of the Reserve Bank of Fiji Act 1983- (a) any material financial risks to the Reserve Bank arising from climate change risks and climate change opportunities; (b) measures adopted by the Reserve Bank to reduce its exposure to these material financial risks; (c) how consideration of climate change risks are integrated into investment policies, risk management policies and investment decision-making processes; and (d) the climate change impacts of the Reserve Bank's activities and of the use of goods and services it produces and the extent to which the Reserve Bank complies with the long-term temperature goal in Article 2 of the Paris Agreement.
section_header: Disclosure of financial risks of climate change and measures adopted to reduce them by the Reserve Bank
extraction_rationale: This is a statutory climate-related disclosure requirement for the central bank.

policy_statement: Any person may bring court proceedings to remedy or restrain a breach of the Climate Change Act.
source_quote: Any person may bring proceedings in the Court for an order to remedy or restrain a breach of this Act. Where the Court is satisfied that a breach of this Act has been committed or that a breach of this Act will, unless restrained by order of the Court, be committed, the Court may make such order as it thinks fit to remedy or restrain the breach.
section_header: Enforcement of this Act by third parties
extraction_rationale: This creates a third-party enforcement mechanism for the climate law. It is procedural but has a binding accountability effect for all climate policies under the Act.

policy_statement: Courts may order environmental restoration, remediation or offsetting of harm, including through purchase and cancellation of Fijian Mitigation Outcome Units or other emission reduction units.
source_quote: The Court, when convicting a person for an offence under this Act or when making an order to remedy or restrain a breach of this Act, and having regard to the nature of the offence or the breach and the circumstances surrounding its commission, may, in addition to any penalty or order imposed, make an order prohibiting the person from doing any act or engaging in any activity or undertaking that may result in the continuation or repetition of the offence or breach- (b) requiring the restoration, improvement or remediation of an area or the offsetting of any harm caused, including through the purchase and cancellation of Fijian Mitigation Outcome Units or other emission reduction units, with the purpose of restoring the environment to as near to its original condition with the cost to be borne by the person convicted of an offence;
extraction_rationale: This is an enforcement remedy involving restoration and carbon-unit cancellation; it is specific and legally binding when ordered.
