policy_statement: Hong Kong will strive to achieve carbon neutrality before 2050.
source_quote: The Chief Executive announced in the 2020 Policy Address that Hong Kong would strive to achieve carbon neutrality before 2050. In 2019, electricity generation was the largest source of carbon emissions, accounting for about two-thirds (66%) of the total emissions in Hong Kong, followed by transport (about 18%), waste (about 7%, mainly from landfills), other end use of fuel (about 5%), and industrial processes and product use (about 4%).
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified, time-bound economy-wide climate target and therefore a core mitigation policy.

policy_statement: Hong Kong will reduce total carbon emissions by half from the 2005 level before 2035.
source_quote: To press ahead with deep decarbonisation for the purpose of proactively mitigating climate change, we need to set a more ambitious medium-term target. Adopting the prevailing technologies that are relatively mature and cost-effective, we aim to reduce the total carbon emissions by half before 2035 from the 2005 level, i.e. from about 40 million tonnes in 2005 to nearly 20 million tonnes in 2035.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified medium-term emissions reduction target with a clear baseline and deadline.

policy_statement: Hong Kong will pursue net-zero carbon emissions in electricity generation before 2050 by increasing zero-carbon energy.
source_quote: At present, fossil fuels, including natural gas and coal, account for over 70% of Hong Kong's fuel mix for electricity generation. Under the overall strategy of achieving carbon neutrality, we must progressively increase the use of zero-carbon energy for electricity generation before 2050.
extraction_rationale: This sets a sectoral decarbonisation target for electricity generation, the largest emissions source.

policy_statement: Hong Kong will increase renewable energy to 15% of the electricity fuel mix before 2050.
source_quote: Our goal is to increase the share of RE in the fuel mix for electricity generation from the existing less than 1% to 15% before 2050. Specifically, the Government can strive to develop more advanced waste-to-energy facilities to turn waste into electricity.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified renewable energy target with a deadline and specific implementation channels.

policy_statement: Hong Kong will cease using coal for daily electricity generation by 2035, retaining it only for backup support.
source_quote: By 2035, we will cease using coal for daily electricity generation and will only keep it for providing backup support. Coal will be replaced by natural gas with lower carbon emissions and zero-carbon energy (e.g. RE and nuclear energy) by then.
section_header: Medium-term targets: Phasing out coal for electricity generation · Developing RE
extraction_rationale: This is a time-bound fuel-switching commitment that directly reduces electricity-sector emissions.

policy_statement: Hong Kong will increase renewable energy in the electricity fuel mix to 7.5% to 10% by 2035.
source_quote: To expedite transformation to low-carbon energy, we are committed to increasing the share of RE in the fuel mix for electricity generation from less than 1% at present to 7.5% to 10% by 2035. To achieve this target, we will strive to develop more advanced waste-to-energy facilities, including the infrastructure for recycling of food waste and construction of another large-scale integrated waste management facility.
section_header: Medium-term targets: Phasing out coal for electricity generation · Developing RE
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified renewable electricity target supported by named infrastructure actions.

policy_statement: Hong Kong will develop advanced waste-to-energy facilities, including food waste recycling infrastructure and another large-scale integrated waste management facility.
source_quote: To achieve this target, we will strive to develop more advanced waste-to-energy facilities, including the infrastructure for recycling of food waste and construction of another large-scale integrated waste management facility. It is estimated that around 3% to 4% of Hong Kong's electricity demand would be met by the electricity generated by such facilities by 2035.
section_header: Medium-term targets: Phasing out coal for electricity generation · Developing RE
extraction_rationale: This is a specific infrastructure intervention with quantified expected electricity contribution by 2035.

policy_statement: The Government and power companies will review proposals to develop offshore wind farms capable of supplying about 3.5% to 4% of electricity demand by 2035.
source_quote: The Government and the two power companies are reviewing proposals to develop offshore wind farms. The two power companies expect that improvement in the design of wind farms and the adoption of new technologies can increase the amount of electricity generated and the economic benefits.
section_header: Medium-term targets: Phasing out coal for electricity generation · Developing RE
extraction_rationale: This is a specific renewable energy development action with an estimated contribution stated in the surrounding paragraph.

policy_statement: Hong Kong will continue the Feed-in Tariff Scheme to encourage distributed renewable energy such as solar energy.
source_quote: The Government has introduced with the power companies the FiT Scheme in recent years to encourage the community to develop distributed RE, such as solar energy. The Government has also developed a wide range of RE projects in various premises, such as reservoirs, restored landfills, government buildings and other suitable facilities.
section_header: Medium-term targets: Phasing out coal for electricity generation · Developing RE
extraction_rationale: The Feed-in Tariff is a named financial incentive for renewable energy deployment.

policy_statement: The Government will incorporate renewable energy technologies in all capital works projects and raise renewable energy requirements for new government buildings.
source_quote: The Government will continue to take the lead in developing RE and strive to incorporate RE technologies in all capital works projects. We will update the Government circular on Green Government Buildings and raise the requirements of applying RE technologies in new government buildings.
section_header: Medium-term targets: Phasing out coal for electricity generation · Developing RE
extraction_rationale: This is an operational and standards-based commitment for public works and government buildings.

policy_statement: The Government will increase the proportion of available roof space for renewable energy systems in new government buildings from 10% to 25%.
source_quote: For instance, the proportion of available roof space for installing RE systems will be increased from the current 10% to 25%. We will also continue to install RE systems in existing government buildings (including outdoor parking lots) as far as possible.
section_header: Medium-term targets: Phasing out coal for electricity generation · Developing RE
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified design requirement for government building renewable energy installations.

policy_statement: The Water Supplies Department will install larger floating solar systems at reservoirs and study a system over 100 MW at Plover Cove Reservoir.
source_quote: The Water Supplies Department (WSD) plans to install larger floating solar energy generation systems with a generating capacity of 5-10 megawatts (MW) each at various reservoirs, including Plover Cove Reservoir, Shek Pik Reservoir and Tai Lam Chung Reservoir. In addition, WSD has embarked on a study on installing a floating solar energy generation system with a generating capacity of over 100 MW at Plover Cove Reservoir.
section_header: Medium-term targets: Phasing out coal for electricity generation · Developing RE
extraction_rationale: This is a named renewable energy project pipeline with specified capacity figures.

policy_statement: The Government will develop renewable energy at restored landfills, including a solar pilot scheme at the South East New Territories Landfill.
source_quote: We will also make use of landfills to generate RE. Apart from utilising landfill gas for electricity generation, we are actively exploring the installation of solar energy generation systems at restored landfills.
section_header: Medium-term targets: Phasing out coal for electricity generation · Developing RE
extraction_rationale: This is a specific intervention to deploy renewable energy on restored landfill sites.

policy_statement: The Housing Authority will install solar generation systems at new public rental housing domestic blocks where feasible and explore rooftop systems on existing estates.
source_quote: Since May 2011, the Housing Authority has been installing solar energy generation systems at domestic blocks of new public rental housing estates where it is technically feasible and the rooftop conditions permit, with the target to provide at least 1.5% of the communal electricity consumption. In addition to new domestic blocks, the Government will explore the installation of solar energy generation systems on the rooftops of domestic blocks of existing public rental housing estates where technically feasible.
section_header: Medium-term targets: Phasing out coal for electricity generation · Developing RE
extraction_rationale: This is a specific public housing renewable energy programme with a quantified communal electricity target.

policy_statement: The Government will facilitate private-sector renewable energy installations on land and properties, including open car parks.
source_quote: To assist the private sector in developing and applying RE, the Government will explore ways to facilitate the installation of RE systems by the private sector on their land and properties, such as measures to facilitate installation of solar energy generation systems by the private sector in open car parks. Coupled with the FiT Scheme, this can help foster the development of RE.
section_header: Medium-term targets: Phasing out coal for electricity generation · Developing RE
extraction_rationale: This is a facilitative policy for private renewable energy deployment and is tied to the existing FiT incentive.

policy_statement: The Government and power companies will pursue regional cooperation and joint investment opportunities for zero-carbon energy projects near Hong Kong.
source_quote: The Government, together with the power companies, will also explore ways to enhance regional cooperation on zero-carbon energy and identify sources of zero-carbon energy in neighbouring regions, including seeking joint investment and development opportunities for participating in and operating zero-carbon energy projects near Hong Kong. We will also keep abreast of developments in technologies that utilise RE for electricity generation.
section_header: Medium-term targets: Phasing out coal for electricity generation · Developing RE
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete cooperation and investment strategy for sourcing zero-carbon electricity.

policy_statement: Hong Kong will raise the share of zero-carbon energy in the electricity fuel mix to about 60% to 70% before 2035.
source_quote: To achieve the target of reducing the total carbon emissions by 50% from the 2005 level before 2035, more options are needed for raising the share of zero-carbon energy in the fuel mix for electricity generation to about 60% to 70%.
section_header: Medium-term targets: Phasing out coal for electricity generation · Developing RE
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified electricity-sector decarbonisation target directly linked to the 2035 emissions goal.

policy_statement: The Government and power companies will study hydrogen and other new energy sources for local electricity generation trials and adoption.
source_quote: The Government and the power companies are actively studying the development and application of new energy such as hydrogen, including importing hydrogen or other forms of new energy for use as fuels, so that they may be adopted for trial and application in Hong Kong when the technologies become relatively mature. We hope that technological advancement will allow Hong Kong to achieve net-zero electricity generation before 2050 by the adoption of hydrogen or other forms of zero-carbon energy and technologies in local electricity generation.
extraction_rationale: This is a technology development and trial policy for zero-carbon electricity generation.

policy_statement: Hong Kong will reduce electricity consumption of commercial buildings by 30% to 40% and residential buildings by 20% to 30% by 2050, relative to 2015 operating conditions.
source_quote: In this connection, we will strive to gradually reduce the electricity consumption of new and existing commercial buildings by 30% to 40%, and that of residential buildings by 20% to 30% by 2050, using the operational conditions of 2015 as the comparison basis. To achieve the above targets, we need to adopt a multi-pronged approach in planning for energy conservation.
section_header: Long-term targets: Reduce the electricity consumption of commercial buildings by 30% to 40%, and that of residential buildings by 20% to 30% by 2050
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified, time-bound energy efficiency target for buildings.

policy_statement: Hong Kong will reduce electricity consumption of commercial buildings by 15% to 20% and residential buildings by 10% to 15% by 2035, relative to 2015 operating conditions.
source_quote: To promote continuous decarbonisation in buildings, we have also set a medium-term target of reducing the electricity consumption of new and existing commercial buildings by 15% to 20%, and that of residential buildings by 10% to 15% by 2035, using the operational conditions of 2015 as the comparison basis. More green innovations and energy efficient elements will also be added to the design of new government buildings to achieve an energy efficiency performance of 10% better than statutory level, with a view to leading the trades to further optimise the energy efficiency performance of new buildings.
section_header: Medium-term targets: Reduce the electricity consumption of commercial buildings by 15% to 20%, and that of residential buildings by 10% to 15% by 2035
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified medium-term building energy consumption target, with a specific government building performance requirement.

policy_statement: The Government will explore expanding building energy efficiency regulation to high-energy-consumption buildings such as data centres.
source_quote: We will actively explore the possibility of expanding the scope of regulation to cover all buildings with high energy consumption, such as data centres, so as to further enhance the overall energy efficiency performance of buildings in Hong Kong. To explore and utilise decarbonisation opportunities in a systematic manner, we will consider conducting energy audits more frequently and mandating the implementation of identified energy management opportunities.
section_header: Medium-term targets: Reduce the electricity consumption of commercial buildings by 15% to 20%, and that of residential buildings by 10% to 15% by 2035
extraction_rationale: This is a potential regulatory expansion targeting energy efficiency in high-consuming buildings.

policy_statement: The Government will consider more frequent energy audits, mandatory implementation of identified energy management opportunities, and regular commissioning for large commercial buildings.
source_quote: To explore and utilise decarbonisation opportunities in a systematic manner, we will consider conducting energy audits more frequently and mandating the implementation of identified energy management opportunities. At the same time, we will strengthen the promotion of RCx to check the performance of the existing buildings in energy and other areas and make appropriate adjustments to the systems, with a view to reducing electricity consumption.
section_header: Medium-term targets: Reduce the electricity consumption of commercial buildings by 15% to 20%, and that of residential buildings by 10% to 15% by 2035
extraction_rationale: This is a specific regulatory and operational measure to improve building energy performance.

policy_statement: The Government will tighten thermal transfer standards for commercial, hotel and residential buildings through OTTV and RTTV reviews.
source_quote: The Government is conducting a review on the OTTV, and plans to complete the review for tightening up the statutory standards by 2025. The Government also plans to complete two reviews on the Residential Thermal Transfer Value (RTTV) by 2023 and 2030.
extraction_rationale: This is a building energy regulatory standard update with specified review deadlines.

policy_statement: The Government will integrate district cooling systems into development projects and study their feasibility in additional new development areas.
source_quote: We will work on the infrastructure by integrating energy efficient facilities in development projects. We will study the feasibility of incorporating DCS in more new development areas, such as Hung Shui Kiu/Ha Tsuen New Development Area and the artificial islands in the Central Waters, so as to promote energy efficiency and mitigate the heat island effect in the areas.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific infrastructure policy to reduce energy demand through district cooling.

policy_statement: The Government is constructing district cooling systems in Tung Chung New Town Extension (East) and Kwu Tung North New Development Area.
source_quote: As for infrastructure, following the Kai Tak Development, construction works of two more DCS projects in the Tung Chung New Town Extension (East) and Kwu Tung North New Development Area have commenced. When the two DCSs come into full operation, it is estimated that about 70 million kWh of electricity can be saved annually, and about 49 000 tonnes of carbon emissions can be reduced (i.e. around 0.12% of Hong Kong's total carbon emissions).
extraction_rationale: This is a specific infrastructure investment with quantified energy and carbon savings.

policy_statement: The Government will release energy data, introduce energy benchmarking tools, and consider time-of-use tariffs to reduce peak electricity demand.
source_quote: We plan to, through releasing energy data and introducing energy benchmarking tools, facilitate the comparison of building energy consumption performance and establish a two-way partnership in carbon reduction. Smart meters also provide the smart infrastructure required for introducing demand-side management measures, such as consideration of setting time-of-use tariffs as in some other economies to encourage users to change their habits and reduce electricity consumption during peak demand hours.
extraction_rationale: This combines transparency tools and a possible tariff instrument to manage electricity demand.

policy_statement: The Government will review and strengthen the Mandatory Energy Efficiency Labelling Scheme by upgrading grading standards, considering minimum requirements, and expanding coverage.
source_quote: We will keep the scheme under review. Apart from upgrading the grading standards, we will also consider setting a minimum energy efficiency requirement so that certain appliances must meet the minimum energy efficiency standards before they can be supplied in Hong Kong, with a view to further raising the energy efficiency performance of products.
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory appliance energy efficiency policy, including possible minimum standards and scope expansion.

policy_statement: The Government has set a Green Energy Target to improve whole-government energy performance by 6% by 2024-25.
source_quote: We have also set a new Green Energy Target to further improve the energy performance of the whole Government by 6% by 2024-25. Carbon reduction cannot be achieved by the Government alone.
section_header: For energy saving, many a little makes a mickle
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified public-sector energy performance target with a deadline.

policy_statement: Hong Kong will achieve zero carbon emissions from vehicles and the transport sector before 2050 through electrification, new energy transport and traffic management.
source_quote: We expect to achieve the long-term target of zero carbon emissions from vehicles and the transport sector before 2050 through the electrification of vehicles and ferries, development of new energy transport and implementation of measures to improve traffic management. The measures outlined in the Hong Kong Roadmap on Popularisation of Electric Vehicles announced by the Government in 2021 cover various aspects, including ceasing the new registration of fuel-propelled and hybrid private cars in 2035 or earlier, as well as setting strategies and targets for providing charging facilities.
section_header: Long-term target: Zero carbon emissions from vehicles and transport sector before 2050
extraction_rationale: This is a sectoral zero-emissions transport target with specified implementation mechanisms.

policy_statement: Hong Kong will cease new registration of fuel-propelled and hybrid private cars in 2035 or earlier.
source_quote: The measures outlined in the Hong Kong Roadmap on Popularisation of Electric Vehicles announced by the Government in 2021 cover various aspects, including ceasing the new registration of fuel-propelled and hybrid private cars in 2035 or earlier, as well as setting strategies and targets for providing charging facilities. Besides private cars, commercial vehicles, including goods vehicles, buses, light buses and taxis, are also major sources of carbon emissions.
section_header: Medium-term target: Set a concrete timetable for adopting new energy public transport
extraction_rationale: This is a clear time-bound regulatory phase-out of fossil-fuel private cars.

policy_statement: The Government will proactively develop an EV charging network and review charging facility targets around 2025.
source_quote: A full-fledged charging network is also indispensable for supporting the popularisation of EVs. In around 2025, we will review this year's target for the installation of charging facilities to keep up with the latest developments in EV.
section_header: Medium-term target: Set a concrete timetable for adopting new energy public transport
extraction_rationale: This is a supporting infrastructure commitment for electric vehicle deployment, with a review date.

policy_statement: The Government will actively test electric and new energy public transport and commercial vehicles and set a concrete timetable around 2025.
source_quote: The Government will play an active role in developing new energy transport, and will partner with different sectors in the coming years to actively test the technological and commercial viability of various electric and new energy public transport and commercial vehicles, with a view to setting a more concrete way forward and timetable in around 2025. A full-fledged charging network is also indispensable for supporting the popularisation of EVs.
section_header: Medium-term target: Set a concrete timetable for adopting new energy public transport
extraction_rationale: This is a named technology-testing and planning commitment for transport decarbonisation.

policy_statement: The Government will test hydrogen fuel cell electric buses and heavy vehicles with bus companies and stakeholders over the next three years.
source_quote: Following the release of the Plan, the Government has set up an Interdepartmental Working Group on the application of hydrogen energy in Hong Kong. We plan to collaborate with the franchised bus companies and other stakeholders in the next three years to test out hydrogen fuel cell electric buses and heavy vehicles.
section_header: Medium-term target: Set a concrete timetable for adopting new energy public transport
extraction_rationale: This is a specific time-bound pilot programme for zero-emission vehicle technology.

policy_statement: The Government will subsidise trials of electric and hybrid ferries and explore replacing traditional ferries with new energy ferries before 2035.
source_quote: As regards ferries, the Government will subsidise ferry operators to conduct trials for electric and hybrid ferries. Subject to the trial results and relevant technological developments, the Government will explore with the ferry operators the possibility of progressively replacing traditional ferries with new energy ferries before 2035.
section_header: Medium-term target: Set a concrete timetable for adopting new energy public transport
extraction_rationale: This is a financial instrument and technology trial aimed at decarbonising marine transport.

policy_statement: The Government will roll out free-flow tolling and pursue congestion charging to improve road network efficiency and reduce emissions from congestion.
source_quote: For instance, the Free-flow Tolling System will be rolled out at government tolled tunnels and the Tsing Sha Control Area, while 'congestion charging' will be pressed ahead actively, with a view to charging different toll levels according to the traffic condition of the tunnels and the Control Area during different time periods. We commenced a traffic survey in September 2021 to collect the latest data and draw up preliminary proposals for 'congestion charging' in 2022.
extraction_rationale: This is a transport demand management and pricing policy, with implementation steps and a proposal timeline.

policy_statement: The Government will continue maintaining a railway-backed public transport system and promote cycling and walkability.
source_quote: The Government will continue the current approach of maintaining a public transport system with railway as the backbone, and will adopt different new technologies as well as traffic management measures. Furthermore, the Government will continue to promote cycling for short-distance commuting and enhance walkability.
extraction_rationale: This is an operational urban transport policy promoting lower-carbon mobility modes.

policy_statement: The Government will continue first registration tax waivers and concessions to promote electric vehicles.
source_quote: The Government has been waiving the first registration tax (FRT) on electric commercial vehicles in full, and has introduced the 'One-for-One Replacement' Scheme to provide higher FRT concessions to car owners who replace their old PCs with EVs. Vehicle licence fees for e-PCs are relatively low.
extraction_rationale: This is a fiscal incentive policy to accelerate EV adoption.

policy_statement: The Government will use the EV-charging at Home Subsidy Scheme to subsidise EV charging-enabling infrastructure in existing private residential car parks.
source_quote: To enhance the EV charging network in Hong Kong and facilitate the switch to EVs by members of the public, the Environmental Protection Department (EPD) launched the $2 billion EHSS in October 2020 to subsidise the installation of EV charging-enabling infrastructure in the car parks of existing private residential buildings. It is expected to benefit more than 60 000 parking spaces.
extraction_rationale: This is a named subsidy scheme with committed funding and expected deployment scale.

policy_statement: The New Energy Transport Fund subsidises trials and applications of green transport technologies.
source_quote: The New Energy Transport Fund (NET Fund) subsidises the transport sector to try out and apply green transport technologies. As of end-June 2021, the NET Fund had approved nearly 150 projects on electric commercial vehicles, over 70 projects on hybrid commercial vehicles and 8 projects on technologies upgrading conventional buses or ferries.
extraction_rationale: This is a named subsidy fund supporting low-carbon vehicle technology deployment.

policy_statement: The Government will run pilots for electric buses, electric public light buses and electric taxis.
source_quote: The NET Fund has granted subsidies to two franchised bus companies to purchase double-deck electric buses, and the trials of these electric buses are expected to commence progressively within two years. Moreover, the Government has earmarked $80 million for a pilot scheme for electric public light buses which is expected to commence in 2023; and is in parallel exploring the implementation of a trial scheme of electric taxis to subsidise the taxi trade to test the operation and business mode.
extraction_rationale: This is a set of specific funded pilots for electrifying public transport fleets.

policy_statement: Hong Kong will move away from reliance on landfills for municipal waste disposal by 2035 and pursue carbon neutrality in waste management before 2050.
source_quote: The Waste Blueprint sets out targets for per capita MSW disposal and recovery rate, and the goal of developing adequate waste-to-energy facilities, with the aim to move away from the reliance on landfills for municipal waste disposal by 2035. Waste reduction and resources circulation will also help foster a low-carbon and sustainable lifestyle.
extraction_rationale: This is a time-bound waste-sector decarbonisation policy tied to zero landfill and waste-to-energy infrastructure.

policy_statement: The Government will implement municipal solid waste charging to drive waste reduction and recycling.
source_quote: The Legislative Council (LegCo) passed the bill on municipal solid waste (MSW) charging in August 2021. MSW charging will be the main driving force for various sectors and the public to practise waste reduction and recycling.
extraction_rationale: This is a binding fee-based waste management instrument established through legislation.

policy_statement: Hong Kong will reduce per capita municipal solid waste disposal by 40% to 45% and raise the recovery rate to about 55%.
source_quote: Through implementing MSW charging and other waste reduction and recycling initiatives, and encouraging the whole community to work together, we aim to progressively reduce the per capita MSW disposal by 40% to 45% and raise the recovery rate to about 55%. Enhancing recycling is also an integral part of decarbonisation at source.
section_header: Medium-term target: Enhance waste reduction and recycling
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified waste reduction and recovery target.

policy_statement: The Government will expand central collection services and the community recycling network for food waste, waste plastics and waste paper.
source_quote: We will continue to expand and enhance the central collection services for food waste, waste plastics and waste paper. The community recycling network covering all districts in Hong Kong will be enhanced to cover more areas and target participants, thereby raising the effectiveness of recycling.
section_header: Medium-term target: Enhance waste reduction and recycling
extraction_rationale: This is a specific operational waste recovery intervention.

policy_statement: The Government will support the recycling trade to adopt technologies, produce higher value-added products and strengthen downstream waste-to-resources capabilities.
source_quote: Besides, we will further promote low-carbon transformation of the recycling trade by supporting the industry to apply technologies to produce high value-added products and achieve re-industrialisation as well as circular economy; and consolidating and strengthening downstream recovery, recycling and waste-to-resources capabilities, in order to achieve the targets of reducing waste and carbon emissions.
section_header: Medium-term target: Enhance waste reduction and recycling
extraction_rationale: This is an industrial transformation policy for recycling and circular economy, with explicit waste and carbon objectives.

policy_statement: The Government will continue expanding food waste recycling infrastructure and use biogas from food waste treatment as renewable energy.
source_quote: We also need to develop another waste-to-energy facility to process municipal waste, continue to expand our food waste recycling infrastructure, and make use of the biogas generated during the food waste treatment process as an additional source of RE. Only by doing so can we move away from reliance on landfills for municipal waste disposal.
section_header: Long-term target: Carbon neutrality in waste management
extraction_rationale: This combines waste diversion with renewable energy production from biogas.

policy_statement: The Government will enhance recovery of landfill gases for thermal energy, electricity, town gas supply and power grids.
source_quote: In the meantime, we will enhance the recovery of landfill gases from the three landfills currently in operation for providing thermal energy and electricity to support landfill operation and export to the gas company and power grids to provide energy for the public.
section_header: Medium-term target: Enhance waste reduction and recycling
extraction_rationale: This is a specific landfill gas recovery policy that reduces methane-related climate impacts and supplies energy.

policy_statement: The Government will pursue a long-term plastic-free approach by regulating, publicising and expanding recycling support for waste plastics.
source_quote: We will map out a long-term solution and go 'plastic-free' by adopting a multi-pronged approach, which includes formulating suitable policies and regulations, stepping up publicity, and expanding waste plastics recycling supporting facilities for turning waste into resources, as well as encouraging the public to replace single-use plastics with reusable or alternative materials. Among the various types of waste, plastics in particular generate GHG in their entire life cycle, from the extraction of crude oil, the manufacturing process to post-disposal treatment.
section_header: Long-term target: Carbon neutrality in waste management
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory and operational waste policy explicitly linked to life-cycle GHG emissions from plastics.

policy_statement: The Government will regulate disposable plastic tableware in phases from 2025.
source_quote: The Government will continue to adopt a multi-pronged approach to support the turning of waste plastics into resources, including formulating suitable policies and regulations, stepping up publicity, and developing further waste plastics recycling supporting facilities, as well as promoting the replacement of single-use plastics with reusable or alternative materials. The Government will regulate disposable plastic tableware in phases from 2025.
extraction_rationale: This is a time-bound regulatory commitment targeting single-use plastic waste.

policy_statement: The Government will allocate about HK$240 billion over 15 to 20 years for climate mitigation and adaptation measures.
source_quote: The Government plans to allocate about $240 billion in the next 15 to 20 years to implement mitigation and adaptation measures to combat climate change, including the four main actions mentioned in this Chapter, covering energy saving and green buildings, RE, green transport and waste management, etc. Moreover, the Government will undertake measures to adapt to climate change, including strengthening coastal defences, stabilising slopes and conducting drainage improvement works, etc.
extraction_rationale: This is a committed public expenditure line for climate mitigation and adaptation.

policy_statement: The Government Green Bond Programme will fund green public works and broader green projects.
source_quote: The Government Green Bond Programme (GGBP) established in 2018 provides funding for the Government's green public works projects. The Government successfully offered its inaugural green bond with a total issuance size of US$1 billion in May 2019, while the second Government green bond with a total issuance size of US$2.5 billion was successfully offered in January 2021.
extraction_rationale: This is a named green finance instrument for climate-related public investment.

policy_statement: Hong Kong will issue about HK$175.5 billion in green bonds within five years from 2021-22 and pilot retail green bonds and diverse issuance formats.
source_quote: We plan to issue green bonds further, totalling some HK$175.5 billion within the next five years from 2021-22, having regard to the market situation. We also plan to pilot the issuance of green bonds that involves more types of currencies, project types and issuance channels, thereby further enriching the green finance ecosystem in Hong Kong.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified green bond issuance plan and financial instrument.

policy_statement: The Government will use the HK$200 million Green Tech Fund to support R&D projects for decarbonisation and environmental protection.
source_quote: In 2020, the Government allocated $200 million for setting up the Green Tech Fund to provide better and more focused funding support for R&D projects which can help Hong Kong decarbonise and enhance environmental protection, thereby helping Hong Kong pursue the target of striving to achieve carbon neutrality. While supporting local I&T development, we may also explore growth opportunities through cooperation with neighbouring regions, such as strengthening exchanges and collaboration with cities in the GBA in building low-carbon communities, developing decarbonisation technologies, promoting low-carbon products and nurturing talent.
section_header: Regional Cooperation in Innovation and Technology
extraction_rationale: This is a named grant fund with committed funding for decarbonisation R&D.

policy_statement: The Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group will assess developing Hong Kong into a regional carbon trading centre.
source_quote: The Steering Group has set up a Carbon Market Work Stream to assess the feasibility of developing Hong Kong into a regional carbon trading centre, leveraging its unique advantages in financial services. Based on the existing pilot ETSs in Guangdong, the development of a unified carbon market in GBA will also be explored, having regard to the opportunities presented by both the compliance carbon market and the voluntary carbon market in China and overseas, including the potential size of the carbon product market and policy support needed.
extraction_rationale: This is a market-based climate finance and carbon pricing development policy, though framed as feasibility assessment.

policy_statement: The Government will review Hong Kong's Climate Action Plan about every five years to update decarbonisation strategies, targets and other climate actions.
source_quote: Combating climate change is a long-term task. We will, in line with the spirit of the Paris Agreement, review Hong Kong's Climate Action Plan about every five years to update the strategies and targets for decarbonisation and other actions to combat climate change.
extraction_rationale: This is a governance commitment with a defined five-year review cycle.

policy_statement: The Government will set up the Office of Climate Change and Carbon Neutrality to coordinate and promote deep decarbonisation.
source_quote: To ensure effective implementation of the measures and follow-up actions, ENB will set up the Office of Climate Change and Carbon Neutrality to strengthen coordination and promote deep decarbonisation, etc. ENB had also set up an inter-departmental Carbon Neutrality Task Force this year, bringing together the experts from relevant departments to explore forward-looking decarbonisation policies, having regard to the latest developments in advance decarbonisation technologies globally.
extraction_rationale: This is an institutional implementation mechanism for climate policy coordination.

policy_statement: The Government will explore establishing a dedicated advisory committee on climate change and upgrade the 4T Partnership to a Carbon Neutrality Partnership.
source_quote: We will explore ways to establish a dedicated advisory committee on climate change through the integration of the existing advisory platforms, with the aim to encourage different sectors in the community, including our young generation, to actively participate in climate actions. On the basis of the existing '4T' dialogue platform, we will upgrade the '4T' Partnership to 'Carbon Neutrality' Partnership.
extraction_rationale: This is a governance and stakeholder mobilisation commitment tied directly to climate action.

policy_statement: The Government will enrich climate change, low-carbon technology and green finance education in schools, universities and tertiary institutions.
source_quote: We will broaden school teachers' knowledge about climate change. Schools may strengthen the relevant learning materials in different subjects and provide diversified learning experiences, so as to enhance students' awareness of climate change and its impacts, encourage the students to practise what they have learned, and promote low-carbon transformation.
extraction_rationale: This is a capacity-building policy for climate education; it is concrete but less directly emissions-reducing.

policy_statement: Hong Kong will adopt a comprehensive climate adaptation and resilience strategy to protect life, health and property from extreme weather.
source_quote: To combat climate change effectively, apart from implementing ambitious decarbonisation strategies, we also need to adopt a comprehensive strategy on climate change adaptation and resilience to protect the life, health and property of the people from extreme weather and strengthen the resilience of the community. We will, on the basis of the Hong Kong's Climate Action Plan 2030+, explore the measures Hong Kong must take before 2050 to enhance the adaptation and resilience capability.
extraction_rationale: This is an overarching adaptation commitment with a defined purpose and 2050 planning horizon.

policy_statement: The Climate Change Working Group on Infrastructure will coordinate adaptation efforts for government infrastructure and report to the Steering Committee.
source_quote: The Government attaches great importance to the capability of Government's infrastructure in combating climate change and extreme weather, and established in 2016 the Climate Change Working Group on Infrastructure (CCWGI) under the leadership of the Civil Engineering and Development Department (CEDD) to coordinate the efforts of the works departments in adapting to climate change. The Working Group has coordinated studies relating to the potential effects of extreme temperatures, extreme storm surges and super typhoons on government critical infrastructure (CI).
extraction_rationale: This is an institutional adaptation coordination mechanism for public infrastructure.

policy_statement: The Government will update infrastructure design standards to account for climate change parameters and IPCC findings.
source_quote: The CCWGI updates the design standards for various types of infrastructure in a timely manner, taking into account the relevant climate change parameters. With reference to the Fifth Assessment Report published by the IPCC, the relevant government departments had in the past few years updated the design manuals and guidance notes, including Port Works Design Manual, Stormwater Drainage Manual, Guidance Notes on Road Pavement Drainage Design and the design guide for drainage installation for government buildings.
extraction_rationale: This is a standards-based climate adaptation policy for infrastructure resilience.

policy_statement: Government departments will formulate measures and implementation plans to enhance critical infrastructure resilience based on the resilience study.
source_quote: The resilience study included strategic assessment and review to formulate scopes of enhancement works. The study was completed in 2020. The relevant government departments will formulate measures and implementation plans to enhance their CI's resilience with reference to the recommendations of the study.
extraction_rationale: This is a commitment to implement critical infrastructure resilience measures after a completed study.

policy_statement: CEDD will assess low-lying coastal and windy locations and implement coastal improvement works and management measures by priority.
source_quote: To enhance the capability of coastal areas to withstand strong waves in the long run, CEDD commenced a consultancy study in 2019 to comprehensively review the low-lying coastal or windy locations in Hong Kong, and to carry out investigations of related storm surges and waves in order to assess the impacts of extreme weather and climate change at those locations. The Government plans to implement suitable improvement works and formulate management measures for some of the concerned low-lying coastal or windy locations in order of priority.
section_header: Combating Sea Level Rise and Marine Protection
extraction_rationale: This is a specific coastal protection adaptation policy addressing sea level rise, storm surges and waves.

policy_statement: CEDD will commence a strategic shoreline management study to formulate long-term coastal protection strategies and measures.
source_quote: CEDD also plans to commence a strategic study on shoreline management to analyse the impacts of climate change on the development of coastal areas, so as to formulate suitable long-term strategies and protection measures, and to strengthen the capabilities of the Government and relevant stakeholders in coping with climate change.
section_header: Combating Sea Level Rise and Marine Protection
extraction_rationale: This is a named planning action for long-term coastal climate adaptation.

policy_statement: DSD will continue reviewing district Drainage Master Plans and allocate resources for drainage improvement works.
source_quote: DSD has updated the Stormwater Drainage Manual by including the impacts on the drainage system design caused by rainfall increase and sea level rise due to climate change. DSD will continue to review the Drainage Master Plan of various districts in Hong Kong to assess the flood risk, and allocate resources for implementing drainage improvement works.
section_header: Combating Extreme Rainstorms and Tropical Cyclones
extraction_rationale: This is a resource-allocation and planning policy for flood risk reduction under climate change.

policy_statement: DSD will implement a three-pronged flood prevention strategy involving upstream stormwater interception, midstream storage and downstream drainage improvement.
source_quote: DSD has adopted the 'three-pronged flood prevention strategy', i.e. stormwater interception at upstream, flood storage at midstream, and drainage improvement at downstream, to formulate appropriate flood prevention and drainage management measures. It has completed a number of major flood prevention projects, including four drainage tunnels in Hong Kong Island West, Lai Chi Kok, Tsuen Wan and Kai Tak; four stormwater storage schemes in Tai Hang Tung, Sheung Wan, Happy Valley and On Sau Road; and improvement works for rivers in the New Territories with a total length of over 100 kilometres, as well as the implementation of 27 village flood protection schemes in low-lying villages for combating extreme weather events such as tropical cyclones and rainstorms.
section_header: Combating Extreme Rainstorms and Tropical Cyclones
extraction_rationale: This is a named flood prevention strategy with specific infrastructure interventions.

policy_statement: DSD will promote stormwater storage tanks, flood lakes, floodable areas, river revitalisation, bioretention systems and other sustainable drainage systems in new development areas.
source_quote: To further enhance the flood prevention and flood resilience capabilities of the city, DSD is also planning, designing and constructing a number of drainage improvement works such as the Inter-reservoirs Transfer Scheme and the Yuen Long Barrage Scheme, as well as actively promoting the introduction of stormwater storage tank, flood lake, floodable area, river revitalisation, bioretention system, and other sustainable drainage systems, etc. in new development areas.
section_header: Combating Extreme Rainstorms and Tropical Cyclones
extraction_rationale: This is a flood adaptation policy that explicitly includes ecological/sustainable drainage measures.

policy_statement: The Inter-reservoirs Transfer Scheme will reduce flood risk while collecting additional fresh water annually.
source_quote: Through the construction of a 2.8 kilometres long water tunnel, the Inter-reservoirs Transfer Scheme connects Kowloon Byewash Reservoir and Lower Shing Mun Reservoir, reducing the flood risk caused by the overflow from Kowloon Byewash Reservoir to the downstream areas such as the Lai Chi Kok, Cheung Sha Wan and Sham Shui Po areas. The project can also collect an average of around 3.4 million m³ of additional fresh water annually to achieve the dual goals of flood prevention and water conservation.
extraction_rationale: This is a named infrastructure project with quantified water conservation and flood prevention benefits.

policy_statement: MTRCL will implement flood prevention measures for stations and underwater tunnels to address flooding threats from inclement weather.
source_quote: To tackle the threats of flooding at MTR stations and underwater tunnels caused by inclement weather, MTRCL has implemented the following measures: The entrances/exits of most MTR stations are by design at least 450 mm above street level and equipped with 1.2 m high flood boards; waterproof doors are installed at the underground entrances/exits connecting MTR stations and other facilities as needed; intercepting ditches or floodgates are also installed at the entrances/exits connecting depots and railway tunnels where necessary to prevent ingress of flood water. Underground stations and tunnels are equipped with water pumps.
extraction_rationale: This is a named set of transport infrastructure flood resilience measures with sub-actions listed underneath.

parent_statement: MTRCL's flood prevention measures
policy_statement: MTRCL will protect station and tunnel entrances through elevated entrances, flood boards, waterproof doors, intercepting ditches and floodgates.
source_quote: The entrances/exits of most MTR stations are by design at least 450 mm above street level and equipped with 1.2 m high flood boards; waterproof doors are installed at the underground entrances/exits connecting MTR stations and other facilities as needed; intercepting ditches or floodgates are also installed at the entrances/exits connecting depots and railway tunnels where necessary to prevent ingress of flood water. Underground stations and tunnels are equipped with water pumps.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific listed flood resilience intervention under the MTRCL flood prevention programme.

parent_statement: MTRCL's flood prevention measures
policy_statement: MTRCL will equip underground stations and tunnels with water pumps.
source_quote: Underground stations and tunnels are equipped with water pumps. Emergency procedures for coping with catastrophic floods have been formulated to evacuate passengers from MTR stations as soon as possible in case of emergency, and drills are conducted on a regular basis.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific listed infrastructure measure for flood response in rail facilities.

parent_statement: MTRCL's flood prevention measures
policy_statement: MTRCL will maintain emergency procedures and regular drills for evacuating passengers during catastrophic floods.
source_quote: Emergency procedures for coping with catastrophic floods have been formulated to evacuate passengers from MTR stations as soon as possible in case of emergency, and drills are conducted on a regular basis. With regard to railway and road infrastructure, MTRCL carries out the design, construction and maintenance of the flood protection and drainage systems of the railway and its facilities in accordance with the requirements stipulated by DSD.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific emergency preparedness commitment for flood events under the listed MTRCL measures.

policy_statement: CEDD will continue the Landslip Prevention and Mitigation Programme and enhance slope drainage standards for extreme rainstorms.
source_quote: More frequent and intense rainstorm events increase landslide risk. CEDD will continue to implement the Landslip Prevention and Mitigation Programme to upgrade government man-made slopes and to mitigate natural terrain landslide risk.
section_header: Combating Extreme Rainstorms and Tropical Cyclones
extraction_rationale: This is a named adaptation programme addressing landslide risks from more intense rainstorms.

policy_statement: WSD will implement the updated Total Water Management Strategy to contain demand growth and build freshwater supply resilience to climate change.
source_quote: WSD has updated the Total Water Management Strategy to cater for the forecast water demand up to 2040. The updated Strategy adopts a two-pronged approach with emphasis on containing fresh water demand growth and building resilience in the fresh water supply to cope with the extreme effects of climate change with diversified water resources.
section_header: Combating Extreme Droughts and Safeguarding Water Supply
extraction_rationale: This is a named water adaptation strategy with a 2040 planning horizon and explicit climate resilience objective.

policy_statement: Hong Kong will reduce average fresh water per capita consumption by 10% by 2030 and contain annual freshwater demand at about 1 billion m³ before 2040.
source_quote: To achieve the goal of reducing the average fresh water per capita consumption by 10% in 2030, using 2016 as the base year, and containing the fresh water demand at the level of around 1 billion m³ per annum before 2040, WSD is taking forward three major water demand management initiatives, namely water conservation, water loss management and expansion of the use of lower grade water (viz. seawater and recycled water) for non-potable purposes.
section_header: Combating Extreme Droughts and Safeguarding Water Supply
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified water conservation and demand management target motivated by drought and water security.

policy_statement: WSD will expand smart water management and lower-grade water systems, supplying recycled water in phases from 2024.
source_quote: WSD enhances implementation of various water demand management initiatives through wide adoption of smart technologies, including establishment of the Water Intelligent Network and installation of the Automatic Meter Reading, etc. Construction of the relevant infrastructure for expanding the use of lower grade water for non-potable purposes, including the reclaimed water supply system in Sheung Shui and Fanling and the grey water recycling supply system at the Anderson Road Quarry Development site, is in progress for supplying recycled water to the public in phases starting from 2024.
section_header: Combating Extreme Droughts and Safeguarding Water Supply
extraction_rationale: This is a specific water efficiency and drought resilience infrastructure programme with a start date.

policy_statement: WSD will construct the first stage of the Tseung Kwan O Desalination Plant to provide climate-resilient potable water supply.
source_quote: To cope with the possible extreme dry weather, WSD is constructing the first stage of Tseung Kwan O Desalination Plant to exploit alternative water resources other than rainfall. The plant, targeted to be commissioned in 2023, will adopt the latest reverse osmosis technology in producing potable water that complies with the Hong Kong Drinking Water Standards.
extraction_rationale: This is a named infrastructure project to diversify water supply under extreme drought risk.

policy_statement: The Government will enhance building design standards and review thermal expansion requirements to cope with extreme temperatures.
source_quote: We will continue to enhance building design and promote urban forestry with a view to alleviating and coping with temperature rise. Based on the recommendations of the Study of Design Considerations for Government Infrastructures under Extreme Temperatures, ArchSD is coordinating with relevant departments to follow up and review the design standards relating to public infrastructure and government buildings.
extraction_rationale: This is an adaptation policy addressing extreme heat through building and infrastructure design standards.

policy_statement: The Government will promote urban forestry, active planting, tree maintenance and preservation to lower urban temperature and reduce heat island effects.
source_quote: Promoting urban forestry and increasing tree planting can lower urban temperature and attenuate the heat island effect. The Development Bureau is studying and exploring feasible measures to improve the growing environment of urban trees, which include the application of smart technologies in tree management, review of soil volume for new roadside trees and improvement of soil quality for existing planting areas.
extraction_rationale: This uses trees and urban forestry as climate infrastructure to address extreme heat.

policy_statement: The Government will strengthen preparedness, response and recovery capabilities for natural disasters under climate change.
source_quote: Extreme weather conditions are expected to become more frequent due to climate change. The Government will continue to strengthen preparation for and response to natural disasters, and to enhance capabilities in post-disaster recovery.
extraction_rationale: This is an emergency management adaptation policy responding to increased extreme weather.

policy_statement: The Government will activate the Emergency Monitoring and Support Centre for substantial natural disasters requiring extensive emergency response.
source_quote: According to the Contingency Plan for Natural Disasters formulated by the Security Bureau, the Government will act in preparedness, response and recovery to guard against natural disasters by enhancing situation assessment at the early stage, devising the response strategy and plan as well as redeploying resources and manpower in a timely manner. In the event of natural disasters of a substantial scale, such as severe rainstorm and serious flooding where extensive government emergency response operations are required, the Emergency Monitoring and Support Centre will be activated to provide a holistic response.
extraction_rationale: This is a defined emergency response mechanism for severe rainstorms and flooding.

policy_statement: Hong Kong will maintain a high-level inter-departmental Steering Committee and Extreme Conditions announcement mechanism for super typhoons and major natural disasters.
source_quote: One of the new measures requires that in the event of a super typhoon or other natural disasters of a substantial scale, a high-level inter-departmental Steering Committee chaired by the Chief Secretary for Administration (CS) will be set up, as and when necessary, to oversee the work of relevant bureaux and departments and to set priorities in a coordinated manner. Should a super typhoon or other natural disasters of a substantial scale cause damages that paralyse the city and seriously affect the working public to resume work, the CS, having regard to the views of the Steering Committee, may make a territory-wide 'Extreme Conditions' announcement to extend the time for resumption of work so as to minimise possible injuries to members of the public.
extraction_rationale: This is a procedural adaptation measure for governance during extreme weather disasters.

policy_statement: HKO, District Offices and DSD will operate an early alert mechanism for storm surges associated with tropical cyclones.
source_quote: Owing to the complex coastline of Hong Kong, the degree of impacts from storm surges associated with tropical cyclones can vary significantly across different locations. HKO, in collaboration with District Offices and DSD, has established an early alert mechanism.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific warning system for a named climate hazard: tropical cyclone storm surges.

policy_statement: DSD will operate an Emergency Control Centre and real-time flood monitoring system using telemetry at over 140 locations.
source_quote: In addition, DSD has set up an Emergency Control Centre (ECC). The Flood Monitoring and Reporting System in the ECC will monitor rainfall and water level of major rivers and channels in real-time.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific flood monitoring and emergency preparedness system.

policy_statement: The Office of the Communications Authority will establish an emergency alert system for mobile dissemination of time-critical public messages during extreme weather and other emergencies.
source_quote: The Office of the Communications Authority has engaged local mobile network operators to set up an emergency alert system for dissemination of time-critical public announcements and messages by the Government via mobile networks to mobile service users during emergency situations, such as extreme weather, so that the public can adopt contingency measures quickly.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific public warning infrastructure policy for extreme weather emergencies.

policy_statement: TD will maintain emergency transport contingency plans and coordinate temporary transport arrangements during infrastructure closures and service suspensions.
source_quote: TD has formulated a series of contingency plans to handle various emergency situations at major transport infrastructure such as railways and road tunnels. In the event of an emergency, TD's Emergency Transport Coordination Centre will activate the relevant contingency plan to coordinate all parties concerned to implement temporary traffic and public transport arrangements in response to the closure of the relevant facilities and suspension of services.
extraction_rationale: This is an adaptation and emergency response policy for transport system resilience.

policy_statement: The two strategic growth areas under planning will adopt the target of carbon neutrality, and new development areas will be planned as low-carbon liveable communities.
source_quote: The two strategic growth areas (SGAs) under planning (i.e. New Territories North and artificial islands in the Central Waters) will indeed adopt the target of carbon neutrality. As Hong Kong continues to switch to clean energy for electricity generation and electrify transport, all NDAs and the two SGAs are aspired to be further enhanced to carbon-neutral communities in the medium and long run.
extraction_rationale: This is a spatial planning commitment to apply carbon-neutral targets to major growth areas.

policy_statement: The Government will build low-carbon communities in planned new development areas using district cooling, green building design, railway services, EV charging, walking, cycling and recycling facilities.
source_quote: Examples include building DCSs to reduce energy demand; adopting green and sustainable design in buildings as far as possible to reduce energy consumption; providing railway services and installing charging networks for EVs at an early stage; saving energy through proper land use planning and building layout; providing the public with green mobility options, such as walking and cycling; and setting up waste separation and recycling facilities in the community. The two strategic growth areas (SGAs) under planning (i.e. New Territories North and artificial islands in the Central Waters) will indeed adopt the target of carbon neutrality.
extraction_rationale: This is a package of specific low-carbon planning interventions for new development areas.

policy_statement: The Government will adopt and encourage Modular Integrated Construction and more electric machinery at construction sites to reduce embodied carbon, construction waste and pollution.
source_quote: The Government will continue to adopt, and encourage the construction sector to follow suit, Modular Integrated Construction (MiC) method in suitable projects by carrying out most of the operations at construction sites in off-site prefabrication yards, thereby simplifying the construction process and reducing construction wastes. More electrical machinery will also be used at construction sites to reduce carbon emissions and other pollution, with a view to alleviating the impact of buildings on the environment throughout their life cycle.
extraction_rationale: This is a construction-sector resource efficiency and emissions-reduction policy with named methods and technologies.

policy_statement: The Hong Kong-Shenzhen Innovation and Technology Park will reserve about 30% of its area for greening and use smart environmental features including a district cooling system.
source_quote: Located in the Lok Ma Chau Loop, the Hong Kong-Shenzhen Innovation and Technology Park has reserved about 30% of its area for greening to complement the ecological environment of the adjacent wetland and bird habitat. The design of the Park is in line with the target of achieving carbon neutrality before 2050 with adoption of smart and environmentally friendly features, such as a solid waste recycling system.
section_header: Hong Kong-Shenzhen Innovation and Technology Park
extraction_rationale: This is a site-specific low-carbon development policy with quantified greening and named infrastructure.

policy_statement: Indonesia will pursue the LCCP pathway to peak national GHG emissions in 2030 with a net sink in forestry and land use, reach 540 MtCO2e in 2050, and explore net-zero emissions by 2060 or sooner.
source_quote: Under LCCP, rapid decrease in emissions will occur after 2030, reaching 540 Mton CO 2 e by 2050 or equivalent to about 1.61 ton CO 2 e per capita. Through low carbon scenario compatible with the Paris Agreement target (LCCP), Indonesia foresees to reach the peaking of national GHGs emissions in 2030 with net sink in forestry and land uses (FOLU), and with further exploring opportunity to rapidly progress towards net-zero emission in 2060 or sooner.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified national mitigation target with dates and emissions levels. It is a core climate policy commitment rather than background.

policy_statement: Indonesia will reduce the impact of climate change on national GDP loss by 3.45% in 2050 by increasing resilience in food, water, energy, and environmental health across economic, social-livelihood, and ecosystem-landscape resilience areas.
source_quote: By extending adaptation strategy in Updated NDC, the adaptation pathways set the goal to reduce the impact of climate change on national GDP loss by 3.45% in 2050, through increasing resilience in four basic necessities (food, water, energy, and environmental health), with three target areas of resilience (economy, social and livelihood, ecosystem and landscape). The economic resilience is manifested in the form of long-term investments based on risk codes such as climate hotspots, climate vulnerability, sectoral and regional-based adaptive development.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified long-term adaptation target and identifies concrete resilience domains. It qualifies as a policy even though specific sector actions are elaborated later.

policy_statement: Ministerial Regulation No. 33/2016 guides national and local governments to plan climate adaptation actions and integrate them into regional or sectoral development plans.
source_quote: Ministerial Regulation (Minister for Environment and Forestry) No.33/2016 provides guidance for national governments and local governments in planning climate change adaptation actions and integrating them into development plans of specific regions and/or sectors. Furthermore, Ministerial Regulation (Minister for Environment and Forestry) No. 7/2018 provides guidance for national and local government (and general society) on: a) determining the scope of the analysis, selection of methods, indicators, indicator data, and data sources for formulating vulnerability, risk and impact assessments of climate change; and b) determining the criteria for verification of vulnerability, risk, and climate change impact assessment results.
section_header: 3.4. Framework on Climate Change Actions in Indonesia
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory mechanism requiring or guiding climate adaptation planning and mainstreaming into development plans.

policy_statement: Ministerial Regulation No. 7/2018 establishes guidance and verification criteria for climate vulnerability, risk, and impact assessments.
source_quote: Furthermore, Ministerial Regulation (Minister for Environment and Forestry) No. 7/2018 provides guidance for national and local government (and general society) on: a) determining the scope of the analysis, selection of methods, indicators, indicator data, and data sources for formulating vulnerability, risk and impact assessments of climate change; and b) determining the criteria for verification of vulnerability, risk, and climate change impact assessment results. In addition, the vulnerability component should cover climate-related hazards, exposure, sensitivity and adaptive capacity in accordance with standard practice.
section_header: 3.4. Framework on Climate Change Actions in Indonesia
extraction_rationale: The regulation creates a specific planning and assessment mechanism for climate risk, which is a concrete adaptation policy.

policy_statement: Indonesia will transform PROKLIM into a national movement for joint local adaptation and mitigation actions under Ministerial Regulation No. 84/2016.
source_quote: Climate Village Programme (PROKLIM) has been continuously improved, including by transforming the PROKLIM become national movement on joint adaptation and mitigation which aims at increasing understanding on climate change and its impacts and to encourage the implementation of adaptation and mitigation actions at the local level through Minister Regulation (Minister of Environment and Forestry) No. 84/2016. Furthermore, some Ministerial Regulations relating to strategic environmental assessment (KLHS) were also put into effect far before and after the issuance of Government Regulation on KLHS, such as Minister Regulation (Minister for Environment) No. 9/2011, Minister Regulation (Minister for Home Affairs) No. 67/2012, and Minister Regulation (Minister for Home Affairs) No. 7/2018.
section_header: 3.4. Framework on Climate Change Actions in Indonesia
extraction_rationale: This is a named programme with regulatory backing and explicit local adaptation and mitigation objectives.

policy_statement: Indonesia will implement coastal protection programmes for coastal and fishery adaptation under RPJMN 2020-2024 in line with the NDC.
source_quote: This climate-related evidence suggested the important role of ocean in adaptation to climate change and Indonesia has included ocean in adaptation component of the NDC. The National Medium-Term Plan (RPJMN) 20202024 has put adaptation in coastal and fishery through coastal protection programmes, which is in-line with NDC.
section_header: 3.3. Role of Ocean and Integrated Terrestrial and Marine Ecosystem Management and Conservation
extraction_rationale: This is a specific adaptation intervention addressing coastal climate risks and embedded in a national plan.

policy_statement: Indonesia will pursue integrated terrestrial and marine ecosystem management and conservation to increase climate resilience, reduce vulnerability and exposure, adapt to climate change, and deliver emission reductions.
source_quote: As the country that has ratified the three Rio Conventions (UNFCCC, CBD, and UNCCD), Indonesia also foresees synergy effects of these Conventions in realizing integrated terrestrial and marine ecosystem management and conservation. Through this synergic implementation, Indonesia will increase climate resilience, reduce vulnerability and exposure, and adapt to climate change, as well as deliver emission reduction.
section_header: 3.3. Role of Ocean and Integrated Terrestrial and Marine Ecosystem Management and Conservation
extraction_rationale: This is a named ecosystem-management approach with explicit climate adaptation and mitigation outcomes. It is somewhat broad but still identifies a specific intervention mechanism.

policy_statement: Indonesia included mangroves in national GHG inventory, FREL, and REDD+ results accounting, and recognizes seagrass carbon sequestration as part of blue carbon mitigation research.
source_quote: Mangrove has been included in the national GHGs inventory under wetland category as well as in the establishment of Forest Reference Emission Level (FREL) for REDD+ and so does in the estimation of REDD+ results. Seagrass also can absorb carbon as well. Furthermore, a study recorded carbon sequestration from seagrass ecosystem meadows in Indonesia ranges from 1.6-7.4 Mton C per year.
section_header: 3.3. Role of Ocean and Integrated Terrestrial and Marine Ecosystem Management and Conservation
extraction_rationale: This is an accounting and policy integration measure for blue carbon sinks. The seagrass element is research-oriented, but mangrove inclusion in GHG/FREL/REDD+ accounting is a concrete climate governance measure.

policy_statement: Indonesia implemented 15,000 hectares of mangrove planting and 50 hectares of coral reef restoration in Bali marine tourism areas in 2020 as part of COVID-19 recovery.
source_quote: Coastal and marine based activities have also been part of COVID-19 recovery programme, including 15 thousands hectare mangrove planting and 50 hectare coral reef restoration in marine tourism area in Bali in 2020.
section_header: 3.3. Role of Ocean and Integrated Terrestrial and Marine Ecosystem Management and Conservation
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified ecosystem restoration intervention with coastal and marine climate relevance. The quote is one sentence, but it contains the full commitment and quantities.

policy_statement: Indonesia will implement a package of AFOLU policies and measures to reduce deforestation and degradation, restore peat ecosystems, improve agriculture productivity and land-use efficiency, reduce food loss and waste, and halt marine and coastal ecosystem service loss.
source_quote: PaMs are directed to reduce deforestation either planned and un-planned (illegal deforestation) and forest degradation, accelerating reforestation and restoration of peat ecosystem, improving agriculture productivity and land use eff.shorticiency, reducing food loss and waste and improving diets and food diversification and access. Indonesia has committed through REDD+ to maintain the remaining natural forest.
section_header: 4.2.1. Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Uses (AFOLU)
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella AFOLU policy package with multiple sub-actions listed beneath and throughout the AFOLU section.

parent_statement: AFOLU policies and measures for low-carbon land-use transformation
policy_statement: Indonesia will permanently extend forest and peatland moratoriums through Presidential Instruction No. 5/2019.
source_quote: Policies that have been issued include (i) permanent extension of the forest and peatland moratoriums (Presidential Instruction 5/2019); (ii) implementation of mandatory certification for sustainable forest management; (iii) integrated, comprehensive, spatially explicit land use planning at national and sub-national level guided by the Government Regulation 46/2016 on strategic environmental assessments (SEAs) through landscape approach aiming at securing food, water, and energy security based on sound ecosystem management; (iv) establishment of new financial models for conservation and restoration in sustainable jurisdictions with the issuance of Government Regulation No. 46/2017 on Environmental economic instrument and other fiscal incentives; and (v) establishment of Indonesia Environmental Fund ( Badan Pengelola Dana Lingkungan Hidup /BPDLH) through Presidential Regulation No. 77/2018 concerning Management of Environmental Fund. Indonesia is also in the process of issuing another innovative policy on economic value of carbon.
section_header: 4.2.1. Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Uses (AFOLU)
extraction_rationale: A presidential instruction permanently extending moratoriums is a binding land-use regulatory policy to protect carbon-rich ecosystems.

parent_statement: AFOLU policies and measures for low-carbon land-use transformation

Indonesia is also in the process of issuing another innovative policy on economic value of carbon.

extraction_rationale: Mandatory certification is a concrete regulatory instrument to reduce forest degradation and support forest carbon sinks.

policy_statement: Indonesia will implement strategic environmental assessments with a landscape approach for spatially explicit land-use planning at national and sub-national levels.
source_quote: Policies that have been issued include (i) permanent extension of the forest and peatland moratoriums (Presidential Instruction 5/2019); (ii) implementation of mandatory certification for sustainable forest management; (iii) integrated, comprehensive, spatially explicit land use planning at national and sub-national level guided by the Government Regulation 46/2016 on strategic environmental assessments (SEAs) through landscape approach aiming at securing food, water, and energy security based on sound ecosystem management; (iv) establishment of new financial models for conservation and restoration in sustainable jurisdictions with the issuance of Government Regulation No. 46/2017 on Environmental economic instrument and other fiscal incentives; and (v) establishment of Indonesia Environmental Fund ( Badan Pengelola Dana Lingkungan Hidup /BPDLH) through Presidential Regulation No. 77/2018 concerning Management of Environmental Fund. extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory planning mechanism for sustainable land use and ecosystem management with mitigation and resource-security aims.

extraction_rationale: This is a financial-instrument policy supporting conservation and restoration in sustainable jurisdictions.
