policy_statement: Indonesia established the Environmental Fund Management Agency (BPDLH) to manage environmental and climate-related funds across forestry, energy, carbon trading, environmental services, industry, transport, agriculture, and marine and fisheries.
source_quote: BPDLH will manage funds related to forestry, energy and mineral resources, carbon trading, environmental services, industry, transportation, agriculture, marine and fisheries, and other fields related to the environment. The goal is to be able to manage funds more optimally and synergistically, as well as optimise the use of funds and mobilise funding resources both domestic and international sources. This agency is guided by principles of transparency and accountability and meets international governance standards.
section_header: 4.2.1. Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Uses (AFOLU)
extraction_rationale: BPDLH is an institutional financial mechanism for climate and environmental funding, including carbon trading and land-sector activities.

parent_statement: AFOLU policies and measures for low-carbon land-use transformation
policy_statement: Indonesia will use REDD+ result-based payments to incentivize local governments and concessions that conserve forests beyond existing regulations.
source_quote: Under the implementation of REDD+, the local governments and concessions who can conserved the forest beyond the existing regulation, are eligible for receiving Result-based Payment (RBP) under the Ministerial Regulation (Minister for Environment and Forestry) No. 70/2017. In addition, Indonesia is also in the process of preparing innovative regulation related to fiscal incentive, as part of the implementation of Government Regulation No. 46/2017.
extraction_rationale: Result-based payments are a financial incentive for verified forest conservation and emission reductions.

policy_statement: Under LCCP, Indonesia will limit cumulative future deforestation to about 6.8 Mha.
source_quote: The CPOS and LCCP indicate that expected cumulative area to be deforested in the future are about 14.6 Mha and 6.8 Mha respectively (see Figure 7). LCCP which requires future deforestation to be limited to 6.8 Mha to bring this sector becoming net sink also faces some challenges.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified deforestation limit tied to achieving a net sink in the land sector.

policy_statement: Indonesia will expand protected forest areas from 51.8 Mha to about 65 Mha under RPJMN 2020-2024.
source_quote: In the RPJMN 2020-2024, Indonesia has increased the area of forest under the protection zone to about 65 Mha, in which some of forest area under the production zone are allocated as protection zone. About 5.2 Mha forested lands allocated as the protection zone are in the concessions and in the APL.
section_header: b. Conservation and Sustainable Forest Management
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified nature-based protection target that preserves forest carbon stocks and ecosystem services.

policy_statement: Under LCCP, all forest concession companies will implement sustainable harvesting practices by 2050.
source_quote: With this policy, many forest concessions have improved their management practices. Under LCCP, by 2050 all forest concession companies have implement sustainable harvesting practices. At present, the forest concessions that have received the good forest certification reach about 76%.
section_header: b. Conservation and Sustainable Forest Management
extraction_rationale: This is a time-bound forest management requirement that directly supports reduced degradation and carbon sequestration.

policy_statement: Under LCCP, Indonesia will restore production forests through enhanced natural regeneration, reaching about 1.70 Mha after 2030 and 8.8 Mha by 2050.
source_quote: Efforts to restore the degraded production forest through enhanced natural regeneration (ENR) or forest restoration will also be increased. It is expected that under LCCP, area of production forest that being restored through the ENR programme after 2030 should reach about 1.70 Mha, about 2 times of the CPOS, and by 2050 it will reach 8.8 Mha or about 6 times of the CPOS.
section_header: b. Conservation and Sustainable Forest Management
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified ecosystem restoration target with explicit carbon sink implications.

policy_statement: Indonesia will prohibit new permits for peatland use under Presidential Instruction No. 5/2019 and mandate improved peatland and water management under Ministerial Regulation No. 15/2017.
source_quote: Indonesia has issued a number of key policies to protect peatland and improve its management. Under Presidential Instruction No. 5/2019, there will not be any new permit for the use of peatland. In addition, the Ministerial Regulation No. 15/2017 (Minister for Environment and Forestry) mandates private sector and local governments to improve the use of peatland and water management.
section_header: c. Protection and Restoration of Peatland
extraction_rationale: These are binding regulatory measures targeting a major AFOLU emissions source from peat decomposition and fires.

policy_statement: Under LCCP, Indonesia will improve peatland and water management on 0.95 Mha by 2030 and 1.04 Mha by 2050, and restore degraded peatland on 2.7 Mha by 2030 and 4.2 Mha by 2050.
source_quote: Under CPOS, it is expected that the improvement of peatland and water management by 2030 and 2050 reaches 0.86 Mha and 1.04 Mha consecutively, while under LCCP it should reach 0.95 Mha by 2030 and 1.04 Mha by 2050. For peatland restoration, CPOS figures the area of degraded peatland being restored should reach 1.03 Mha by 2030 and 1.7 Mha by 2050. While under LCCP, the target will be increased to 2.7 Mha by 2030 and 4.2 Mha by 2050.
section_header: c. Protection and Restoration of Peatland
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified peat restoration and water-management commitment with mitigation benefits from reduced peat emissions.

policy_statement: Under LCCP, Indonesia will rehabilitate 5.3 Mha of unproductive lands by 2030 and 10.6 Mha by 2050 through afforestation, reforestation, land rehabilitation, social forestry, and multi-permit forest concession policies.
source_quote: Under CPOS, Indonesia aims to rehabilitate the unproductive lands with priority in critical and very critical lands about 4.32 Mha by 2030 and 8.6 Mha by 2050. Under the LCCP, this target is increased to 5.3 Mha by 2030 and 10.6 Mha by 2050. Several programmes have been launched for accelerating the rehabilitation of the land, i.e. social forestry and land rehabilitation programmes and multi permit policies for forest concessions that allow to use the degraded lands for agriculture commodities in the form of agroforestry.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified land rehabilitation and sink enhancement policy using ecosystem restoration and agroforestry.

policy_statement: Indonesia will adopt low-emission rice varieties on 0.97 Mha by 2030 and 2.07 Mha by 2050 under LCCP.
source_quote: Under CPOS, the adoption of low emission variety is expected to be 0.93 Mha by 2030 and 1.96 Mha by 2050. Under LCCP, an ambitious target is set to 0.97 Mha by 2030 and 2.07 Mha by 2050. The adoption scale approximately reaches 24% of the total rice field area by 2050.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific agricultural mitigation technology with quantified adoption targets.

policy_statement: Indonesia will scale up SPR/STT water-saving paddy cultivation to 1.31 Mha under LCCP by 2050.
source_quote: The main emphasis of the SPR/STT programme is to increase rice production with minimum input and improved water use eff.shorticiency (e.g. intermittent flooding) and organic fertilizer application. Currently, SPR/STT is implemented as a pilot activity and the attainment from the pilot programme will be replicated to the other region. By 2050, the technology programme is expected to be scaled up to 1.18 M ha and 1.31 M ha under CPOS and LCCP, respectively.
extraction_rationale: This is a named technology programme with a quantified scale-up target and resource-efficiency mechanism.

policy_statement: Indonesia will implement livestock waste-to-biogas mitigation covering 41,000 head in 2030 and 94,000 head in 2050 under both CPOS and LCCP.
source_quote: The mitigation actions comprise the utilization of livestock waste for biogas and improvement of livestock feed supplement. The CPOS and LCCP are setting a similar target for biogas implementation, accounted for 41,000 head in 2030 and 94,000 head in 2050. However, the number is considerably low compared to the national livestock population as this activity requires high investment for biodigester and flaring facility and continues supply of livestock waste.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific methane mitigation intervention with quantified deployment targets.

policy_statement: Indonesia will improve livestock feed supplements to reduce methane emissions, targeting 6.58 million head in 2050 under LCCP.
source_quote: Research finds that shifting from high concentrate livestock feed to greenery feed, specifically in beef and dairy cattle, is potentially reduce methane emission from enteric fermentation. The feed supplement is a combination of the greenery and an additional feed supply of tannin from legume crops or urea molasses block. The target in CPOS and LCCP scenarios in 2050 is 3.42 million head and 6.58 million head, respectively.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific livestock methane-reduction practice with quantified coverage targets.

policy_statement: Under LCCP, Indonesia will reduce urea use by 5,374 tons in 2030 and 65,697 tons in 2050 through organic fertilizer substitution.
source_quote: Applying organic fertilizer is expected to reduce dependency on nitrogen fertilizer usage. Cropland farmers are encouraged to use organic fertilizer to substitute the urea application. Under LCCP, the reduction of total urea used in 2030 and 2050 is expected to be 5,374 ton and 65,697 ton, respectively.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified fertilizer substitution policy that reduces agricultural N2O emissions and improves input efficiency.

policy_statement: Under LCCP, Indonesia will increase crop productivity across major commodities by 2050, including rice, corn, vegetables, cassava, palm oil, sugar cane, fruits and nuts, and industrial crops, to reduce pressure on forests while maintaining food and export targets.
source_quote: Increasing agricultural productivity and cropping intensity are key factors in meeting food demand in line with population and GDP growth, at the same time maintaining emission by reducing deforestation. This can be achieved by using high quality seeds, fertilizing, and adoption of agricultural technology. The targets for increasing the optimal productivity for other agricultural commodities by 2050 is 8% (CPOS) and 22% (LCCP) for corn, 10% (CPOS) and 24% (LCCP) for vegetables, 27% (CPOS) and 48% (LCCP) for cassava, 74% (CPOS) and 95% (LCCP) for palm oil, 32% (CPOS) and 51% (LCCP) for sugar cane, 31% (CPOS and LCCP) for fruits and nuts, and 65% (CPOS and LCCP) for industrial crops.
section_header: a. Improvement of Crop Productivity and Cropping Intensity
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified agricultural productivity policy designed to meet demand while reducing deforestation-related emissions. Primary mechanism is land/resource-use efficiency.

policy_statement: Indonesia will increase rice cropping intensity by 2050 to 2.09 in Java and 1.78 outside Java under LCCP.
source_quote: The rice cropping intensity in Java in 2010 was 1.8 and must increase by 22% to 2.08 under CPOS and 2.09 under LCCP. Meanwhile, cropping intensity for rice outside Java in 2010 was 1.45 and must increase by 31% in 2050 to 1.72 under CPOS and 1.78 under LCCP. Increasing rice cropping intensity in 2050 will be achieved by targeting a growth up to 20% in 2010-2030 and 22% in 2030-2050 for the CPOS.
section_header: a. Improvement of Crop Productivity and Cropping Intensity
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified land-use-efficiency target that reduces pressure for land conversion.

policy_statement: Indonesia will use the Social Forestry Programme and TORA agrarian reform to grant legal land access and support agroforestry-based productivity improvements for communities in forest areas.
source_quote: By granting legal access through Social Forestry Programme, the farmers are eligible to receive supports from the government for the improvement of the farming activities by integrating the agriculture commodities with forest trees as agroforestry. Indonesia considers the Social Forestry Programme is a part of key solutions for addressing tenure issues and providing more access for community to utilise forest area and reducing poverty. Furthermore, Government provides land right to the farmers through agrarian reform (TORA Programme).
section_header: a. Improvement of Crop Productivity and Cropping Intensity
extraction_rationale: This is a named land-tenure and agroforestry intervention that supports forest-compatible livelihoods and reduced deforestation pressure.

policy_statement: Indonesia will promote agricultural technology and machinery adoption, supported by government assistance and improved farmer access to bank and non-bank credit.
source_quote: Government has encouraged the use of technology and machinery in agricultural production and provided assistance to support the adoption of technology by farmers. However, the technology adoption rate is limited due to financial constraints. Increasing financial access for the adoption of better technology and machinery in both scenarios is very important to ensure that the target of increasing productivity is achieved.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete support programme for mechanization and productivity improvements. Climate relevance is tied to the land-use efficiency strategy, but the action could also exist for agricultural development.

policy_statement: Under LCCP, Indonesia will increase farmer access to credit from banks and non-bank financial institutions to purchase agricultural machinery based on local needs.
source_quote: Under LCCP, technology adoption is assumed to be much higher due to an increase of farmers/farmers group access to credits from bank or NBFIs to purchase agricultural machinery based on their needs. Empowerment of farmers group and innovative agriculture credit schemes (individual or group lending) is a key to higher adoption technology in the future.
extraction_rationale: Credit access and innovative lending schemes are financial instruments supporting low-carbon agricultural intensification.

policy_statement: Indonesia will develop agricultural value-chain finance, including warehouse receipt systems, peer-to-peer lending, and credit programmes, to support low-carbon agriculture technology adoption.
source_quote: The development of innovative schemes in agriculture value finance is needed to increase access to capital from all actors along the chain (farmers, input traders and collectors/traders) to increase productivity of commodities. Under CPOS, value chain finance such as Warehouse receipt system, Peer to Peer lending (P2P) and credit programme provide credits to buy agricultural inputs and tools for technology adoption to support low carbon agriculture. Optimizing the implementation of the National Strategy for Financial Inclusion (SNKI) by actively involving the financial services industry (bank) and NBFIs and related institutions is important to increase financing for the agricultural sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a set of named credit and finance instruments explicitly linked to low-carbon agriculture.

policy_statement: Indonesia will expand integrated oil palm-livestock farming to 21.11% of oil palm area by 2030 and 34.33% by 2050 under LCCP, and examine incentives for climate-friendly farming practices.
source_quote: Under CPOS, integrated farming of oil palm-livestock is targeted to reach 11.70% (1.68 Mha) in 2030 and 22.72% (3.25 Mha) in 2050. Under LCCP, the target is increased to 21.11% (3.02 Mha) in 2030 and to 34.33% ( 4.91 Mha) in 2050. To increase the adoption of the integrated farming practices, particularly for large scale plantations, Government will examine possible incentive for encouraging climate-friendly farming practices.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified integrated farming target and includes possible incentives for climate-friendly practices.

policy_statement: Indonesia will optimize unproductive non-forest land and non-forested forest land for cropland expansion and social forestry, while enforcing the ban on conversion of agricultural land under Law No. 41/2009.
source_quote: The use of current unproductive land in non-forest area will be optimised for expansion of cropland. In addition, the use of non-forested land in forest areas for agriculture production under the scheme of Social Forestry Programme will also be accelerated as well as the issuance of multi permit for concession to allow for producing non-timber forest products, including agriculture production through partnership with communities as part of approaches in addressing land tenure issues. Restriction of conversion of agriculture lands as mandated by the Law No. 41/2009 on sustainable agriculture land is enforced.
section_header: c. Optimizing Use of Unproductive Land
extraction_rationale: This is a land-use efficiency and regulatory enforcement policy intended to reduce forest conversion while meeting agricultural demand.

policy_statement: Under LCCP, Indonesia will reduce rice paddy land conversion in Java to 0.10% per year and reduce expansion of rice paddy outside Java to 0.80% per year, supported by higher cropping intensity, irrigated land expansion, and new reservoirs.
source_quote: Under CPOS, the conversion of rice paddy land in Java will reduce significantly from 1.34% per year to 0.60% per year, while in LCCP it will reduce to 0.10%. On the other hand, with expansion of rice paddy outside Java also decreases from 1.31% to 1.00% per year in CPOS and to 0.80 in LCCP. This will occur if cropping intensity for rice in Java can be increased from 1.80 to 2.08 under CPOS and to 2.09 under LCCP, while for rice outside Java, from 1.45 to 1.72 under CPOS and to 1.78 under LCCP which will be carried out through expanding irrigated land outside Java and the establishment of a new reservoir in Java.
section_header: c. Optimizing Use of Unproductive Land
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified land-use conversion and agricultural intensification policy. Reservoirs and irrigation are named interventions but the primary mechanism is resource-efficient land use.

policy_statement: Under LCCP, Indonesia will reduce food loss from 71 kg per capita in 2010 to 34 kg per capita in 2050 through harvesting tools, cold storage, packaging technology, campaigns, and green certification for large-scale consumers.
source_quote: Modernization of harvesting tools is needed to improve harvesting techniques and reduce yield losses. Furthermore, assistance with cold storage facilities and packaging technology are essential to reduce food loss during food distribution. Improvements in harvest and post-harvest technology are expected to reduce food loss from 71 Kg per capita in 2010 to 40 Kg per capita in 2050 under CPOS and to 34 Kg per capita under LCCP.
section_header: d. Reducing Food Loss and Food Waste
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified food-loss reduction target with named interventions. It reduces land and resource demand and associated emissions.

policy_statement: Indonesia will implement seven energy mitigation guidelines focusing on power, energy efficiency, efficient transport and electrification, biofuels, industrial fuel switching, renewable energy, and BECCS/CCS/CCUS.
source_quote: Based on the understanding of type of fuels and energy-consuming sectors, taking into account past development and future projection of energy demand and supply, the LTS-LCCR was developed using the following general guidelines: 1. Focussing on power sector. 2. Minimize energy demand without sacrificing people welfare and economic development (energy eff.shorticiency measure),
section_header: 4.2.2.3. GHG Emission Projections and Mitigation Strategy
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella energy-sector mitigation package followed by enumerated sub-actions.

policy_statement: Indonesia will prioritize the power sector for energy-sector mitigation.
source_quote: Based on the understanding of type of fuels and energy-consuming sectors, taking into account past development and future projection of energy demand and supply, the LTS-LCCR was developed using the following general guidelines: 1. Focussing on power sector. 2. Minimize energy demand without sacrificing people welfare and economic development (energy eff.shorticiency measure),
section_header: 4.2.2.3. GHG Emission Projections and Mitigation Strategy
extraction_rationale: The power sector is identified as the determinant of energy-sector emissions and is explicitly named as the first mitigation focus.

parent_statement: Energy-sector mitigation guidelines under LTS-LCCR
policy_statement: Indonesia will minimize energy demand through energy-efficiency measures without sacrificing welfare and economic development.
source_quote: Based on the understanding of type of fuels and energy-consuming sectors, taking into account past development and future projection of energy demand and supply, the LTS-LCCR was developed using the following general guidelines: 1. Focussing on power sector. 2. Minimize energy demand without sacrificing people welfare and economic development (energy eff.shorticiency measure),
section_header: 4.2.2.3. GHG Emission Projections and Mitigation Strategy
extraction_rationale: This is a named energy-efficiency mitigation measure. It is specific enough because it is an enumerated guideline within a sector strategy.

parent_statement: Energy-sector mitigation guidelines under LTS-LCCR
policy_statement: Indonesia will promote mass public transport, electrify vehicles and end-use equipment, and use decarbonized electricity.
source_quote: 3. Develop more eff.shorticient transport system (promote mass public transport), electrification of vehicles and other equipment at end-users (residential and commercial) with decarbonized electricity. 4. Develop biofuels for transport and power plants, including biofuel resource base (feedstock, plantation). 5. Shifting fuel from coal to gas and renewable in industry.
section_header: 4.2.2.3. GHG Emission Projections and Mitigation Strategy
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete transport and end-use electrification policy with efficiency and decarbonized electricity mechanisms.

parent_statement: Energy-sector mitigation guidelines under LTS-LCCR
policy_statement: Indonesia will develop biofuels for transport and power plants, including the feedstock and plantation resource base.
source_quote: 3. Develop more eff.shorticient transport system (promote mass public transport), electrification of vehicles and other equipment at end-users (residential and commercial) with decarbonized electricity. 4. Develop biofuels for transport and power plants, including biofuel resource base (feedstock, plantation). 5. Shifting fuel from coal to gas and renewable in industry.
section_header: 4.2.2.3. GHG Emission Projections and Mitigation Strategy
extraction_rationale: This is a specific renewable fuel intervention for mitigation. It has potential land-use implications, but the primary stated mechanism is fossil fuel substitution.

parent_statement: Energy-sector mitigation guidelines under LTS-LCCR
policy_statement: Indonesia will shift industrial fuel use from coal to gas and renewable energy.
source_quote: 3. Develop more eff.shorticient transport system (promote mass public transport), electrification of vehicles and other equipment at end-users (residential and commercial) with decarbonized electricity. 4. Develop biofuels for transport and power plants, including biofuel resource base (feedstock, plantation). 5. Shifting fuel from coal to gas and renewable in industry.
section_header: 4.2.2.3. GHG Emission Projections and Mitigation Strategy
extraction_rationale: Fuel switching in industry is a named mitigation action.

parent_statement: Energy-sector mitigation guidelines under LTS-LCCR
policy_statement: Indonesia will develop renewable energy in power, transport, and industry, including domestic capacity to produce solar PV and batteries.
source_quote: 6. Develop renewable energy (hydro, geothermal, solar PV and wind, including capacity development to produce solar PV and batteries) in power, transport and industry, which will consequently reduce coal for power. 7. BECCS (negative emission) will be used and the remaining coal power plants will be equipped with CCS/CCUS.
section_header: 4.2.2.3. GHG Emission Projections and Mitigation Strategy
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete renewable energy deployment and industrial capacity policy.

parent_statement: Energy-sector mitigation guidelines under LTS-LCCR
policy_statement: Indonesia will use BECCS and equip remaining coal power plants with CCS/CCUS.
source_quote: 6. Develop renewable energy (hydro, geothermal, solar PV and wind, including capacity development to produce solar PV and batteries) in power, transport and industry, which will consequently reduce coal for power. 7. BECCS (negative emission) will be used and the remaining coal power plants will be equipped with CCS/CCUS.
section_header: 4.2.2.3. GHG Emission Projections and Mitigation Strategy
extraction_rationale: BECCS and CCS/CCUS are specific mitigation technologies for power-sector emissions reduction and negative emissions.

policy_statement: Under LCCP, Indonesia will nearly decarbonize power by 2050 through massive renewable deployment, CCS/CCUS on most coal plants, and BECCS, targeting 43% renewables, 38% coal, 10% natural gas, and 8% BECCS in the power generation mix.
source_quote: It is expected that in 2050 the power sector will nearly decarbonised, through: (i) utilization of renewables (hydro, geothermal, solar, wind, biomass) in massive scale; (ii) most coal powerplants are equipped with CCS/CCUS; and (iii) biomass-coal cofiring power plants are connected to CCS (Biomass Energy with Carbon Capture and Storage or BECCS). It is envisaged that the power situation in 2050 under LCCP will be as follows: Power generation mix are: renewables (43%), coal (38%), natural gas (10%) and BECCS (8%).
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified power-sector transformation target with specific technology pathways.

policy_statement: Under LCCP, Indonesia will equip around 76% of coal power plants with CCS and achieve a power generation carbon intensity of 104 gCO2/kWh.
source_quote: Around 76% of the coal power plant are equipped with CCS to achieve zero emissions in coal power plants. Installed capacity of renewable power generation mix are: solar PV 113 GW, hydro 68 GW, geothermal 23 GW, wind power 17 GW, biomass 13 GW, biofuel 14 GW and BECCS 23 GW with negative emissions. The carbon intensity of power generation: 104 gram CO 2 /kWh.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified CCS deployment and emissions-intensity target in the power sector.

policy_statement: Under LCCP, Indonesia will install renewable power capacity by 2050 of 113 GW solar PV, 68 GW hydro, 23 GW geothermal, 17 GW wind, 13 GW biomass, 14 GW biofuel, and 23 GW BECCS.
source_quote: Around 76% of the coal power plant are equipped with CCS to achieve zero emissions in coal power plants. Installed capacity of renewable power generation mix are: solar PV 113 GW, hydro 68 GW, geothermal 23 GW, wind power 17 GW, biomass 13 GW, biofuel 14 GW and BECCS 23 GW with negative emissions. The carbon intensity of power generation: 104 gram CO 2 /kWh.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified renewable and negative-emissions power capacity target.

policy_statement: Indonesia will increase off-grid and micro-grid development and deploy smart grids and smart micro-grids to integrate large shares of intermittent renewable energy.
source_quote: Increasing development of 'off-grid' and 'micro-grid'. Due to significant portion of intermittent renewable (solar and wind) will be deployed in the future, it will require development of smart grid that can handle large supply intermittency. Power plant with 100% renewable energy in remote areas will need Smart Micro Grid.
extraction_rationale: This is a named grid infrastructure intervention that enables renewable-energy mitigation.

policy_statement: Under LCCP, Indonesia will transform transport energy by 2050 to 46% biofuels, 20% oil fuels, 30% electricity, and 4% natural gas, continuing biodiesel blends B30, B40, and B50 from sustainable sources.
source_quote: The breakdown of transport energy in 2050 are: biofuels (46%), oil fuels (20%), electricity (30%) and natural gas (4%). The biofuel (CPO-based) programme is considered successful and will be continued to 2050 by supplying biofuel with higher biodiesel proportions (B30, B40, B50), which will be produced from sustainable sources.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified transport fuel-switching target and a named biofuel blending programme.

policy_statement: Indonesia will build 3,200 km of inter-city train tracks in Sumatra, Java, Kalimantan, and Sulawesi to support lower-carbon transport.
source_quote: Many cities are connected by inter-city trains especially in Java. Existing plan shows that 3,200 km of train tracks will be built to serve transport in Sumatra, Java, Kalimantan, and Sulawesi.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified rail infrastructure investment supporting modal shift. Climate relevance is indirect but substantial within the transport decarbonization section.

policy_statement: Indonesia will prepare workforce transition from fossil-based energy systems to low-carbon energy systems and green jobs.
source_quote: Preparation of employment transition from fossil-based energy system to low-carbon energy system will be part of overall energy transition efforts. The transition will require preparation of human resources which will be aligned with policies and programmes on human resource development, including policies and programmes towards Indonesia Vision 2045.
section_header: c. Preparation of Migration to Green Jobs
extraction_rationale: This is a specific transition-management commitment accompanying energy mitigation. It is not itself a mitigation technology, but it supports implementation of the climate transition.

policy_statement: Indonesia will implement a long-term low-carbon waste strategy using reduction, avoidance, destruction, and utilization of methane emissions from municipal solid waste, domestic wastewater, and industrial waste.
source_quote: Four following pillars of guidance are used to develop a long-term low-carbon strategy toward zero emissions in the waste sector, taking into account past development and projection of future waste management activities through reduction, avoidance, destruction, and utilization of GHG emissions, particularly methane (CH 4 ) gas, which generated during the treatment of municipal solid waste (MSW), domestic wastewater, and industrial solid waste and wastewater. In the MSW treatments, the reduction is implemented through the utilization of aerobic treatment for the management of solid waste disposal sites (SWDS), the avoidance is implemented by reducing the waste to be treated to avoid the generation of methane gas emissions, i.e. recycling (3R), waste banks, ITF (Intermediate Treatment Facilities), and composting (compost house), MSW bio-digester, and the destruction/utilization is implemented by burning the landfill gas (LFG) for flaring, power generation, or gas cooking in household, producing the RDF (refuse derived fuel), and burning the waste in PLTSa 6 (MSW power plant).
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella waste-sector mitigation strategy followed by sector-specific sub-actions for MSW, wastewater, and industrial waste.

parent_statement: Long-term low-carbon waste strategy
policy_statement: Indonesia will manage municipal solid waste through 30% source reduction using 3R and composting and 70% treatment through landfilling, composting, and waste-to-energy, including PLTSa and RDF.
source_quote: Under CPOS, the MSW will be managed through waste reduction at sources (30%) by 3R (reduce-reuse-recycle) and waste treatment (70%) through landfilling, composting, and converting waste to energy. This 3R is a part of Circular Economy which is promoted in Indonesia. Under CPOS, 70% of the MSW will be managed in landfill and/or converted to energy as PLTSa and/or RDF.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified MSW management target with named waste reduction and waste-to-energy interventions.

parent_statement: Long-term low-carbon waste strategy
policy_statement: Under LCCP, Indonesia will increase SWDS landfill-gas recovery, MSW use for PLTSa and RDF/SRF, biodigesters with biogas and sludge recovery, paper recycling, composting, and septic tanks with biogas recovery or aerobic treatment.
source_quote: LCCP increases the potential of TRNS and CPOS mitigation significant adding the number of SWDS equipped with LFG recovery, the amount of MSW used for PLTSa and RDF/SRF, the number of biodigester equipped with biogas and sludge recovery, and the number of paper recycling and composting. The mitigation also covers the increase of septic tanks utilisation (100% new houses) equipped with biogas recovery or aerobic, sludge recovery systems and increased utilization of waste for energy. Increased use of septic tanks (100% new houses) equipped with biogas recovery, aerobic systems, sludge recovery and maximizing the utilization of liquid waste and industrial solid waste for energy.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete package of waste-sector methane mitigation and waste-to-energy measures under the ambitious scenario.

parent_statement: Long-term low-carbon waste strategy
policy_statement: Indonesia will increase access to septic tanks from 71% to 85% for rural residents and from 88% to 99% for urban residents by 2050, using lower-emission technologies as mitigation measures.
source_quote: Government programs to increase the number of septic-tank from 71% in 2020 to 85% in 2050 for people live in rural and from 88% in 2020 to 99% in 2050 for people live in urban are implemented in order to increase the access of people to the toilet (individual and communal) could be implemented as mitigation measures by introducing technologies that reduces or lower the GHG emissions. Under CPOS, mitigation under unconditional NDC are extended until 2050, which include additional septic tank with biogas recovery and sludge removal and implementation of aerobic system.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified sanitation infrastructure target with explicit lower-GHG technology measures.

parent_statement: Long-term low-carbon waste strategy
policy_statement: Under LCCP, Indonesia will increase centralized aerobic domestic wastewater treatment to 36% of urban residents by 2050 and deploy aerobic septic tanks and biodigester septic tanks with methane recovery.
source_quote: Under TRNS and LCCP, more ambitious mitigation mitigation can be deployed to decrease the level of GHG emissions through the additional aerobic septic tank, biodigester septic tank equipped with methane recovery for new toilet/ septic-tank, and centralised WWT for domestic wastewater. Under TRNS, it is assumed that the use of aerobic centralised will increase from 1% of people live in urban in 2020 to 14% in 2050 while under LCCP it will increase to 36% in 2050.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified domestic wastewater mitigation target with specific treatment technologies.

parent_statement: Long-term low-carbon waste strategy
policy_statement: Under TRNS and LCCP, Indonesia will treat industrial wastewater and sludge as energy and material sources using anaerobic digesters with methane recovery and sludge utilization.
source_quote: Under TRNS and LCCP, most of wastewater from significant emissions contributor industries will be treated for energy and material sources, such as the use of anaerobic digester equipped with methane gas recovery and utilizing the sludge from WWT unit for energy, compost and materials sources. The GHG emissions level of the three scenarios is presented in Figure 28. Under LCCP, all of the above mitigation actions are expected to increase significantly.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete industrial waste methane mitigation and resource-recovery policy.

policy_statement: Under LCCP, Indonesia will reduce waste-sector GHG emissions from 198 MtCO2e in 2030 to 120 MtCO2e in 2050.
source_quote: Under LCCP, the GHG emissions will decrease 2.5% per year from 198 Mton CO 2 e in 2030 to 120 Mton CO 2 e in 2050 with the rate of 2.5% per year. If it is compared to the GHG emissions level in 2010, under LCCP the GHG emissions level will be 1.35 times with those in 2010 7 . Under LCCP, all potential mitigation under CPOS and TRNS are maximized by adding several ambitious mitigations, particularly in the MSW and industrial waste treatments.
section_header: 4.2.3.2. GHG Emission Projection and Mitigation Strategy
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified sectoral GHG target for waste.

policy_statement: Indonesia will implement IPPU mitigation strategies for cement, ammonia-urea, nitric acid, aluminium, and iron and steel production to lower industrial-process emissions.
source_quote: Under LCCP, it is assumed that mitigation actions include (a) significant increasing of cement production using blended cement technology with clinker/cement ratio of 0.70 in 2050, (b) increasing ammonia production using advanced and eff.shorticient technology with natural gas consumption at a rate of 35 GJ per ton NH 3 in 2050, (c) increasing the use of secondary catalyst for N 2 O digestion/destruction in nitric acid production industry ((higher than those in TRNS), (d) the use of improved (advanced processing technology for Aluminium production, and (e) the use of scrap up to 20% (higher than those in TRNS) as raw material in iron and steel industries but it is limited by the availability of the scrap materials. Under this scenario, although GHG emissions are estimated to continue increasing at a rate of 0.9% per year (2010-2050) to reach 50.2 Mton CO 2 e in 2050 or 0.9 times the level of GHG emissions in 2010.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella IPPU mitigation package with clearly listed sub-actions and quantified technology assumptions.

parent_statement: IPPU mitigation strategies
policy_statement: Under LCCP, Indonesia will increase blended cement production by implementing a clinker-to-cement ratio up to 0.70 for most cement production from 2030 to 2050.
source_quote: Blended cement mitigation under CPOS are the extend of clinker to cement ratio in 50% of cement production capacities at the level of clinker to cement ratio of 0.75 to 2050. Under TRNS, blended cement mitigation under CPOS is increased by implementing clinker to cement ratio of 0.75 from 2030 to 2050 for most cement productions. Under LCPP, blended cement mitigation are increased by implementing clinker to cement ratio up to 0.70 for most cement productions in 2030 to 2050.
section_header: a. Blended Cement in Cement Industry
extraction_rationale: This is a specific industrial-process mitigation technology and quantified material-intensity target.

parent_statement: IPPU mitigation strategies
policy_statement: Under LCCP, Indonesia will improve ammonia-urea plant technology so most plants reach at least 36.6 GJ natural gas per ton NH3 or best practice technology by 2050.
source_quote: Under LCCP, the natural gas consumption in the most plant should at least have natural gas consumption rate of 36.6 GJ natural gas /ton NH 3 or at least Best Practice Technology (BPT) in 2050. It should be noted that current world BPT has natural gas consumption rate of 32 GJ/ton NH 3 while the European best available technology (BAT) has 31.8 GJ/ ton NH 3 , the world BAT has 28 GJ/ton NH 3 (IEA, 2015), and some of ammonia plants in Indonesia have 33-35 GJ/ton NH 3 .
section_header: b. Technology Improvement of New Ammonia Urea Plants
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified industrial energy-efficiency technology target that reduces emissions intensity.

parent_statement: IPPU mitigation strategies
policy_statement: Under LCCP, Indonesia will deploy secondary catalyst reduction for N2O destruction in nitric acid production.
source_quote: Other selective catalytic process, e.g. secondary catalyst reduction (SCR) will also be applied as secondary mitigation for the N 2 O emissions destruction in nitric acids productions in 2022, with the EF decreased to 2.5 Kg N 2 O per ton HNO 3 . The deployment potential for future mitigation is relatively small due to high cost, therefore, this mitigation will be deployed under the LCCP.
section_header: c. Secondary Catalyst for N 2 O Destruction in Nitric Acid Industry
extraction_rationale: This is a specific industrial N2O abatement technology and explicitly assigned to the LCCP scenario.

parent_statement: IPPU mitigation strategies
policy_statement: Under TRNS and LCCP, Indonesia will deploy improved aluminium processing technology to reduce PFC emissions by reducing anode effects.
source_quote: Improving the aluminium production plant with an advanced technology that could reduce PFCs (CF 4 /C 2 F 6 ) emissions has been implemented, i.e. reducing the Anode Effect (AE) at smelter facilities. This mitigation is planned to be deployed in the aluminium industry for additional mitigation potential in 2050 under TRNS and LCCP. By maintaining this mitigation technology, in 2050, PFC emissions level under TRNS and LCCP can be reduced from 577 Kton CO 2 e (CPOS) to 462 Kton CO 2 e.
section_header: d. Improvement of Aluminium Processing Technology
extraction_rationale: This is a specific industrial-process mitigation technology with a quantified emissions reduction outcome.

parent_statement: IPPU mitigation strategies
policy_statement: Under LCCP, Indonesia will use scrap as up to 20% of raw material in iron and steel industries, subject to scrap availability.
source_quote: Under LCCP, it is assumed that mitigation actions include (a) significant increasing of cement production using blended cement technology with clinker/cement ratio of 0.70 in 2050, (b) increasing ammonia production using advanced and eff.shorticient technology with natural gas consumption at a rate of 35 GJ per ton NH 3 in 2050, (c) increasing the use of secondary catalyst for N 2 O digestion/destruction in nitric acid production industry ((higher than those in TRNS), (d) the use of improved (advanced processing technology for Aluminium production, and (e) the use of scrap up to 20% (higher than those in TRNS) as raw material in iron and steel industries but it is limited by the availability of the scrap materials. Under this scenario, although GHG emissions are estimated to continue increasing at a rate of 0.9% per year (2010-2050) to reach 50.2 Mton CO 2 e in 2050 or 0.9 times the level of GHG emissions in 2010.
extraction_rationale: Scrap use is a concrete material-efficiency measure in steel production with an explicit GHG mitigation purpose.

policy_statement: Indonesia will increase additional investment for mitigation, reaching USD 73.3 billion in 2050 under LCCP.
source_quote: Moreover, higher emission reduction target requires higher growth in additional investment of 5.8% per year for CPOS and 8.2% per year for TRNS and LCCP. In 2050, additional investment will reach USD 39.7 billion under CPOS, USD 73.4 billion under TRNS and USD 73.3 billion under LCCP (see Figure 37).
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified investment requirement/public-private investment line for mitigation implementation.

policy_statement: Indonesia will implement regional and sectoral adaptation pathways to prioritize climate adaptation actions for food, water, energy, environmental health, ecosystems, and disaster risk.
source_quote: The process in translating all climate resilience components as reflected in Figure 39 is in the early stage. Therefore, climate resilience pathways were developed by using two approaches namely regional and sectoral approaches (see Figure 40). The regional pathway focuses on the priority areas to implement adaptation actions based on several basic necessities (food, water, energy, and environmental health), taking into account the aspect of climate, climate sensitive, non-climate sensitive, and social economy.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella adaptation-planning policy followed by regional and sectoral sub-pathways.

parent_statement: Regional and sectoral adaptation pathways
policy_statement: Indonesia will use regional pathways based on climate hotspots, vulnerability index data, and priority areas to identify regions most affected by climate change for adaptation interventions.
source_quote: Regional pathway focuses on the priority areas to implement the adaptation actions based on several basic necessities such as food, water, energy, and environmental health (see Figure 41). The basic analysis on the development of regional pathway is the climate change hotspot, as the Pathway focuses on the activities in the regions that are impacted by climate change. The Pathway, then, is combined with priority areas to identify regions that are mostly affected by climate change, which can be used to determine the priority regions for adaptation interventions.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete climate-risk planning mechanism for prioritizing adaptation interventions.

parent_statement: Regional and sectoral adaptation pathways
policy_statement: Indonesia will focus priority programmes in regions that are both potentially exposed to climate change hotspots and categorized as vulnerable.
source_quote: Overlay of climate hotspot maps with vulnerability maps is carried out with the consideration of not all regions that are potentially exposed to climate hotspots are considered vulnerable. For instance, settlements in flood-prone cities have good economic conditions and educational levels, hence they survive despite the hazards. Therefore, priority programmes need to be focused in regions that are potentially exposed to climate change and are included in the category of vulnerable regions.
extraction_rationale: This is a prioritization rule for adaptation programme targeting based on hazard and vulnerability.

parent_statement: Regional and sectoral adaptation pathways
policy_statement: Indonesia will develop sectoral adaptation pathways by mapping NDC priority areas, key programmes, strategies, strategic pillars, and adaptation programmes across sectors.
source_quote: Sectoral pathway was developed through mapping modalities used in NDC including identification of priority areas, key programs, strategies and strategic pillars, and adaptation programmes in various sectors (see Figure 43). The targets and objectives of various fields in the NDC are elaborated through various key programs as an effort to increase resilience in the economic, social and livelihood fields, as well as in ecosystems and landscapes (see Figure 44).
extraction_rationale: This is a planning policy for translating NDC adaptation priorities into sectoral programmes.

parent_statement: Regional and sectoral adaptation pathways
policy_statement: Indonesia will plan and implement sectoral adaptation based on basic necessities and strengthen coordination among sectoral ministries and agencies to avoid maladaptation.
source_quote: Planning and implementing adaptation in sectoral pathway must be conducted based on basic necessities (see Figure 45). It is also important to avoid mal-adaptation that potentially occur if the adaptation is carried out without coordination amongst sectors. The synergy between sectoral ministries/ agencies is needed in climate change adaptation.
extraction_rationale: This is a governance policy for coordinated adaptation implementation and maladaptation avoidance.

policy_statement: Indonesia estimates adaptation financing needs of at least IDR 33.12 trillion to IDR 173.10 trillion, up to IDR 577.01 trillion, and allocates 5-10% for roadmap governance and 90-95% for implementation.
source_quote: Referring to the impacts of climate change which can affect 0.66% to 3.45% of national GDP or around IDR 110.38 T to 577.01 T (2020 value, without considering the incidence of COVID-19), the estimated need for adaptation costs to climate change in Indonesia reaches at least about IDR 33.12 T to 173.10 T (assuming an investment ratio of 30%) to IDR 577.01 T (assuming the same amount of investment as the impact costs). Funding needs for adaptation are divided into two parts, namely funding for road map governance (5% - 10%) and funding for adaptation implementation (90% - 95%).
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified adaptation financing allocation framework.

policy_statement: Indonesia estimates IDR 12.84 trillion for adaptation roadmap governance, with the largest allocation for adaptive technology implementation.
source_quote: As for funding for the road map governance (i.e., enabling condition for the implementation of adaptation actions), the estimated total funding required is about IDR 12.84 trillion. The largest allocation of funding needs is needed for the adaptive technology implementation strategy (~27.19%), while the least amount is for policy formulation and strengthening commitment by 2.24%.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified budget estimate for adaptation governance and enabling conditions.

policy_statement: Indonesia will strengthen investment conditions, supportive policies, political stability, transport and infrastructure, efficient financial markets, and incentives for climate-friendly investment to achieve LCCP mitigation targets.
source_quote: In general, to achieve the mitigation targets under LCCP, the growth of investment is essential. Supportive environment for investment will continuously be strengthened, including supportive policies, political stability, transport and infrastructure, as well as eff.shorticient financial markets to encourage climateconscious investment and incentives for climate-friendly investments.
section_header: 6.1. Prerequisites for Successful Implementation of LTS-LCCR
extraction_rationale: This is an enabling financial and investment policy for climate mitigation, including incentives for climate-friendly investments. It is broad but anchored in investment and incentives.

policy_statement: Indonesia will implement cross-cutting transformative policies and measures for successful LCCP implementation across AFOLU, energy, waste, IPPU, adaptation, and food loss/waste.
source_quote: Table 4 depicts cross cutting issues to be addressed for the successful implementation of the LCCP, transformation needed, policy and measures for the required transformation, and institutional engagement. High political commitment, enhanced coordination and synergy among line Ministries, sound think tank, as well as effective engagement of non-state actors/non-party stakeholders will be determining factors for the success of the LTS-LCCR implementation.
section_header: 6.1. Prerequisites for Successful Implementation of LTS-LCCR
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella table of cross-cutting measures with clear sub-actions listed in rows.

parent_statement: Cross-cutting transformative policies and measures for successful LCCP implementation
policy_statement: Indonesia will enhance farmer access to land, finance, technology, capacity building, and markets to enable high-quality seeds and improved technologies and practices for agricultural productivity.
source_quote: Improvement in agriculture productivity | Enhanced access to land, finance, technology, capacity building, and market for farmers, to enable them to use high quality seeds and adopt improved technologies and practices. | Ministries responsible in agriculture, forestry, finance, industry, Trade, UMKM, Financial Institutions, Education and Training
section_header: 6.1. Prerequisites for Successful Implementation of LTS-LCCR
extraction_rationale: This table row states a concrete package of support measures for low-carbon agriculture. The quote is a table entry rather than prose.

parent_statement: Cross-cutting transformative policies and measures for successful LCCP implementation
policy_statement: Indonesia will optimize unproductive non-forest land for cropland expansion and enforce bans on converting agricultural lands to other land uses.
source_quote: Increasing land use eff.shorticiency (including integrated farming or complex agroforestry, optimizing the use of unproductive lands/idle lands) | Optimization in the use of unproductive land in non-forest areas for cropland expansion, along with the enforcement of banning conversion of agriculture lands to other land uses. | Ministries responsible in agriculture, forestry, and local government
section_header: 6.1. Prerequisites for Successful Implementation of LTS-LCCR
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete land-use efficiency and regulatory enforcement measure supporting AFOLU mitigation.

parent_statement: Cross-cutting transformative policies and measures for successful LCCP implementation
policy_statement: Indonesia will provide incentives for large-scale businesses that contribute to emission reductions and other environmental benefits.
source_quote: Increasing commitment of large-scale business to environmentally sound practices | Provision of incentives for the contribution to emission reduction and other environmental benefits | Ministries responsible in agriculture, forestry, finance, industry, trade and local government
section_header: 6.1. Prerequisites for Successful Implementation of LTS-LCCR
extraction_rationale: This is an incentive-based financial policy to encourage emission reductions and environmental benefits.

parent_statement: Cross-cutting transformative policies and measures for successful LCCP implementation
policy_statement: Indonesia will strengthen environmental impact assessment compliance and account for deforestation reduction needs in infrastructure and land-use planning.
source_quote: Environmentally sound land use across Indonesia's geography | Enhanced compliance on environmental impact assessment and consideration of development needs and the needs to reduce deforestation during the planning process. | Ministries responsible in infrastructure, environment, forestry, economy, and local government
section_header: 6.1. Prerequisites for Successful Implementation of LTS-LCCR
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory planning measure to avoid deforestation during development and infrastructure planning.

parent_statement: Cross-cutting transformative policies and measures for successful LCCP implementation
policy_statement: Indonesia will enhance investment in renewables and align policies across ministries to reduce trade-offs between energy demand and emission reduction targets.
source_quote: Implementation of energy eff.shorticiency measures, decarbonization in power sector using large renewables, coal with CCS/ CCUS, and biofuels in transport | Enhanced investment in renewables and policy alignment across related Ministries/ institutions to minimize 'trade off' between meeting energy demand and achieving emission reduction target | Ministries responsible in energy, transport, forestry, agriculture, industry
section_header: 6.1. Prerequisites for Successful Implementation of LTS-LCCR
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete investment and policy-alignment measure for energy mitigation.

parent_statement: Cross-cutting transformative policies and measures for successful LCCP implementation
policy_statement: Indonesia will provide incentives and access to capital for domestic solar PV and electric vehicle battery companies and accelerate joint ventures with technology transfer.
source_quote: Capacity building and technology transfer/ development to accelerate domestic industry of solar PV and electric car battery | Provision of incentives and access to capital for domestic companies and acceleration of joint ventures with technology transfer | Ministry of Industry and Ministry of Finance
section_header: 6.1. Prerequisites for Successful Implementation of LTS-LCCR
extraction_rationale: This is an industrial support and finance measure for clean energy and EV supply chains.

parent_statement: Cross-cutting transformative policies and measures for successful LCCP implementation
policy_statement: Indonesia will strengthen enforcement and compliance with waste-management regulations and create enabling conditions for circular economy development.
source_quote: Waste management which reduce GHGs emissions | • Enhanced enforcement and compliance to the regulatory frameworks relating to waste management • Enhanced enabling environment for Circular Economic development. | Ministries responsible in home affairs, economy, environment, and local government
section_header: 6.1. Prerequisites for Successful Implementation of LTS-LCCR
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory and enabling policy for waste-sector GHG reduction and circular economy.

parent_statement: Cross-cutting transformative policies and measures for successful LCCP implementation
policy_statement: Indonesia will create an enabling environment for investments that shift industry from fossil-based technology to green technology and strengthen technology-development partnerships.
source_quote: The use of environmentally sound/green technology and technology advancement | • Creating enabling environment for attracting investments that facilitate the shift from fossil-based technology to green technology, • Strengthen partnership for technology development | Ministries responsible in industry, energy, technology, foreign affairs, economy
section_header: 6.1. Prerequisites for Successful Implementation of LTS-LCCR
extraction_rationale: This is an investment-enabling and technology partnership policy for industrial decarbonization.

parent_statement: Cross-cutting transformative policies and measures for successful LCCP implementation
policy_statement: Indonesia will align adaptation policies and programmes among ministries, regions, and local governments to improve implementation of regional and sectoral pathways.
source_quote: Enhanced effectiveness of the planning and implementation of the two pathways | Policy and programme alignment among line ministries, among regions and between ministries and local governments (vertical and horizontal alignment) and coherent institutional arrangement | Ministries responsible in agriculture, forestry, fisheries, infrastructure, health, energy, planning and development
section_header: 6.1. Prerequisites for Successful Implementation of LTS-LCCR
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete governance measure for adaptation pathway implementation.

policy_statement: Indonesia will implement pre-2030 just-transition interventions to support workers, cities, sectors, and regions during the shift to low-carbon development.
source_quote: In line with the LTS-LCCR objectives to guide the implementation of NDC and the development of the subsequent NDCs beyond 2030, interventions to address just transition issues are divided into two following phases : (i) pre 2030 (20212030, the period of Indonesia first NDC), and (ii) post 2030 (2031 - 2050, the subsequent NDCs). Table 5 describes key interventions to be carried out during the first phase (2021 to 2030), along with the transition towards Indonesia 2045 and 2050 climate goals.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella just-transition policy package with tabled sub-interventions for the first implementation phase.

parent_statement: Pre-2030 just-transition interventions
policy_statement: Indonesia will strengthen climate governance and SDG implementation at all levels to address transition challenges faced by sectors, cities, regions, and affected workers.
source_quote: Addressing challenges faced by sectors, cities and regions in transitioning to low carbon development and in ensuring a decent future for workers affected by the transition. | Strengthening climate governance and implementation of sustainable development goals at all levels | Ministries responsible in climate change, national development, finance, and local governments
extraction_rationale: This is a governance intervention for just transition linked directly to low-carbon development.

parent_statement: Pre-2030 just-transition interventions
policy_statement: Indonesia will enhance green investments and align investment, climate policies, programmes, and COVID-19 recovery to create quality jobs in cities and regions.
source_quote: Promoting low greenhouse gas emission and sustainable economic activities that will create quality jobs in cities and regions. | Enhancement of green investments and alignment between investment and climate policies and programmes, including alignment of COVID-19 recovery with climate policies | Ministries responsible on economic development, investment, finance, and environment - forestry and land uses -natural resources
extraction_rationale: This is a green investment and policy-alignment measure for low-GHG economic activities.

parent_statement: Pre-2030 just-transition interventions
policy_statement: Indonesia will strengthen skilling, upskilling, reskilling, and human resource development programmes to help workers access decent and quality green jobs.
source_quote: Enhancing capacity of workforces to facilitate access to decent work and quality jobs, taking into account gender and inter-generational equalities, as well as the needs of vulnerable groups. | Strengthening and evolving programmes on 'skilling - upskilling - reskilling' and human resource development in general, | Ministries responsible on man-power/workforce, gender and inter- generation, education, social affairs.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete workforce capacity-building policy for the low-carbon transition.

parent_statement: Pre-2030 just-transition interventions
policy_statement: Indonesia will improve participatory public dialogue mechanisms to support high employment, social protection, labour standards, and worker/community wellbeing during transition.
source_quote: Enhancing participatory public dialogue to foster high employment rates, adequate social protection, labour standards and wellbeing of workers and their communities. | Increase effectiveness of existing communication mechanisms and platforms. | Ministries responsible on man-power/workforce, social affairs.
extraction_rationale: This is a named governance and participation intervention supporting just transition. Climate relevance is direct because it is embedded in transition to low-carbon development.

policy_statement: Indonesia will use the National Strategy for Acceleration of Gender Mainstreaming Implementation as a basis for addressing gender issues under LTS-LCCR 2050, including climate-related challenges in water, energy, sanitation, food scarcity, and disasters.
source_quote: The policy implementation since 2015 (RPJM 2015-2019) suggested the need for improvement to be taken in RPJM 2020-2024 and beyond, including : (i) gender equality and justice in education, (ii) life expectancy, (iii) health, (iv) workforce, (v) economy, (vi) political representation in parliament, (vii) eradication of domestic violence, and (viii) tackling climate related challenges (access to water, energy and sanitation and capacity to face food scarcity and disaster). Strategies to be implemented includes : (i) strengthening policy and regulation, (ii) accelerating gender mainstreaming, (iii) awareness raising, (iv) enhancing role and participation of women in development, and (v) improving network and coordination among stakeholders, which are part of 'National Strategy for Acceleration of Gender Mainstreaming Implementation'. This national strategy will be a strong basis for addressing gender issues under LTS-LCCR 2050 and Indonesia Vision 2045.
extraction_rationale: This is a cross-cutting social policy explicitly applied to climate-related adaptation challenges. Climate relevance is indirect because gender mainstreaming is broader than climate policy.

policy_statement: Indonesia will promote sustainable supply-chain initiatives, product certification, and measures addressing unsustainable production practices under RCEP implementation.
source_quote: In order to contribute to the effectiveness of RCEP implementation, the government will create a trading and investment environments which promote sustainable supply chain initiatives, product certification and potential future means to address unsustainable production practices.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete trade and certification policy relevant to avoiding deforestation and sustainable commodity production, though climate is not the sole objective.

policy_statement: Indonesia will strengthen domestic and international research collaboration on low-carbon farming, food loss reduction, ocean contributions to mitigation and adaptation, and sustainability transitions.
source_quote: Low carbon farming, food handling and processing to reduce food loss, the extent of contribution of ocean in mitigation and adaptation are among priority areas of research to support transition in nature-based sector. Research to support sustainability transition in all sectors will also needed. Indonesia will strengthen research collaboration among institutions within the country and national institutions with international partners, including think tanks and research institutions.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete research collaboration commitment targeting named mitigation and adaptation research areas.

policy_statement: Indonesia will seek technology cooperation under the Paris Agreement and Convention to support AFOLU productivity technologies, renewable power, and technology changes in energy, IPPU, and waste.
source_quote: With the ambitious target for the LTS-LCCR, Indonesia seeks opportunity for technology cooperation under the framework of technology development and transfer of the Paris Agreement and the Convention. Indonesia considers technology cooperation under this framework as a key element for the ambitious scenario of the LTS-LCCR.
extraction_rationale: This is a technology-transfer implementation policy for the ambitious mitigation scenario. It is broad, but it is tied to specified sectors and international mechanisms.

policy_statement: Indonesia will develop a climate mitigation and adaptation financing strategy by diversifying finance sources, strengthening finance institutions, and improving stakeholder access to finance.
source_quote: Financing strategy for climate mitigation and adaptation in Indonesia is currently at the preliminary stage of development. The concept of financing strategy is built with the assumption that the finance needs for climate actions should be addressed by optimizing climate finance system, starting from finance sources, finance institutions and their mechanisms as well as institutions receiving finance to carry out programmes/activities to achieve the set target. Therefore, the current efforts as part of the financing strategy for climate mitigation and adaptation includes increasing diversification of sources of finance, strengthening capacity of finance institutions, and strengthening capacity of stakeholders in accessing finance.
extraction_rationale: This is a national climate finance strategy with defined institutional and access components.

policy_statement: Indonesia will optimize national climate finance sources, including state budget, green sukuk or green bonds, carbon pricing instruments such as fees and carbon levy, intergovernmental fiscal transfers, PAD, and other income sources.
source_quote: At the national level, the opportunities to optimise state budget are explored (e.g. using instruments of green sukuk or green bonds and draft of PERPRES NEK on Carbon Pricing Instruments such as fees and carbon levy; instruments of intergovernmental fiscal transfer; instruments of PAD and other sources of income). Furthermore, Indonesia continue to mobilise international financial sources through bilateral, regional, and multilateral channels, including result-based payment for REDD+ under the Paris Agreement, grant, and other potential sources and mechanisms.
extraction_rationale: This lists specific financial instruments for climate action, including carbon pricing, bonds, fiscal transfers, grants, and REDD+ payments.

policy_statement: Indonesia will develop an integrated capacity-development approach for LTS-LCCR, including energy workforce transition, mitigation sectors, adaptation, just transition, gender, intergenerational and vulnerable groups, MHA, and local communities.
source_quote: For example, the transition in energy sector which requires transition of the workforce to green jobs will need well- designed capacity development; similarly for other mitigation sectors, adaptation, and for addressing cross cutting issues (incl. just transition, gender, intergeneration and vulnerable groups, MHA and local communities). An integrated approach in capacity development to support the LTS-LCCR will be developed and aligned with capacity development to progress towards Prosperous Indonesia 2045. International support for capacity building under the Paris Agreement and the Convention will continue to be mobilised to support the achievement of the ambitious target under LCCP of LTS-LCCR.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete capacity-development commitment for implementing climate mitigation and adaptation pathways.

policy_statement: During 2021-2030, Indonesia will implement the LTS-LCCR through the Updated NDC and nine NDC Implementation Strategy Programmes, supported by NDC road maps for mitigation, adaptation, and means of implementation.
source_quote: During the period of 2021-2030, implementation of LTS-LCCR will follow the implementation of first NDC (Updated NDC), which is guided by nine NDC Implementation Strategy Programmes as described in Updated NDC document. Presidential Regulation on Carbon Pricing (draft of PERPRES NEK) sets norms for four following main areas: (1) NDC target achievement, (2) carbon economic instrument, (3) transparency framework, and (4) low carbon development. Furthermore, NDC Road Maps (mitigation, adaptation, and means of implementation) provide detail guidance on policy, programme, and actions to achieve 2030 target of the NDC, as well as periodic monitoring and evaluation of the progress and achievement during this period .
extraction_rationale: This is an implementation policy framework with named programmes and roadmaps for the 2030 NDC target.

policy_statement: Indonesia will finalize and use the Presidential Regulation on Carbon Pricing (PERPRES NEK) to regulate NDC target achievement, carbon economic instruments, transparency, low-carbon development, and roles of parties and non-party stakeholders.
source_quote: Presidential Regulation on Carbon Pricing (draft of PERPRES NEK) sets norms for four following main areas: (1) NDC target achievement, (2) carbon economic instrument, (3) transparency framework, and (4) low carbon development. The draft of PERPRES-NEK also regulates the roles of Parties and Non-Party Stakeholders in the NDC implementation. Under this regulation, the NDC will be implemented by national government, sub-national governments (provinces, districts and cities), private sectors, and communities.
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory carbon-pricing framework and carbon economic instrument. It is a financial instrument because it establishes carbon economic instruments.

policy_statement: Post-2030 NDC development and LTS-LCCR implementation will follow LTS-LCCR targets and guidance, including peaking emissions in 2030, a FOLU net sink, and progress toward net-zero emissions by 2060 or sooner.
source_quote: Through ambitious pathway (LCCP) Indonesia will reach peaking in emission in 2030 with net sink in forestry and land use, and with further exploring opportunity to rapidly progress towards net-zero emission by 2060 or sooner. Hence, the implementation of LTS-LCCR post 2030 will follow the implementation of the corresponding NDC. Development of post 2030 NDC shall be in line with the set target and other guidance under LTS-LCCR, taking into account relevant regulatory frameworks and policies.
extraction_rationale: This is a commitment to align future NDCs with the long-term emissions pathway and targets.

policy_statement: Indonesia will continuously improve mechanisms for effective engagement of non-party stakeholders in LTS-LCCR implementation.
source_quote: Effective engagement of non-party stakeholders (NPS) will be a key driver of successful implementation of the LTS-LCCR. Therefore, taking into account relevant regulatory frameworks and policies, the mechanism for enhancing the effectiveness of NPS engagement will be continuously improved.
extraction_rationale: This is an implementation governance policy for stakeholder engagement. It is somewhat process-oriented, but it is anchored to LTS-LCCR implementation.

policy_statement: Indonesia will monitor, review, and update the LTS-LCCR 2050 as necessary based on national circumstances, capacity, capability, and Paris Agreement provisions.
source_quote: The Indonesia's LTS-LCCR 2050 reflects the most recent data and information, analysis, and scenario for possible future in order to contribute the global climate actions in achieving Paris Agreement's goal. As a developing country, Indonesia will likely experience dynamic changes due to national and global changes as well as current COVID-19 pandemic. In this regard, the Indonesia's LTS-LCCR 2050 will be monitored, reviewed and updated, as necessary, taking into consideration national circumstances, capacity and capability, and the provision under the Paris Agreement.
extraction_rationale: This is a monitoring and review commitment for the long-term climate strategy. It is mainly procedural but qualifies because it governs implementation of climate targets.

policy_statement: Reduce non-ETS greenhouse gas emissions by 33% by 2030 compared with 2005 levels.
source_quote: In order to meet the objective of reducing greenhouse gas emissions in the period 2021-2030, equal to -33% in relation to 2005, as provided for by Regulation (EU) 2018/842, Italy will make use of various existing measures as well as new policies which will be introduced. The sectors responsible for greenhouse gas emissions and removals that fall within the scope of application of Regulation (EU) 2018/842 are transport, housing, the services sector, industry not falling within the emissions trading system (ETS) sector, waste, agriculture and the land use, land use change and forestry (LULUCF) sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified national emissions-reduction commitment with a 2030 deadline and identifies covered sectors.

policy_statement: Develop a general strategic circular economy plan identifying intervention areas and high-impact sectors.
source_quote: Given the cross-cutting nature of the circular economy, it is necessary to draw up a general strategic plan that identifies specific areas of intervention and the sectors that have the greatest impact. At the same time, the plan must ensure consistency and synergies with other policies planned.
extraction_rationale: This is a named planning commitment for circular economy action linked to emissions reduction, with sectors specified elsewhere in the paragraph.

parent_statement: General strategic circular economy plan
policy_statement: Extend product service life, promote reuse and repair, lower-carbon materials, material light-weighting, cleaner production, sharing, industrial symbiosis, recycling and end-of-waste status.
source_quote: Some studies have identified the following strategies to that end: extending the service life of products reuse-repair opting for less carbon-intensive materials at production stage reducing materials used and opting for lighter materials improving the production process sharing goods industrial symbiosis recycling and end-of-waste status. By way of example, Ministerial Decree No 62 of 15 May 2019 'Regulation of the end-of-waste status of absorbent hygiene products' sets out the criteria under which various polyolefinbased plastics, super-absorbent polymers and pulp derived from the recovery of absorbent hygiene product waste cease to be classified as waste within the meaning of, and pursuant to, Article 184ter of Legislative Decree No 152 of 3 April 2006.
extraction_rationale: The list contains concrete interventions under the circular economy plan; the end-of-waste decree is a binding regulatory example.

policy_statement: Increase sorted waste collection and recycling to reduce waste-sector emissions.
source_quote: The reduction of emissions in the waste sector is therefore linked primarily to increasing the sorted collection and subsequent recycling of the waste thus collected. In fact, secondary raw materials produced by collecting and transforming waste into new resources allow saving on emissions in a consistent way in relation to the use of raw material.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific waste-management intervention explicitly tied to emissions reduction.

policy_statement: Expand organic waste collection and local aerobic/anaerobic processing into compost and fertiliser.
source_quote: As regards the organic fraction of sorted collection, the subsequent aerobic/anaerobic processing for compost production enables the transformation into fertiliser rich in organic material of waste that would otherwise be disposed of in landfill, with consequent emission of methane into the atmosphere. In the future, sorted collection of organic waste is expected to increase.
extraction_rationale: The policy names a specific intervention—organic waste collection and processing—and explicitly links it to avoided methane.

policy_statement: Implement the EU waste package to increase collection and recycling and reduce landfilling.
source_quote: As regards the future, the approval of the 'waste package' will establish the need to further increase national performance in terms of collecting and recycling waste, concurrently reducing the quantities of waste disposed of in landfill. The new legislation that is being prepared for transposition of the 'waste package' provides important measures in terms of competences, responsibilities and incentives in order to fully implement the new objectives.
extraction_rationale: This is a planned legislative transposition with defined waste-reduction and recycling outcomes.

policy_statement: Provide €40 million in non-repayable contributions from 2019 to 2024 for trial 'green corners' selling loose or draught products.
