source_quote: Law No 141 of 12 December 2019 introduced the following measures: in order to reduce the production of waste and GHGs, a non-repayable economic contribution of €40 million for 2019-2024 has been allocated for the trial of 'green corners' in city shops; here loose or on-draught products are sold, starting with smaller establishments with a view to eventually opening entirely 'green' shops. to limit the production of plastic waste, an experimental programme called ' mangiaplastica ' is planned.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete funded grant-like measure with an emissions and waste objective.

policy_statement: Allocate €27 million from 2019 to 2024 for 'mangiaplastica' plastic bottle collection machines in municipalities and supermarkets.
source_quote: to limit the production of plastic waste, an experimental programme called ' mangiaplastica ' is planned. A total of €27 million has been allocated for 2019-2024 to provide municipalities and supermarkets, on demand, with 'plastic-eating' machines in which consumers can dispose of their used plastic bottles in exchange for a voucher;
extraction_rationale: This is a named, funded waste-reduction programme with specified recipients and timeframe.

policy_statement: Grant tax credits for packaging reuse/recycling and for purchases of recycled-content products and quality compost.
source_quote: The Legislative Decree on Growth has set out provisions on waste and packaging. A business selling a certain commodity can give the buyer a voucher to redeem against the price of future purchases. The seller re-using the packaging, or sorting it to be sent for recycling, receives a tax credit equal to double the amount granted to the purchaser as a voucher.
extraction_rationale: This is a fiscal instrument to incentivise reuse, recycling, and circular material use.

policy_statement: Phase out coal-fired electricity generation by 2025 while implementing infrastructure measures for system security.
source_quote: Italy has planned gradual termination of production of electricity with carbon by 2025, with the first significant step by 2023, compensated, in addition to the sharp increase in renewable energy, by a plan for changing infrastructures (to flexible generation, networks and storage systems) to be carried out in the coming years. The implementation of these two processes in parallel is vital to ensure that the result is achieved in safe conditions for the energy system.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified deadline-based mitigation policy with dependent infrastructure sub-actions.

parent_statement: Coal phase-out by 2025
policy_statement: Install new gas capacity, storage systems, transmission reinforcements, synchronous condensers and Sardinia-specific interconnection or storage measures to enable coal phase-out.
source_quote: In fact, without prejudice to the need to accelerate growth of renewable energies, in the context of the overall measures (storage, networks, flexible generation, other network operations) to be implemented by the target year 2030, some infrastructure changes are linked in particular to the phasing out of carbon and, in particular, are to be launched in the period 2020-2025: new gas capacity for around 3 GW, of which around 50% is substantially linked to the phase-out, in line with regional planning and regulations (on landscape and the environment), and new storage systems for 3 GW in the centre south and south zones, and in Sicily; the reinforcement of the transmission network in the Brindisi plant to ensure operational safety. for the phasing-out of coal in Sardinia, a new electricity interconnection between Sardinia, Sicily and the continent is being looked into, along with new capacity for gas generation or storage capacity of 400 MW located on the island and the installation of condensers for at least 250 MVAR.
extraction_rationale: The source lists specific infrastructure interventions tied to implementing the coal phase-out; gas capacity is transitional but part of the stated decarbonisation pathway.

policy_statement: Apply the 2017 Po Basin Agreement measures to reduce agricultural and animal-husbandry emissions, including manure storage coverage and correct manure spreading.
source_quote: The Po Basin Agreement 2017 identifies joint measures and actions to combat emissions, including greenhouse emissions and fine particles. Regarding measures in the agricultural and animal husbandry sectors, the Italian Regions must, as part of the air quality plans, apply practices aimed at the reduction of emissions produced by agricultural activity, including coverage of structures for storing sewage, using the correct methods for spreading of manure and the burial of soil surfaces used to apply fertilisers, where these practices are technically feasible and economically sustainable.
extraction_rationale: This is a binding regional implementation commitment with named agricultural emissions-control measures.

policy_statement: Adopt a national code of good agricultural practices to control ammonia emissions.
source_quote: The code, which will become part of the national programme for controlling atmospheric pollution, takes account of the following factors for reducing ammonia emissions: nitrogen management, taking into account the whole nitrogen cycle; livestock feeding strategies; low-emission manure storage and spreading techniques; low-emission animal housing systems; possibilities for limiting ammonia emissions from the use of mineral fertilisers. The code provides mandatory measures for mitigating and reducing ammonia by means of: different use of fertilisers; techniques for spreading manure and storage.
extraction_rationale: This is a named code with mandatory measures to reduce agricultural emissions; ammonia is an air pollutant but also linked to climate and agricultural emissions policy.

policy_statement: Use CAP 2021-2027 instruments to strengthen environmental conditionality, ecological regimes, and payments for environmental and climate commitments.
source_quote: The measures indicated in the aforementioned national code are reflected in terms of both budget and application in the instruments of the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP), which, in comparison to the 2014-2020 CAP, places greater focus on improving the environment. These measures will be viable in the period 2021-2027 and provide for: reinforcement of the cross-compliance that will involve direct payments subject to more rigorous environmental requirements; the obligation of Member States to introduce ecological regimes that have a positive impact on climate and the environment.
extraction_rationale: This is an economic and regulatory agricultural policy package with explicit climate/environment conditions and a 2021-2027 timeframe.

policy_statement: Assess and promote CO2 sequestration measures in agricultural soils and forest systems, including payments for ecosystem services.
source_quote: With due consideration for the outcome of the public consultation, an assessment will be made of potential measures to promote initiatives aimed at CO2 sequestration in agricultural soils and forest systems (soils, subterranean and above-ground biomass, wood, etc.). This will also take into account potential payment measures for ecosystem services for forestry and those linked to agricultural soils and to herbaceous (arable, etc.) and arboreal farming systems.
extraction_rationale: This is somewhat tentative but qualifies because it identifies a specific sequestration intervention and potential payment mechanism.

policy_statement: Prepare an Annual Report on Italian Forests consolidating updated data on forest natural, productive and economic aspects.
source_quote: The report foresees consolidation of up-to-date understanding of Italian forests in every aspect: natural, productive, economic, etc. Collection of information from all of the stakeholders involved is also envisaged, including the Regions, regional bodies, ISTAT, and the economic and scientific sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a named planning/monitoring measure for forest-sector climate accounting and policy implementation.

policy_statement: Implement the Consolidated Law on Forests and Forest Supply Chains to support sustainable forest management and increase carbon absorption.
source_quote: The TUFF provides advice and guidelines to support regional administrations in relation to forestry management. The TUFF updates the coordination arrangements and the national guidelines in relation to Sustainable Forestry Management and development of forestry supply chains. With this measure, the goal is to recognise Sustainable Forestry Management as a tool aimed at ensuring an increase in carbon absorption, including in the production of quality timber products.
extraction_rationale: This is a binding law and implementing decree framework explicitly aimed at carbon absorption via forests.

policy_statement: Develop the National Forestry Strategy through the White Paper on Italian forests to guide climate mitigation and adaptation commitments.
source_quote: In order to support the process of drafting a new national forestry strategy, the white paper on the forests of Italy has been published and is open for consultation, with the aim of providing support to the establishment of the new National Forestry Strategy (NFS). The goal is to contribute to making the new NFS consistent and effective in fulfilling the needs of the forestry sector, consistent with European recommendations and international commitments in relation to mitigation of and adapting to climate change, in order to guarantee stability and well-being for present and future generations.
extraction_rationale: This is a named forestry strategy process explicitly linked to mitigation and adaptation; still in consultation, but with a concrete strategic output.

policy_statement: Implement Directive (EU) 2016/2284 through national air pollution control programmes, emissions inventories, projections and ecosystem impact monitoring.
source_quote: Italian Legislative Decree No 81/2018, transposing Directive (EU) No 2016/2284, provides for the reduction of certain atmospheric pollutants (sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides, nonmethane volatile organic compounds, ammonia and fine particulate matter) by means of: the drawing up, adopting and implementing of national air pollution control programmes in conjunction with policies adopted in relation to climate change; the creation of a national emissions inventory and national emission projections; monitoring of emissions not subject to a requirement for reduction; monitoring of the impacts on ecosystems.
extraction_rationale: This is a binding decree and programme requirement that integrates air pollution and climate policy.

policy_statement: Certify solid biomass heat generators based on environmental and emissions performance standards.
source_quote: The Decree establishes the requirements, procedures and responsibilities for issuing an environmental certificate for heat generators powered by firewood, charcoal and combustible biomass. The Decree identifies, additionally, the emission performance standards for different quality classes, the related test methods and checks to be carried out for the purposes of issuing the environmental certification, and specific obligations relating to guidance to be provided about the correct methods of installation and management of heat generators which have obtained the environmental certificate.
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory certification standard for biomass heating systems with emissions performance requirements.

policy_statement: Implement Regulation (EU) No 517/2014 by certifying F-gas operators and creating a database for F-gas sales and equipment operations.
source_quote: In order to reduce emissions of fluorinated greenhouse gases that occur during operations for the installation, maintenance, repair and dismantling of equipment that contain these gases, the new Italian Presidential Decree adopted in November 2018 provides for the adaptation of the certification system for natural persons and for companies that carry out these operations, and the establishment of a 'database' for the collection and retention of information relating to sales of fluorinated greenhouse gases and of equipment containing these gases, as well as all of the registrations relating to operations for the installation, maintenance, repair and dismantling of such equipment.
extraction_rationale: This is a binding regulatory measure targeting fluorinated greenhouse gas emissions.

policy_statement: Use the Environmental Code to reduce greenhouse gas emissions through environmental assessment, soil and water protection, waste management, air pollution controls and damage compensation.
source_quote: The Environmental Code represents a tool, already active today on a national level, which contributes to reducing greenhouse gas emissions by means of: implementation of procedures for Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA), for Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) and for Integrated Environmental Authorisation (IPPC); providing of soil conservation measures and combating desertification, protecting water from pollutants and digestion of water resources; management of waste and remediation of contaminated sites; air pollution prevention and reduction of emissions into the atmosphere; compensation for environmental damage.
extraction_rationale: This is an existing regulatory framework with multiple binding environmental mechanisms relevant to emissions reduction.

policy_statement: Create an Energy Transition Fund for industry using EU ETS auction revenue to fund decarbonisation and energy efficiency measures.
source_quote: Decree-Law No 101 of 3 September 2019 established the 'Fund for energy transition in the industrial sector' to support energy transition in sectors or sub-sectors that are considered to be at a high risk of re-localisation of carbon emissions owing to costs linked to greenhouse gas emissions being transferred onto the price of electricity. The fund is constituted by that part of the annual revenue deriving from EU ETS auctions that exceeds 1,000 million. This excess amount, up to a maximum of €100 million per year for 2020 and €150 million as of 2021, will be used to fund decarbonisation and energy efficiency measures in the industrial sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a named fund with revenue source, annual caps and explicit decarbonisation and efficiency uses.

policy_statement: Implement the Action Plan for Improving Air Quality with measures in agriculture, mobility, domestic heating, coal phase-out and subsidy reduction.
source_quote: In June 2019 the 'Action plan for improving air quality' was launched. Signed by the Prime Minister's Office, six Ministries, and the Regions and Autonomous Provinces, the plan contains measures on transport, agriculture and biomass-fuelled domestic heating, the sectors most responsible for the current high levels of pollution. The plan covers two years and contains measures targeting both air quality and decarbonisation.
section_header: Possible effects of the plan on air quality
extraction_rationale: This is a named two-year plan with specified sectors and decarbonisation relevance; it has listed sub-measures.

parent_statement: Action plan for improving air quality
policy_statement: Link rural development funding in 2021-2027 to ammonia emissions reduction and limit burning of plant residues.
source_quote: Agriculture, with measures for reducing ammonia emissions and limiting the burning of plant residues. Specifically: in the framework of future rural development programmes, forms of funding will be linked to ammonia emissions reduction, in order to guarantee, for the 2021-2027 programming period, an increased use of such measures among farmers, with a concurrent reduction in polluting emissions; amendment of Legislative Decree No 152/2006, which is intended to limit the practice of burning plant residues, also with a view to recovering and utilising those residues.
section_header: Possible effects of the plan on air quality
extraction_rationale: This is a funded and regulatory agriculture measure under the air quality plan; climate relevance is through emissions reduction.

parent_statement: Action plan for improving air quality
policy_statement: Introduce mobility measures including environmental criteria for non-urban traffic, limited traffic zone monitoring, hybrid vehicle guidelines, electric personal mobility trials, bonus/malus criteria and active mobility guidance.
source_quote: Mobility, with the introduction of environmental criteria for non-urban traffic, limited to sections of motorway adjacent to urban centres and within the scope of limited traffic zones, with disincentives for the use of highly polluting vehicles. Specifically: proposed amendment of Legislative Decree No 285 of 30 April 1992, designed to introduce environmental criteria for the adoption of traffic reduction provisions, limited to sections of motorway adjacent to urban centres and with particular reference to speed limits; proposed amendment of the existing legislation in order to explicitly provide for the possibility of using devices to monitor limited traffic zones, including within those areas and not only at 'gateway' points.
section_header: Possible effects of the plan on air quality
extraction_rationale: The quoted plan lists specific traffic and mobility regulatory interventions targeting pollution and decarbonisation.

parent_statement: Action plan for improving air quality
policy_statement: Reduce domestic biomass heating emissions by conditioning incentives on certified solid biofuels, traceability and sustainability criteria, and assessing limits on biomass district heating in polluted areas.
source_quote: Domestic heating, with measures to reduce polluting emissions from biomass-fuelled stoves and heaters and to limit the use of gasoil-fired heaters, and to promote the training of installers of renewable energy-fuelled heaters. Regarding the measures designed to reduce pollution from biomass fuel, the following specific measures are envisaged. Updates to the sectoral legislation to makes incentives to replace heaters fuelled by firewood, briquettes and wood chips conditional upon the certification of such solid biofuels, by the relevant bodies, as complying with the relevant technical standards.
section_header: Possible effects of the plan on air quality
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete regulatory and incentive-conditioning measure for heating equipment and fuel standards.

policy_statement: Implement the Climate Decree through sustainable mobility, reforestation, environmental zones, Green Italy, and sustainable development governance measures.
source_quote: The Decree provides for the creation of a national strategic plan identifying urgent measures to combat climate change and correctly and fully implement Directive 2008/50/EC. In line with the European 'Green New Deal', this new planning approach targets both climate change and air pollution in parallel, with the aim of fostering maximum synergy between the two sectors.
section_header: Possible effects of the plan on air quality
extraction_rationale: The Climate Decree is a binding legal framework with multiple listed climate-related sub-measures.

parent_statement: Climate Decree
policy_statement: Establish the Experimental Mobility Voucher Programme with funding from 2019 to 2024 for scrapping polluting vehicles and buying public transport passes or bicycles.
source_quote: Incentives for sustainable mobility in metropolitan areas, setting up a special fund called the 'Experimental Mobility Voucher Programme', with an allocation of €5 million for 2019, €70 million for 2020, €70 million for 2021, €55 million for 2022, €45 million for 2023 and €10 million for 2024. establishing a 'Mobility Voucher' for residents of the municipalities subject to EU infringement proceedings No 2147/2014 of 10 July 2014 and No 2043/2015 of 28 May 2015 for non-compliance of Italy with the obligations set out in Directive 2008/50/EC, who take for scrapping, by 31 December 2021, type-approved passenger vehicles up to Euro Class 3, or type-approved motorcycles up to Euro Class 2 and Euro Class 3 two-stroke motorcycles;
section_header: Possible effects of the plan on air quality
extraction_rationale: This is a named funded incentive programme with specified amounts, eligible actions and deadline.

parent_statement: Climate Decree
policy_statement: Fund hybrid or electric sustainable school transport programmes with €10 million per year for 2020 and 2021.
source_quote: introducing measures to promote 'Sustainable school transport', with €10 million earmarked for each of the years 2020 and 2021 to fund experimental programmes to set up and run a school transport service for children attending state and municipal infant schools and for pupils in their first cycle of state school, using hybrid or electric means of transport, selected by the Ministry of the Environment on the basis of the number of students involved and the estimated reduction in air pollution;
section_header: Possible effects of the plan on air quality
extraction_rationale: This is a funded sustainable transport intervention with specified vehicle types and target users.

parent_statement: Climate Decree
policy_statement: Allocate €15 million per year in 2020 and 2021 for tree planting, replanting, forestry and urban/suburban forests in metropolitan cities.
source_quote: reforestation measures, with a grant of €15 million for each of the years 2020 and 2021 for an experimental programme for tree planting, replanting and forestry and the creation of urban and suburban forests in metropolitan cities;
section_header: Possible effects of the plan on air quality
extraction_rationale: This is a funded nature-based measure with a concrete activity and timeframe.

parent_statement: Climate Decree
policy_statement: Create Economic Environmental Zones in national parks to support businesses reducing greenhouse gas emissions, renewable energy and energy efficiency.
source_quote: establishing Economic Environmental Zones (ZEAs) in areas within national parks. In such areas forms of support can be set up, in compliance with EU rules on State aid, for new and existing businesses that launch a programme of economic or investment activity aimed in particular at reducing greenhouse gas emissions and promoting renewable energy and energy efficiency.
section_header: Possible effects of the plan on air quality
extraction_rationale: This is a named economic support instrument with explicit GHG, renewable energy and efficiency objectives.

policy_statement: Pursue a 30% renewable energy share in gross final energy consumption by 2030.
source_quote: Italy plans to pursue the target of obtaining 30% of gross final consumption of energy from renewable sources in 2030 by defining a pathway of sustainable growth for renewable sources and the full integration thereof into the system. In particular, the target for 2030 projects a gross final consumption of energy of 111 Mtoe, with approximately 33 Mtoe of that coming from renewable sources.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified national renewable energy target for 2030.

policy_statement: Achieve a 55% renewable electricity share, 33.9% renewable heating share and 22% renewable transport share by 2030.
source_quote: Without prejudice to the statement made at the end of section i. above (which applies to all of the following information, including section iii.), the contribution of renewables to meet total gross final consumption by 2030 (30%) is expected to have the following distribution between the different sectors: 55.0% renewables share in the electricity sector; 33.9% renewables share in the heating sector (for heating and cooling); 22.0% with regard to the incorporation of renewables in the transport sector (calculated using the target accounting criteria established by RED II).
extraction_rationale: This establishes quantified sectoral renewable energy targets for 2030.

policy_statement: Support self-consumption through tariff rules, net metering evolution, renewable obligations in buildings and minimum quota extensions.
source_quote: The rules governing the collection of general system charges and electricity tariffs, introduced in 2018 as part of the plan for adaptation to EU guidelines on State aid for energy and the environment, provide, in themselves, a regulatory framework that favours instantaneous self-consumption. Work will also be carried out on development of the net metering mechanism (which enables the use of the network as a storage system), to promote rewards for plants on the basis of their quota of self-consumed energy, which can also be increased by installing accumulation systems, and for plants which go on to provide services to ensure the safety of the electricity system on medium- and low-voltage networks.
extraction_rationale: This is a set of regulatory and economic measures to expand renewable self-consumption.

parent_statement: Energy plants for individual and collective self-consumption
policy_statement: Strengthen minimum renewable-source quota obligations in new buildings and major renovations and gradually extend renewable quota obligations to existing buildings.
source_quote: Further instruments to support self-consumption, both individual and collective, will be: reinforcing minimum quota obligations for renewable energy sources in new buildings or buildings subject to major renovation, in line with the targets for near-zero emissions buildings; progressive and gradual extension of the minimum quota obligation for renewable energy sources (which, as mentioned, is currently envisaged only for new buildings or buildings subject to major renovation) to existing buildings, starting with several categories such as warehouses used for manufacturing activities and service sector buildings.
extraction_rationale: This is a binding-style building obligation to integrate renewable energy.

policy_statement: Introduce simplified and homogeneous procedures for small renewable plants, including a uniform model and expanded simplified authorisation procedure.
source_quote: To introduce simplified and homogeneous procedures for the construction, commissioning and management of plants, including expanding the scope of the uniform model, currently operative for certain photovoltaic installations with power up to 20 kW: it involves a mechanism which allows, with a single procedure, management of features relating to authorisation, network connection and accessing support mechanisms. In line with the outcome of the public consultation, there are plans to extend the use of the Simplified Authorisation Procedure (SAP), which today can be used for individual plants with power between a few dozen and several hundreds of kW;
section_header: Other measures for small-scale energy plants
extraction_rationale: This is an administrative/regulatory streamlining measure for renewable deployment.

policy_statement: Promote photovoltaic installations on agricultural structures and reward PV plants replacing asbestos-containing roofs.
source_quote: To promote the installation of photovoltaic plants in existing agricultural structures that do not fall within the definition of a building, including by introducing the concept of 'rural building' to facilitate access to support measures. introduce rewards for construction of photovoltaic plants where the modules are installed as replacements for roofing containing asbestos.
section_header: Other measures for small-scale energy plants
extraction_rationale: This combines a specific renewable deployment intervention with an incentive reward; climate relevance is renewable generation.

policy_statement: Promote renewable energy communities through economic support for production and locally consumed energy, information and standard tools.
source_quote: Renewable energy communities will be promoted in economic terms by means of direct support mechanisms for production, including by more than one plant (similarly to the general production support mechanisms) and for locally consumed energy. Renewable energy communities will also be promoted through information on locally available resources (also making use of the procedure for identifying suitable local areas, as mentioned below) and on the opportunities offered by support mechanisms.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific programme to support community renewable production and consumption.

policy_statement: Use competitive tenders and contracts for difference to support large-scale renewable energy plants, including RES1 auctions and registers.
source_quote: We will continue to employ the mechanisms of competitive tender, which have already been trialled, adopting a neutral approach among groups of technologies with similar structure and levels of cost, possibly with safeguarding mechanisms where technologies deemed necessary to reach targets in any event are repeatedly unsuccessful, it being understood that one of the aims of this mechanism is to support market parity. The tenders will be for the purpose of entering into contracts for difference based on the overall value of the recognised tariff once the procedure has been carried out, according to the 'two way' criteria.
section_header: Large-scale energy plants (typically with power above 1MW): regulatory and economic measures
extraction_rationale: This is an economic support mechanism for renewable electricity deployment with a defined tender and contract structure.

policy_statement: Promote long-term renewable power purchase agreements through a market platform, reference nomenclature and removal of barriers.
source_quote: Italy intends to widely promote use of this tool, alongside contracts for difference, with regulations that encourage investors to enter into Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) with parties interested in purchasing the energy that the plant will produce over a period of time long enough to guarantee the return on the investment necessary to construct a production plant, or to renovate or improve an existing plant. The Ministerial Decree of 4 July 2019 provides that a regulatory framework for the creation of a market platform for long-term trading be set up within 180 days of its entry into force.
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory and market-development measure for renewable energy investment.

policy_statement: Share renewable targets with Regions and identify areas suitable and unsuitable for renewable energy plants through agreed criteria and mapping.
source_quote: The renewables targets, especially in the electricity sector, will be met chiefly through wind and photovoltaic energy. Adequate land surface will therefore be needed. While in the photovoltaic sector existing buildings and compromised areas not suitable for other uses will be exploited, national objectives will be shared and agreed with the Regions under a national regulatory framework.
section_header: Common measures for large- and small-scale energy plants
extraction_rationale: This is a land-use and permitting planning measure for renewable deployment; it has specific target-sharing and area-identification mechanisms.

policy_statement: Support innovative renewable technologies through RES2 auctions/registers and possible investment contributions, including offshore wind, geothermal, biomass, biogas and marine energy reconversion projects.
source_quote: For technologies which are still far from being economically competitive in Italy, or which have significant potential for innovation, procedures based on their specific characteristics will be implemented. The use of tariff instruments will be assessed by taking into account the state of development, the capacity for cost reduction, the exploitable potential, the possible contribution to reaching the target, compatibility with limiting the amounts due in bills, improvement of environmental performance and concurrence with other targets. In this context a provision to support these technologies (RES2) is being drafted.
section_header: Common measures for large- and small-scale energy plants
extraction_rationale: This is a planned support mechanism for specified innovative renewable technologies.

policy_statement: Use smaller islands as test projects for high renewable penetration, network modernisation, storage, electric transport and system integration.
source_quote: Italy has already started a process for the gradual coverage of the requirements of smaller islands not interlinked with energy from renewable sources. In this context, the Ministerial Decree of 14 July 2017 sets out specific targets for covering consumption with renewable energy sources, available locally for each island.
section_header: Common measures for large- and small-scale energy plants
extraction_rationale: This is a named place-based pilot approach with specific renewable targets and listed sub-actions.

parent_statement: Smaller islands as test projects for higher levels of penetration of renewables and electrification of consumption
policy_statement: Modernise island electricity networks and implement pilots using storage, electric transport, water-system integration and scalable demand.
source_quote: The aim is to promote, for each island: modernisation of electricity networks to allow in more renewables; implementation of pilot projects designed to increase the use of renewables by using storage systems, developing electric transport, integrating the electricity system with the island water systems and with the scalable demand on the island. The public call for projects is being finalised and will allow experimentation with innovative technological solutions that could potentially be used in the national energy system.
section_header: Common measures for large- and small-scale energy plants
extraction_rationale: This is a set of concrete pilot interventions for islands, directly supporting renewable penetration and electrification.

policy_statement: Simplify revamping, repowering and reconversion of existing renewable plants, including environmental screening simplification and performance information.
source_quote: The specific measures of a non-economic nature for revamping and repowering existing installations include the following. SAPs, setting criteria that enable actions to be taken to extend them and exclude or simplify EIA/environmental screening. In particular, for assessments of an environmental nature, an approach will be favoured which essentially evaluates the variations of the impact in relation to the situation prior to the revamping or repowering;
section_header: Specific measures for safeguarding and improving existing plants
extraction_rationale: This is an administrative simplification measure to preserve and increase renewable generation.

policy_statement: Grant incentives to existing agricultural biogas plants that meet sustainability, manure-use and programmability requirements.
source_quote: To that end, the Budget Law for 2020 envisages the right to use an incentive on electricity produced. This applies to existing biogas-powered plants that started operating before 31 December 2017 and were built by agricultural entrepreneurs acting singly or in groups who do not benefit from other public incentives on electricity production. The incentive must comply with the sustainability criteria set out in Directive (EU) 2018/2001.
section_header: Specific measures for safeguarding and improving existing plants
extraction_rationale: This is a fiscal/economic incentive for renewable biogas generation with eligibility criteria.

policy_statement: Reform large hydroelectric concessions to require minimum energy improvements and environmental rehabilitation.
source_quote: Law No 12 of 11 February 2019 converting Decree-Law No 135 of 14 December 2018 gives the Regions authority in the area of existing large concessions. The Law provides, among other things, that where there is no overriding public interest in another use of the waters that is incompatible with their use for hydroelectric purposes, the Regions can grant concessions for large-scale diversions of water for such purposes to qualified operators on the basis of certain criteria. These include a) minimum improvements in terms of energy, production power and production potential to be achieved from the diversion, conveyance, regulation and supply of water and from the installations for generating, transforming and connecting electricity.
section_header: Specific measures for safeguarding and improving existing plants
extraction_rationale: This is a binding concessions reform with renewable energy performance and environmental conditions.

policy_statement: Maintain mandatory biofuel release for consumption through quotas up to 2022, including bonuses for advanced biofuels and biofuels from waste oils and animal fats.
source_quote: Mandatory release of biofuels for consumption, based on a share system in which, inter alia , a bonus is recognised for advanced biofuels and biofuels from waste oils and animal fats. In this respect, it is important to adopt measures that are consistent Europe-wide, promoting the supply chain of energy based on biomethane, biofuels from waste oils and category 1 and 2 animal fats, safeguarding investments by biodiesel industries and further stimulating research and creation of innovative solutions.
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory biofuel quota obligation with defined fuel categories.

policy_statement: Require a 6% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions from fuels by 2020.
source_quote: In 2020, fuel suppliers will have to meet a savings target, in terms of GHG emissions in the total fuels released for consumption in that year, in relation to a reference value.
extraction_rationale: This is a binding quantified fuel-emissions target for suppliers.

policy_statement: Incentivise biomethane and advanced biofuels for 2018-2022, targeting around 1.1 billion cubic metres per year of biomethane demand in road transport.
source_quote: Incentives to use biomethane and advanced biofuels for the purposes of meeting the existing obligation to mix fossil fuels with biofuels, through a system of collecting the biomethane produced, with issuing of certificates of release for consumption for a duration of ten years. The cost of the incentive is borne by the obligated parties (oil companies that release fossil fuels for consumption) and does not impact electricity and gas bills. It is envisaged that this incentivisation system will cover the predicted demand for methane in road transport with biomethane, corresponding to around 1.1 billion cubic metres a year.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific certificate-based incentive mechanism for advanced renewable fuels with a quantified biomethane expectation.

policy_statement: Transpose RED II by updating renewable fuel quotas to 2030, including advanced biofuels, renewable hydrogen and recycled-carbon fuels.
source_quote: The drafting and issuing of an Italian Legislative Decree transposing RED II and subsequent interministerial decrees updating the decrees currently in force in the sector are planned. The main objectives are: updating the mandatory quotas for release for consumption of normal and advanced biofuels up to 2030; introducing differentiated targets for petrol, diesel and possibly methane; adding hydrogen from renewable sources and possibly fuels from recycled carbon to the list of biofuels and fuels that can be used for the purpose of meeting the quotas;
extraction_rationale: This is a planned legal transposition with explicit mandatory quotas and eligible fuels.

policy_statement: Promote electric mobility to reach about 4 million all-electric cars and 6 million electric and plug-in hybrid cars by 2030.
source_quote: Electricity from RES in the road transport sector: a gradual increase is expected, from year to year, in new registrations of electric cars as well, in order to reach the cumulative target of around 4 million electric cars or electric vehicles by 2030, which, if added to plug-in hybrid cars, would reach a total of approximately 6 million electric cars 2030. Projections for the development of electric transport are linked to the expected technological improvements in batteries and will therefore be constantly monitored as part of periodic updates.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified electric vehicle deployment target tied to renewable electricity in transport.

policy_statement: Promote renewable hydrogen production and use in transport, including direct use in vehicles and injection into the gas network.
source_quote: Non-organic renewable fuels: the contribution of hydrogen in 2030 is realistically expected to be around 1% of the RES transport target, through direct use in hydrogen cars and buses as well as trains (for some non-electrified lines) or through the introduction of methane into the network, in that, within certain mixing thresholds (some studies indicate 515%) it is possible to exploit existing infrastructures without taking any special measures. Through research, development and demonstration, the production and use of hydrogen produced from renewable electricity will be promoted, as it offers the dual advantage of reducing fuel emissions and emissions from other refining products.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific renewable-fuel technology policy for hydrogen with explicit emissions rationale.

policy_statement: Promote renewable heat and energy efficiency through tax deductions, Conto Termico, white certificates, renewable building obligations, and municipal grants.
source_quote: The principal instruments that are expected to be used to promote the use of thermal renewable energy sources are often integrated with those for energy efficiency and are already operational. These are: tax deductions for energy efficiency measures and restoration of existing buildings, both also intended for thermal renewables; 'Conto Termico' (Thermal energy account); White Certificates system, including promotion of high efficiency cogeneration; mandatory integration of energy from renewable sources in buildings; contributions to municipalities towards investment in the field of energy efficiency and sustainable local development.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella package of operational instruments for thermal renewables and efficiency.

parent_statement: Thermal renewable energy support instruments
policy_statement: Use tax deductions to support solar thermal, heat pumps, geothermal installations, and biomass systems in buildings.
source_quote: Tax deductions for energy-efficient retrofitting of buildings are currently in place and have played a vital role in the development of energy efficiency and of thermal renewable energy sources in the housing sector. For thermal renewables, the fitting of solar thermal installations, heat pumps, geothermal installations in buildings, replacing existing winter heating systems, and biomass installations is made easier.
extraction_rationale: This is a fiscal incentive for specified renewable heat technologies in buildings.

parent_statement: Thermal renewable energy support instruments
policy_statement: Use Conto Termico incentives for heat pumps, biomass heat generators, solar thermal systems, heat pump water heaters and hybrid heat pump systems.
source_quote: With Italian Ministerial Decree of 28 December 2012, the Conto Termico was introduced, an incentive for promoting the production of renewable thermal energy and, at the same time, to permit access by public sector bodies to energy-efficient building works and installations. In relation to production of heat from renewable sources, one or more interventions, listed below, carried out by public authorities and by private individuals, are incentivised:
extraction_rationale: This is a named incentive scheme for renewable heat and efficiency, with eligible interventions listed immediately after the quote.

parent_statement: Thermal renewable energy support instruments
policy_statement: Require renewable energy integration in new buildings and major renovations, including 50% domestic hot water coverage and rising heating/cooling shares.
source_quote: Annex 3 of Legislative Decree No 28 of 2011, transposing the RED Directive, identifies obligations to integrate energy from renewable sources in new buildings or in buildings subject to major renovation, in force from 31 May 2012. The requirements are currently fixed in terms of percentages (increasing per year) of coverage with renewable energy sources of the building's energy requirement for providing heating, cooling and domestic hot water services.
extraction_rationale: This is a binding building requirement with quantified renewable coverage obligations.

parent_statement: Thermal renewable energy support instruments
policy_statement: Provide municipal contributions for energy efficiency, public lighting, renewable plants, sustainable mobility, school/public building safety, and barrier removal.
source_quote: Decree-Law No 34 of 30 April 2019 (the Growth Decree-Law) established a contribution for municipalities, up to a maximum of €500 million for 2019, drawn from the Development and Cohesion Fund (FSC), to be channelled into investment in energy efficiency and sustainable local development. The contributions are to be used for public works in the areas of: increasing energy efficiency, including public lighting, energy saving in publicly owned buildings and public housing, and the installation of energy production plants fuelled by renewable sources; sustainable local development, including measures for sustainable mobility, upgrading and safety assurance in schools, public buildings and municipal property, and removing architectural barriers;
extraction_rationale: This is a public investment/grant line with specified eligible climate and efficiency uses.

policy_statement: Pursue 2030 energy efficiency reductions of 43% in primary energy consumption and 39.7% in final energy consumption compared with PRIMES 2007.
source_quote: Italy intends to pursue an indicative reduction target for 2030 of 43% for primary energy consumption and of 39.7% for final energy consumption, with respect to the reference PRIMES 2007 scenario. By contrast, with regard to the absolute level of energy consumption for 2030, Italy is pursuing a target of 125.1 Mtoe of primary energy and 103.8 Mtoe of final energy, following the trajectory indicated in the following figure, starting with the estimated consumption for 2020.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified national energy efficiency target for 2030.

policy_statement: Achieve at least 51.4 Mtoe of cumulative final energy savings in 2021-2030 through obligation schemes and alternative measures.
source_quote: In order to achieve the minimum cumulative end-use energy saving to be attained in the period 2021-2030 within the meaning of Article 7 of the EED, confirmed at 51.4 Mtoe, compared with 50.98 Mtoe calculated on the basis of average end-use energy consumption in 2016-2018, Italy will use the set of requirements based on White Certificates and a set of alternative measures that are already in place, to be revised and strengthened in the next few years in order to reach the targets set.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified cumulative savings target and identifies policy instruments.

policy_statement: Use White Certificates, tax deductions, Conto Termico, the National Fund, Industry 4.0, PREPAC, cohesion policies, information programmes and transport measures to deliver energy savings.
source_quote: In particular, the instruments in place expressly dedicated to the promotion of energy efficiency and monitored for the purposes of achieving the savings target pursuant to Article 7 of the EED are the following: the White Certificates scheme; tax deductions for energy-efficient measures and restoration of existing buildings; the 'Conto Termico'; The National Fund for Energy Efficiency; Industry 4.0 programme for upgrading the energy efficiency of central government buildings (PREPAC); programme of energy efficiency measures under the cohesion policies 2021-2027; national energy efficiency information and training plan (PIF).
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella package of named instruments for the 2030 efficiency target with sub-instruments listed.

parent_statement: Energy efficiency instruments under Article 7 EED
policy_statement: Reform and strengthen the White Certificates scheme to simplify procedures, improve savings quantification and broaden eligible sectors and behavioural measures.
source_quote: The process for updating and reinforcing the White Certificates will be continued with a view to simplifying the scheme and optimising the methodologies for quantifying and recognising energy savings, and reducing the time frames for approval, issuance and supply of certificates on the market. The possibility of implementing a radical reform of the scheme is being examined.
extraction_rationale: This is a named tradable certificate obligation scheme reform for energy efficiency.

parent_statement: Energy efficiency instruments under Article 7 EED
policy_statement: Integrate Ecobonus, Sismabonus and Bonus Casa into a single scalable tax deduction mechanism rewarding cost-effective deep renovations.
source_quote: A tax deduction scheme for the energy-efficient retrofitting and restoration of existing buildings, to run for three years, is currently being assessed. In order to strengthen the measure, maximise results and optimise resources, the plan is to integrate the Ecobonus, Sismabonus and Bonus Casa schemes into a single mechanism. The scheme will provide a benefit scalable in relation to the expected saving, based on the total technical life of the measure, for works to improve buildings' energy performance.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific fiscal measure for building energy renovation with an explicit design change.

parent_statement: Energy efficiency instruments under Article 7 EED
policy_statement: Focus Conto Termico on energy-efficient retrofitting and restoration of non-residential public and private tertiary buildings, simplifying access and extending eligible interventions.
source_quote: As the results of the public consultation showed, to avoid fragmentation and overlapping of instruments for promoting energy efficiency, the plan is to focus the Conto Termico scheme on energy-efficient retrofitting and restoration of non-residential buildings, in the public and private tertiary sector. The intention is to continue the task of simplifying access to the scheme for public bodies, also through promotion of the ESCo model and the use of energy performance contracts (EPCs).
extraction_rationale: This is a named incentive scheme reform for energy-efficient building retrofits.

parent_statement: Energy efficiency instruments under Article 7 EED
policy_statement: Increase the National Fund for Energy Efficiency and direct it toward civil and transport sector efficiency, including guarantees for building retrofit finance.
source_quote: In order to increase the capacity of the Fund to promote energy-efficient measures, the financial allocation currently available will be increased, favouring the payment of resources dedicated to energy efficiency managed by central and local public bodies (structural funds, European investment funds) and directing the scheme towards the promotion of measures in the civil sector (both the housing and tertiary sectors) and the transport sector. For 2021-2030 the additional funding mentioned above will be €733 million.
extraction_rationale: This is a public financial instrument with specific additional funding and target sectors.

parent_statement: Energy efficiency instruments under Article 7 EED
policy_statement: Use the Industry 4.0 tax credit for investments in new capital goods, including intangible assets for technological transformation.
source_quote: The Budget Law for 2020 (Law No 160 of 27 December 2019) changes the existing regulations governing Industry 4.0, introducing a new tax credit for expenses incurred in investing in new capital goods. The provision applies to all businesses and, for certain investments, also to professionals. The tax credit is granted at a differentiated rate according to the type of goods invested in.
extraction_rationale: This is a tax credit instrument that the plan counts toward efficiency savings, although climate is partly indirect through industrial modernisation.

parent_statement: Energy efficiency instruments under Article 7 EED
policy_statement: Continue and strengthen PREPAC funding for energy efficiency upgrades in central government buildings through 2030.
source_quote: Funding for the measure will cover 2021-2030 and updating and strengthening measures will be implemented in order to simplify administrative procedures. The aim is to draw on the synergies between the public bodies involved in managing the scheme and enable adequate management IT support to be developed.
extraction_rationale: This is a named public-building efficiency programme with a 2021-2030 continuation.

parent_statement: Energy efficiency instruments under Article 7 EED
policy_statement: Use 2021-2027 cohesion policies to finance energy efficiency, particularly decarbonisation of building stock and mobility measures.
source_quote: In the shared planning of the structural funds intended for Italy for the period 2021-2027, with particular reference to the European Regional Development Fund (ERDF) and the Cohesion Fund currently under discussion, and for the successive period 2028-2034, priority will be given to implementing the INECP, including to facilitate the building of the 2014-2020 partnership agreement. In line with the other objectives in the planning cycle, particular attention will be paid to the allocation of significant resources at a local and national level for initiatives aimed at decarbonisation of the public and private building stock and at measures for limiting mobility requirement and increase in collective mobility, in particular via rail, in particular the switching of the transport of goods from road to rail.
extraction_rationale: This is a financing and investment programming measure using EU funds for efficiency and sustainable mobility.

parent_statement: Energy efficiency instruments under Article 7 EED
policy_statement: Launch or continue consumer information and training programmes for energy efficiency and behavioural change.
source_quote: From 2021 to 2030 more importance will be placed on information-sharing and training activities, and the launch of a potential new programme based on experience gained as a result of the one coming to a close will be assessed. The theme of monitoring the savings generated by awareness-raising programmes will be explored, with a view to offering evermore robust support to decision-making in that area, as well as to meeting the energy efficiency targets.
extraction_rationale: This is a planned programme area for behavioural efficiency savings; somewhat softer but tied to monitored savings.

policy_statement: Accelerate mandatory purchase shares of electric, plug-in hybrid, methane and hydrogen vehicles for public bodies and public utilities, reaching 85% by 2030.
source_quote: It is proposed to accelerate the provisions set out in paragraph 10 of Article 18 of Italian Legislative Decree 257/2016 (transposition of the DAFI directive) stipulating that the public administration, the Regions, local bodies and providers of public utilities for activities carried out in the provinces with high levels of PM10 particle pollution, when replacing their respective fleets of cars, buses and public utility vehicles, including those for collecting urban waste, must ensure that 30% by 2022, at least 50% by 2025 and 85% by 2030 of new vehicles purchased are electric vehicles and hybrid vehicles with off-vehicle charging, powered by methane and hydrogen, and electricity and methane in the case of buses. In the case of replacing transport fleets used for local public transport, this limit applies solely to urban services.
extraction_rationale: This is a binding procurement quota for public vehicle fleets with quantified deadlines.

policy_statement: Continue and reinforce Marebonus and Ferrobonus incentives to shift freight from road to sea and rail.
source_quote: Marebonus and Ferrobonus are fundamental measures for improving energy efficiency in the transport sector, because the modal shift is a highly effective measure in terms of the cost to benefit ratio. It will therefore be important to relaunch them for 2021-2030, to update and reinforce them on the basis of experience gained, and to monitor the resulting energy savings more effectively.
extraction_rationale: These are named economic incentives for freight modal shift and energy savings.

policy_statement: Implement the National Plan for Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure and expand charging infrastructure, including tax deductions and coordination with fuel network rationalisation.
source_quote: The PNIRE is currently being updated using an integrated approach, which also considers other measures to sustain demand for electric vehicles and to strengthen and increase the usability of the related infrastructure. In addition, the possibility of coordinating the development of recharging infrastructure with the plans to rationalise the fuel network is being assessed.
extraction_rationale: This is a named infrastructure plan for electric mobility; climate relevance is direct via vehicle electrification.

policy_statement: Implement DAFI alternative-fuel infrastructure targets, including at least 6,500 EV charging points by 2020, 2,400 CNG stations and 800 LNG stations by 2030.
source_quote: In summary, Italian Legislative Decree No 257/2016 provides for an increase of: charging points (public and private) for electric vehicles from the current 2,900, approximately, up to at least 6,500 in 2020; sales points supplying CNG from the current number of around 1,100 to around 2,400 in 2030; sales points supplying LNG from the current number of a few dozen to around 800 in 2030.
extraction_rationale: This is a binding infrastructure deployment policy with quantified targets.

policy_statement: Fund and implement rapid mass transport, regional rail electrification and cycling infrastructure to support modal shift.
source_quote: The Budget Law for 2017 planned for the establishing of a fund, with an allocation of €1 900 million for the year 2017, €3 150 million for the year 2018, €3 500 million for the year 2019, and €3 000 million for each of the years from 2020 to 2032, to ensure the financing of investments and infrastructure developments across the country in spending areas relating to, among other things, transport, road systems, sustainable mobility, road safety, upgrading and accessibility of railway stations. Through the Budget Laws for 2016 and 2017, the national system of cycle paths has been funded with national resources at a total of €372 million from 2016 to 2024.
extraction_rationale: This is a public investment package for sustainable transport infrastructure, including mass transport and cycling.

policy_statement: Require Sustainable Urban Mobility Plans for metropolitan cities, large municipalities and cities with high PM10 or nitrogen dioxide pollution.
source_quote: For all metropolitan cities, bodies covering extensive areas, municipalities with more than 100,000 inhabitants and for cities with high levels of PM10 and/or nitrogen dioxide pollution (also with a population of fewer than 100,000 inhabitants), it will be mandatory to prepare a SUMP (no longer linked to mere provision of funding) by 2021, providing also that municipalities with a population of more than 50,000 inhabitants, using simplified guidelines, will have to prepare a SUMP as a mandatory requirement for access to funding by 2025. The SUMPs make it necessary to harmonise existing measures and interventions within the framework of the replacement of the current LPT, sustainable mobility and the optimisation of the management of the movement of goods and people.
extraction_rationale: This is a binding urban mobility planning mandate with deadlines.

policy_statement: Require public bodies to redevelop public lighting systems by 31 December 2023 to reduce electricity consumption by at least 50%.
source_quote: In this connection, the Budget Law for 2018 established that public bodies are obliged to redevelop public lighting systems by 31 December 2023, guaranteeing a reduction in electricity consumption of at least 50% in relation to the average consumption 2015-2016. The companies, involved in development of measures, may take advantage of the subsidies supplied from the revolving Fund for supporting companies and investment in research, where €300 million have been allocated for the granting of subsidised loans.
extraction_rationale: This is a binding efficiency obligation with a quantified consumption reduction and deadline; includes loan support.

policy_statement: Continue mandatory energy audits for large and energy-intensive companies and extend them to gas-intensive companies while linking benefits to efficiency measures.
source_quote: In the period 2021-2030, the plan is to carry out the energy audit preparation programme in large companies and in energy-intensive companies, extending it also to energy-intensive companies in the gas sector and correlating the benefit perceived by the energy-intensive companies with carrying out energy efficiency measures as part of their own production process, as also emerged from the public consultation. It is however considered important to update provisions in order to increase the effectiveness of the instrument, focusing the audit on companies and on sites with the greatest energy savings potential.
section_header: Energy audits and energy management systems
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory programme requiring audits and linking benefits to efficiency actions.

policy_statement: Prepare and implement a long-term building renovation strategy with 2030, 2040 and 2050 milestones for residential and non-residential buildings.
source_quote: In order to make promotion of energy efficiency in the civil sector consistent with the targets and effective in relation to the goal by periodically evaluating the progress made, a long-term strategy will be prepared for renovation of building stock that provides intermediate and final targets, in accordance with the provisions of Directive (EU) 2018/844 on energy performance in buildings. Specifically, the strategy will be published upon transposition of the aforesaid Directive, expected by 10 March 2020.
extraction_rationale: This is a named long-term renovation strategy with milestones and a publication deadline.

policy_statement: Promote energy performance contracts and ESCo models in public buildings by defining EPCs in public procurement rules and removing barriers.
source_quote: The proposed model is aimed at public bodies, to facilitate for the latter the signing of contracts to promote energy efficiency in buildings occupied by them; it is designed to encourage the involvement of private operators (ESCos, credit institutions, etc.) in order to generate economies of scale, and to be clear and transparent about the results to be achieved, while complying with both contracting procedures in accordance with current legislation and with new provisions on energy efficiency in buildings. Therefore, in order to promote a more widespread use of the EPC, eliminating the current barriers, the plan is to introduce into the Italian Code of Public Contracts (Legislative Decree 50/2016 as amended and supplemented), the definition of the EPC for buildings as a special contract, and a new type of PPP contract for EPCs for buildings which sets out the specific details.
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory reform to expand public-sector energy service contracting.

policy_statement: Ensure gas security through preventive and emergency plans, network adaptation, LNG diversification, solidarity measures and storage planning.
source_quote: The main interventions put in place to ensure that the security levels of the electricity, gas and petroleum products systems are sufficiently high and maintained can be attributed to the measures described below. Update of Annex I to the Ministerial Decree of 18 October 2017. The Preventive Action Plan contains the results of the assessment carried out on the risks that could affect the security of the national natural gas system, setting out crisis scenarios and impacts, and also the measures that can be put in place to maximise supply and contain demand, in order to sufficiently offset any supply disruptions in good time, guaranteeing in any case that protected customers (household customers and public services) are supplied, and the preventive measures for managing and containing the risks.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella set of energy security measures; climate link is indirect except where gas supports renewables integration.

policy_statement: Update electricity resilience plans to strengthen networks against extreme weather events and reduce restoration times.
source_quote: Extreme weather events are becoming increasingly common, due in part to climate change, and can pose major difficulties to the electricity sector and other essential services, in some cases at the same time, in vast areas covering several Regions. In the medium to long term, on the one hand, action needs to be taken to increase the number of interventions carried out on infrastructure by meshing and reinforcing the network, and also diversify the technologies used. In the short term, meanwhile, mitigation measures need to be put in place, for instance by installing anti-rotation devices to prevent the ice load sag effect, and using remote control.
extraction_rationale: This directly responds to climate-related extreme weather risks through resilience measures.

policy_statement: Implement a capacity market to ensure electricity system adequacy while favouring low-emission, flexible resources.
source_quote: The measure, (Ministerial Decree of 28 June 2019) initially approved by the EC in 2018 and then in 2019 in its revised version with new emissions limits for participating plants, provides for annual auctions to be introduced by Terna, open to all technologies capable of contributing to the adaptation objective, in order to supply resources, including those from outside Italy, to cover the requirement expressed by Terna, which is based on a long-term assessment that is updated every year. The measure is crucial for encouraging long-term, efficient, flexible and less-polluting investments, with a view to rendering the sector carbon-free and achieving the ambitious targets for phasing in renewable sources between now and 2030.
extraction_rationale: This is a market instrument with auctions and emissions limits supporting system adequacy and decarbonisation.

policy_statement: Adapt cyber-security measures for the energy system in line with the NIS Directive and future network code.
source_quote: Adapting the national cyber-security measures (identification of risks and actions to combat them) with respect to the changes made to the regulations governing that field, resulting both from the implementation of the NIS Directive, and from the planned adoption by the European Commission of a suitable network code for that field. These national measures, together with those coordinated with the other EU Member States, will form part of the Risk Preparation Plan provided for in Regulation 2019/941.
extraction_rationale: This is an energy system risk-preparedness measure; climate relevance is peripheral to indirect, but it supports resilient low-carbon infrastructure.

policy_statement: Develop electricity interconnections with neighbouring countries, including northern borders, southeast Europe and northern Africa, subject to cost-benefit analysis.
source_quote: A first set of new infrastructure has been identified (Annex III to the NES), which is to be produced in line with TERNA's development plan and also involves interconnections with other countries, especially with: those lying on Italy's northern border (France, Switzerland, Austria and Slovenia); the border with South-East Europe, where there is a diversified and competitive production capacity that will increase in the medium to long term, which provides an alternative to gas and petroleum, owing to the mineral and water resources that are present in the countries in South-East Europe and to the potential synergies with the electricity systems in that region.
extraction_rationale: This is a transmission infrastructure policy supporting market integration and renewable/security objectives; climate relevance is indirect.

policy_statement: Reinforce internal electricity networks, including the Adriatic Spine HVDC line and Sardinia connections, to reduce congestion and integrate renewables.
source_quote: Further network reinforcements between the North-Central and Central-South zones, aimed at reducing the number of hours of congestion between those sections. The new interventions include the so-called 'Dorsale Adriatica' ('Adriatic Spine'), which consists of a HVDC power line running between the Central-South and North-Central market sections, which is connected to the electricity hubs of Villanova (or Villavalle) and Fano (or Porto Tolle). The decarbonisation objective is posing a number of problems as regards managing the security of the Sardinian network.
extraction_rationale: This is a named electricity transmission infrastructure intervention tied to decarbonisation and congestion reduction.

policy_statement: Develop new storage systems for electricity network security and renewable integration, with market-based procurement and TSO fallback.
source_quote: The development of renewables expected by 2030 has already led the TSO to quantify the requirements of new storage systems that will be needed (listed in section 2.3 iv), together with the development of the networks, in order to ensure that management is maintained under secure conditions. In addition, in line with the EU Directive that is in the course of being adopted, the current rules governing storage infrastructure will be amended and a new regulatory framework will be defined, which will be able to foster the development and coming into operation of the new storage capacity needed according to a market model in which stakeholders compete to offer network services that are different from today's.
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory and market measure for storage deployment directly enabling renewables integration.

policy_statement: Use a prototype regulatory approach and dedicated fund to facilitate innovative energy network projects, including temporary waivers and cost recognition.
source_quote: Definition of a regulatory framework that facilitates innovative projects, including by means of a dedicated fund, allowing operators to conduct tests on site and at prototype stage, if necessary granting temporary waivers from the regulations in force, while at the same time providing for adequate mechanisms for effective cost recognition. Network operators will be particularly involved, activating a new approach of system innovation that involves commercial parties in the development of new business models downstream in the chain and in trialling multiservice offers at urban and local level.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific regulatory sandbox/fund mechanism for energy network innovation.

policy_statement: Develop LNG refuelling infrastructure in TEN-T ports and along road networks for maritime and heavy-duty transport.
source_quote: Legislative Decree No 257 of 16 December 2016, transposing the 'DAFI' Directive and concerning ' Rules for implementing Directive 2014/94/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 22 October 2014 on the deployment of alternative fuels infrastructure ', stipulates, under Article 6, as regards the supply of natural gas for transportation, that by 31 December 2025 in maritime ports, and by 31 December 2030 in inland ports, a sufficient number of LNG refuelling points will have been put in place to allow LNG-fuelled vessels used for inland navigation or LNG-powered vessels used for sea navigation to navigate in the TENT Core Network. The same Article also stipulates that by 31 December 2025, a sufficient number of LNG refuelling points also combined with CNG (compressed natural gas) refuelling points will have been gradually put in place, to which the public will have access at least along the Italian sections of the TEN-T Core Network, in order to ensure the circulation of LNGfuelled heavy-duty vehicles, taking account of the current levels of demand and the shortterm development thereof.
extraction_rationale: This is a binding alternative-fuel infrastructure rollout; climate relevance is indirect and transitional.

policy_statement: Continue electricity market coupling, implement intraday market target model, and integrate balancing markets with EU platforms.
source_quote: Market coupling will continue to be developed - it is already at full speed on the day-ahead market, and is currently evolving on the intraday markets and on the dispatching services market - as regards the implementation of the provisions set out in the applicable European network codes (the CACM and Balancing Regulations). The shift to the target model for the intraday market (continuous trading and near real-time closure) is planned for the second half of 2020, in tandem with the reform of dispatching and the rules on imbalances.
extraction_rationale: This is an electricity market integration policy that improves system flexibility for renewable integration; direct climate link is not the primary objective.

policy_statement: Introduce negative electricity prices and ensure incentives are not granted during negative-price hours.
source_quote: To foster an even better integration with European markets, in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2019/943, which provides that market rules must not constrain pricing in any way, Italy plans to remove the floor, thus allowing negative price bids on the day-ahead and intraday markets. In this respect it will be necessary to make sure that, during the hours in which the closing prices on the day-ahead and intraday markets are negative, no incentives associated with loading electricity onto the grid are granted.
extraction_rationale: This is a market regulatory reform to improve efficient dispatch and integration of variable renewables.

policy_statement: Reorganise self-consumption arrangements, energy communities and closed distribution systems under EU electricity and renewable directives.
source_quote: The rolling-out of self-consumption arrangements and, looking further ahead, of energy communities is aimed at promoting a more decentralised electricity system and the active role of distributed generation and demand. First of all, the self-generation arrangements that can be achieved and the features thereof will be identified, also on the basis of the new EU guidelines. This will allow new, closed-off distribution systems to be produced, and measures will be identified for other private systems connected to plants powered by renewable sources or to high-efficiency cogeneration plants, including those integrated with the stockpile.
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory reform for distributed renewable generation and demand participation.

policy_statement: Deploy vehicle-to-grid rules and pilot projects so electric vehicle batteries can provide electricity network services.
source_quote: With the expected conversion of the sector to electric power, connected mobility could also become a flexible resource for meeting the needs that arise in managing the network, by developing innovative technologies like vehicle-to-grid. During a first phase, mechanisms and new rules for participating in the service markets for systems for recharging electric vehicles will be introduced, also providing for specific rebalancing measures for payment of the general charges of the system; in that sense, these initiatives will initially be rolled out on a trial basis.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific technology and market reform supporting electric mobility and grid flexibility.

policy_statement: Update dispatching rules and DSO roles to enable distributed generation, demand, storage and aggregations to provide services.
source_quote: During a first phase, ARERA will receive guidelines for reforming the operational structure of the dispatching market which, even though within the scope of a central dispatch model, provide for the DSOs to play a more active role by updating their responsibilities with respect to the provision of the network services rendered from the distributed resources and through new models of cooperation between the TSO and the DSOs; this is needed in light of the greater active participation and the resulting greater importance of the distributed consumption and generation resources (including by encouraging the aggregation of installations, potentially starting with pilot projects).
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory reform for distributed resource integration; climate relevance is direct through renewable and demand flexibility.

policy_statement: Develop distributed storage systems and premiums for self-consumed renewable energy.
source_quote: Plans are in place to adopt a specific measure which, in line with the changes to Net Metering (see section 3.1.2, point i.), will allow renewable energy plants that fulfil specific requirements to benefit from a premium on self-consumed energy. The measure, which will be put in place through suitable regulatory provisions, will need to attract distributors by giving them an active role, with the aim of making production from non-relevant entities easier to predict and restricting over-generation.
extraction_rationale: This is an incentive and regulatory measure for storage and renewable self-consumption.

policy_statement: Open service and balancing markets to aggregations of generation, storage, consumption units and electric vehicle batteries.
source_quote: Legislative Decree No 102/2014 introduced the possibility of creating aggregations of power generation plants, including alongside storage systems, and of consumption units for accessing the service markets for which the TSO needs to resolve any possible congestion and promote better integration of renewables. To that end, during a first phase, the network operator defines the rules for organising the participation in the services market of those new aggregations through pilot projects that are approved by ARERA.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific market-access policy enabling demand response, distributed resources and renewables integration.

policy_statement: Complete liberalisation of retail electricity and gas markets while strengthening consumer protections and last-resort services.
