source_quote: The process for liberalising the retail market by 1 January 2020 will be completed by identifying the measures instrumental in scrapping the regulated price plans for household customers and small businesses, in accordance with criteria for promoting a competitive retail market structure. These actions will need to be aimed at: preventing operators from exercising their market powers (especially in the household segment, which is still the most concentrated segment) and making the rules on unbundling, which currently give a competitive advantage to vendors integrated with distribution, more stringent; qualifying the retail market, which is currently extremely fragmented; encouraging consumers to be mobile and play an active role, and simplifying switching procedures.
extraction_rationale: This is a market reform; climate relevance is peripheral to indirect, mainly enabling active consumers and competitive energy services.

policy_statement: Deploy second-generation smart electricity meters and smart gas meters to enable consumption awareness, demand response and market services.
source_quote: The new smart meters will play an important role in providing consumers with all the information they need to understand and monitor their energy consumption. From that perspective, these smart meters will be made fully operational, and the necessary network infrastructure will be developed. For electricity, the replacement of existing digital meters with the new second generation smart meters is a fundamental vehicle for the products, services and offers to be inserted into the new models of generation, distribution and consumption, also from a demandresponse perspective, and smart grids.
extraction_rationale: This is an operational deployment of enabling infrastructure for efficiency, demand response and smart grids.

policy_statement: Combat energy poverty through an observatory, social bonus reform, low-income subsidies and energy efficiency in social housing.
source_quote: The priority strategy for combating energy poverty involves several principal measures: setting up a National Observatory of Energy Poverty; reviewing the existing instruments, in particular the electricity and gas social bonuses; subsidies for low income families; putting in place a programme for making social housing buildings more energy efficient.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella strategy with named sub-measures; climate link is mainly through energy efficiency and access to clean energy.

parent_statement: Energy poverty strategy
policy_statement: Set up a National Observatory of Energy Poverty coordinated operationally by GSE to monitor energy poverty and support policy design.
source_quote: As regards the first measure, in order to better coordinate existing efforts, and given also the fragmented nature of skills and resources, an Observatory of Energy Poverty is scheduled to be set up by the Ministry of Economic Development at the beginning of 2020. Although the Observatory will be coordinated by GSE at operational level, various entities and institutions will be called upon to take part.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete institutional measure with timing and coordinating body.

parent_statement: Energy poverty strategy
policy_statement: Replace electricity and gas social bonuses with a new energy social bonus based on ISEE and household size, with automated identification of eligible households.
source_quote: This will involve replacing the current electricity and gas social bonuses with a new 'energy social bonus', and adjusting the benefit on the basis of the Equivalent Economic Status Indicator and the number of household members; the benefit will be, at most, equivalent to three months' energy costs (these consisting of both electricity and heating costs) - ideal for covering heating costs (during the winter) or air-conditioning costs (during the summer). The measures to automate recognition of economic or physical hardship, and the resulting simplification and streamlining of the procedures, accompanied by appropriate and widereaching training and information campaigns, will play a decisive role in broadening the base of bonus recipients, currently estimated by ARERA to be between 30% and 35% of potential beneficiaries.
extraction_rationale: This is a financial support mechanism for vulnerable households; climate relevance is indirect.

parent_statement: Energy poverty strategy
policy_statement: Create an 'energy income' revolving fund to cover 100% of photovoltaic installations for domestic use up to 20 kW for low-income households.
source_quote: As for subsidies for households on low incomes (point 3), a provision entitled 'energy income' is being created. This involves setting up a rotation fund for granting capital contributions covering 100% of the cost of investment in photovoltaic installations for domestic use (up to 20 KW).
extraction_rationale: This is a financial subsidy fund for low-income household solar PV.

parent_statement: Energy poverty strategy
policy_statement: Launch a large-scale programme to improve energy efficiency in social housing buildings.
source_quote: The measure referred to in point 4 involves exploring the option of launching a large-scale programme for making social housing more energy efficient. Such an initiative would pursue a variety of objectives at the same time: making the use of energy resources taken up by the residential sector more efficient (thus having positive effects on both comfort and emission levels), bringing down energy bills for the most vulnerable families who will be using this service, and increasing the value of the public housing assets.
extraction_rationale: This is somewhat exploratory but describes a concrete programme for social housing efficiency with emissions benefits.

policy_statement: Double public clean-energy research funding under Mission Innovation from about €222 million in 2013 to about €444 million from 2021.
source_quote: As regards financial resources in the context of Mission Innovation, Italy has undertaken to double the value of the resources portfolio for public research in the field of clean energy, from around €222 million in 2013 (the year taken as the baseline) to around €444 million from 2021, which represents for all intents and purposes the minimum commitment necessary to guarantee that the indicated targets will be reached.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified public R&D funding commitment for clean energy.

parent_statement: Mission Innovation and SET Plan clean-energy research agenda
policy_statement: Research and develop photovoltaics, storage including power-to-gas, energy materials, resilient electricity networks, building technologies, industrial efficiency, smart buildings, energy communities, electric mobility, heat pumps and marine renewables.
source_quote: Goal 1) monitor and develop product and process technologies vital to the energy transition: development of components and systems for highly efficient photovoltaics, which allows better exploitation of occupied areas and provides opportunities for new entrepreneurship; development of storage systems, including thermal, electrochemical and power-togas, and related interfaces with the networks, in order to guarantee high levels of penetration for non-programmable renewables; development of power-to-gas storage systems, particularly for the purpose of storage of excess production of non-programmable renewables by means of secure and reliable storage of hydrogen in liquid and gaseous energy carriers.
extraction_rationale: This is a detailed R&D programme for specific clean-energy technologies; it is less deployment-focused but qualifies through named interventions and funding context.

parent_statement: Mission Innovation and SET Plan clean-energy research agenda
policy_statement: Promote system models and demonstrators for renewable integration, self-production, storage, energy communities, aggregators, smart grids, peer-to-peer trading and electric transport integration.
source_quote: Goal 2) promote the introduction of technologies, organisational and operational models and systems used for the energy transition and for safety: development of architectural and operational models for the system and for electricity networks which promote the integration of renewable, non-programmable energy production, self-production, storage, energy communities and aggregators, and which take into account electrical penetration; application of advanced information technologies, the internet of things, peer to peer electricity trading, to improve the safety and resilience of networks.
extraction_rationale: This is a defined innovation and demonstration programme for energy transition systems.

policy_statement: Finance energy R&D through the Electric System Research Fund, including €210 million for the 2019-2021 three-year plan aligned with the SET Plan and Mission Innovation.
source_quote: A new Three-Year Plan for 2019-2021 has been approved by Decree of the Ministry of Economic Development of 9 August 2019, which will set new research objectives in line with the SET Plan and the involvement in Mission Innovation. The allocation provided for the three-year period amounts to €210 million, the same as for the previous three years, so as to avoid increasing the burden on the A5 tariff component of the electricity bill.
extraction_rationale: This is a named R&D fund with a quantified allocation and clean-energy alignment.

policy_statement: Use the Fund for technological and industrial development to support renewable energy and energy efficiency actions and demonstration projects.
source_quote: A fund held at the Fund for Energy and Environmental Services (CSEA), set up by Legislative Decree No 28/2011 and financed through a levy placed on electricity and natural gas tariffs sufficient to ensure resources of around €100 million/year. It aims to support actions and measures for technological and industrial development in the field of renewable sources and energy efficiency. If necessary, the fund may also be called on to support demonstration projects.
extraction_rationale: This is a named financial instrument for renewable and efficiency technology development.

policy_statement: Provide tax credits for research and development investments, including enhanced support for Southern regions.
source_quote: This instrument, which forms part of National Industrial Plan 4.0, is for the more immediate use by companies, and is aimed at stimulating private investments in R&D in order to innovate processes and products and guarantee the future competitiveness of the companies (not only in the energy sector). It consists of a 50% tax credit for incremental Research and Development costs, which may be granted up to a maximum annual amount of €20 million per recipient and is calculated on a fixed basis stemming from the average Research and Development costs for the 2012-2014 period.
extraction_rationale: This is a broad R&D fiscal instrument; climate relevance is indirect because it is not energy-exclusive but is part of the plan’s clean-tech competitiveness tools.

policy_statement: Use CO2 auction proceeds to support experimental development and demonstration projects, including aviation biofuels from microcellular algae.
source_quote: The funds available from CO2 auctions (Legislative Decree No 30/2013) will cover experimental development, in particular in order to ensure that demonstration projects (first-of-a-kind) are supported, with the results being passed on to the production system. In particular, research centres and public administrative bodies have agreed to work together in order to develop the production and use of biofuels in the aviation sector, and ENAC has launched a research project with the aim of producing an alternative fuel derived from microcellular algae.
extraction_rationale: This is a financial use of carbon-market proceeds for clean technology demonstration and aviation biofuels.

policy_statement: Create a fund for investment programmes and innovative projects supporting circular economy, decarbonisation, emissions reduction, energy savings and environmental sustainability.
source_quote: Law No 60 of 27 December 2019 establishes in the statement of estimates of the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Finance a fund with an allocation of €435 million for 2020, €880 million for 2021, €934 million for 2022, €1,045 million for 2023, €1,061 million for 2024, €1,512 million for 2025, €1,513 million for 2026, €1,672 million for each of the years from 2027 to 2032 and €1,700 million for each of the years 2033 and 2034. The fund is intended for the relaunch of investments of the central government bodies and for national development, also with reference to the circular economy, the decarbonisation of the economy, emission reductions, energy savings, environmental sustainability and, in general, investment programmes and innovative projects.
extraction_rationale: This is a large public investment fund with explicit climate, circular economy and efficiency purposes.

policy_statement: Gradually reduce environmentally harmful fossil-fuel subsidies and use revenues for ecological transition, climate projects, tax shifts or public debt reduction.
source_quote: Among the many proposals being assessed, there is the possibility of a progressive, gradual reduction of environmentally harmful subsidies in the energy sector, with the reuse of the revenue recovered to reinvest, at least in part, in compensating and encouraging the ecological energy transition in the sectors directly involved and to compensate the economic actors who benefit from these subsidies in order to create greater social acceptability of their reduction/elimination. As an alternative, the recovered revenue may be used to invest in projects to combat climate change, to reduce the tax wedge on labour and capital income, or to reduce public debt.
extraction_rationale: This is a fiscal reform proposal to phase out fossil-fuel subsidies; somewhat tentative but specific and explicitly climate-linked.

policy_statement: Reduce Japan's greenhouse gas emissions by 46 percent in fiscal year 2030 from fiscal year 2013 levels, while continuing efforts toward a 50 percent reduction and aligning with net-zero by 2050.
source_quote: Japan aims to reduce its greenhouse gas emissions by 46 percent in fiscal year 2030 from its fiscal year 2013 levels, setting an ambitious target which is aligned with the longterm  goal  of  achieving  net-zero  by  2050.  Furthermore,  Japan  will  continue  strenuous efforts in its challenge to meet the lofty goal of cutting its emission by 50 percent.
section_header: Japan's Greenhouse Gas Emission Reduction Target
extraction_rationale: This is the central economy-wide NDC mitigation target with a quantified percentage reduction, baseline year, and target year. The 50 percent language is framed as a challenge rather than a firm target, but it is still a stated national effort linked to the binding NDC target.

policy_statement: Establish net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050 as a Basic Principle under the Act on Promotion of Global Warming Countermeasures to accelerate decarbonization policies, investment, and innovation.
source_quote: Japan aims to reduce greenhouse gas emissions to net-zero, that is, to realize carbon neutrality by 2050, based on the idea that addressing climate change is no longer a constraint on economic growth and that proactive climate change measures bring transformation of industrial structures as well as its economy and society, leading to dynamic economic growth. By the Act Partially Amending the Act on Promotion of Global Warming Countermeasures (Act No. 54 of 2021) which was enacted in 204th session of the Diet, net-zero by 2050 became a Basic Principle of the Act. The legislative amendment will enhance the continuity and predictability of policies and accelerate efforts and investments as well as innovation for decarbonization towards not only the achievement of the mid-term target, but also the realization of a decarbonized society.
extraction_rationale: This qualifies because it sets a long-term mitigation target and embeds it in legislation, creating a binding policy principle. It overlaps with the NDC target but is distinct because it concerns legal codification of the 2050 net-zero goal.

policy_statement: Use the Plan for Global Warming Countermeasures to conduct annual progress reviews, evaluate countermeasures, improve delayed measures, and consider new measures toward emissions reduction goals.
source_quote: Every year since the formulation of the plan, the Global Warming Prevention Headquarters, led by the Prime Minister with all Cabinet Ministers as its members, has made rigorous reviews and examinations on, among others, the state of progress in each countermeasure taken by the Government, by using the outcome in emission reductions including figures by greenhouse gases and other classifications, and indicators to evaluate the progress in implementing countermeasures. Specifically, by administering evaluations on each section of measures and policies and identifying sections whose progress is delayed, the Government conducted examinations on, among others, how to improve progress in the identified sections. In so doing, the Government considered not only the enhancement of measures and policies that are already included in the Plan for Global Warming Countermeasures but also the introduction of new measures and policies.
extraction_rationale: This is an operational governance commitment tied to a named national plan and emissions-reduction progress management. It is partly procedural, but it qualifies because it commits the government to evaluate and improve specific mitigation measures under the plan.

policy_statement: Implement thorough energy efficiency measures as part of Japan's efforts to achieve its fiscal year 2030 greenhouse gas emissions reduction goal.
source_quote: On top of that, Japan aims to reduce its greenhouse gas emissions by 46 percent in fiscal year 2030 from its fiscal year 2013 levels, setting an ambitious target which is aligned with the long- term goal of achieving net-zero by 2050. Furthermore, Japan will continue strenuous efforts in its challenge to meet the lofty goal of cutting its emissions by 50 percent. In order to create a virtuous cycle of the economy and the environment and to realize robust growth toward its ambitious goal for fiscal year 2030, Japan will put forward all possible efforts in all areas including by thorough energy efficiency measures, maximum introduction of renewable energy, as well as decarbonization of public sectors and local communities.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific named intervention, energy efficiency, explicitly linked to Japan's quantified 2030 emissions target. The wording is broad and does not specify sectoral standards or funding, but it qualifies as a deliberate mitigation measure.

policy_statement: Maximize the introduction of renewable energy as part of Japan's all-area efforts to meet its fiscal year 2030 greenhouse gas emissions reduction goal.
source_quote: On top of that, Japan aims to reduce its greenhouse gas emissions by 46 percent in fiscal year 2030 from its fiscal year 2013 levels, setting an ambitious target which is aligned with the long- term goal of achieving net-zero by 2050. Furthermore, Japan will continue strenuous efforts in its challenge to meet the lofty goal of cutting its emissions by 50 percent. In order to create a virtuous cycle of the economy and the environment and to realize robust growth toward its ambitious goal for fiscal year 2030, Japan will put forward all possible efforts in all areas including by thorough energy efficiency measures, maximum introduction of renewable energy, as well as decarbonization of public sectors and local communities.
extraction_rationale: This qualifies as a specific mitigation intervention because it commits to expanding renewable energy deployment in support of the national emissions target. The commitment is directionally strong but lacks a quantified renewable energy capacity or share target in this text.

policy_statement: Decarbonize public sectors and local communities as part of Japan's national efforts toward its fiscal year 2030 greenhouse gas emissions reduction goal.
source_quote: On top of that, Japan aims to reduce its greenhouse gas emissions by 46 percent in fiscal year 2030 from its fiscal year 2013 levels, setting an ambitious target which is aligned with the long- term goal of achieving net-zero by 2050. Furthermore, Japan will continue strenuous efforts in its challenge to meet the lofty goal of cutting its emissions by 50 percent. In order to create a virtuous cycle of the economy and the environment and to realize robust growth toward its ambitious goal for fiscal year 2030, Japan will put forward all possible efforts in all areas including by thorough energy efficiency measures, maximum introduction of renewable energy, as well as decarbonization of public sectors and local communities.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific intervention area targeting decarbonization of public and local community sectors. It is broad and does not list implementation instruments, but it is explicitly tied to national mitigation goals.

policy_statement: Implement the Strategy for Sustainable Food Systems, MeaDRI, to advance decarbonization, resilience, productivity, and sustainability in food, agriculture, forestry, and fisheries through innovation.
source_quote: In food, agriculture, forestry, and fisheries industries, based on the 'Strategy for Sustainable Food Systems, MeaDRI (Measures for achievement of Decarbonization and Resilience with Innovation) (decided by Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries on May 12 th , 2021),' Japan aims to enhance productivity potentials and ensure sustainability in a compatible manner through innovation. Based on the 'MLIT's Green Challenge (decided by Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism on July 6 th , 2021),' Japan will steadily carry out efforts in cross-sectoral decarbonization in national land, urban and regional spheres.
extraction_rationale: This is a named sectoral strategy with an explicit decarbonization objective and specific affected sectors. The resilience reference is explicit but does not name a climate hazard, so no secondary adaptation category is assigned under the provided rules.

policy_statement: Carry out MLIT's Green Challenge to advance cross-sectoral decarbonization in national land, urban, and regional spheres.
source_quote: In food, agriculture, forestry, and fisheries industries, based on the 'Strategy for Sustainable Food Systems, MeaDRI (Measures for achievement of Decarbonization and Resilience with Innovation) (decided by Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries on May 12 th , 2021),' Japan aims to enhance productivity potentials and ensure sustainability in a compatible manner through innovation. Based on the 'MLIT's Green Challenge (decided by Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism on July 6 th , 2021),' Japan will steadily carry out efforts in cross-sectoral decarbonization in national land, urban and regional spheres.
extraction_rationale: This qualifies because it is a named government initiative with a clear commitment to cross-sectoral decarbonization. The text does not specify quantitative targets or detailed measures, so the extracted policy remains high-level.

policy_statement: Proceed with strategic transitions to a circular economy as a decarbonization-related transformation toward 2030 and 2050.
source_quote: Japan will create new industries and jobs by proceeding efforts in strategic transitions to a circular economy, which is necessary for decarbonization, as well as through nature-based solutions (NbS). Japan will continue its strenuous efforts towards 2030, and further towards 2050. Realizing carbon-neutrality by 2050 and cutting emissions by 46 percent in fiscal year 2030 is certainly not an easy task; it is therefore essential to position decarbonization as one of the main issues in all socio-economic activities and to bring forward the transformation into sustainable and resilient socio-economic systems.
extraction_rationale: Circular economy transition is a specific resource-use strategy explicitly framed as necessary for decarbonization and linked to the 2030 emissions target. The policy is broad and does not specify material streams or regulatory instruments.

policy_statement: Use nature-based solutions as part of Japan's transformation toward decarbonization and sustainable, resilient socio-economic systems.
source_quote: Japan will create new industries and jobs by proceeding efforts in strategic transitions to a circular economy, which is necessary for decarbonization, as well as through nature-based solutions (NbS). Japan will continue its strenuous efforts towards 2030, and further towards 2050. Realizing carbon-neutrality by 2050 and cutting emissions by 46 percent in fiscal year 2030 is certainly not an easy task; it is therefore essential to position decarbonization as one of the main issues in all socio-economic activities and to bring forward the transformation into sustainable and resilient socio-economic systems.
extraction_rationale: This qualifies because nature-based solutions are explicitly named as an implementation approach in the climate planning section. The text is high-level and does not identify specific ecosystems, hazards, or sequestration actions, so no secondary category is assigned.

policy_statement: Establish and implement the Joint Crediting Mechanism to secure approximately 100 million t-CO2 of accumulated international emission reductions and removals by fiscal year 2030 and count acquired credits toward Japan's NDC.
source_quote: Japan will establish and implement the Joint Crediting Mechanism (JCM) in order to quantitatively evaluate contributions of Japan to greenhouse gas emission reductions and removals which are achieved through the diffusion of, among others, leading decarbonizing technologies, products, systems, services, and infrastructures as well as through the implementation of measures in developing countries and others, and in order to use such contributions to achieve Japan's NDC. By doing so, through public-private collaborations, Japan aims to secure accumulated emission reductions and removals at the level of approximately 100 million t-CO 2 by fiscal year 2030. Japan will appropriately count the acquired credits to achieve its NDC.
section_header: 5. Assumptions and methodological approaches, including those for estimating and accounting for anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions and, as appropriate, removals:
extraction_rationale: This is a named international crediting mechanism with a quantified 2030 mitigation outcome and accounting use for the NDC. It is classified as a financial instrument because it is a carbon crediting/market mechanism.

policy_statement: Secure environmental integrity and avoid double-counting in the Joint Crediting Mechanism in line with international rules including the Paris Agreement.
source_quote: With regards to the JCM which Japan has initiated to establish, Japan secures environmental integrity and the avoidance of double-counting in line with the international rules including the Paris Agreement. Also, based on its experience in the JCM, Japan intends to lead international discussions, thereby contributing to the development of appropriate international rules for the use of market mechanisms.
section_header: 5. Assumptions and methodological approaches, including those for estimating and accounting for anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions and, as appropriate, removals:
extraction_rationale: This is a governance safeguard for a mitigation crediting mechanism, ensuring the counted emission reductions are environmentally sound. It is not itself the financial instrument; rather, it is an accounting and integrity rule applied to that instrument.

policy_statement: Promote international cooperation for decarbonization and resilience in developing countries through policy and institutional platforms, sector- and city-level efforts, and technology diffusion.
source_quote: Also, based on its experience in the JCM, Japan intends to lead international discussions, thereby contributing to the development of appropriate international rules for the use of market mechanisms. Furthermore, Japan will also make proactive efforts in the area of international cooperation to promote decarbonization and to improve resilience in developing countries and others, including from developing policies and institutional platforms to promoting sector- and city-level efforts as well as facilitating technology diffusion.
section_header: 5. Assumptions and methodological approaches, including those for estimating and accounting for anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions and, as appropriate, removals:
extraction_rationale: This is a specific international cooperation commitment naming implementation channels such as institutional platforms, sectoral and city efforts, and technology diffusion. Resilience is mentioned, but no specific climate hazard is named in this policy text, so no secondary adaptation category is assigned.

policy_statement: Implement green belts and the Kuwait Green Wall Project by planting 315,000 trees along a 420 km border wall to reduce dust-storm impacts.
source_quote: Implementing green belts project and increasing the protected areas to adapt to dust storms. Kuwait has undertaken some adaptation projects such as implementing green belts project and increasing the protected areas to adapt to a dust storm. The green belt projects consist of planted areas with trees and shrubs of 50-180 Km in length areas with trees and shrubs of 50-180 Km in length and 5-20 Km in width.
extraction_rationale: This is a named, concrete adaptation intervention with quantified planting and length targets. It directly addresses dust storms, a climate-related health hazard.

policy_statement: Develop and introduce heat-, salinity-, and drought-resistant crops and more than 50 tree types for greenery and landscape under Kuwait’s agricultural climate adaptation efforts.
source_quote: Kuwait's agricultural efforts to mitigate climate change in 2012 . Many agricultural projects have been undertaken by Kuwait Institute for Scientific Research (KISR) in order to develop crops that can adapt to high temperatures and different spans of seasons and crops resistant to salinity and drought (Al Dosery et al., 2012). More than 50 types of trees for greenery and landscape that can reduce climate change effect, were introduced under the Agriculture Master Plan by (KISR) and the Public Authority for Agricultural Affairs and Fish Resources (PAAFR).
extraction_rationale: This is a specific agricultural adaptation programme with named institutions and interventions. The wording uses 'mitigate' loosely, but the mechanism is primarily adaptation to heat, salinity and drought.

policy_statement: Establish a food security programme with FAO covering fisheries, water, natural resources, animal production, animal health and technical capacity development over 1–5 years with an $850,000 budget.
source_quote: In 2016, the project ' Food security ' was established. FAO in cooperation with the State of Kuwait planned to undertake twelve projects in the following fields: Fisheries management; Water resource management; Natural resource management; Animal production; Animal health; Technical capacity development. These projects have a time frame between 1-5 years under the Food Security Sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a named programme with a timeframe, responsible party and budget. It is climate-relevant because it is listed as an adaptation initiative for food security, though the fields are broad.

policy_statement: Establish a regional database and information center to support fisheries management and aquaculture development.
source_quote: Establishment of a regional database and information center to support the fisheries management and aquaculture development , a joint project between PAAFR in Kuwait and FAO in December 2016. The project aims at establishing a regional database and information center to support the fisheries management and aquaculture development in the region. Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and the Public Authority of Agriculture Affairs and Fish Resources (PAAFR) were the responsible authorities with a budget of $250,000/year.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific capacity and information-system project with named implementing institutions and an annual budget. It supports climate adaptation in fisheries and aquaculture.

policy_statement: Establish fisheries farms using Nile tilapia aquaculture in agricultural farms in Al-Wafra, Abdali and Al-Sulybia to support food security under climate change.
source_quote: Fisheries Farms . Fisheries are considered a vital source of food in Kuwait. The establishment of fisheries farms is an important step to adapt to climate change under the food security sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific intervention—fish farming—with named locations and a climate adaptation purpose. It is primarily an adaptation and food security measure.

policy_statement: Assess historic climate records for 70 years and develop future climate projection scenarios to 2100.
source_quote: Assessment of historic climate records and future projection . The project aimed at assessing the historic climate records for the past 70 years and make future projection climatic scenarios until the year 2100. The project started in 2012 by the Kuwait University and UN Environment.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete climate-information project with a historical period and projection horizon. It supports adaptation planning rather than being a direct physical intervention.

policy_statement: Maintain the Environmental Monitoring Information System of Kuwait (eMISK) as a geo-environmental database and GIS system for updating and analyzing environmental data.
source_quote: Environmental Monitoring Information System of Kuwait (eMISK) . eMISK is an electronic system established by the Environment Public Authority (EPA) of Kuwait and aims at building and maintaining a comprehensive geo-environmental database of Kuwait and a GIS system to facilitate updating and analyzing environmental data. The project starts in 2015 by EPA and is still ongoing.
extraction_rationale: This is a named operational information system supporting climate and environmental monitoring. The climate relevance is direct in the NAP context but the system is broader than climate alone.

policy_statement: Establish eMISK Industry to collect a national environmental inventory of industrial facilities for public health adaptation.
source_quote: eMISK Industry ; this project aims at establishing a national program for collecting an environmental inventory of industrial facilities in Kuwait. The Adaptation Sector for this project is Public Health.
extraction_rationale: This is a named environmental inventory programme with a public health adaptation sector. It is climate-relevant through air quality and health resilience, though its climate link is partly indirect.

policy_statement: Implement eMISK Waste to manage industrial liquid waste vehicle fleets and logistics.
source_quote: eMISK Waste ; this project aims at finding and implementing a solution to be able to manage the fleet of industrial liquid waste vehicles and organizing the logistics process. The Adaptation Sector for this project is the Waste Sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific waste-management logistics intervention. Its climate relevance is indirect through improved waste-sector management.

policy_statement: Implement eMISK Marine as an information management system supporting integrated coastal and ocean management policies and programmes.
source_quote: eMISK Marine ; The project aims at promoting and facilitating information management system in support of policies and programs that enhance integrated coastal and ocean management in Kuwait. The Adaptation Sector for this project is the Coastal Zones/SLR.
extraction_rationale: This is a named information-management intervention linked explicitly to coastal zones and sea-level rise adaptation.

policy_statement: Build and commission desalination plants, including Al-Zour North, Al-Zour South, Al Khiran and Doha, to protect freshwater supplies and maintain ecological stability.
source_quote: Building desalination plants . In the process of protecting freshwater sources and to maintain ecological stability. Kuwait has constructed several desalination plants in addition to water distribution systems via pipelines and irrigation systems to farmers.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete infrastructure investment with named plants and capacities elsewhere in the paragraph. It is an adaptation response to water scarcity, though desalination can increase energy use.

policy_statement: Invest USD 5.5 million jointly with MIT in research on updating current desalination plants and next-generation desalination plants.
source_quote: Kuwait is investing USD 5.5 million jointly with MIT to conduct researches on updating the current desalination plants and next-generation desalination plants . The adaptation Sector for this project is the Water Resources Sector, and the Government is responsible for the implementation of this project since 2016 and it is still ongoing.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified public investment in water adaptation technology research. It is a financial instrument because it commits a specific funding amount.

policy_statement: Educate rural households in low-cost in-house water desalination techniques.
source_quote: Education on household desalination . Kuwait jointly with United Nations taught the Kuwaiti people in rural areas the 'in-house water desalination techniques', where households can have freshwater at low cost and short time. The Adaptation Sector for this project is the Water Resources and the Awareness sectors.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific capacity-building and technology-transfer intervention for household freshwater access. It supports adaptation to water scarcity.

policy_statement: Implement Kuwait Integrated Environmental Information Network Phase IV as a GIS-based environmental indicator and spatial decision-support system.
source_quote: Kuwait Integrated Environmental Information Network Phase-IV . The KIEIN-IV is an integrated GIS-based system that compiles the environmental indicator data and acts as a spatial decision support system tools (SDSS). This project can: Compile data about environmental indicators for Kuwait.
extraction_rationale: This is a named information-system project with a budget and specified decision-support functions. It is relevant to adaptation monitoring and planning.

policy_statement: Implement the Kuwait Environmental Governance Initiative to design the National Adaptation Plan and related initiatives in water, city planning and other sectors.
source_quote: Kuwait Environmental Governance Initiative (KEGI) . The Project supports the design of the National Adaptation Plan (NAP) of Kuwait and the relevant initiatives linked to water, city planning, and other sectors. This project was running from 2017-2018 by the UNDP and EPA with a budget of $2,000,000.
extraction_rationale: This is a named, budgeted adaptation-governance project. It directly supports the NAP and sectoral adaptation initiatives.

policy_statement: Establish a series of land and marine nature reserves to safeguard Kuwait’s marine and land ecosystems.
source_quote: Establishment of land and marine nature reserves . The project aims to establish a series of land and marine nature reserves in the State of Kuwait. National reserves were implemented to safeguard the Kuwait marine and land ecosystems.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific ecosystem-protection intervention. It qualifies as a nature-based solution supporting resilience, though the quoted passage frames it broadly as ecosystem safeguarding.

policy_statement: Apply water conservation technologies to reduce water consumption by 20%.
source_quote: Water Conservation (Partially implemented) Kuwait's Initial National Communications ; the application of water conservation technologies was also one of the adaptation options to reduce water consumption by 20 %. The Water Resources Sector was responsible, and the project started in 2012 and is still ongoing.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantifiable water-efficiency target using named technologies. It is an adaptation option but the primary mechanism is resource efficiency.

policy_statement: Establish a Coastal Information System to support protection of coastal zones and marine environments and inform planners and decision makers.
source_quote: Establishing a Coastal information system (CIS) ; Coastal Information System (CIS) was established to help in the protection of coastal zones and marine environments in Kuwait. CIS provides information about Kuwait's coastal area to planners and decision makers. The CIS system is an important initiative under the technology needs assessment of the coastal zones and shore protection sector as a climate change adaptation measure.
extraction_rationale: This is a named adaptation technology and information system for coastal protection. It directly supports adaptation to coastal climate risks.

policy_statement: Construct tidal gate systems and offshore breakwaters in new coastal developments to protect against wave erosion and rising sea levels.
source_quote: Constructing tidal barriers in new developments ; Sabah Al Ahmad Sea City, which is located near the Saudi Arabia border, is a new development which constructed a tidal gate system and offshore breakwater was built to protect the artificial promenade from erosion of waves and to cope with the rising sea levels as the adverse impact of climate change. The project was completed in 2016 under the Technology Needs Assessment / Coastal Zones Sectors by different Developers.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete coastal engineering intervention explicitly tied to sea-level rise and climate change impacts.

policy_statement: Conduct awareness campaigns and symposiums on sea-level rise adaptation for stakeholders and the public.
source_quote: Conducting awareness campaigns and symposiums regarding Sea level rise ; the 'Our Seas: Theories, Data, and Policies' Symposium highlighted the importance of human intervention regarding rising sea levels. International specialists, local researchers, and non-governmental organizations attended this symposium. This symposium aimed at increasing the awareness of the concerned stakeholders and the public about the adaptation to sea level rise as an impact of climate change.
extraction_rationale: This is a named awareness and capacity-building intervention focused on adaptation to sea-level rise.

policy_statement: Implement the Coastal Management Program and Integrated Coastal Zone Management to identify best-practice guidelines for coastal development.
source_quote: Coastal Management Program ; the CMP produces physical modeling, numerical modeling and field survey measurements. The CMP was responsible to produce Integrated Coastal Zone Management (ICZM) for Kuwait. The ICZM consists of two phases, Phase 1 has already completed.
extraction_rationale: This is a named planning and modeling programme for coastal management. It qualifies because it provides a concrete governance mechanism for climate-vulnerable coastal zones.

policy_statement: Implement the Water Resources Development and Management Program to optimize water use and management and develop integrated water policies and action plans.
source_quote: Establishment of the Water Resources Program ; A water resources development and management program (WRDM) was initiated by the Kuwait Institute for Science and Research (KISR). This program helps to identify ways to optimize the water resources use and management through applied research. WRDM program was designed to develop integrated water policies, management options, and action plans to solve water scarcity problems and increase Kuwait's water security and resilience.
extraction_rationale: This is a named programme with explicit water-management and policy outputs. It is primarily resource efficiency, with direct adaptation relevance through water security and resilience.

policy_statement: Operate Multi-Stage Flash desalination units with a total production capacity of 234 MGD.
source_quote: Constructing Desalination using Multi-Stage Flash technology ; Kuwait has a total of 40 operating Multi-Stage Flash desalination units (MSF), with a total production capacity of 234 MGD. The project was completed by the Government and the MEW under the Technology Needs Assessment / Water Resources Sectors.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific water-supply infrastructure measure with quantified capacity. It is adaptation-relevant for water scarcity, though energy implications are not addressed in the quote.

policy_statement: Conduct wastewater treatment and reclamation research and reuse treated wastewater for irrigation.
source_quote: Wastewater Treatment and Reclamation Technologies Program ; this program has been initiated by KISR and it aims at conducting research on reclaiming and reusing Kuwait's wastewater to utilize it in irrigation purposes. This is a good example to adapt to climate change stresses on water resources. Ministry of Public Works (MPW) stated that about 65% of its treated wastewater is reused in irrigation already.
extraction_rationale: This is a named wastewater reuse programme with a quantified reuse figure. The primary mechanism is resource efficiency, and the text explicitly frames it as adaptation to climate stress on water resources.

policy_statement: Conduct an awareness campaign on Articles 76 and 79 concerning ambient air, air quality zone compliance, emission sources and evaluation.
source_quote: Awareness Campaign of KEPA Articles 76 and 79; an awareness campaign has been conducted to increase the awareness about Article No. 76 regarding the ambient air and Air Quality Zone Compliance actions and Article No. 79 regarding the emission sources and evaluation. The responsible parties for this project were the EPA and the UNDP and the adaptation sectors for this project were the Technology Needs Assessment / Public Health sectors.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete awareness campaign tied to regulatory air-quality provisions. The climate link is indirect through public health and air-quality resilience.

policy_statement: Operate the Beatona Initiative website to provide real-time environmental information and GIS layers to raise public awareness of climate change adaptation.
source_quote: Beatona Initiative ; Beatona Initiative is a website established by EPA and aims to increase the public awareness of the health sector of the climate change adaptation through sharing real-time environmental news and information with the public. The beatona website includes multi-layers GIS maps such as the monitoring stations of air quality, the noise monitoring locations, the drainage streamlines, and water bodies. The project started in 2012 by the EPA and is still ongoing.
extraction_rationale: This is a named public-awareness and information platform with specific monitoring content. It directly supports climate adaptation awareness in the health sector.

policy_statement: Implement the Tarsheed campaign to reduce per-capita consumption of electricity and water.
source_quote: Tarsheed Campaign ; Tarsheed campaign was an Initiative made to reduce the percapita consumption of electricity and water. This awareness initiative is a good adaptation step to climate change in water resources. The responsible parties were Kharafi National and the EPA.
extraction_rationale: This is a named resource-conservation campaign. It is primarily resource efficiency, with adaptation relevance for water resources.

policy_statement: Implement Tarsheed Campaign II to encourage Reduce, Reuse and Recycle waste management.
source_quote: Tarsheed Campaign II ; Tarsheed campaign II was an Initiative to encourage the implementation of the 'Reduce, Reuse and Recycle' waste management. Such an initiative is useful as a climate change adaptation under the waste sector. The Kharafi National was able to complete this project in 2013 under the Public awareness sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a named waste-reduction campaign with a concrete 3R intervention. The text frames it as climate adaptation in the waste sector.

policy_statement: Use treated sewage effluent from Umm Al-Hayman wastewater treatment plant for irrigation of green and agricultural areas.
source_quote: Utilizing TSE water generated from Umm Al-Hayman WWTP in Irrigation purposes ; TSE is utilized to irrigate the green areas and agricultural areas and serve the expected population growth of Kuwait, in addition, to mitigate the negative effects on the environment. The Ministry of Public Works (MPW) held this project from 20122018 under the Water Resources Sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific water-reuse project tied to irrigation and population growth. It is primarily resource efficiency and supports water adaptation.

policy_statement: Issue and implement a national law stopping outdoor work from 11:00 AM to 16:00 PM during June through August.
source_quote: Adjust the official working hours Initiative Source : the Ministry of Social Affairs and Labor of Kuwait issued a national law in 2005 to stop any outdoor work from 11:00 AM to 16:00 PM during the months of June through August. The EPA started this project in 2018 under the Public Health Sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a binding labor regulation with a precise seasonal and daily schedule. It directly reduces heat-related health risks.

policy_statement: Prepare Kuwait’s Second National Communication and first Biennial Update Report to meet UNFCCC obligations.
source_quote: Enabling Kuwait to Prepare it's Second National Communication (SNC) and Biennial Update Report (BUR) to the UNFCCC ; the project aims at supporting Kuwait to prepare and deliver its Second National Communication and first Biennial Update Report. The project also enables Kuwait to fulfill its UNFCCC obligations. The Global Environmental Facility (GEF) started this project in 2014 with a budget of $1,517,000.
extraction_rationale: This is a named reporting and capacity-building project with budgeted funding. It supports both mitigation and adaptation reporting under the UNFCCC.

policy_statement: Implement the Environmental Pollution and Climate Program to assess pollution and climate change challenges across Kuwait’s atmospheric, aquatic and terrestrial environments.
source_quote: The Environmental Pollution and Climate (EPC) Program ; this program aims at assessing the pollution and climate change challenges concerning the atmospheric, aquatic, and terrestrial environment of Kuwait. This project is still ongoing under the responsibility of KISR.
extraction_rationale: This is a named research and assessment programme explicitly addressing climate challenges. It supports adaptation planning across multiple environmental systems.

policy_statement: Collect and recycle empty plastic bottles through the Omniya initiative instead of sending them to landfills.
source_quote: Omniya Plastic bottles recycle ; an initiative to collect the empty plastic bottles and recycling it instead of sending to landfills which is one of few practical initiatives to adapt to climate change in waste sectors. The project started in 2015 by an NGO and is still ongoing under the Waste Sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific recycling initiative. It is primarily resource efficiency and waste diversion, with the document framing it as climate adaptation in the waste sector.

policy_statement: Ratify the UNFCCC as a general climate policy framework.
source_quote: Table 17 provides the main policies and strategies on adaptation to climate change that were ratified by Kuwait. UNFCCC Ratification | Kuwait has ratified the UNFCCC. | General | 1995 | EPA/ Kuwait.
section_header: 4.3 Policies and Strategies on Climate Change Adaptation
extraction_rationale: Ratification of the UNFCCC is a binding international climate-policy commitment. It is broad rather than sector-specific.

policy_statement: Ratify the Kyoto Protocol.
source_quote: Table 17 provides the main policies and strategies on adaptation to climate change that were ratified by Kuwait. Kyoto Protocol Ratification | Kuwait has ratified the Kyoto protocol. | General | 2005 | EPA/ Kuwait.
section_header: 4.3 Policies and Strategies on Climate Change Adaptation
extraction_rationale: Kyoto Protocol ratification is a binding international climate mitigation commitment. The table does not specify domestic implementation measures.

policy_statement: Ratify the Paris Agreement on climate change.
source_quote: Table 17 provides the main policies and strategies on adaptation to climate change that were ratified by Kuwait. Paris Agreement on climate change | Kuwait has ratified the Paris Agreement on climate change. | General | 2016 | EPA/ Kuwait.
section_header: 4.3 Policies and Strategies on Climate Change Adaptation
extraction_rationale: Paris Agreement ratification is a binding international climate-policy commitment covering mitigation and adaptation. The table gives no detailed national measures.

policy_statement: Ratify the UN Convention to Combat Desertification.
source_quote: Table 17 provides the main policies and strategies on adaptation to climate change that were ratified by Kuwait. UNCCD Ratification | Kuwait has ratified the UNCCD. | General | 1995 | EPA/ Kuwait.
section_header: 4.3 Policies and Strategies on Climate Change Adaptation
extraction_rationale: UNCCD ratification is a binding international environmental commitment relevant to arid-land climate adaptation and desertification control.

policy_statement: Ratify and implement biodiversity monitoring and institutional capacity commitments under the Convention on Biological Diversity.
source_quote: CBD Ratification | Monitor the biological diversity of Kuwait. Build the necessary institutional structure to deal with biodiversity issues in Kuwait 36 . | General | 2002 | EPA/Kuwait / UNDP. Table 17 provides the main policies and strategies on adaptation to climate change that were ratified by Kuwait.
section_header: 4.3 Policies and Strategies on Climate Change Adaptation
extraction_rationale: This is a ratified environmental policy with concrete biodiversity monitoring and institutional actions. Its climate relevance is indirect through ecosystem resilience.

policy_statement: Ratify the Convention on Wetlands of International Importance, especially waterfowl habitat.
source_quote: The Convention on Wetlands | The convention was on Wetlands of International Importance especially waterfowl habitat, in Ramsar, Iran. | General | 2014 | EPA/ Kuwait. Table 17 provides the main policies and strategies on adaptation to climate change that were ratified by Kuwait.
section_header: 4.3 Policies and Strategies on Climate Change Adaptation
extraction_rationale: Wetland protection is an ecosystem-based policy relevant to biodiversity and potential climate resilience. The table does not explicitly name climate hazards, so climate relevance is indirect.

policy_statement: Issue Articles 76 and 79 on ambient air, air quality zone compliance, emission sources and evaluation.
source_quote: Issuing new Articles No. 76 and 79. | Article No. 76 regarding the ambient air and Air Quality Zone Compliance actions and Article No. 79 regarding the emission sources and evaluation. | Air Quality /Public Health | 2010 | EPA/Kuwait.
section_header: 4.3 Policies and Strategies on Climate Change Adaptation
extraction_rationale: These are regulatory provisions addressing air quality and emission sources. Their climate relevance is indirect through public health and emissions management.

policy_statement: Adopt a national policy for funding environmental research projects, especially oil pollution and burning oil wells impact projects.
source_quote: Environmental Research National policy | National policy has been adopted for funding the Environmental Research Projects in Kuwait, especially the projects dealing with the impacts of oil pollution and burning oil wells. | General | 1991 | EPA/ Kuwait.
section_header: 4.3 Policies and Strategies on Climate Change Adaptation
extraction_rationale: This is a funding policy for environmental research. Its climate relevance is indirect because it addresses environmental impacts of oil pollution and burning oil wells rather than a specific climate adaptation or mitigation target.

policy_statement: Implement Environment Protection Law No. 42/2014 to adapt to climate impacts, reduce desertification, manage natural reserves and water resources, and create disaster-management plans.
source_quote: Environment Protection Law No. 42/2014 | Adapting to the adverse impacts of climate change. The protection of land and soil, reducing desertification, management of natural reserves and water resources and creating plans for disaster management. | General/ Safety and Health | 2014 | The Environmental Public Authority / Environmental Supreme Council / / Kuwait.
section_header: 4.3 Policies and Strategies on Climate Change Adaptation
extraction_rationale: This is a binding national law explicitly addressing climate adaptation and disaster management. It includes ecosystem, land, reserve and water measures.

policy_statement: Implement a budgeted adaptation plan to increase the resilience of Kuwait’s fisheries and marine sector to climate change.
source_quote: Increase the resilience of the fisheries and marine sector to climate change. Budget 3.4 million USD. Responsibility • Public Authority for Agricultural Affairs and Fish Resources (PAAFR). • Kuwait Environment Protection Authority (KEPA) • Kuwait Institute for Scientific Research (KISR). • The General Secretariat of the Supreme Council for Planning and Development (SCPD)
section_header: 5.3.1 Adaptation Plans to enhance the resilience of the Fisheries and Marine Sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a named sectoral adaptation plan with a specified budget and responsible institutions. It has multiple listed short-, medium- and long-term actions.

parent_statement: Increase the resilience of the fisheries and marine sector to climate change
policy_statement: Undertake short-term fisheries and marine actions on awareness, financial and technical support, risk assessment and capacity building.
source_quote: Short-term actions ▪ Enhance awareness by involving the local community in the protection and sustainable consumption of marine life. ▪ Provide financial and technical support to institutions and sectors responsible for marine life protection. ▪ Increase awareness about the Marine Ecosystem and the impact of climate change on it. ▪ Undertake risk and vulnerability assessment of the fishers' value chain. ▪ Enhance technical (individual and institutional) capacities on the impact of climate change on fisheries.
section_header: 5.3.1 Adaptation Plans to enhance the resilience of the Fisheries and Marine Sector.
extraction_rationale: The short-term action package lists concrete interventions for marine-life protection and climate-risk capacity building. One item is financial support, but the package is primarily operational rather than a broad financial instrument.

parent_statement: Increase the resilience of the fisheries and marine sector to climate change
policy_statement: Designate new marine protected areas and implement marine conservation, restoration, research and biodiversity initiatives.
source_quote: Medium-term actions ▪ Designation of new marine protected areas. ▪ Develop and implement local marine conservation and restoration options. ▪ Develop adaptation and development plans for Marine life and Fisheries. ▪ Support research and initiatives to gather and obtain enough information on the impact of Climate Change on the marine ecosystem in Kuwait. ▪ Develop medium-term initiatives to conserve marine biodiversity in the rapidly changing climate.
section_header: 5.3.1 Adaptation Plans to enhance the resilience of the Fisheries and Marine Sector.
extraction_rationale: This package includes concrete protected-area designation, conservation and restoration actions. The primary mechanism is ecosystem-based protection, with explicit climate adaptation planning.

parent_statement: Increase the resilience of the fisheries and marine sector to climate change
policy_statement: Prepare ecosystem-based adaptation, adaptive management, prediction, monitoring, modeling and crisis-management measures for marine climate impacts.
source_quote: Long-term actions ▪ Prepare of marine ecosystem-based adaptation strategy measures in areas at risk of climate change impacts. ▪ Develop adaptive management to rapidly changing marine regimes with Climate Change. ▪ Develop prediction capacity to anticipate possible future consequences of Climate Change and most threatened ecosystems in the marine.
section_header: 5.3.1 Adaptation Plans to enhance the resilience of the Fisheries and Marine Sector.
extraction_rationale: These are concrete long-term governance, modeling and ecosystem-based adaptation actions. The text explicitly names ecosystem-based adaptation and climate change impacts.

policy_statement: Implement a budgeted adaptation plan to improve resilience of Kuwait’s water sector systems.
source_quote: Improve the resilience of systems for the water sector. Budget 6.2 million USD. Responsibility • Ministry of Electricity and Water • KISR. • Kuwait Environment Protection Authority (KEPA) • The General Secretariat of the Supreme Council for Planning and Development (SCPD) • Kuwait Municipality • The oil sectors.
section_header: 5.3.2 Adaptation Plans to enhance the resilience of the Water Resources
extraction_rationale: This is a named sectoral plan with a quantified budget and responsible institutions. It contains short-, medium- and long-term water adaptation measures.

parent_statement: Improve the resilience of systems for the water sector
policy_statement: Raise awareness, deploy water conservation technologies and assess climate-change risks to water-resource depletion.
source_quote: Short-term actions ▪ Raise awareness of Climate Change Effects on Water Resources in the country. ▪ Utilize water conservation technologies. ▪ Develop risk assessment on water resources depletion in the face of Climate Change conditions in Kuwait.
section_header: 5.3.2 Adaptation Plans to enhance the resilience of the Water Resources
extraction_rationale: This short-term package includes specific awareness, technology and risk-assessment actions. It is resource efficiency with explicit climate adaptation relevance.

parent_statement: Improve the resilience of systems for the water sector
policy_statement: Integrate climate adaptation into water-sector actions, use water-level modeling, manage pricing and tariffs, reduce consumption and improve irrigation efficiency.
source_quote: Medium-term actions ▪ Incorporate measures for adaptation to climate change into actions carried out by the Ministry of Electricity and Water. ▪ Invest in high end and accurate programs to refer to information about water level based on hydraulic models. ▪ Control water prices such as water consumption are fair and reasonable by all consumers. ▪ Increase water block-tariff to control unnecessary water consumption.
section_header: 5.3.2 Adaptation Plans to enhance the resilience of the Water Resources
extraction_rationale: This package includes specific policy, modeling, pricing and tariff measures. The tariff element is a financial instrument, and the primary causal mechanism is reducing inefficient water use.

parent_statement: Improve the resilience of systems for the water sector
policy_statement: Develop long-term policies, research, reverse-osmosis treatment, household water-efficient devices and integrated climate-hydrological models for water management.
source_quote: Long-term actions ▪ Design effective policies to preserve and protect water resources. ▪ Support research and development to model the impact of climate change on water resources. ▪ Involve more environmentally sustainable methods of water treatment like Reverse osmosis, where the net energy consumption is lower than other methods. ▪ Invest in the installment of water-efficient devices in homes, where the consumption of water is better regulated and limited.
section_header: 5.3.2 Adaptation Plans to enhance the resilience of the Water Resources
extraction_rationale: This package commits to policy design, R&D, efficient treatment technology and household devices. It is resource efficiency with explicit climate-impact modeling.

policy_statement: Implement a budgeted adaptation plan to enhance coastal-zone resilience to sea-level-rise risks.
source_quote: Enhancing the resilience of coastal zones to face SLR risks. Budget 7.8 million USD. Responsibility • Kuwait Environment Protection Authority (KEPA) • The General Secretariat of the Supreme Council for Planning and Development (SCPD). • KISR • Kuwait University • Ministry of Municipal Affairs.
section_header: 5.3.3 Adaptation Plans to enhance the resilience of the Coastal Zone
extraction_rationale: This is a named sectoral plan with budget, responsible agencies and listed action packages. It directly targets sea-level-rise risks.

parent_statement: Enhancing the resilience of coastal zones to face SLR risks
policy_statement: Develop coastal vulnerability and risk assessments, open information networks, capacity building, decision-maker awareness and project reviews based on SNC and NAP findings.
source_quote: Short-term actions ▪ Develop vulnerability and risk assessment reports ▪ Provide open access for information and communication networks for parties and sectors responsible ▪ Capacity-building for government and non- government stakeholders on the deployment of adaptation activities. ▪ Increase decision-makers awareness of the risks of SLR and the damages to nearby urban areas. ▪ Review existed projects and update them based on SNC and NAP findings.
section_header: 5.3.3 Adaptation Plans to enhance the resilience of the Coastal Zone
extraction_rationale: This package contains concrete planning, information-access and capacity-building measures for sea-level-rise adaptation.

parent_statement: Enhancing the resilience of coastal zones to face SLR risks
policy_statement: Provide financial aid and resources for coastal protection, incorporate sea-level-rise scenarios into development plans, and legislate restrictions on harmful coastal activities.
source_quote: Medium-term actions ▪ Provide financial aid for preventative and protective actions for coastal damage. ▪ Make sure that the required resources to undergo projects and initiatives concerning the construction, research or communication are available. ▪ Raising awareness among decision-makers in Kuwait to incorporate SLR scenarios into development plans ▪ Legislating laws to restrict negative anthropogenic activities in the coastal zones to maintain the coastal wildlife
section_header: 5.3.3 Adaptation Plans to enhance the resilience of the Coastal Zone
extraction_rationale: This package includes financial aid, resource allocation, planning integration and legislation. It directly targets coastal damage and SLR adaptation.

parent_statement: Enhancing the resilience of coastal zones to face SLR risks
policy_statement: Establish a coastal management center, build coastal protection barriers, strengthen coastline laws and require future coastal construction to withstand sea-level-rise scenarios.
source_quote: Long-term actions ▪ Establish a specialized center for coastal management and build and organize information and tools for climate risk modeling and generation of qualified responses within the Coastal Zone. ▪ Protect coastlines from SLR by constructing protection barriers. ▪ Develop better and more intensive laws and policies regarding coastline protection and conservation. ▪ Prepare for better adaptation potential for future setbacks and scenarios (i.e. new construction projects near the high-risk coastline should withstand SLR scenario in the future).
section_header: 5.3.3 Adaptation Plans to enhance the resilience of the Coastal Zone
extraction_rationale: These are concrete institutional, infrastructure, regulatory and construction-resilience measures for sea-level-rise risk.

policy_statement: Implement a budgeted plan to build health-sector capacity for increased climate-related health risks.
source_quote: Enhance and building the capacity of the health sector to be prepared for increased health risks due to climate change. Budget 4.1 million USD. Responsibility Ministry of Health Ministry of Higher Education Ministry of Electricity and Water KEPA. Ministry of Finance. Ministry of Services Affairs. Ministry of Information
section_header: 5.3.4 Adaptation Plans to enhance the resilience of the Human Health Sector
extraction_rationale: This is a named health adaptation plan with a specified budget and responsible ministries. It directly addresses climate-related health risks.

parent_statement: Enhance and building the capacity of the health sector to be prepared for increased health risks due to climate change
policy_statement: Raise public and media awareness, assess health vulnerability, adjust work hours, and establish national health alerts for dust storms and heat waves.
source_quote: Short term actions ▪ Increase public awareness of climate changes effects and impacts on general health. ▪ Conduct risk assessments and vulnerability to Climate Change on the general public. ▪ Involve the media in carrying the message of issues of Health, as people get more influenced and receive the message more directly and subconsciously through advertisement and social media sites.
section_header: 5.3.4 Adaptation Plans to enhance the resilience of the Human Health Sector
extraction_rationale: This short-term package lists public awareness, risk assessment and communication interventions. The longer bullet list also includes work-hour adjustment and health alerts, making it a concrete health adaptation package.

parent_statement: Enhance and building the capacity of the health sector to be prepared for increased health risks due to climate change
policy_statement: Develop warning systems for extreme weather and increase drought-proof vegetation to reduce dust fallout from dust storms.
source_quote: Medium-term actions ▪ Develop warning systems for extreme weather conditions combined with a communication strategy for alerts. ▪ Increase drought-proof vegetation to reduce dust fallout from dust storms.
section_header: 5.3.4 Adaptation Plans to enhance the resilience of the Human Health Sector
extraction_rationale: This package includes early warning and vegetation-based dust control. The vegetation measure is an ecosystem-based adaptation response to the named hazard of dust storms.

parent_statement: Enhance and building the capacity of the health sector to be prepared for increased health risks due to climate change
policy_statement: Include climate-health information in early education curricula and establish a climate and health research and monitoring network.
source_quote: Long-term actions ▪ Include information and instructions about Climate Change Effects on Health in the early education curriculum. ▪ Establish a research and monitoring network on climate and health, with a focus on analyzing the expected climate change impact on health.
section_header: 5.3.4 Adaptation Plans to enhance the resilience of the Human Health Sector
extraction_rationale: This long-term package specifies curriculum integration and a research-monitoring network for climate-health impacts.

policy_statement: Incorporate resiliency and climate action/adaptation into all City land-use planning, policies, and standards.
source_quote:
Intentionally incorporate key issues of resiliency and climate action/adaptation into all land-use planning, policies, and standards.

Consider energy and water related goals to reduce demand such as human-scaled interventions, building scale incentive programs, deep energy retrofits, building code provisions, and partnerships at the City scale.
section_header: To achieve a resilient Las Vegas, we must:
extraction_rationale: This is a citywide planning and standards commitment explicitly tied to climate action/adaptation. It is somewhat broad, but qualifies because it names the binding implementation domains: land-use planning, policies, and standards.

policy_statement: Use energy and water demand-reduction measures such as building-scale incentives, deep energy retrofits, building code provisions, and partnerships.
source_quote:
Consider energy and water related goals to reduce demand such as human-scaled interventions, building scale incentive programs, deep energy retrofits, building code provisions, and partnerships at the City scale.

Lead policy  and  actions  as  a  City  within  a  framework  of  increased  multi-jurisdictional  cooperation  and regional partnership building.
section_header: To achieve a resilient Las Vegas, we must:
extraction_rationale: This qualifies because it names specific interventions: incentives, deep energy retrofits, building code provisions, and partnerships. The word 'consider' makes the commitment less binding, but it appears under a list of actions the City 'must' undertake.

policy_statement: Use smart growth development practices to protect limited resources and mitigate the urban heat island.
source_quote:
Protect  the  environment  for  future  generations  and  mitigate  urban  heat  island  by  using  smart  growth development practices to protect and maintain limited resources.

Effectively communicate the issues and risks we are facing as a community and the steps we are taking to address them.
section_header: To achieve a resilient Las Vegas, we must:
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete land-use policy direction using smart growth practices to address a named climate-related hazard, urban heat island. It is broad but action-oriented enough to qualify.

policy_statement: Adopt a strategic, balanced growth approach that aligns higher-density redevelopment with transit and transportation infrastructure improvements.
source_quote: The 'Strategic, Balanced Growth approach identifies key  opportunities  for  increased  density  and  mixed-use development  patterns  where  they  are  most  feasible  and desired. It aligns higher density redevelopment opportunities with transit and transportation infrastructure improvements and slightly more dense traditional suburban development in outlying areas. This approach  is the most effective and the basis of recommendations in the land use chapter.
extraction_rationale: The plan selects a specific growth alternative as the basis for land-use recommendations. It is climate-relevant through resource-efficient land use and transportation alignment, though climate is not the primary stated objective in this passage.

policy_statement: Implement an infill and transit-oriented development land-use strategy, supported by new place types, zoning typologies, and amendments to Title 19.
source_quote: To accomplish an infill strategy that ties with many additional goals throughout the plan, the plan links identified regional centers with mixed-use transit-oriented development (TOD) corridors, accented at key nodes. These corridors must be prioritized for higher density development that integrates a diverse range of affordable housing types. A number of new place types are recommended, as well as a corresponding land use tool-box, zoning typology, and modest amendments to Title 19, including:
extraction_rationale: This is a land-use implementation policy with specific interventions: infill, TOD corridors, higher-density prioritization, zoning typologies, and Title 19 amendments. Climate relevance is indirect through compact growth and transportation efficiency.

policy_statement: Use urban forestry and green infrastructure to reduce urban heat hazards.
source_quote:
Due to notable increases in the urban heat island effect, steps must be taken to reduce heat hazards with appropriate green infrastructure, including:

- LVMC and zoning amendments for trees
- At least 100,000 public and private high quality, native and adaptive trees that increase the canopy are planted to increase the canopy to 20%
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella initiative with listed sub-actions. It directly addresses the urban heat island effect through green infrastructure.

parent_statement: Urban Forestry
policy_statement: Amend the Las Vegas Municipal Code and zoning standards to support trees.
source_quote:
Due to notable increases in the urban heat island effect, steps must be taken to reduce heat hazards with appropriate green infrastructure, including:

- LVMC and zoning amendments for trees
- At least 100,000 public and private high quality, native and adaptive trees that increase the canopy are planted to increase the canopy to 20%
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory commitment to amend municipal code and zoning for trees. It is climate-relevant because it is explicitly framed as reducing heat hazards from the urban heat island effect.

parent_statement: Urban Forestry
policy_statement: Plant at least 100,000 high-quality native and adaptive public and private trees to increase canopy cover to 20%.
source_quote:
Due to notable increases in the urban heat island effect, steps must be taken to reduce heat hazards with appropriate green infrastructure, including:

- LVMC and zoning amendments for trees
- At least 100,000 public and private high quality, native and adaptive trees that increase the canopy are planted to increase the canopy to 20%
extraction_rationale: This is a quantifiable urban forestry target with a specific number of trees and canopy goal. It directly addresses urban heat hazards.

policy_statement: Improve the parks system through a Parks System Plan, higher park acreage, and expanded access to parks and trails.
source_quote:
Because parks and recreational facilities are an important quality of life component, park facilities, amenities, connections, and safety were frequently noted throughout public outreach. As a result, the City will

- Develop  a  Parks  System  Plan  and  achieve  CAPRA certification
- Increase park acreage to 7 acres per 1,000 residents, specifically in noted areas of need
- Ensure 85% of dwelling units are within a short walk of a park or trail
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella parks initiative with measurable and programmatic sub-actions. Its climate relevance is peripheral because the quoted text frames it primarily as quality of life, although parks and trails can function as urban green infrastructure.

parent_statement: Parks and Connectivity
policy_statement: Develop a Parks System Plan and achieve CAPRA certification.
source_quote:
