policy_statement: Require all new passenger cars, pickup trucks, and SUVs sold in New York to be zero-emission by 2035 through regulations modeled on California's Advanced Clean Cars II rule.
source_quote: Governor Hochul directed DEC to adopt regulations that will require all new passenger cars, pickup trucks, and SUVs sold in New York State be zero-emission by 2035 and be modeled on California's Advanced Clean Cars II regulation finalized in 2022. Chapter 423 of the Laws of 2021 commits 100% of all new, light-duty on-road vehicle sales in New York to be ZEVs by 2035, and directs DEC to develop and propose regulations, to the extent consistent with federal law, such as Advanced Clean Cars 2.
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory mandate with a quantifiable deadline for zero-emission vehicle sales.

policy_statement: Implement Advanced Clean Trucks standards for medium- and heavy-duty zero-emission trucks and large entity reporting.
source_quote: Advanced Clean Trucks (DEC 6 NYCRR Part 218 Regulation), adopted in 2021, incorporated California's Advanced Clean Truck zero-emission vehicle standards for MHD trucks as well as large entity reporting requirements for owners and operators of MHD trucks as part of New York's existing low emission vehicle program. In December 2021, DEC finalized the adoption of these regulations.
extraction_rationale: This is an adopted vehicle emissions regulation requiring zero-emission truck sales standards.

policy_statement: Regulate oil and natural gas sector methane and VOC emissions to support Climate Act goals.
source_quote: Oil and Natural Gas Sector regulations (DEC 6 NYCRR Part 203 Regulations), adopted and effective in 2022 to support the goals and requirements of the Climate Act, lowers methane and volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions for sources in New York's oil and natural gas sector. In addition to rigorous leak detection and repair requirements, the regulation aims to reduce or prohibit the venting of fossil natural gas at wells, compressor stations, storage sites, and metering and regulating stations.
extraction_rationale: This is an adopted regulatory standard targeting methane, a greenhouse gas, from oil and gas infrastructure.

policy_statement: Implement HFC standards and reporting rules prohibiting specified high-GWP HFC uses and updating rules to reflect Scoping Plan recommendations.
source_quote: Hydrofluorocarbon Standards and Reporting (DEC 6 NYCRR Part 494 Regulations) prohibits specific HFCs, potent GHGs in certain refrigerants, aerosol propellants, and foam-blowing agent end uses that represent avoidable HFC emissions where safer alternatives are available. In 2022, DEC began pre-proposal stakeholder outreach to update Part 494 to reflect the Scoping Plan recommendations.
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory greenhouse gas phase-down policy for high-GWP refrigerants and related uses.

policy_statement: Require large food scrap generators to donate edible food and recycle remaining scraps where organics recycling is available.
source_quote: Food Donation and Food Scraps Recycling (DEC 6 NYCRR Part 350 Regulations), adopted in 2022 pursuant to ECL Article 27, Title 22, requires large generators of food scraps to donate excess edible food and to recycle all remaining food scraps if they are located within 25 miles of an organics recycler, which will reduce methane and VOC emissions in support of the goals and requirements of the Climate Act. In 2019, New York passed the Food Donation and Food Scraps Recycling law.
extraction_rationale: This is a binding waste-management regulation that reduces methane by diverting organics from disposal.

policy_statement: Use sea-level rise projection regulations in permitting and decision-making under the Community Risk and Resiliency Act.
source_quote: Projected Sea-Level Rise (DEC 6 NYCRR Part 490 Regulations), finalized in early 2017, establishes statewide sea-level rise projections for use in the consideration of permits and other decision-making processes specified under CRRA. Under CRRA, DEC is required to update these sea-level rise projection regulations at least every five years.
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory adaptation policy using climate projections in permitting and public decisions.

policy_statement: Continue the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative cap-and-invest program for CO2 emissions from electric generation.
source_quote: Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative (RGGI; DEC 6 NYCRR Part 242 Regulations and NYSERDA 21 NYCRR Part 507) is the first mandatory market-based emissions trading program in the United States to reduce CO2 emissions and the first anywhere to use the cap-and-invest model for reducing pollution. New York and other RGGI-participating states set a cap for total emissions of CO2 from electric generation facilities in the region.
extraction_rationale: This is a market-based carbon cap-and-invest regulation with an emissions cap for power plants.

policy_statement: Impose a two-year moratorium on certain fossil-powered proof-of-work cryptocurrency mining permits and require a generic environmental impact statement.
source_quote: Chapter 628 of the Laws of 2022 established a two-year moratorium on the issuance of certain permits by DEC for cryptocurrency mining operations that use behind-the-meter electricity and proof-of-work authentication methods to validate blockchain transactions. This law directs DEC, in consultation with the New York State Department of Public Service (DPS), to prepare a generic environmental impact statement on this type of cryptocurrency mining operation.
extraction_rationale: This is a binding legislative moratorium targeting energy-intensive operations with potential emissions impacts.

policy_statement: Require DEC to study disproportionate urban heat island impacts in Disadvantaged Communities.
source_quote: Chapter 563 of the Laws of 2022 directs DEC to study the impacts of disproportionate heat conditions, otherwise known as urban heat islands, in Disadvantaged Communities. Recently enacted legislation requires the State to conduct a study on the impacts of the urban heat island effect in Disadvantaged Communities.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific statutory study requirement for a climate adaptation hazard affecting vulnerable communities.

policy_statement: Establish a regulatory structure for utility thermal energy networks and require utility pilot projects.
source_quote: Chapter 375 of the Laws of 2022 (Utility Thermal Energy Network and Jobs Act) requires the PSC to develop a regulatory structure for utility thermal energy networks, including district geothermal and other community-scale thermal infrastructure projects, for heating and cooling homes and to direct utilities to launch pilot projects in their service territories. For the operations and maintenance of thermal energy networks, the statute prioritizes hiring transitioning gas utility workers and requires that the utility enter into a labor peace agreement with a labor organization that represents gas and electric utility workers.
extraction_rationale: This is a binding statutory framework and pilot requirement for clean thermal infrastructure.

policy_statement: Strengthen building energy efficiency and GHG reduction through advanced building codes and expanded appliance and equipment efficiency standards.
source_quote: Chapter 374 of the Laws of 2022 (Advanced Building Codes, Appliance and Equipment Efficiency Standards Act of 2022) bolsters New York's regulatory and policy environment to support energy efficiency and GHG reduction strategies in buildings, expanded appliance standards, and changed building code law to allow the utilization of certain HFC substitutes. The Advanced Building Codes, Appliance and Equipment Efficiency Standards Act of 2022 requires the New York State Energy Conservation Construction Code (Energy Code) to be updated to achieve energy efficiency and GHG emission reductions in support of the Climate Act.
extraction_rationale: This is a statutory building code and appliance standards policy with explicit energy efficiency and GHG reduction objectives.

policy_statement: Require prevailing wage for qualifying renewable energy projects one megawatt and larger.
source_quote: Chapter 372 of the Laws of 2022 requires prevailing wage for renewable energy projects one megawatt and larger that involve the procurement of renewable energy credits from a public entity. These measures represent positive steps toward expanded labor standard coverage that should be replicated across sectors at appropriate junctures throughout the remaining work of Climate Act implementation, and again should apply across all construction, operations, maintenance, and repair activities.
extraction_rationale: This is a labor standard tied specifically to renewable energy project development; climate relevance is direct but implementation mechanism is workforce-focused.

policy_statement: Establish procurement guidelines for low-embodied-carbon concrete.
source_quote: Chapter 724 of the Laws of 2021 established procurement guidelines for low-embodied carbon concrete. New York recently passed a law that instructs OGS to examine available incentives, including bid discounts, to encourage the use of low-embodied carbon concrete in State agency projects.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific low-carbon materials procurement policy to reduce embodied emissions.

policy_statement: Target new non-road vehicles and equipment sold in New York to be zero-emission by 2035 and new medium- and heavy-duty vehicles by 2045.
source_quote: Chapter 423 of the Laws of 2021, as amended by Chapter 109 of the Laws of 2022, related to ZEV sales states that new non-road vehicles and equipment sold in New York are targeted to be zero-emissions by 2035 and that new MHD vehicles sold in New York are targeted to be zero-emissions by 2045. On September 8, 2021, Governor Hochul signed legislation establishing a goal that all new LDVs and non-road vehicles sold in the State be zero-emission by 2035 and all new MHD vehicles be zero-emission by 2045.
extraction_rationale: This is a statutory zero-emission vehicle and equipment target with dates.

policy_statement: Streamline siting and construction of large-scale renewable energy projects through the Accelerated Renewable Energy Growth and Community Benefit Act and Office of Renewable Energy Siting.
source_quote: Chapter 58 of the Laws of 2020 established the Accelerated Renewable Energy Growth and Community Benefit Act as part the State Fiscal Year 2020-2021 budget to dramatically speed up the siting and construction of clean energy projects to combat climate change and help jumpstart the State's economic recovery from the COVID-19 health crisis. This law created a first-in-the-nation Office of Renewable Energy Siting (ORES) to improve and streamline the process for the environmentally responsible and cost-effective siting of large-scale renewable energy projects across New York, while also delivering significant benefits to local communities.
extraction_rationale: This is a binding statutory siting reform for renewable energy deployment.

policy_statement: Implement congestion pricing in Manhattan's Central Business District to reduce congestion and enhance mobility.
source_quote: Chapter 59 of the Laws of 2019 established the Metropolitan Transportation Authority (MTA) Reform & Traffic Mobility Act (Congestion Pricing) that directs MTA to design, develop, build, and run a toll program that applies to vehicles that enter or remain in Manhattan's Central Business District. The purpose of the program is to reduce congestion and enhance mobility in Manhattan's Central Business District.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific transport pricing mechanism that reduces vehicle travel and associated emissions; climate objective is indirect in the quoted purpose but climate co-benefits are substantial.

policy_statement: Implement Community Risk and Resiliency Act requirements to build resilience to sea-level rise and extreme flooding.
source_quote: Chapter 355 of the Laws of 2014 established New York CRRA to build New York's resilience to rising sea levels and extreme flooding. The Climate Act made modifications to CRRA, expanding the scope of climate hazards and projects for consideration, which became effective January 1, 2020.
extraction_rationale: This is a statutory adaptation framework for climate hazards including sea-level rise and flooding.

policy_statement: Phase out coal-fired power plants in New York through CO2 emission limits for generating facilities.
source_quote: Chapter 388 of the Laws of 2011 established the Power NY Act, which directed DEC to promulgate rules and regulations limiting emissions of CO2 by newly constructed major generating facilities. DEC adopted 6 NYCRR Part 251 in 2012, setting CO2 emission limits that effectively prohibited new coal-fired power plants.
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory emissions standard that prohibited new coal plants and led to coal phaseout.

policy_statement: Implement the State Smart Growth Public Infrastructure Policy Act to prohibit State infrastructure support inconsistent with smart growth criteria.
source_quote: Chapter 433 of the Laws of 2010 established the State Smart Growth Public Infrastructure Policy Act, ECL Article 6, prohibiting a state infrastructure agency from approving, undertaking, supporting, or financing a 'public infrastructure project' unless, to the extent practicable, the project is consistent with 11 smart growth criteria. Smart growth land use patterns reduce GHG emissions largely in the transportation sector by reducing automobile use, measured as VMT.
extraction_rationale: This is a binding infrastructure approval standard that indirectly reduces transportation emissions through smart growth.

policy_statement: Transition the transportation sector to zero-emission vehicles and equipment.
source_quote: Transitioning the transportation sector to zero-emission technologies is central to achieving the State's GHG emission reduction requirements. In most cases, this means replacing existing vehicles that run on gasoline or diesel fuel with either battery electric, hydrogen fuel cell, or future zero-emission propulsion technologies.
section_header: Transition to Zero-Emission Vehicles and Equipment
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella transportation mitigation initiative with specific sub-strategies for light-duty vehicles and medium/heavy-duty vehicles, buses, and equipment.

parent_statement: Transition the transportation sector to zero-emission vehicles and equipment.
policy_statement: Accelerate adoption of light-duty zero-emission vehicles through Advanced Clean Cars II, purchase incentives, awareness, infrastructure investment, utility rate design, workforce development, and State fleet electrification.
source_quote: Chapter 423 of the Laws of 2021 commits 100% of all new, light-duty on-road vehicle sales in New York to be ZEVs by 2035, and directs DEC to develop and propose regulations, to the extent consistent with federal law, such as Advanced Clean Cars 2. DEC should adopt the Advanced Clean Cars 2 regulation that requires 100% light-duty ZEV sales by 2035, now that it has been finalized by California.
extraction_rationale: This is a named strategy with regulatory, incentive, infrastructure, and fleet actions to reduce transport emissions.

parent_statement: Transition the transportation sector to zero-emission vehicles and equipment.
policy_statement: Adopt and incentivize zero-emission trucks, buses, and non-road equipment, prioritizing fleets operating in overburdened communities.
source_quote: Converting New York's trucks, buses, and non-road equipment (including construction, farm, and forestry equipment) to zero-emissions technologies plays a dual role of both reducing GHG emissions from a major source and reducing local air pollution from one of the most significant sources of poor air quality and adverse health impacts. The State should fund direct incentives supporting the purchase of zero-emission trucks and buses, with a focus on fleets operating in LMI and overburdened communities, small fleets, and school buses, as well as non-road vehicles and equipment such as airport ground support equipment, port cargo handling equipment, construction, farm, and forestry equipment.
section_header: T2. Adoption of Zero-Emission Trucks, Buses, and Non-Road Equipment
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete zero-emission vehicle and equipment deployment policy with incentives and regulatory actions.

policy_statement: Enhance public transportation and mobility alternatives to reduce vehicle miles traveled and emissions.
source_quote: One of the more impactful supporting strategies for achieving the Climate Act's energy efficiency, housing, and land use GHG emission reduction requirements is through enhancing the availability, accessibility, reliability, and affordability of public transportation services with an emphasis on unserved and underserved communities. The strategies to achieve these goals involve service enhancements, MOD, convenience and connectivity, and fleet modernization.
section_header: Enhance Public Transportation and Mobility Alternatives
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella transportation resource-efficiency policy with multiple sub-strategies.

parent_statement: Enhance public transportation and mobility alternatives to reduce vehicle miles traveled and emissions.
policy_statement: Identify, plan, and implement community-based public transportation service enhancements and shared mobility or micro-transit services.
source_quote: The State should work with communities and service providers to design strategies that increase utilization of existing and new public transportation options and alternatives. Strategies should be context-specific and will differ between urban, suburban, and rural communities.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific transport service enhancement strategy to shift travel from personal vehicles.

parent_statement: Enhance public transportation and mobility alternatives to reduce vehicle miles traveled and emissions.
policy_statement: Improve public transportation ease of use through integrated fare media and user-friendly digital tools.
source_quote: The State should facilitate the development and implementation of strategies for making public transportation easier to use. This includes working with the public and private sector on simplified and integrated statewide fare media and deploying new phone-based application technologies that makes public transportation more logical and easier to navigate.
section_header: T4. Customer Convenience and Service Connectivity
extraction_rationale: This is a specific intervention to increase public transportation use and reduce reliance on personal vehicles.

parent_statement: Enhance public transportation and mobility alternatives to reduce vehicle miles traveled and emissions.
policy_statement: Transition public transportation fleets to zero-emission vehicles.
source_quote: The State should work with municipally sponsored public transportation systems on a plan to transition to all-electric, zeroemission public transportation vehicles at defined replacement schedules appropriate for the transit provider. The State has already taken action to implement this strategy by committing more than $100 million toward the electrification of 25% of the five largest fleets, outside the MTA, by 2025 and 100% by 2035.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified fleet electrification policy with committed funding and deadlines.

policy_statement: Promote smart growth and mobility-oriented development to reduce vehicle miles traveled and support low-carbon transportation.
source_quote: Smart growth land use patterns facilitate reductions in GHG emissions in the transportation sector by reducing VMT, increasing the viability and practicality of low-carbon transportation modes, and decreasing the travel distance between locations through a denser concentration and mix of residential and commercial development. Personal travel is often enhanced by the increased availability of mobility alternatives, including walking, biking, and public transportation.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella land-use and transportation policy with multiple specific sub-strategies.

parent_statement: Promote smart growth and mobility-oriented development to reduce vehicle miles traveled and support low-carbon transportation.
policy_statement: Coordinate investments in mobility-oriented development, tie business development incentives to mobility access, revise design manuals, and designate priority development areas.
source_quote: To reach GHG emissions reduction requirements, the State should place greater emphasis on programs and projects that that enable greater use of public transportation and other low-carbon mobility alternatives and investments that are informed by criteria that maximize sustainable land use/development patterns and climate outcomes. The State should establish an interagency, multi-stakeholder, multi-disciplinary strategy to coordinate investments in and around mobility centers, which should include DOS, DOT, ESD, DASNY, DEC, NYSERDA, DOL, the Office of Just Transition, and other relevant agencies.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific land-use and transport planning strategy that supports emissions reduction through mode shift and compact development.

parent_statement: Promote smart growth and mobility-oriented development to reduce vehicle miles traveled and support low-carbon transportation.
policy_statement: Launch public education and awareness efforts on smart growth, transportation, transit, housing, and climate benefits.
source_quote: Public perception is critical to understanding and expanding smart growth. Led by DOS, the State should develop and launch an expansive, multi-dimensional, grass-roots public education campaign on the links between smart growth, transportation, transit, and housing; their roles in reversing climate change; best practices for sustainable smart growth actions at the local level; and the many benefits of smart growth.
section_header: T7. Smart Growth Public Education and Awareness
extraction_rationale: This is a capacity-building and outreach policy to support adoption of smart growth climate strategies.

parent_statement: Promote smart growth and mobility-oriented development to reduce vehicle miles traveled and support low-carbon transportation.
policy_statement: Expand low-carbon transportation alternatives through smart growth law updates, low-emission zones, car-free streets, bike, pedestrian, transit, and complete streets funding.
source_quote: MOD and priority development areas are highly dependent upon the availability of low- and zeroemission transportation alternatives to complete the first mile/last mile of trips. The State should prioritize investments in local projects that establish low-emission transportation zones, car-free streets, and similar concepts that encourage travelers to take alternative transportation modes and support the infrastructure required to shift freight to lower-emission modes, like rail, cargo bikes, and electric trucks.
section_header: T8. Expanding the Availability of Low-Carbon Transportation Alternatives
extraction_rationale: This is a specific package of mobility infrastructure interventions to reduce vehicle travel and emissions.

parent_statement: Promote smart growth and mobility-oriented development to reduce vehicle miles traveled and support low-carbon transportation.
policy_statement: Support intelligent transportation systems, automated vehicle policies, open transportation data, cybersecurity, and apps that support efficient low-carbon mobility.
source_quote: Emerging technologies like automated vehicles (aVs), shared mobility services, and Internet-of-Things-enabled infrastructure could be used to reduce energy use and emissions from transportation if used in a coordinated and constructive manner. NYSERDA should invest in research, development, and demonstration (RD&D) and demonstrations of emerging intelligent transportation systems, connected vehicles and aVs, and fund the broader adoption of technologies that prove effective in improving transportation system efficiency, such as smart parking systems, adaptive traffic lights, and Internet-of-Things-enabled streetlights.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific technology and RD&D strategy for transportation system efficiency and emissions reduction.

policy_statement: Facilitate market-based transportation solutions and financing to fund and incentivize decarbonization.
source_quote: The strategies and policies referenced in this chapter for decarbonizing the transportation sector will require substantial private and public investment. These investments should be facilitated, in part, through marketbased and other supportive policies that generate resources necessary to implement investments required to achieve the Climate Act requirements and goals.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella financial and market-based transportation decarbonization initiative with several sub-policies.

parent_statement: Facilitate market-based transportation solutions and financing to fund and incentivize decarbonization.
policy_statement: Adopt transportation market-based policies including parking pricing, vehicle registration fees, mileage-based user fees, and special assessment mechanisms.
source_quote: Market-based policies focused solely on the transportation sector can provide the dual benefits of discouraging more costly carbon-intensive behavior and providing a revenue source for investment in other strategies. The State should enact legislation establishing a system of registration fees that would discourage the purchase and continued use of more carbon intensive vehicles.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific financial instrument strategy to discourage high-carbon travel and fund alternatives.

parent_statement: Facilitate market-based transportation solutions and financing to fund and incentivize decarbonization.
policy_statement: Unlock private financing for zero-emission vehicles through first-loss protection, fleet feasibility studies, and expanded NY Green Bank authority.
source_quote: The purchase of ZEVs can be facilitated by increasing the availability of low-cost capital/bank loans to fund the higher upfront costs of commercial ZEVs. New York should identify a State agency or authority to guarantee at least a portion of the residual value of the ZEVs being financed at the end of the loan term (such as First Loss Protection).
extraction_rationale: This is a financial-support policy to overcome upfront capital barriers to transport electrification.

parent_statement: Facilitate market-based transportation solutions and financing to fund and incentivize decarbonization.
policy_statement: Evaluate and consider adopting a clean transportation standard that prioritizes electrification and supports low-carbon transportation fuels where appropriate.
source_quote: DEC and NYSERDA should evaluate and consider adopting a variation on a clean fuel standard that would, as described in more detail below, support the transition to electrification, expanded transit, and clean transportation alternatives, particularly in Disadvantaged Communities. A traditional clean fuel standard is a policy mechanism to facilitate decarbonization of transportation fuels by requiring fossil fuel providers to reduce the carbon content of the fuels they provide by either acquiring credits from providers of electricity for transportation use or other zero-carbon or lower-carbon fuels into the stream of commerce or by blending lower-carbon fuels into their fuel mixes.
extraction_rationale: This is a market-based fuel decarbonization policy under evaluation; it is concrete but still framed as evaluate and consider.

policy_statement: Adopt zero-emission codes and standards and require energy benchmarking for buildings.
source_quote: When new buildings are constructed, clear and cost-effective opportunities exist for decarbonizing building operations and reducing embodied carbon emissions. Advanced codes will minimize the near-term installation of additional fossil fuel equipment and ensure that new buildings going forward are resilient to the impacts of climate change.
section_header: Adopt Zero-Emission Codes and Standards and Require Energy Benchmarking for Buildings
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella buildings policy with sub-strategies on codes, standards, and benchmarking.

parent_statement: Adopt zero-emission codes and standards and require energy benchmarking for buildings.
policy_statement: Adopt advanced State codes for highly efficient, zero-emission, and resilient new construction.
source_quote: This Scoping Plan recommends adopting zero-emission State codes as an important policy lever that can contribute to the rapid transformation presented in the integration analysis. The State should adopt comparable codes, applicable to all municipalities, to prohibit fossil fuel combustion systems and fossil fuel combustion equipment in new construction.
section_header: B1. Adopt Advanced Codes for Highly Efficient, Zero-Emission, and Resilient New Construction
extraction_rationale: This is a clear building code policy prohibiting fossil fuel equipment in new construction and requiring efficiency/resilience.

parent_statement: Adopt zero-emission codes and standards and require energy benchmarking for buildings.
policy_statement: Adopt standards for zero-emission equipment and energy performance in existing buildings, including phaseout of fossil fuel equipment at end of useful life.
source_quote: For existing buildings, New York should require the sale and installation of energy-efficient and zeroemission new equipment for space heating and hot water, when replaced at the equipment's end of useful life in residential and commercial buildings. The State should further require efficiency upgrades for large buildings through a building performance standard.
section_header: B2. Adopt Standards for Zero-Emission Equipment and the Energy Performance of Existing Buildings
extraction_rationale: This is a specific regulatory standards strategy for existing building equipment and performance.

parent_statement: Adopt zero-emission codes and standards and require energy benchmarking for buildings.
policy_statement: Require building energy benchmarking, disclosure, audits, and energy performance information at sale or lease.
source_quote: Energy consumption benchmarking provides building decision-makers with information to improve building operations and investment decisions, and the data collected statewide will inform building performance standards. The State must also mitigate against and monitor for potential harm to Disadvantaged Communities.
section_header: B3. Require Energy Benchmarking and Disclosure
extraction_rationale: This is a specific reporting and disclosure policy to support efficiency and performance standards.

policy_statement: Scale up public financial incentives and expand low-cost financing for building decarbonization.
source_quote: A substantial infusion of both public resources and private capital will be needed to pay for the building upgrades necessary to decarbonize buildings, while also expanding access to safe and healthy housing and bolstering resilience to climate impacts. The integration analysis indicates that to meet the Climate Act's GHG emission reduction requirements, more than 250,000 housing units each year will need to adopt electric heat pumps and energy efficiency measures from around 2030 onward.
section_header: Scale Up Public Financial Incentives and Expand Access to Public and Private Low-Cost Financing for Building Decarbonization
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella financial strategy for building electrification, efficiency, and resilience.

parent_statement: Scale up public financial incentives and expand low-cost financing for building decarbonization.
policy_statement: Scale up direct incentives for weatherization, energy efficiency, electrification-readiness, heat pumps, and resiliency measures in residential and commercial buildings.
source_quote: The State should scale up direct incentives for weatherization (including sealing of cracks and holes, insulation of attics and walls, replacement or repair of windows and outside doors, and mitigation of energy-related health and safety issues), additional energy efficiency upgrades, electrification-readiness, and electrification with highly efficient heat pumps and resiliency measures in residential and commercial buildings. Financial incentive programs will need to scale up dramatically to motivate millions of homeowners and building owners to install high-efficiency electric heat pumps and make energy efficiency improvements such as sealing air leaks, adding insulation, and using building controls.
section_header: B4. Scale Up Public Financial Incentives
extraction_rationale: This is a broad financial incentive policy for building efficiency and electrification.

parent_statement: Scale up public financial incentives and expand low-cost financing for building decarbonization.
policy_statement: Expand low-cost financing for building electrification, energy efficiency, electrification readiness, solar PV, storage, resiliency, and related improvements.
source_quote: Low-cost financing products for energy efficiency, electrification, electrification readiness, solar photovoltaics (PV), energy/thermal storage, resiliency measures, and related improvements are also needed so that single-family, multifamily, and commercial and institutional building owners can access low-cost capital at the scale needed to pay for the building upgrades necessary for decarbonization. The State should provide greater access to low-cost financing products for upgrades, including for low-income homeowners and buildings located in Disadvantaged Communities.
section_header: B5. Expand Access to Public and Private Low-Cost Financing
extraction_rationale: This is a financial instrument strategy for building decarbonization investments.

parent_statement: Scale up public financial incentives and expand low-cost financing for building decarbonization.
policy_statement: Support development of clean thermal energy networks, including utility pilots and workforce transition for gas workers.
source_quote: Thermal energy networks offer an important pathway to both scale up zero-emission heating and cooling in buildings and to transition highly skilled gas workers into a similar sector, utilizing the existing skills of utility workers and the building trades workforce. The Utility Thermal Energy Networks and Jobs Act allows gas and combined gas and electric utilities to become holistic thermal energy providers.
section_header: B6. Support Development of Thermal Energy Networks
extraction_rationale: This is a specific clean heating infrastructure strategy using community-scale thermal systems.

parent_statement: Scale up public financial incentives and expand low-cost financing for building decarbonization.
policy_statement: Align energy price signals with building decarbonization goals through carbon pricing, electric rate design, and low-income bill discount alignment.
source_quote: The low relative cost of gas compared with electricity is a major barrier to building electrification. Over time, the costs of operating high-efficiency electric heat pumps will need to become more attractive compared with heating with fossil natural gas.
section_header: B7. Align Energy Price Signals with Policy Goals
extraction_rationale: This is a pricing and rate design strategy to incentivize efficient electrification.

policy_statement: Expand New York's commitment to market development, innovation, and leading by example in State building projects.
source_quote: In coordination with financial incentives and regulations, State support for market development and innovation is important for ensuring the delivery of building decarbonization solutions that perform well and make our lives better. Areas of focus should include workforce skills and broad public awareness and engagement that motivates behavioral change.
section_header: Expand New York's Commitment to Market Development, Innovation, and Leading-by-Example in State Projects
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella buildings market development and innovation initiative with workforce, education, innovation, and embodied carbon sub-strategies.

parent_statement: Expand New York's commitment to market development, innovation, and leading by example in State building projects.
policy_statement: Invest in workforce development for building decarbonization, including training for heat pump installation, codes, refrigerants, building operations, and fossil workforce transition.
source_quote: Consistent with the just transition framework and implementation partners described in Chapter 7. Just Transition , equipping a workforce to design, install, inspect, maintain, and operate healthy, comfortable, zero-emission buildings needs to include expanded or new training. Overall, workforce development investments are critical to close skill gaps and address the shortage of qualified, skilled workers who are ready to deliver the unprecedented speed and scale of adoption of heat pumps and energy efficiency measures that is needed over this decade to meet New York's climate requirements.
extraction_rationale: This is a workforce capacity policy tied to implementation of building decarbonization.

parent_statement: Expand New York's commitment to market development, innovation, and leading by example in State building projects.
policy_statement: Scale up public awareness and consumer education campaigns on building decarbonization, incentives, and benefits.
source_quote: New York should expand its support for broad public awareness and consumer education, create strategic partnerships with trusted community leaders, and scale up targeted outreach and decision-making support to increase market demand and accelerate the transition to low-carbon, energy-efficient, and electrified buildings. NYSERDA, the PSC and DPS, and utilities should lead these efforts, in coordination with local governments and community-based organizations and leaders.
section_header: B9. Scale Up Public Awareness and Consumer Education
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete outreach and education intervention supporting climate building retrofits.

parent_statement: Expand New York's commitment to market development, innovation, and leading by example in State building projects.
policy_statement: Support innovation, RD&D, demonstrations, technology transfer, and commercialization for next-generation building decarbonization, grid-interactive buildings, resilience, and alternative fuels research.
source_quote: For nearly all buildings in New York, technologies exist today that can dramatically reduce the building's energy use and, with zero-emission electricity, decarbonize the building. The State should continue to support RD&D and help to bring new companies and manufacturers to New York that offer innovative solutions for highly efficient, electrified, and resilient buildings; for grid-interactive buildings; and for reducing embodied carbon in buildings.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific RD&D and commercialization policy for building decarbonization technologies.

parent_statement: Expand New York's commitment to market development, innovation, and leading by example in State building projects.
policy_statement: Reduce embodied carbon from building construction through State procurement requirements, design specifications, building reuse, and low-carbon materials innovation.
source_quote: A specific area for RD&D and for the State to lead by example is to reduce the embodied carbon associated with building construction, which describes all GHG emissions that result from the mining, harvesting, processing, manufacturing, transportation, and installation of the products and materials that are used in buildings, as well as end-of-life emissions associated with the disposal of those materials. To lower the embodied carbon of products and materials used in the buildings sector, New York should establish procurement requirements and design specifications for State-funded projects, building on the framework established in Executive Order 22 directing the GreenNY Council to issue operational directives and guidance for common construction materials to be used in projects using the state procurement process.
section_header: B11. Reduce Embodied Carbon from Building Construction
extraction_rationale: This is a specific materials procurement and building reuse strategy for emissions reduction.

policy_statement: Advance a managed and just transition from reliance on hydrofluorocarbons through education, codes, refrigerant management, food-store support, and phaseout of high-GWP HFCs.
source_quote: HFC use is currently widespread in refrigeration and HVAC equipment, including in heat pumps that are being recommended to electrify space conditioning and water heating and in foams that provide insulation for higher efficiency buildings. New York State agencies should continue to coordinate with U.S. Climate Alliance states on HFC reduction policies and ensuring an effective phasedown of HFCs.
section_header: B12. Advance a Managed and Just Transition from Reliance on Hydrofluorocarbon Use
extraction_rationale: This is a named HFC mitigation strategy for refrigerants and related equipment.

policy_statement: Transform power generation to meet 70% renewable electricity by 2030 and 100% zero-emission electricity by 2040.
source_quote: With fossil natural gas currently being the principal fossil fuel source for electricity generation in the State, a significant transformation of the power sector is necessary to meet the Climate Act's 70x30 and 100x40 requirements. To decrease the use of emitting fuels in the electricity sector, New York must deploy clean energy resources such as land-based wind and solar, offshore wind, hydropower, fuel cells that use renewable fuels, and energy storage.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella electricity-sector mitigation initiative with specific sub-strategies.

parent_statement: Transform power generation to meet 70% renewable electricity by 2030 and 100% zero-emission electricity by 2040.
policy_statement: Retire or repurpose fossil fuel-fired generation facilities while maintaining electric reliability and prioritizing zero-emission alternatives.
source_quote: Achieving a 100% zero-emission power grid will require phasing out the use of fossil fuel for power generation over time. To facilitate and enable retirement and/or repurposing (meaning use of this space for siting clean energy transition activities such as energy storage, operations and maintenance activities, training facilities, etc.) of fossil fuel-fired facilities, New York needs to continue and accelerate its deployment of new renewable generators.
section_header: E1. Retirement and/or Repurposing of Fossil Fuel Fired Facilities
extraction_rationale: This is a specific phaseout and repurposing policy for fossil generation assets.

parent_statement: Transform power generation to meet 70% renewable electricity by 2030 and 100% zero-emission electricity by 2040.
policy_statement: Accelerate deployment of large-scale renewable energy generation through Clean Energy Standard procurements, siting reforms, permitting goals, transmission identification, and workforce measures.
source_quote: New York needs to get new renewable energy projects built. This points to the need for efficient processes to deploy large-scale renewable generation and improved transmission and distribution systems.
section_header: E2. Accelerate Growth of Large-Scale Renewable Energy Generation
extraction_rationale: This is a specific deployment and procurement strategy for large-scale renewable generation.

parent_statement: Transform power generation to meet 70% renewable electricity by 2030 and 100% zero-emission electricity by 2040.
policy_statement: Facilitate clean distributed energy resources through hosting capacity upgrades, interconnection improvements, rate design, incentives, zoning, and aggregation.
source_quote: Clean DERs will continue to be pursued alongside the expansion of large-scale renewables. These resources generate electricity closer to end users, thereby increasing the efficiency and reducing carbon pollution compared with other generation facilities as well as improving grid resiliency and potentially curtailing the need for costly transmission investments.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific distributed clean energy deployment strategy.

parent_statement: Transform power generation to meet 70% renewable electricity by 2030 and 100% zero-emission electricity by 2040.
policy_statement: Support clean energy siting and community acceptance through agrivoltaics, mapping, planning support, public education, host benefits, and community engagement.
source_quote: New York will need to accelerate the deployment of renewable energy projects (both large-scale renewables and DERs) in order to achieve the Climate Act's mandates. New York needs a multi-pronged approach with communities to support the siting and acceptance of renewable energy facilities, including wind, solar, storage, and transmission upgrades.
section_header: E4. Support Clean Energy Siting and Community Acceptance
extraction_rationale: This is a siting, planning, and engagement strategy for renewable energy deployment.

parent_statement: Transform power generation to meet 70% renewable electricity by 2030 and 100% zero-emission electricity by 2040.
policy_statement: Promote Community Choice Aggregation and community distributed initiatives to connect homes, businesses, and institutions with renewable energy, community solar, microgrids, and clean energy services.
source_quote: Community choice aggregation (CCA) programs allow local governments to make bulk power purchases on behalf of participating homes and businesses in their jurisdiction, making it easier for residents and employers to benefit from local clean energy projects, while also improving project economics and advancing the Climate Act requirements. Most communities in New York that have implemented a CCA program procure 100% renewable energy as their default supply.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific local clean energy procurement and aggregation policy.

policy_statement: Enhance the electric grid to support reliability, renewable integration, energy storage, transmission upgrades, demand-side solutions, and lower emissions.
source_quote: While transformation of the power sector is critical to achieving the State's goals and requirements, it also presents the opportunity to make enhancements to the electric grid. Enhancements can improve the efficiency, delivery, and reliability of electricity, facilitate the integration of renewable energy, and prioritize clean resources consistent with the Climate Act.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella grid modernization initiative with specific sub-strategies.

parent_statement: Enhance the electric grid to support reliability, renewable integration, energy storage, transmission upgrades, demand-side solutions, and lower emissions.
policy_statement: Deploy existing energy storage technologies and provide increased funding to reach at least 6,000 MW of storage by 2030.
source_quote: NYSERDA and DPS are currently in the process of updating the State's Energy Storage Roadmap to update and revise the storage deployment goal to achieve 6,000 MW of energy storage by 2030 in recognition of the substantially higher requirements identified in the Power Grid Study. The PSC should consider methods to create a market for retail and wholesale storage, such as establishing Clean Dispatch Credits or expanding the CES to better integrate storage or to initiate a new docket that sets new binding targets and creates a dedicated funding mechanism that is similar to the CES for storage as soon as practicable and no later than the end of 2023.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified storage deployment and funding policy to support clean grid reliability.

parent_statement: Enhance the electric grid to support reliability, renewable integration, energy storage, transmission upgrades, demand-side solutions, and lower emissions.
policy_statement: Invest in transmission and distribution infrastructure upgrades to integrate renewable energy, support electrification, and phase out SF6 equipment.
source_quote: As New York State moves forward in meeting the Climate Act requirements, there will be a need for significant investments in New York's electricity transmission and distribution system to allow for the utilization of new renewable and energy storage resources and to meet growing electric load due to electrification. SF6 is most commonly used as an insulator in electricity transmission and distribution equipment and its use continues to grow.
section_header: E7. Invest in Transmission and Distribution Infrastructure Upgrades
extraction_rationale: This is a public/utility infrastructure investment and grid modernization policy with explicit climate objectives.

parent_statement: Enhance the electric grid to support reliability, renewable integration, energy storage, transmission upgrades, demand-side solutions, and lower emissions.
policy_statement: Improve reliability planning and electricity markets to support clean resource integration, climate resilience, and resource adequacy.
source_quote: Generation resources combined with the transmission and distribution systems, control centers, and wholesale markets provide a continuously operating, reliable system to service New York's electric needs. All of these elements will need to make the transition and come together effectively to provide continuity of a reliable power system, while implementing the goals and requirements of the Climate Act.
section_header: E8. Improve Reliability Planning and Markets
extraction_rationale: This is a planning and market-design policy to maintain reliability while decarbonizing electricity.

parent_statement: Enhance the electric grid to support reliability, renewable integration, energy storage, transmission upgrades, demand-side solutions, and lower emissions.
policy_statement: Advance demand-side solutions including demand response, geothermal, appliance standards, opt-out demand flexibility programs, and benefit-cost updates.
source_quote: Responsive demand presents an opportunity to optimize for the lowest system cost and most expeditious deployment of both clean supply and demand solutions by reducing the need for electricity, especially during peak hours. Reducing demand and creating demand flexibility can significantly reduce scope and costs of infrastructure buildout and will yield GHG reductions, criteria pollutant reductions, and health benefits in the near term by reducing reliance on high-polluting peaker facilities.
extraction_rationale: This is a demand response and energy efficiency strategy with explicit GHG reduction impacts.

policy_statement: Explore zero-emission dispatchable technology solutions, long-duration storage, alternative fuels, and nuclear options needed for a 100% zero-emission grid.
source_quote: Whether the answer is new long-duration storage technology or other new zero-emission, dispatchable technologies that may emerge due to RD&D efforts over the next two decades, the costs are likely to be high and aggressive action and smart planning will be necessary to make these fundamental shifts in our energy systems in the next two decades. The PSC, in coordination with NYSERDA, DEC, and other agencies should identify, explore, evaluate, and support the development of dispatchable technologies and solutions as they emerge in support of the Climate Act's requirements for a zero-emission electricity system by 2040 and for consistency with Section 7(2) and 7(3) of the Climate Act.
extraction_rationale: This is an electricity-sector RD&D and planning strategy for hard-to-meet zero-emission reliability needs.

policy_statement: Provide financial and technical assistance to industry for energy efficiency, electrification, and decarbonization.
source_quote: The State should help overcome these barriers by providing technical and financial assistance in implementing various solutions for decarbonization. Specific solutions could include NYSERDA's engineering study support, financial incentives to buy down project costs, and potentially NYPA's Energy Solutions programs and its Power Proceeds programs within the geographic regions they serve.
section_header: I1. Provide Financial and Technical Assistance
extraction_rationale: This is a financial and technical support policy for industrial emissions reduction.

policy_statement: Use procurement incentives to increase demand for low-carbon products and materials, especially building materials.
source_quote: Another strategy that has been identified to reduce emissions in the industrial sector is to create State procurement incentives so that manufacturers will produce less emission-intensive goods to capitalize on the increased demand for such goods. The initial focus for this effort should be to incentivize the manufacturing of lower-carbon building materials such as cement, steel, and aluminum.
section_header: I2. Incentivize Procurement of Low-Carbon Products
extraction_rationale: This is a low-carbon procurement and market-shaping policy for industrial decarbonization.

policy_statement: Support industrial clean energy workforce development and training.
source_quote: The workforce development enabling initiative is intended to expand the State's existing green workforce and focus on training workers on existing decarbonization technologies and on newer solutions as they become available. NYSERDA and DOL have a long history of collaborating and delivering successful clean energy workforce development and training programs and can build upon that success to meet the Climate Act requirements and goals between now and 2050.
extraction_rationale: This is a workforce-development policy supporting industrial decarbonization implementation.

policy_statement: Facilitate RD&D for industrial decarbonization solutions including efficiency, electrification, alternative fuels/feedstocks, and carbon capture.
source_quote: Given current trends, many of the required technologies for deep decarbonization of the industrial sector will not be available in the timeframe necessary for the State to meet its targets. However, the State could speed the deployment of some of these solutions with a robust RD&D agenda.
section_header: I4. Facilitate Research, Development, and Demonstration
extraction_rationale: This is a specific industrial RD&D policy for hard-to-decarbonize technologies.

policy_statement: Establish or expand a greenhouse gas registry and reporting system for industrial and other emission sources.
source_quote: DEC should promulgate regulations to establish a new GHG registry and reporting system or expand the existing GHG reporting requirements. This could be accomplished as a component of another regulatory program, such as an economywide program of the type discussed in Chapter 17. Economywide Strategies.
section_header: I5. Establish Greenhouse Gas Registry and Reporting System
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory reporting policy enabling emissions tracking and compliance.

policy_statement: Provide economic incentives to attract and grow green economy businesses and supply chains in New York.
source_quote: The State should continue to develop an in-state supply chain of green economy businesses by offering economic incentives like loans, grants, tax credits, technical assistance programs, or even venture capital investments. One of the most prominent economic incentives that the State can use in attracting these businesses is the enhanced Excelsior Jobs Program for green economy companies that make products or develop technologies that are primarily aimed at reducing GHG emissions or supporting the use of clean energy.
extraction_rationale: This is a broad economic incentive policy for clean technology and emissions-reducing industry development.

policy_statement: Promote sustainable forest management to increase carbon sequestration, storage, and climate resilience.
source_quote: Promoting a wide diversity of site-specific forest management strategies across the landscape, including harvesting, thinning, and/or leaving mature forests intact, will best help increase New York's carbon sequestration, storage, and climate resilience. Guidance is needed to promote forest management regarding carbon storage and sequestration, climate resilience, and other climate-related issues using the strategies described below.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella nature-based climate policy with multiple forest-management sub-strategies.

parent_statement: Promote sustainable forest management to increase carbon sequestration, storage, and climate resilience.
policy_statement: Identify where forest management provides the greatest carbon, resilience, and ecosystem benefits.
source_quote: Identifying and prioritizing locations for forest management is an enabling strategy that will allow the State to target areas for forest management to maximize carbon sequestration and storage and climate resilience. DEC is currently working with SUNY ESF to develop site-specific models of aboveground forest carbon across the landscape which is expected to be complete in 2023, with updates and improvements expected to be ongoing.
section_header: AF1. Identify Where Forest Management Provides the Greatest Benefits
extraction_rationale: This is a specific forest planning and prioritization strategy for carbon and resilience benefits.

parent_statement: Promote sustainable forest management to increase carbon sequestration, storage, and climate resilience.
policy_statement: Prevent forest pests, diseases, and invasive species and restore degraded forests to protect forest carbon sequestration.
source_quote: By altering the forest ecosystem, preventing regeneration, reducing the growth and vigor of trees, and causing direct mortality, invasive species negatively impact the ability of New York's forests to store and sequester carbon. Climate change is expected to increase the competitiveness of invasive plants and increase the range and survival of native and invasive insects and diseases.
section_header: AF2. Prevent Forest Pests, Diseases, and Invasive Species and Restore Degraded Forests
extraction_rationale: This is a nature-based forest health intervention explicitly protecting carbon storage and sequestration.

parent_statement: Promote sustainable forest management to increase carbon sequestration, storage, and climate resilience.
policy_statement: Maintain and improve sustainable forest management practices and mitigation strategies, including forest carbon research, BMPs, restoration, and financing for equipment upgrades.
source_quote: Improving and expanding the use of sustainable forest management practices and mitigation strategies is ongoing and has direct benefits for carbon storage and sequestration. Current efforts by DEC include sustainability certification on State lands, the Forest Stewardship Program, EQIP run by USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS), the 480-a Forest Tax Law program, and the Regenerate NY cost share grant program.
section_header: AF3. Maintain and Improve Sustainable Forest Management Practices and Mitigation Strategies
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete set of forest management interventions to increase sequestration and storage.

parent_statement: Promote sustainable forest management to increase carbon sequestration, storage, and climate resilience.
policy_statement: Assist private forest landowners in implementing sustainable forest management and mitigation strategies through outreach, tax incentives, cost share, and equipment access.
source_quote: Of New York's forests, 73%, or 13.7 million acres, are owned by private landowners. The majority of all the carbon sequestration and storage occurs on these lands.
section_header: AF4. Assist Landowners in Implementation of Sustainable Forest Management and Mitigation Strategies
extraction_rationale: This is a targeted technical and financial assistance policy for private land-based carbon management.

parent_statement: Promote sustainable forest management to increase carbon sequestration, storage, and climate resilience.
policy_statement: Support local communities in forest protection and management, including urban forestry planning, grants, and youth conservation corps.
source_quote: Local governments including counties and municipalities own approximately 1% of forested areas large and productive enough for wood production and have jurisdiction over land use planning and restrictions for forests within their boundaries. Increasing forest protection and management in local and urban communities will increase carbon sequestration and storage as well as climate resilience.
section_header: AF5. Support Local Communities in Forest Protection and Management
extraction_rationale: This is a local nature-based climate policy for urban and community forest carbon and resilience.

parent_statement: Promote sustainable forest management to increase carbon sequestration, storage, and climate resilience.
policy_statement: Monitor progress and advance forestry science and technology for forest carbon tracking and decision tools.
source_quote: Tracking the carbon sequestered and stored by New York's forests is critical to enabling and evaluating the success of carbon sequestration and storage. Monitoring forest carbon progress will help the State identify successful forest management strategies and provide further insight into what land use patterns can lead to the greatest carbon sequestration and storage.
section_header: AF6. Monitor Progress and Advance Forestry Science and Technology
extraction_rationale: This is a monitoring and science policy enabling forest carbon management.

parent_statement: Promote sustainable forest management to increase carbon sequestration, storage, and climate resilience.
policy_statement: Conduct education and outreach on climate-focused forest management, urban forestry, and wood products.
source_quote: Education and outreach to New York's private and public landowners who can implement forest management practices and mitigation strategies is needed to ensure and enable the success of the strategies described in this chapter, which will in turn increase carbon sequestration and storage and climate resilience. In addition, the benefits forests and wood products provide should be promoted to the public to increase their use and for a better understanding of why protecting and managing forests is beneficial for carbon sequestration, wildlife, and the people of New York.
section_header: AF7. Conduct Education and Outreach on Forest Management
extraction_rationale: This is a capacity-building policy for forest-based mitigation and adaptation.

policy_statement: Advance livestock management strategies to reduce agricultural methane and nitrous oxide emissions.
source_quote: The highest level of agricultural emissions, primarily methane and secondarily N2O, is attributed to livestock. Therefore, the following strategies contribute to the deepest reductions in agricultural emissions, addressing methane reduction through manure management practices and precision animal feeding.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella agriculture mitigation initiative with manure and feed management sub-strategies.

parent_statement: Advance livestock management strategies to reduce agricultural methane and nitrous oxide emissions.
policy_statement: Advance alternative manure management systems to prevent, capture, destroy, or beneficially use methane emissions.
source_quote: This strategy can reduce methane emissions by implementing practice systems specifically planned and designed for each farm, including but not limited to cover and methane capture systems, anaerobic digester systems, composting, and other innovative systems that collect, capture, and destroy methane from manure storages or prevent methane production through alternative manure management practice systems. This strategy can also lead to creation of a renewable, alternative fuel to self-supply farm energy needs.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific agricultural methane mitigation policy using manure management technologies and practices.

parent_statement: Advance livestock management strategies to reduce agricultural methane and nitrous oxide emissions.
policy_statement: Advance precision feed, forage, and herd management to reduce enteric methane and nitrous oxide emissions.
source_quote: To reduce methane and N2O emissions while achieving desired ruminant growth and lactation goals, this strategy requires the evaluation of new processes, technologies, costs, and returns; demands sustained adaptive management by farmers and advisors; flattening the learning curve by farmers, advisors, and the feed industry; filling gaps in applied research; and overcoming weather and market disruptions that can lower performance (producing lower quality forage). This strategy acknowledges that additional methane emission reduction may be realized from feed additives developed in the future and supports research to evaluate their potential.
section_header: AF9. Advance Precision Feed, Forage, and Herd Management
extraction_rationale: This is a specific livestock emissions mitigation strategy focused on feed and herd management.

policy_statement: Improve soil health, nutrient management, and agroforestry to reduce nitrous oxide emissions, increase carbon sequestration, and improve resilience.
source_quote: Healthy soils and nutrient management provide for many functions and ecosystem services including sustaining the biological activity and diversity of the soil, water quality protection, nutrient cycling, and carbon sequestration. Practices that improve soil health help to buffer many of the impacts of climate change also increasing a farm's resiliency.
section_header: Improve Soil Health, Nutrient Management, and Agroforestry
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella agricultural land-management initiative with multiple mitigation, sequestration, and resilience sub-strategies.

parent_statement: Improve soil health, nutrient management, and agroforestry to reduce nitrous oxide emissions, increase carbon sequestration, and improve resilience.
policy_statement: Advance agricultural nutrient management to reduce nitrous oxide emissions and nitrogen pollution while maintaining yields.
source_quote: Farmers in New York have improved nutrient management on lands while increasing crop yields. Farms across New York will continue to reduce N2O emissions and nitrogen pollution to waterways while achieving desired yield and quality through continued and expanded nutrient management planning and implementation on crop fields, hay fields, pastures, orchards, vineyards, and other agricultural lands receiving nutrients.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific agricultural emissions-reduction and water-quality strategy using nutrient management.

parent_statement: Improve soil health, nutrient management, and agroforestry to reduce nitrous oxide emissions, increase carbon sequestration, and improve resilience.
policy_statement: Adopt soil health practice systems such as cover crops, crop rotations, perennial crops, prescribed grazing, and nutrient management.
source_quote: This strategy focuses on reducing net GHG emissions as well as increasing carbon sequestration and other environmental benefits through adoption of soil health management practice systems (such as combinations of cover and double crops, conservation crop rotations, perennial crops, prescribed grazing, and nutrient management), also referred to as regenerative agricultural practices. Implementing soil health management practice systems can also have the added benefit of reducing nitrogen fertilizer inputs, reducing operating costs, and improving a farm's financial viability associated with the impact of extreme weather events caused by climate change.
section_header: AF11. Adopt Soil Health Practice Systems
extraction_rationale: This is a nature-based agricultural soil carbon and resilience policy.

parent_statement: Improve soil health, nutrient management, and agroforestry to reduce nitrous oxide emissions, increase carbon sequestration, and improve resilience.
policy_statement: Increase adoption of agroforestry practices that add trees into agricultural production systems.
source_quote: Adding trees into areas of agricultural production increases carbon sequestration and other environmental benefits. Agroforestry adoption can contribute toward afforestation and reforestation goals, hence having a high GHG emissions mitigation potential.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific nature-based agricultural strategy using trees for sequestration and environmental benefits.

parent_statement: Improve soil health, nutrient management, and agroforestry to reduce nitrous oxide emissions, increase carbon sequestration, and improve resilience.
policy_statement: Develop Agricultural Environmental Management planning for climate mitigation and adaptation, including Carbon Farm Planning.
source_quote: AEM planning for climate mitigation and adaptation or the development of 'Carbon Farm' Planning has the potential to elevate local food production and resiliency, water quality, air quality, storm and flood mitigation, public infrastructure protection, drought resiliency, habitat, scenic vistas, tourism, economic development, and jobs. This strategy is essential to the successful planning and implementation of practice systems that are tailored farm-by-farm for the reduction of GHG emissions, increased carbon sequestration potential, and elevated adaptation and resiliency on farmland.
section_header: AF13. Develop Agricultural Environmental Management Planning for Climate Mitigation and Adaptation
extraction_rationale: This is a farm-level planning policy explicitly addressing mitigation and adaptation.

parent_statement: Improve soil health, nutrient management, and agroforestry to reduce nitrous oxide emissions, increase carbon sequestration, and improve resilience.
policy_statement: Monitor and benchmark agricultural greenhouse gas emissions, sequestration, and adaptation performance.
source_quote: Annual monitoring and benchmarking of GHG emissions mitigation, carbon sequestration, and adaptation performance across applicable areas of management on farms in New York is critical to determining success in meeting targets and providing further insight into what strategies lead to the greatest achievements. Like the farm-level AEM planning strategy, this strategy is central to the success of all other agricultural mitigation efforts.
section_header: AF14. Monitor and Benchmark Agricultural Greenhouse Gas Emissions
extraction_rationale: This is a monitoring and reporting strategy for agricultural climate performance.

parent_statement: Improve soil health, nutrient management, and agroforestry to reduce nitrous oxide emissions, increase carbon sequestration, and improve resilience.
policy_statement: Establish a payment for ecosystem services program for agricultural producers and forest landowners.
source_quote: Establishing a payment for ecosystem services mechanism to provide a new structure for establishing and maintaining practice systems that reduce GHG emissions and sequester carbon in addition to providing other environmental benefits would provide additional incentives to farmers and forest landowners. This strategy supports the implementation of other strategies in this sector that rely on increased adoption of regenerative agricultural practices.
section_header: AF15. Establish a Payment for Ecosystem Services Program
extraction_rationale: This is a financial incentive policy for ecosystem-based mitigation and sequestration.

parent_statement: Improve soil health, nutrient management, and agroforestry to reduce nitrous oxide emissions, increase carbon sequestration, and improve resilience.
policy_statement: Bolster local agricultural economies through local procurement, farmer assistance, and supply-chain development for low-carbon and agroforestry products.
source_quote: This strategy supports emission reductions by enhancing existing programs, and promoting the expansion of those programs, that encourage farm viability and resilient communities through the production and consumption of local food. This strategy is designed to enhance the expansion of markets and support for New York's farming community.
extraction_rationale: This is a market-support strategy with indirect emissions benefits through local food systems and farm viability; climate relevance is direct in the plan but mechanism is partly economic.

policy_statement: Promote a climate-focused bioeconomy based on sustainable biomass, wood products, low-carbon products, and carbon dioxide removal.
source_quote: The bioeconomy produces sustainable, renewable bio-based feedstocks, rather than fossil fuel-based feedstocks, to produce products that achieve the climate and social justice requirements of the Climate Act. In addition, there is an opportunity for enhanced carbon storage as longterm, durable wood products store carbon.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella bioeconomy policy with multiple sub-strategies for mitigation and carbon storage.

parent_statement: Promote a climate-focused bioeconomy based on sustainable biomass, wood products, low-carbon products, and carbon dioxide removal.
policy_statement: Develop forestry training programs to support an expanded workforce and climate knowledge.
source_quote: As additional efforts to create additional wood product markets and the expansion of afforestation, reforestation, and other forest management efforts to enhance the long-term storage of carbon increase, an expansion in New York's forestry workforce will be needed. There needs to be information on forest carbon management and climate resilience incorporated into existing forestry trainings and education programs to help encourage such an expansion.
section_header: AF17. Develop Forestry Training Programs to Support Expanding Workforce and Climate Knowledge
extraction_rationale: This is a workforce training policy supporting forest carbon and bioeconomy implementation.

parent_statement: Promote a climate-focused bioeconomy based on sustainable biomass, wood products, low-carbon products, and carbon dioxide removal.
policy_statement: Expand markets for sustainably harvested durable wood products to store carbon and substitute for high-emission materials.
source_quote: Use of durable, long-lasting wood products, especially as a substitute for fossil fuel-intensive products like steel, concrete, brick, or vinyl, can reduce overall emissions for construction projects. Use of longlasting, durable wood products can reduce GHG emissions when they replace fossil fuel-based products.
section_header: AF18. Expand Markets for Sustainably Harvested Wood Products
extraction_rationale: This is a market-development policy for wood products as carbon storage and materials substitution.

parent_statement: Promote a climate-focused bioeconomy based on sustainable biomass, wood products, low-carbon products, and carbon dioxide removal.
policy_statement: Develop a Sustainable Biomass Feedstock Action Plan for bioenergy and low-carbon products.
source_quote: A Sustainable Biomass Feedstock Action Plan will identify feedstock volumes and production methods that utilize New York biomass resources (wood and wood processing wastes, agricultural crops and waste materials, organics in municipal solid waste, animal manure, and wastewater treatment byproducts) in a sustainable, emissions-reducing and substitution-maximizing manner. The Sustainable Biomass Feedstock Action Plan will also consider other uses for these feedstocks, such as uses in low-carbon product development as described in Strategies AF20 and AF21.
section_header: AF19. Develop a Sustainable Biomass Feedstock Action Plan for Bioenergy and Low-Carbon Products
extraction_rationale: This is a named planning strategy for sustainable biomass use and emissions reduction.

parent_statement: Promote a climate-focused bioeconomy based on sustainable biomass, wood products, low-carbon products, and carbon dioxide removal.
policy_statement: Increase market access for New York low-carbon products, including bio-based substitutes and procurement support.
source_quote: In the emerging field of low-carbon products, agricultural and forest residues are converted into biochemicals and biomaterials that are replacements for the petrochemicals used to create packaging, cosmetics, binders, absorbents, concrete strengtheners, and other products. These substitutes for fossil fuel products and fossil fuel-based products can reduce overall GHG emissions.
section_header: AF20. Increase Market Access for New York Low-Carbon Products
extraction_rationale: This is a market development and procurement policy for low-carbon bio-based products.

parent_statement: Promote a climate-focused bioeconomy based on sustainable biomass, wood products, low-carbon products, and carbon dioxide removal.
policy_statement: Provide financial and technical assistance for low-carbon product development from biomass residuals.
source_quote: In addition to State support for increasing market access, financial and technical assistance is needed to grow bioprocessing industries for low-carbon products from low-grade wood and other biomass residuals to create bio-based substitutes for fossil fuel-based products. Providing this assistance will ensure this strategy mitigates GHG emissions without unintentionally emitting co-pollutants.
section_header: AF21. Provide Financial and Technical Assistance for Low-Carbon Product Development
extraction_rationale: This is a financial and technical assistance strategy for bio-based low-carbon product industries.

parent_statement: Promote a climate-focused bioeconomy based on sustainable biomass, wood products, low-carbon products, and carbon dioxide removal.
policy_statement: Advance bio-based products research, development, and demonstration.
source_quote: Bio-based products have the potential to replace fossil fuel and fossil fuel-based products, including for hard-to-decarbonize uses, to lower GHG emissions. To drive research and development, this strategy recommends developing a demonstration and pilot project portfolio to drive investment in the areas of alternative fuels, low-carbon products, and related sequestration that considers intersection of industrial or manufacturing, agriculture, transportation, and power generation sectors and funding innovation challenges and projects that can scale beyond business as usual to provide GHG emissions reduction benefits.
section_header: AF22. Advance Bio-Based Products Research, Development, and Demonstration
extraction_rationale: This is an RD&D policy for bio-based products with mitigation potential.
