parent_statement: Promote a climate-focused bioeconomy based on sustainable biomass, wood products, low-carbon products, and carbon dioxide removal.
policy_statement: Advance deployment of net-negative carbon dioxide removal technologies and pathways.
source_quote: Carbon dioxide removal (CDR) pathways create a negative emissions profile for bioeconomy products and other economic sectors (long-duration carbon storage beyond net zero), helping to ensure that replacement of fossil fuel and fossil fuel-based products results in lower GHG emissions. Net negative CDR can provide permanent storage of atmospheric carbon.
section_header: AF23. Advance Deployment of Net Negative Carbon Dioxide Removal
extraction_rationale: This is a carbon removal deployment and demonstration strategy with direct mitigation purpose.

policy_statement: Reduce, reuse, and recycle waste to reduce methane, CO2, and lifecycle emissions from materials.
source_quote: Waste reduction, reuse, and recycling is critical to achieve the requirements and goals of the Climate Act. Significant GHG impacts from this sector include the uncaptured emissions of methane from landfills, specifically from organic materials.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella waste-sector climate strategy with multiple sub-policies.

parent_statement: Reduce, reuse, and recycle waste to reduce methane, CO2, and lifecycle emissions from materials.
policy_statement: Reduce and recycle organic waste, including expanding the Food Donation and Food Scraps Recycling Law and supporting organics infrastructure.
source_quote: Reducing the disposal of organics, including food scraps (food grown for human consumption that has not been consumed and is destined for recycling or disposal), is key to reducing the methane and CO2 emissions at landfills and combustion facilities. The State should enact legislation to amend and expand the existing Food Donation and Food Scraps Recycling Law (2019) to include generators of one ton per week or more beginning in 2024, one-half ton per week in 2025, and all generators by 2028.
section_header: W1. Organic Waste Reduction and Recycling
extraction_rationale: This is a specific waste diversion policy with statutory expansion and deadlines to reduce methane.

parent_statement: Reduce, reuse, and recycle waste to reduce methane, CO2, and lifecycle emissions from materials.
policy_statement: Implement waste reduction, reuse, and recycling policies including disposal fees, by-request-only single-use products, container deposits, right-to-repair, materials exchanges, and textile recycling.
source_quote: Waste reduction, reuse, and recycling initiatives significantly reduce the methane and CO2 emissions at landfills and combustion facilities by avoiding disposing of waste in the first place. As stated in Strategy W1, the State should enact legislation in 2023 to establish a disposal disincentive (fee per ton) on all waste generated in New York to provide financial support for reduction, reuse, and recycling.
section_header: W2. Waste Reduction, Reuse, and Recycling
extraction_rationale: This is a broad resource-efficiency and waste prevention policy package; it includes a financial disposal fee.

parent_statement: Reduce, reuse, and recycle waste to reduce methane, CO2, and lifecycle emissions from materials.
policy_statement: Enact extended producer responsibility or product stewardship requirements for packaging, paper, carpet, tires, textiles, batteries, appliances, solar panels, wind turbines, and other products.
source_quote: Enacting broad EPR or product stewardship requirements to cover end-of-life management of postconsumer products will allow the State to ensure their sustainable management. Products that could benefit from new EPR legislation include packaging and printed paper, carpet, tires, textiles, solar panels, wind turbines, all batteries, appliances (especially those containing refrigerants), mattresses, and other methane-generating wastes.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific legislative product stewardship strategy for waste reduction and lifecycle emissions.

parent_statement: Reduce, reuse, and recycle waste to reduce methane, CO2, and lifecycle emissions from materials.
policy_statement: Convert wastewater treatment plants to water resource recovery facilities that capture beneficial products, biogas, and biosolids.
source_quote: Transforming wastewater treatment plants from a waste disposal priority to WRRFs that emphasize the capture of beneficial products is a key component of the circular economy. WRRFs, which represent much of the existing capacity for organics materials management in New York, present tremendous opportunity for reducing GHG emissions.
section_header: W4. Water Resource Recovery Facility Conversion
extraction_rationale: This is a resource recovery and emissions reduction strategy for wastewater infrastructure.

parent_statement: Reduce, reuse, and recycle waste to reduce methane, CO2, and lifecycle emissions from materials.
policy_statement: Reduce and destroy refrigerant leaks from appliances and refrigeration systems, including end-of-life reclamation and restrictions on virgin high-GWP refrigerants.
source_quote: HFCs contained inside well-maintained appliance systems pose minimal threat to the environment; however, 90% of fugitive emissions of these gases happen during end-of-life management of the appliance. Policies incentivizing the destruction of refrigerants at end-of-life would encourage the retirement of old, energy-inefficient equipment so that these materials are not released to the atmosphere.
section_header: W5. Refrigerant Leak Reduction and Destruction
extraction_rationale: This is a specific HFC mitigation policy targeting refrigerant leaks and end-of-life destruction.

policy_statement: Monitor, detect, and reduce fugitive emissions from solid waste management facilities and water resource recovery facilities.
source_quote: The quantification of GHG impacts from fugitive emissions at solid waste management facilities and WRRFs are currently under-reported and will vary based on several site-specific factors such as waste composition and facility design. Assessing these systems both during and beyond the active life of operation as well as minimizing/repairing equipment releasing fugitive emissions (leaks) can significantly reduce waste sector GHG emissions.
section_header: Monitor, Detect, and Reduce Fugitive Emissions
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella methane monitoring and leak-reduction initiative with sub-strategies for solid waste and wastewater facilities.

parent_statement: Monitor, detect, and reduce fugitive emissions from solid waste management facilities and water resource recovery facilities.
policy_statement: Reduce fugitive methane and co-pollutants from solid waste management facilities through landfill gas capture, enhanced covers, monitoring, research, and regulation.
source_quote: Identifying and reducing fugitive emissions of methane from landfills and anaerobic digesters through baseline measurement, increased monitoring, and engineering and regulatory programs can reduce leaks and provide facilities with comprehensive data on their operations. DEC should enhance existing regulations, before 2025, for landfills that will lead to less methane leakage, such as a requirement to install gas collection systems sooner after waste placement, install specialty landfill gas collectors for difficult to access areas, and enhance gas dewatering systems to increase collection efficiency.
section_header: W6. Reduce Fugitive Emissions of Methane and Co-Pollutants from Solid Waste Management Facilities
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete methane monitoring and regulatory strategy for landfills and anaerobic digesters.

parent_statement: Monitor, detect, and reduce fugitive emissions from solid waste management facilities and water resource recovery facilities.
policy_statement: Reduce fugitive methane and co-pollutants from water resource recovery facilities and septic/sewer systems through monitoring, leak reduction, sewer transition support, and operator training.
source_quote: Similar to solid waste management facilities, comprehensive data on existing fugitive GHG emissions from WRRFs is not available, and additional regulations and funding sources will be critical to address wastewater sector impacts. Municipalities will need to measure and reduce GHG emissions from WRRFs, septic, and sewer systems, which can be difficult without the proper equipment and training.
section_header: W7. Reduce Fugitive Emissions of Methane and Co-Pollutants from Water Resource Recovery Facilities
extraction_rationale: This is a specific methane monitoring and reduction policy for wastewater systems.

policy_statement: Establish markets for recovered resources and strategic biogas utilization.
source_quote: The recycling industry needs viable and consistent markets to continue to capture the economic value of materials and promote them for their highest and best use. Capturing these unavoidable gases for strategic and local use while the State transitions to electrification will help meet the requirements and goals of the Climate Act while avoiding future reliance on fossil fuels.
section_header: Establish Markets for Recovered Resources and Biogas Utilization
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella waste-sector market development initiative with recycling and biogas sub-strategies.

parent_statement: Establish markets for recovered resources and strategic biogas utilization.
policy_statement: Develop recycling markets for recovered resources, recycled content products, compost, digestate, aggregate, and building deconstruction materials.
source_quote: The State should support domestic recycling facilities and markets for recovered resources (including compost, digestate, and recycled aggregate/building deconstruction materials) and incentivize public-private partnerships for recycling facility development. The State should also enact legislation to require a minimum level of recycled content in certain products and packaging.
extraction_rationale: This is a market development and recycled-content policy for materials circularity and emissions reduction.

parent_statement: Establish markets for recovered resources and strategic biogas utilization.
policy_statement: Use biogas strategically and locally from landfills and anaerobic digestion where it provides emissions, health, and system benefits.
source_quote: During the implementation of aggressive waste reuse, reduction, and recycling techniques, it is recognized that some amount of waste generation will be unavoidable. Biogas generation from landfills and from anaerobic digestion will continue, and a viable use for the biogas is needed.
extraction_rationale: This is a methane capture and beneficial-use strategy; combustion-related air quality caveats are noted in the document.

policy_statement: Implement an economywide cap-and-invest program to ensure Climate Act emission limits are met and generate revenue for clean energy and Disadvantaged Community investments.
source_quote: The Council recommends implementation of a cap-and-invest program designed to meet the Climate Act's requirements and goals, including meeting the economywide emission limits, promoting climate justice, and mitigating leakage. Mindful of current energy price burdens on New York households, the Council recommends gradually phasing in the program with cost containment mechanisms and rebates or subsidies to offset the burden of increased energy prices on LMI households.
section_header: 17.2 Proposed Program Design to Meet Climate Act Requirements
extraction_rationale: This is a broad market-based financial instrument and regulatory cap to ensure emissions limits are achieved.

policy_statement: Develop a coordinated gas system transition plan for reducing fossil natural gas use, strategically downsizing and decarbonizing the gas system, and maintaining safety, reliability, affordability, equity, and workforce protections.
source_quote: The Council has developed a framework through which agencies can develop a coordinated plan for the reduction of fossil natural gas use and the strategic downsizing and decarbonization of the gas system through an orderly transition that is equitable, cost-effective, and maintains system safety and reliability. Development of the plan should be led by DPS and supported by NYSERDA, Long Island Power Authority (LIPA), New York Power Authority (NYPA), and DEC.
extraction_rationale: This is a named planning framework for fossil gas phase-down and system transition.

policy_statement: Reduce fugitive methane emissions from gas infrastructure through regulation, leak detection and repair, leak-prone pipe prioritization, reporting, and orphaned well plugging.
source_quote: The State should support future efforts from DEC to further control, reduce, and eliminate methane emissions from gas infrastructure. This may include implementing the use of innovative leak detection and repair technology, developing an inventory of all infrastructure and sources of methane emissions potentially subject to State regulation, and establishing operation and maintenance requirements that result in reduced methane emissions.
section_header: Reduce Fugitive Emissions from Gas Infrastructure
extraction_rationale: This is a specific methane mitigation strategy for the gas system.

policy_statement: Protect, restore, and monitor natural and working lands to preserve carbon storage, increase sequestration, and support climate resilience.
source_quote: Current and future use of natural and working lands has important implications for mitigation of GHG emissions and carbon sequestration and storage, including protecting high-value lands through acquisition, avoiding conversion and development, and land restoration. Afforestation and reforestation have the potential to greatly increase carbon sequestration and storage capacity in New York State.
section_header: Protect, Restore, and Monitor of Natural and Working Lands
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella land-use and nature-based solutions policy with multiple sub-strategies.

parent_statement: Protect, restore, and monitor natural and working lands to preserve carbon storage, increase sequestration, and support climate resilience.
policy_statement: Protect forest lands from conversion through Keep Forests as Forests legislation, land acquisition, conservation easements, and local acquisition support.
source_quote: Keeping forests as forests is critical to maintaining and increasing levels of carbon sequestration and storage and preventing emissions, as forests sequester and store much more carbon than any other land use in New York. The State should immediately enact legislation to 'keep forest as forests,' requiring developers to purchase and set aside forested land when forest carbon is lost during development following the principles of avoid, minimize, and mitigate.
section_header: LU1. Mitigate Carbon Emissions by Protection of Forest Lands
extraction_rationale: This is a land conservation and anti-conversion strategy with explicit carbon mitigation purpose.

parent_statement: Protect, restore, and monitor natural and working lands to preserve carbon storage, increase sequestration, and support climate resilience.
policy_statement: Implement statewide afforestation and reforestation, including planning, seedling production, free seedlings, cost-share, rights-of-way reforestation, and a Tree or Climate Corps.
source_quote: Afforestation and reforestation have the potential to greatly increase the carbon sequestration and storage capacity in New York State. DEC should work with other agencies and partners to develop a plan that sets ambitious and collaborative goals that span across agencies and organizations, programs, local municipalities, nurseries and landscaping companies, and landowners for reforestation and afforestation by 2030, 2040, and 2050.
extraction_rationale: This is a nature-based carbon sequestration strategy with quantified timing and implementation tools.

parent_statement: Protect, restore, and monitor natural and working lands to preserve carbon storage, increase sequestration, and support climate resilience.
policy_statement: Avoid agricultural and forested land conversion through protection programs, tax incentives, easements, land access support, and renewable energy siting mitigation.
source_quote: The objective of this strategy is to maintain and protect the State's potential for carbon sequestration on agricultural and forested lands through avoided conversion. It will also help to enhance farm viability, increase food security, potentially reduce future GHG emissions from VMT when implemented with smart growth measures, and protect forest benefits including wildlife habitat, local forest products, and flood protection.
section_header: LU3. Avoid Agricultural and Forested Land Conversion
extraction_rationale: This is a conservation policy preventing land-use emissions and preserving sequestration.

parent_statement: Protect, restore, and monitor natural and working lands to preserve carbon storage, increase sequestration, and support climate resilience.
policy_statement: Protect and restore freshwater and tidal wetlands and coastal habitats to maintain carbon sequestration and climate adaptation benefits.
source_quote: This strategy focuses on maintaining and enhancing the carbon sequestration potential of freshwater, nontidal wetlands; coastal and estuarine tidal wetlands; submerged aquatic vegetation; and other coastal habitats in New York through protection, restoration, and monitoring. While GHG emissions reduction by wetlands may be low compared with forests in New York, it is important to note that many of the State's wetlands are forested, and all wetlands are part of the natural infrastructure necessary for climate adaptation and resilience and collectively contribute to overall carbon storage and sequestration strategies.
extraction_rationale: This is a wetlands protection and restoration policy with explicit carbon and adaptation functions.

parent_statement: Protect, restore, and monitor natural and working lands to preserve carbon storage, increase sequestration, and support climate resilience.
policy_statement: Improve mapping, research, planning, and assistance for wetlands, forests, grasslands, coastal habitats, and natural areas.
source_quote: This strategy focuses on maintaining and enhancing the carbon sequestration potential of natural areas in New York, including wetlands, coastal habitats, forests, and grasslands, through improved mapping (both regulatory and non-regulatory), research, conservation planning guidance, stewardship, and assistance for local governments and landowners. These strategies are needed to pair priority conservation areas with priority growth areas - a key component of smart planning and smart growth that can sustain large, functioning natural areas that provide health benefits to people and other ecosystem services like flood mitigation, habitat for plants and animals, and opportunities for outdoor recreation for residents and visitors.
section_header: LU5. Mapping, Research, Planning, and Assistance
extraction_rationale: This is a planning and data-support policy for nature-based carbon and resilience actions.

policy_statement: Consider forests and farmland in land use policies, including local planning, afforestation, reforestation, and clean energy siting.
source_quote: The following strategies discuss how to better equip municipalities with the proper tools to ensure the protection of New York's natural and working lands, while still advancing renewable energy. Local governments and organizations provide planning, guidance, and support for land use and to residents.
section_header: Consider Forests and Farmland in Land Use Policies
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella land-use planning initiative for balancing conservation and clean energy development.

parent_statement: Consider forests and farmland in land use policies, including local planning, afforestation, reforestation, and clean energy siting.
policy_statement: Provide guidance and support for local and landowner afforestation and reforestation planning and projects.
source_quote: Some municipalities and private landowners lack the expertise and capacity to support afforestation and reforestation projects, which may result in land being put toward other uses. This strategy involves providing funding and personnel resources to directly support communities and landowners in their planning and planting efforts as well as developing trainings and materials to increase outreach and education to local municipalities and organizations.
section_header: LU6. Provide Guidance and Support for Afforestation and Reforestation
extraction_rationale: This is a technical assistance and funding policy for nature-based sequestration projects.

parent_statement: Consider forests and farmland in land use policies, including local planning, afforestation, reforestation, and clean energy siting.
policy_statement: Increase forest and farmland protection in municipal comprehensive plans through inventories, BMPs, and State-funded planning requirements.
source_quote: This strategy proposes creation of tools to help municipalities identify and fund inventories of forest and farmland, development of BMPs, and a requirement to include forestland and farmland in planning efforts, which will help communities target lands for conservation and prevent emissions from land use conversion. Development of tools and BMPs would take several years.
section_header: LU7. Increase Forest and Farmland Protection in Municipal Comprehensive Plans
extraction_rationale: This is a local planning policy to prevent land conversion and preserve carbon sinks.

parent_statement: Consider forests and farmland in land use policies, including local planning, afforestation, reforestation, and clean energy siting.
policy_statement: Provide clean energy siting guidance and support to local governments while minimizing impacts to forests and agricultural lands.
source_quote: The Climate Act contains significant requirements for clean energy development, such as the distributed solar and energy storage targets. Local land use decisions are an important part of meeting these requirements in ways that revitalize communities and grow the economy.
section_header: LU8. Provide Guidance and Support on Clean Energy Siting
extraction_rationale: This is a renewable energy siting support strategy that balances mitigation with land conservation.

policy_statement: Promote smart growth to reduce transportation emissions and align development, conservation, housing, and transportation planning.
source_quote: Smart growth is compact, mixed-use, mixed-income community development that is walkable, bikeable, and transit-accessible and contains a diversity of housing choices, open spaces, and public gathering places accessible to people of all ages, incomes, backgrounds, and mobility capabilities. Smart growth land use patterns reduce GHG emissions largely in the transportation sector by reducing automobile use, measured as VMT.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella land-use resource-efficiency policy with multiple sub-strategies.

parent_statement: Promote smart growth to reduce transportation emissions and align development, conservation, housing, and transportation planning.
policy_statement: Provide regional and county planning and technical assistance for smart growth, priority development areas, priority conservation areas, and regional sustainability alignment.
source_quote: Regional and county planning should guide future growth, redevelopment, and conservation at the multimunicipal scale. There should be facilitation and support of collaborative multi-municipal smart growth comprehensive planning at the county and regional scales to inform and guide land use decisions, including designation of priority development areas and priority conservation areas.
section_header: LU9. Regional and County Planning and Technical Assistance
extraction_rationale: This is a planning support policy for smart growth and conservation.

parent_statement: Promote smart growth to reduce transportation emissions and align development, conservation, housing, and transportation planning.
policy_statement: Provide direct planning, zoning, and pre-development assistance to municipalities for smart growth and equitable development.
source_quote: The State should provide direct planning and zoning assistance to local communities and promote municipal implementation of mitigation strategies through enhanced technical assistance, increased support for local adoption of zoning and land use regulations consistent with smart growth principles, and local policies that support sustainable, equitable development and the accelerated expansion of local clean energy while also ensuring and enhancing public outreach, education and engagement, particularly in frontline communities that have historically been disenfranchised and discriminated against in the local land use decision-making process. This strategy aims to empower local governments to achieve smart growth planning and development.
section_header: LU10. Direct Planning, Zoning, and Pre-Development Assistance to Municipalities
extraction_rationale: This is a municipal technical assistance policy for smart growth and emissions mitigation.

parent_statement: Promote smart growth to reduce transportation emissions and align development, conservation, housing, and transportation planning.
policy_statement: Align State funding priorities with smart growth and equity goals, including amendments to the Smart Growth Public Infrastructure Policy Act.
source_quote: State funding should align with smart growth and equity goals and seek to eliminate funding that induces sprawl, particularly with new infrastructure. This is the stated purpose goal of the State Smart Growth Public Infrastructure Policy Act.
extraction_rationale: This is a public funding alignment policy to avoid sprawl and support low-carbon land use.

parent_statement: Promote smart growth to reduce transportation emissions and align development, conservation, housing, and transportation planning.
policy_statement: Accelerate equitable transit-oriented development around key transit hubs served by rail and bus rapid transit.
source_quote: Smart Growth planning should accelerate mixed-use, mixed-income TOD, with an emphasis on E-TOD, around key transit hubs served by rail and bus rapid transit. TOD creates compact, mixed-use, mixedincome, walkable communities within a half-mile of rail or transit hubs.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific transit-oriented development policy to reduce automobile dependence and emissions.

policy_statement: Establish a statewide community greenhouse gas dashboard for local climate action planning and emissions tracking.
source_quote: This strategy calls for a community dashboard that local governments and other stakeholders can use to understand GHG emissions, energy use trends, and identify opportunities for improvement. The dashboard would bring together data from several sources to describe the complete community GHG emissions picture, including government facilities as well as residential, commercial, and industrial emissions.
section_header: LG1. Establish Community Greenhouse Gas Dashboard
extraction_rationale: This is a specific data and reporting tool for local mitigation planning.

policy_statement: Develop local energy policies through model above-minimum energy codes, NYStretch Energy Code adoption, code enforcement, streamlined permitting, and Property Assessed Clean Energy financing.
source_quote: This strategy is intended to encourage and support local governments to demonstrate leadership in energy efficiency by developing model above-minimum energy conservation codes and construction policies. This includes adopting the NYStretch Energy Code and promoting its adoption, enhanced code enforcement including streamlined permitting, third-party inspections, and shared enforcement, and Property Assessed Clean Energy financing.
extraction_rationale: This is a local energy code and financing support policy for efficiency and emissions reduction.

policy_statement: Provide clean energy siting support for local governments through model local laws, development regulations, and streamlined permitting.
source_quote: This strategy facilitates clean energy siting through development and promotion of model local laws and streamlined permitting. Local governments often have limited capacity to anticipate and plan for renewable energy and energy storage development in their communities.
section_header: LG3. Provide Clean Energy Siting Support for Local Governments
extraction_rationale: This is a local government support policy for renewable energy and storage deployment.

policy_statement: Promote municipal leadership to support clean energy adoption through CCA, microgrids, district systems, and community-scale campaigns.
source_quote: This strategy connects homes, businesses, and community institutions with clean energy products and services through Community Choice Aggregation (CCA) programs, microgrids, district systems, and community-scale campaigns to encourage adoption of innovative technologies to generate savings and reduce GHG emissions for consumers in an equitable manner. To achieve Climate Act mandates, broad-based consumer demand for clean energy products and services is necessary.
section_header: LG4. Promote Municipal Leadership to Support Clean Energy Adoption
extraction_rationale: This is a local clean energy adoption strategy with named interventions.

policy_statement: Provide State support and guidance to local governments for LED lighting, efficiency upgrades, heat pumps, methane recovery, solar, and fleet electrification.
source_quote: This strategy discusses continuing and expanding program opportunities, incentives, technical assistance, financial support, and centralized procurement services to motivate local governments, local government municipal bodies such as Conservation Advisory Committees and Environmental Management Councils, and related public entities to improve assets they control with high-impact actions. This includes LED lighting, energy efficiency upgrades, heat pump projects, methane recovery for energy production from wastewater treatment and landfills, solar on municipal premises, and municipal and school district fleet electrification.
section_header: LG5. Provide State Support and Guidance
extraction_rationale: This is a technical and financial assistance policy for local government climate actions.

policy_statement: Build statewide adaptation and resilience capacity through planning, funding, public education, and financing mechanisms.
source_quote: The 'build capacity' theme comprises four strategies related to statewide planning, consideration of future conditions in State decision-making, enhancement of general understanding of climate change, improving the public's adaptive capacity, and identifying options for financing adaptation actions and reducing or shifting risk. Climate change impacts and the ability to adapt are distributed unevenly across different communities and population groups.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella adaptation policy with multiple capacity-building sub-strategies.

parent_statement: Build statewide adaptation and resilience capacity through planning, funding, public education, and financing mechanisms.
policy_statement: Create, implement, and update a comprehensive and equitable State climate change adaptation and resilience plan, overseen by a Chief State Resilience Officer and sub-cabinet.
source_quote: The Governor should appoint a Chief State Resilience Officer (CSRO) who would convene an adaptation and resilience sub-cabinet. The CSRO and adaptation and resilience subcabinet should oversee development of a comprehensive State climate change adaptation and resilience plan.
section_header: AR1. Commit to Creating, Implementing, and Updating a Comprehensive and Equitable State Climate Change Adaptation and Resilience Plan
extraction_rationale: This is a specific governance and planning policy for statewide climate adaptation.

parent_statement: Build statewide adaptation and resilience capacity through planning, funding, public education, and financing mechanisms.
policy_statement: Incorporate equitable adaptation and risk-reduction considerations into State funding, regulatory programs, projects, and policies.
source_quote: Incorporating equity into adaptation considerations in State programs is important for ensuring Disadvantaged Communities are protected against the effects of climate change and have the capacity and necessary resources to anticipate, plan for and adapt to climate impacts. Implementation of this strategy would be complementary to the goals of the Climate Justice chapter and include mainstreaming equity and justice considerations across programs.
section_header: AR2. Incorporate Equitable Adaptation and Risk-Reduction Considerations into Relevant State Funding and Regulatory Programs, Projects, and Policies
extraction_rationale: This is a cross-government adaptation mainstreaming policy.

parent_statement: Build statewide adaptation and resilience capacity through planning, funding, public education, and financing mechanisms.
policy_statement: Strengthen meaningful community engagement, public education, and adaptive capacity across sectors.
source_quote: Equitable participation in decision-making is particularly critical in adaptation and resilience planning to ensure that impacts and vulnerabilities are recognized and that climate risks are not displaced to communities that have historically been excluded from decision-making processes. Meaningful engagement processes, opportunities to participate in decision-making and capacity-building will be critical for local communities to successfully adapt to climate change.
section_header: AR3. Strengthen Meaningful Community Engagement and Public Education and Build Adaptive Capacity across all Sectors
extraction_rationale: This is a capacity-building and education policy for adaptation planning and implementation.

parent_statement: Build statewide adaptation and resilience capacity through planning, funding, public education, and financing mechanisms.
policy_statement: Identify and evaluate financing, insurance, bonding, and community preservation options to support equitable adaptation and resilience projects.
source_quote: The costs of dealing with the effects of climate change will be significant and will continue to rise as the planet warms. The State should create a resilient infrastructure fund through bonding, such as through the 'Clean Air, Clean Water, and Green Jobs' Environmental Bond Act.
section_header: AR4. Identify and Evaluate Options for Supporting Equitable Adaptation and Resilience Practices and Projects, and to Enhance Insurance Protection
extraction_rationale: This is a financial strategy for adaptation and resilience funding.

policy_statement: Enhance community and infrastructure resilience through planning support, land use tools, flood and heat risk reduction, and energy system resilience.
source_quote: Enhancing resilience of communities and infrastructure includes strategies to assist municipalities to prepare for and react to increasingly severe climate hazards. The strategies include recommendations to expand State support for regional and local planning, assist municipalities and local communities in their efforts to incorporate future conditions into local planning and regulatory decisions, recommendations to address risks due to flooding and extreme heat, and recommendations to ensure resilience of the energy system.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella adaptation policy addressing named climate hazards and infrastructure resilience.

parent_statement: Enhance community and infrastructure resilience through planning support, land use tools, flood and heat risk reduction, and energy system resilience.
policy_statement: Provide State agency planning and technical support for equitable regional and local adaptation and resilience plans and projects.
source_quote: Local officials have consistently advised that they lack resources, including not only funds, but technical expertise and access to information and decision-support tools to support effective adaptation planning. This strategy would accelerate current efforts to provide guidance, and financial and technical support for community and regional planning and implementation, for mainstreaming of climate change considerations into local planning and regulatory programs and for consideration of local economic resilience under future climate conditions in planning decisions.
section_header: AR5. Provide State Agency Planning and Technical Support for Equitable Regional and Local Adaptation and Resilience Plans and Projects
extraction_rationale: This is a technical and financial assistance policy for local adaptation planning.

parent_statement: Enhance community and infrastructure resilience through planning support, land use tools, flood and heat risk reduction, and energy system resilience.
policy_statement: Ensure equitable consideration of future climate conditions in land use planning and environmental reviews.
source_quote: Work to mainstream consideration of climate change in environmental reviews is ongoing, but much remains to be done, and local governments require more explicit authority to consider climate change and biodiversity in comprehensive plans. DEC should accelerate ongoing efforts to develop or update guidance for mitigation of climate change risks, avoiding maladaptation in permit and SEQRA reviews, and amend the SEQRA Handbook and workbooks.
section_header: AR6. Evaluate Opportunities to Ensure Equitable Consideration of Future Climate Conditions in Land Use Planning and Environmental Reviews
extraction_rationale: This is an adaptation policy integrating future climate risk into land use and environmental review.

parent_statement: Enhance community and infrastructure resilience through planning support, land use tools, flood and heat risk reduction, and energy system resilience.
policy_statement: Develop policies, programs, and decision-support tools to reduce risks associated with coastal and inland flooding.
source_quote: Flooding is New York's primary climate hazard, and we can expect both insured and uninsured losses to increase as sea level continues to rise and more frequent extreme precipitation events result in more extensive and deeper floods, including dangerous flash flooding in urban areas not previously considered flood prone. Components of this strategy would provide improved map and other information resources, funding, and regulations to reduce flood risks.
section_header: AR7. Develop Policies, Programs, and Decision Support Tools to Reduce Risks Associated with Coastal and Inland Flooding
extraction_rationale: This is a specific adaptation strategy addressing named hazards of coastal and inland flooding.

parent_statement: Enhance community and infrastructure resilience through planning support, land use tools, flood and heat risk reduction, and energy system resilience.
policy_statement: Develop policies and programs to reduce human risks associated with extreme heat and thermal extremes.
source_quote: In most years, more Americans die from the effects of extreme heat than from flooding and frequency of extreme heat events is one of the most direct effects of global warming. Components of this strategy include support for cooling centers, heat emergency planning, weatherization, and access to thermal resilience programs for vulnerable populations.
section_header: AR8. Develop Policies and Programs to Reduce Human Risks Associated with New Patterns of Thermal Extremes
extraction_rationale: This is a specific adaptation strategy addressing extreme heat and thermal risk.

parent_statement: Enhance community and infrastructure resilience through planning support, land use tools, flood and heat risk reduction, and energy system resilience.
policy_statement: Ensure reliability, resilience, and safety of the energy system under climate hazards through vulnerability assessments, resilience plans, microgrids, storage, PV, and EV charging readiness.
source_quote: The increasing frequency of severe climatic events has exposed vulnerabilities in the State's energy system and the need to improve the reliability and resilience of the energy system, as well as the resilience of those who depend on that energy system in buildings and for transportation. Assessment of system vulnerabilities to increasing climate hazards and investment to ensure system resilience will be required.
section_header: AR9. Ensure the Reliability, Resilience, and Safety of the Energy System
extraction_rationale: This is an adaptation and resilience policy for energy infrastructure and service continuity.

policy_statement: Enhance resilience of living systems, including ecosystems, agriculture, and forests.
source_quote: As used in this document, the term 'living systems' refers to the State's natural ecosystems, its agricultural systems, and its forested lands. Strategies recommended to enhance resilience of living systems include addressing risks to ecosystems and biodiversity, enhancing resilience and adaptation of the agricultural sector, and protecting the ability of forests to serve as carbon sinks.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella nature-based adaptation initiative with ecosystem, agriculture, and forest sub-strategies.

parent_statement: Enhance resilience of living systems, including ecosystems, agriculture, and forests.
policy_statement: Develop policies and programs to reduce climate risks threatening ecosystems and biodiversity, including connectivity, easements, invasive species management, and stream buffers.
source_quote: The components of this strategy provide for a variety of mechanisms to ensure conservation or protection of the most important pieces of our life-sustaining ecosystems. These initiatives include a focus on intentional planning to identify and protect critical ecosystems and to establish and protect connectivity at several scales, ranging from the landscape scale to enable populations to migrate northward and upward as the climate warms, to project-specific planning to ensure wildlife and aquatic organism connectivity.
section_header: AR10. Develop Policies and Programs to Reduce Risks Threatening Ecosystems and Biodiversity
extraction_rationale: This is a nature-based adaptation policy for ecosystem and biodiversity resilience.

parent_statement: Enhance resilience of living systems, including ecosystems, agriculture, and forests.
policy_statement: Enhance climate resilience and adaptive capacity of the agricultural sector through water and energy efficiency, resilient crop research, and watershed BMPs.
source_quote: Included below are recommendations to improve water and energy efficiency on farms, incorporate other climate-resilient practices into farm operations, and continue research and outreach to help farmers prepare for the effects of a changing climate. However, these recommendations do not address the entire gamut of climate hazards New York growers, agricultural workers, and farm communities face and should not be interpreted as a complete agricultural adaptation plan.
section_header: AR11. Enhance Climate Resilience and Adaptive Capacity of Agricultural Sector, while Preparing to Take Advantage of Emerging Opportunities
extraction_rationale: This is an agricultural adaptation policy including explicit efficiency measures.

parent_statement: Enhance resilience of living systems, including ecosystems, agriculture, and forests.
policy_statement: Preserve and protect forest ecosystems' ability to sequester carbon by incorporating resilience criteria in land acquisition and providing forest resilience guidance.
source_quote: In recognition of the important role healthy forests play in sequestering carbon, ensuring forests retain their sequestration potential under future conditions should be considered in State acquisition programs. This strategy complements the strategies described in Chapter 15. Agriculture and Forestry , which serve to enhance the ability of our forests to remove carbon dioxide (CO2) from the atmosphere and sequester it in healthy trees and forest soils.
section_header: AR12. Preserve and Protect the Ability of Forest Ecosystems to Sequester Carbon
extraction_rationale: This is a nature-based adaptation policy that also explicitly preserves carbon sequestration.

policy_statement: Create an Office of Just Transition and Worker Support and Community Assurance Fund to coordinate support for host communities, existing workers, and new workers.
source_quote: That apparatus should take the form of a newly created, dedicated state office charged with realizing a just transition and resourced with an accompanying fund, which would be overseen and administered by the office in consultation with DOL and NYSERDA, to provide support for workers, communities, and other transitional priorities. The Office of Just Transition will help coordinate all funding and financial incentives for workforce development, community support, existing worker support, and new worker support related to the Climate Act transition.
section_header: Office of Just Transition and Worker Support and Community Assurance Fund
extraction_rationale: This is a named institutional and financial policy to support the climate transition workforce and affected communities.

policy_statement: Expand and extend the Electric Generation Facility Cessation Mitigation Program and transfer it to the Office of Just Transition.
source_quote: New York should enact legislation to expand and extend the Electric Generation Facility Cessation Mitigation Program and transfer administration of the program to this proposed Office of Just Transition. The program was created to provide funding assistance to support counties, towns, cities, villages, school districts and special districts that experience a reduction in real property taxes and/or payments in lieu of taxes stemming from the closure of an electric generation facility.
section_header: Office of Just Transition and Worker Support and Community Assurance Fund
extraction_rationale: This is a financial support policy for communities affected by fossil power plant retirements.

policy_statement: Implement the Statewide Community Air Monitoring program in 10 overburdened communities and develop emissions reduction strategies by June 1, 2024.
source_quote: Exceeding the four required by the Climate Act, 10 communities were identified as having a disproportionate air pollution burden. By June 1, 2024, DEC will prepare, in consultation with the CJWG and community-based organizations, strategies to reduce emissions of toxic and criteria air pollutants in Disadvantaged Communities.
section_header: Community Air Monitoring in Disadvantaged Communities
extraction_rationale: This is a statutory monitoring and emissions-reduction program with specified communities and deadline; climate relevance includes GHG and co-pollutant monitoring.

policy_statement: DEC will promulgate enforceable regulations by January 1, 2024 to ensure statewide GHG emission limits are met.
source_quote: DEC will have until January 1, 2024, to draft and promulgate enforceable regulations to ensure that the State meets the Climate Act's statewide GHG emission limits (i.e., 40% reduction in Statewide GHG emissions by 2030 and 85% reduction by 2050, both from 1990 levels) as outlined in the Scoping Plan. The State Energy Plan will be updated to incorporate the recommendations of the Scoping Plan.
extraction_rationale: This is a binding regulatory implementation requirement with deadline and quantified GHG limits.

policy_statement: Update the State Energy Plan to incorporate Scoping Plan recommendations.
source_quote: The State Energy Plan will be updated to incorporate the recommendations of the Scoping Plan. Every five years, the Council will update the Scoping Plan as part of the ongoing process to meet the Climate Act targets and GHG emissions reduction limits.
extraction_rationale: This is a planning requirement for integrating climate strategies into the State Energy Plan.

policy_statement: PSC will biennially review the renewable energy program beginning by July 1, 2024, including 70x30, 100x40, offshore wind, solar, and storage progress.
source_quote: By July 1, 2024, and every two years thereafter, the PSC will issue a comprehensive review of the renewable energy program, including progress in meeting the overall targets for 70% renewable electricity by 2030 and 100% zero-emission electricity by 2040. This review will also include a progress update on the programs the PSC has established to require procurement of 9 GW of offshore wind by 2035, 6 GW of solar PV by 2025, and 3 GW of energy storage by 2030.
extraction_rationale: This is a statutory monitoring and accountability policy for clean electricity targets.

policy_statement: Provide access to updated national, regional and local climate projections data to support climate-risk assessment and adaptation decisions.
source_quote: This w ill give New Zealanders the regional and local climate projections data they need to assess future climate risk and make adaptation decisions. By January 2023, national climate projection datasets for Aotearoa are being produced .
section_header: Action 3.1: Provide access to the latest climate projections data
extraction_rationale: This is a named government action with a timeframe, lead agency and deliverable climate projection datasets for adaptation decision-making.

policy_statement: Design and develop risk, resilience and climate adaptation information portals to provide public access to hazard, climate and decision-making information.
source_quote: Action 3.2: Design and develop risk and resilience and climate adaptation information portals will collate and deliver the vast range of data, information and knowledge needed to make adaptation decisions for all users. Action 3.1: Provide access to the latest climate projections data will make data to calculate future climate risk available to all New Zealanders, as the most up-to-date regional and local climate projections data are produced from the IPCC's global projections data.
section_header: Actions to enable New Zealanders to make better risk-informed decisions
extraction_rationale: This is a specific named intervention to create information portals for climate-risk and adaptation decisions.

policy_statement: Establish a platform for Māori climate action to support Māori partnership, strategy and funded kaupapa Māori climate solutions.
source_quote: The platform for Māori climate action is the key mechanism through which the Government is looking to build a climate response partnership with Māori. It will build Te Tiriti partnership and greater recognition of Māori rights and interests, including Treaty settlement commitments, into the climate response.
section_header: Action 3.3: Establish a platform for Māori climate action
extraction_rationale: This is a named institutional mechanism with defined phases, focus areas and deadlines for Māori-led climate action.

policy_statement: Raise public awareness of climate hazards and emergency preparedness through campaigns, resources and tailored information.
source_quote: Enable and work with communities, including rural communities, iwi and Māori, organisations and others to make emergency preparedness a part of everyday life through public awareness and advice. Examples are public education campaigns and resources, such as GetReady.govt.nz, and tailored information for those who face additional challenges.
section_header: Action 3.4: Raise awareness of climate hazards and how to prepare
extraction_rationale: This is a specific public education and preparedness programme for climate-related hazards.

policy_statement: Implement mandatory climate-related financial disclosures and explore expanding the regime to more entities.
source_quote: The Financial Sector (Climate -related Disclosures and Other Matters) Amendment Act 2021 requires about 200 of Aotearoa New Zealand's largest financial market participants to analyse and publicly disclose their climate-related risks and opportunities each year . The purpose is to ensure the effects of climate change are routinely considered in decisions for business, investment, lending and insurance.
section_header: Action 3.5: Support high-quality implementation of climate-related disclosures and explore expansion
extraction_rationale: This is a binding disclosure regime with statutory requirements and an expansion work programme.

policy_statement: Improve natural hazard disclosure on Land Information Memoranda to support property-risk decisions.
source_quote: Changes to legal requirements for Land Information Memoranda (LIMs) will help people make better-informed decisions about natural hazard risk when buying a property. It will give councils greater certainty about what hazard information to include on the LI M.
section_header: Action 3.6: Improve natural hazard information on Land Information Memoranda
extraction_rationale: This is a legal/regulatory disclosure change targeted at property-level climate and natural hazard risk.

policy_statement: Deliver a rolling programme of non-statutory adaptation guidance for decision makers to assess and manage climate risks.
source_quote: The Government will roll out a programme of non -statutory guidance for decision makers to assess and manage climate risks. This could also support regulatory requirements to be developed through the National Planning Framework.
section_header: Action 3.7: Deliver a rolling programme of targeted adaptation guidance
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella action with numbered sub-actions 3.7.1 through 3.7.8.

parent_statement: Action 3.7: Deliver a rolling programme of targeted adaptation guidance
policy_statement: Promote use of updated Aotearoa New Zealand climate change projections guidance.
source_quote: An update for Aotearoa that highlights changes from the 2021 AR6 IPCC.12 report. The update will enable stakeholders to quickly assess where they may need to adapt their risk management plans to account for the latest science.
section_header: 3.7.1: Promote the use of the Aotearoa New Zealand Climate Change Projections guidance
extraction_rationale: This is a specific guidance product under the rolling adaptation guidance programme.

parent_statement: Action 3.7: Deliver a rolling programme of targeted adaptation guidance
policy_statement: Produce adaptation guidance for central government policy makers.
source_quote: A methodology for central government to ensure it considers adaptation in new policy and services. This will avoid increased exposure or vulnerability to climate impacts.
section_header: 3.7.2: Produce adaptation guidance for central government policy makers
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete guidance methodology for embedding adaptation in government policy and services.

parent_statement: Action 3.7: Deliver a rolling programme of targeted adaptation guidance
policy_statement: Produce dynamic adaptive pathways planning guidance for central and local government.
source_quote: A guide for central and local government on how to plan for adaptation in a context of uncertain climate futures.
section_header: 3.7.3: Produce guidance for dynamic adaptive pathways planning (DAPP)
extraction_rationale: This is a specific adaptation planning tool for decision-making under uncertainty.

parent_statement: Action 3.7: Deliver a rolling programme of targeted adaptation guidance
policy_statement: Produce guidance on using socio-economic scenarios in climate-risk and adaptation planning.
source_quote: Assists central and local government and businesses to consider future socio-economic scenarios when assessing climate risks, and planning how to manage them.
section_header: 3.7.4: Produce guidance on using different socio-economic scenarios for adaptation planning
extraction_rationale: This is a specific guidance action to improve climate-risk planning scenarios.

parent_statement: Action 3.7: Deliver a rolling programme of targeted adaptation guidance
policy_statement: Regularly update adaptation guidance for local government.
source_quote: Supports local government to consider adaptation in planning and decisions. This will include guidance on communicating scientific and technical information to communities, and on making climate decisions.
section_header: 3.7.5: Regularly update adaptation guidance for local government
extraction_rationale: This is a recurring guidance update commitment for local government climate adaptation decisions.

parent_statement: Action 3.7: Deliver a rolling programme of targeted adaptation guidance
policy_statement: Produce guidance on integrating mātauranga Māori into adaptive planning and working with mana whenua.
source_quote: Helps central and local government effectively engage with hapū, iwi and Māori when managing risk and planning for adaptation.
section_header: 3.7.6: Produce guidance on integrating mātauranga Māori into adaptive planning and working with mana whenua
extraction_rationale: This is a specific guidance product for Māori engagement and knowledge integration in adaptation planning.

parent_statement: Action 3.7: Deliver a rolling programme of targeted adaptation guidance
policy_statement: Produce standardised guidance for preparing adaptation plans.
source_quote: Enables communities and different audiences, sectors and levels of government to produce their own adaptation plans, using a standard approach under conditions of uncertainty in climate projections. This could include interpreting downscaled projections.
section_header: 3.7.7: Produce guidance for preparing adaptation plans
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete adaptation plan guidance commitment for multiple audiences.

parent_statement: Action 3.7: Deliver a rolling programme of targeted adaptation guidance
policy_statement: Regularly update the guide to local climate change risk assessments on a six-year cycle.
source_quote: Sets out a step-by-step process for local risk assessments. It will be updated on a six-yearly cycle after the release of each national climate change risk assessment.
section_header: 3.7.8: Regularly update the guide to local climate change risk assessments
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete recurring guidance update linked to national risk assessment cycles.

policy_statement: Develop guidance for infrastructure asset owners to assess and manage climate risks to physical assets and services.
source_quote: Te Waihanga will scope and deliver guidance for asset owners to evaluate risks to their physical assets and the services they provide. This will help them understand, and subsequently manage, the impacts of climate change on existing and new assets.
section_header: Action 3.8: Develop guidance for assessing risk and impact on physical assets and the services they provide
extraction_rationale: This is a named guidance deliverable for infrastructure climate-risk assessment and management.

policy_statement: Complete the Data Investment Plan project to identify and fill central-government data gaps relevant to climate-risk information.
source_quote: The Data Investment Plan project recently completed a stocktake of essential datasets across central government and prioritised data gaps for investment. The data gaps may be filled by acquiring new data or making existing data fit for purpose.
section_header: Action 3.9: Complete the Data Investment Plan project
extraction_rationale: This is a named data investment planning project with identified data-gap actions; climate relevance is via adaptation information systems.

policy_statement: Assess socioeconomic and climate vulnerability for Māori to determine where resilience support is most needed.
source_quote: This action will collect and analyse social data against climate data to determine where support for resilience is most needed. This will enable the Government to better understand what support is needed to strengthen resilience for Māori communities.
section_header: Action 3.10: Assess socioeconomic and climate vulnerability for Māori
extraction_rationale: This is a specific vulnerability assessment action for targeted adaptation support.

policy_statement: Implement the National Disaster Resilience Strategy by designing a pathway to give effect to its resilience goals.
source_quote: The National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) will design a pathway to give effect to the National Disaster Resilience Strategy's vision, goals and objectives. The vision is for a disaster-resilient nation that acts proactively to manage risks and to build resilience in a way that contributes to the wellbeing and prosperity of all.
section_header: Action 3.11: Implement the National Disaster Resilience Strategy
extraction_rationale: This is a named implementation action for disaster resilience, relevant to increasing climate-driven hazards.

policy_statement: Improve the use of science, data, mātauranga Māori and local knowledge in emergency management decisions.
source_quote: The National Emergency Management Agency 's 2021 Science Strategy will be used to create a framework for scientific engagement, promotion and influence for risk reduction, readiness, response and recovery. Research, data, mātauranga Māori, local knowledge and technical expertise will inform strategic decisions on emergency management, and explore practical interventions to improve disaster resilience.
section_header: Action 3.12: Improve how science, data and knowledge are used to inform emergency management
extraction_rationale: This is a specific knowledge-to-policy framework for disaster resilience and emergency management.

policy_statement: Provide forestry planning and advisory services to support climate-risk reduction, restoration, regeneration and land-use decisions.
source_quote: The forestry planning and advisory service will help to reduce climate risks by providing datainformed advice and planning tools. Advice will be on both harvest and non-harvest forestry for example, to help decision makers consider where land is available for new forestry; where restoration, regeneration and reversion may be needed; and where unsuitable land may need to be retired from forestry, including conversion from plantation to indigenous forestry.
section_header: Action 3.13: Provide a forestry planning and advisory service
extraction_rationale: This is a named advisory service supporting land-use and forestry decisions for climate resilience.

policy_statement: Deliver the Integrated Farm Planning Programme to incorporate climate change, greenhouse gases, biodiversity and resilience into farm planning.
source_quote: The Integrated Farm Planning Programme will provide a framework for farmers and growers to incorporate all their key farming areas, including greenhouse gases, into their farm planning. The goal is to enable a farmer or grower, using their preferred data -collection tool, platform or system, to meet all regulatory and business needs within a single framework.
section_header: Action 3.14: Deliver the Integrated Farm Planning Programme
extraction_rationale: This is a named programme with funding and implementation measures to integrate farm climate and environmental planning.

policy_statement: Design and implement the Farm Monitoring Programme to collect farm data supporting climate adaptation, efficiency and greenhouse gas reductions.
source_quote: The Farm Monitoring Programme collects farm -level information from up to 2,000 dairy, sheep and beef, deer, arable and horticulture farms/orchards. Quality data will inform decision-making to enable improved farm management decisions and profitability, while considering compliance and regulations to assist greenhouse gas reductions.
section_header: Action 3.15: Design and implement the Farm Monitoring Programme
extraction_rationale: This is a specific monitoring programme with quantitative scope and climate-relevant farm management outcomes.

policy_statement: Improve consumer understanding of property insurance pricing and climate-related risks through information sheets.
source_quote: Information sheets will help consumers identify, manage or even reduce their climate risks. This links to the work on Land Information Memoranda (LIMs), as greater disclosure can help people make better decisions on where to buy and build property.
section_header: Action 3.16: Improve consumer understanding of property insurance pricing and risks
extraction_rationale: This is a specific information intervention to influence household risk decisions.

policy_statement: Support integration of climate adaptation and mitigation into new and revised standards commissioned by third parties.
source_quote: At the beginning of each relevant project, Standards NZ may bring adaptation and mitigation to the attention of the committee members of a standard it has commissioned. This may help improve resilience in existing and new assets, by guiding industry practice in asset design and operation.
section_header: Action 3.17: Support and promote the integration of climate adaptation and mitigation in new and revised standards commissioned by third parties
extraction_rationale: This is a standards-related intervention to embed climate considerations into industry practice.

policy_statement: Review electricity and gas network management of climate risk and resilience through asset-management plan requirements and performance reviews.
source_quote: The Commerce Commission reviews many of the aspects of regulated electricity and gas networks' performance. The Commission is currently consulting on amending the asset management plan requirements for electricity distributors so that sector stakeholders can better understand distributors' risk management, including managing network resilience challenges posed by climate change.
section_header: Action 3.18: Review electricity and gas networks' management of climate risk and resilience
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory oversight action requiring network operators to address climate resilience in planning.

policy_statement: Develop Te Ara Paerangi to position the research, science and innovation system to address national goals including climate change.
source_quote: Te Ara Paerangi - Future Pathways programme for the research, science and innovation system will position the system for the future. This includes focusing resources on national goals, such as climate change, and addressing other issues facing the research system, such as how best to honour Tiriti obligati ons, system funding and incentives, workforce and institutional design.
section_header: Action 3.19: Develop Te Ara Paerangi - Future Pathways programme for the research , science and innovation system
extraction_rationale: This is a named research-system reform with explicit climate-change focus.

policy_statement: Develop mātauranga Māori indicators to monitor climate impacts on biodiversity, mahinga kai, flora, fauna and human health.
source_quote: Mātauranga Māori indicators will enable monitoring and evaluation of impacts on biodiversity, mahinga kai, flora, fauna and human health. This will create data baselines that centralise indigenous knowledge and values, and can be used in environmental assessments.
section_header: Action 3.21: Develop mātauranga Māori indicators of climate impacts on the natural environment
extraction_rationale: This is a specific indicator-development action for monitoring climate impacts on the natural environment.

policy_statement: Work with community housing providers to improve data and implement climate hazard response strategies.
source_quote: This will provide better data and information on the exposure of community housing providers to climate risks. An action programme will increase the resilience of community housing by supporting strategies for emergency management and long-term adaptation.
section_header: Action 3.22: Work with community housing providers to enable effective climate hazard response
extraction_rationale: This is a specific action programme for community housing climate-risk exposure and adaptation.

policy_statement: Develop 3D coastal mapping to assess sea-level rise, tsunami and storm-surge impacts.
source_quote: Coastal mapping comprises detailed 3D mapping of the coastal zone and the upgrade and addition of Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) sites in the coastal zone. The purpose is to assess the impacts of sea-level rise and model the impacts of tsunami and storm surges on communities, infrastructure and biodiversity.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific geospatial data intervention for named coastal climate hazards.

policy_statement: Produce tools and guidance specific to mātauranga Māori and mātauranga indicators for community action and climate decisions.
source_quote: These resources will be developed in partnership with hapū , iwi and Māori, to help them take action in their communities and to inform decisions. This action will provide targeted guidance on planning in uncertain conditions.
section_header: Action 3.24: Produce new tools and guidance specific to mātauranga Māori and mātauranga indicators
extraction_rationale: This is a specific guidance and tools programme for Māori-led adaptation planning.

policy_statement: Design a methodology for climate-risk assessments of public buildings.
source_quote: Developing a methodology for risk assessment based on the property resilience research (see action 5.7: Reduce and manage the impacts of climate hazards on homes and buildings), to address matters such as cultural and heritage values and seismic hazard risks, will support decision-making. This will help owners of public buildings assess and understand climate ri sks and implement adaptation strategies.
section_header: Action 3.25: Design methodology for risk assessments of public buildings
extraction_rationale: This is a specific assessment methodology for public-building adaptation decisions.

policy_statement: Produce disaster risk management guidance for cultural heritage.
source_quote: This action will improve disaster risk management for cultural heritage through guidance on reducing risks before, during and after disasters.
section_header: Action 3.26: Produce guidance for disaster risk management for cultural heritage
extraction_rationale: This is a specific guidance commitment for protecting cultural heritage from disasters, including climate-related disasters.

policy_statement: Develop a framework for assessing exposure and vulnerability of taonga and cultural assets to climate change.
source_quote: It will develop a framework to identify valued cultural heritage and the actual and potential exposure and vulnerability of cultural heritage to climate change. The framework will take a broad and inclusive approach, recognising the ways in which different communities identify, access and participate in what is culturally important to them.
section_header: Action 3.27: Develop a framework for assessing exposure and vulnerability of taonga/cultural assets to climate change
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete framework-development commitment for climate-risk assessment of cultural assets.

policy_statement: Assess healthcare service resilience to climate events and changing illness and vulnerability patterns.
source_quote: The aim of this action is to understand the healthcare service's vulnerability to climate events, and consider physical risks to infrastructure, and changes in illness patterns and vulnerability. This will help to ensure communities can continue to access the healthcare services they need, even in the face of climate change adversity.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific assessment of health-service resilience to climate events.

policy_statement: Produce an adaptation professional development programme for key audiences.
source_quote: This will target building capability and help circulate new tools and guidance among different audiences. It will encourage uptake and effective use by practitioners and others working on climate adaptation.
section_header: Action 3.29: Produce an adaptation professional development programme for key audiences
extraction_rationale: This is a specific capacity-building programme for adaptation practitioners.

policy_statement: Reform the resource management system to support climate adaptation, natural hazard risk management and lower emissions.
source_quote: The Government's objectives for the reform include better preparation for adaptation and risks from natural hazards, and better mitigation of emissions contributing to climate change. Resource management reform will be essential to supporting the resilience of homes, buildings and places.
section_header: Action 4.1: Reform the resource management system
extraction_rationale: This is a major legislative reform programme with named replacement Acts and climate objectives.

policy_statement: Set national direction on natural hazard risk management and climate adaptation through the National Planning Framework.
source_quote: The National Planning Framework will set clear direction for local authorities on how to achieve the climate resilience outcomes in the Natural and Built Environments Act. It will set out methods and requirements for planning for natural hazards and considering future climate risks.
section_header: Action 4.2: Set national direction on natural hazard risk management and climate adaptation through the National Planning Framework
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory planning direction commitment under a national framework.

policy_statement: Establish an initiative and decision framework for adapting new and existing public housing assets to climate hazards.
source_quote: A framework for public housing assets will be developed to determine the actions to adapt new and existing assets. This will help reduce exposure of public housing tenants to climate hazards.
section_header: Action 4.3: Establish an initiative for resilient public housing
extraction_rationale: This is a specific public-housing resilience initiative with a decision-making framework and deadline.

policy_statement: Embed adaptation and climate-hazard costs into housing and urban development funding programmes, including Māori housing.
source_quote: Existing funding programmes for urban development and housing, including Māori housing, will be updated to consider the costs of existing and future climate hazards. New funding programmes may be created if there are gaps.
section_header: Action 4.4: Embed adaptation in funding models for housing and urban development, including Māori housing
extraction_rationale: This is a specific modification of public funding programmes to account for climate hazards.

policy_statement: Reform water services institutions to improve resilience, water security and climate risk management.
source_quote: The Government will create new water entities that will work with councils and communities to improve health and wellbeing outcomes for our communities and protect our environment for generations to come. The National Climate Change Risk Assessment 2020 identified risk to potable water as the most urgent risk from climate change.
section_header: Action 4.5: Reform institutional arrangements for water services
extraction_rationale: This is institutional and legislative reform for water services with explicit climate-risk provisions.

policy_statement: Integrate climate risk and future adaptation into Treasury infrastructure investment guidance.
source_quote: The Treasury publishes a range of guidance for central government departments and other entities on investment management and state sector performance. It will integrate consideration of climate risks and future adaptation into this guidance.
section_header: Action 4.6: Integrate adaptation into Treasury decisions on infrastructure
extraction_rationale: This is a specific investment-management guidance change affecting public infrastructure decisions.

policy_statement: Integrate adaptation into Waka Kotahi land transport investment and decision-making frameworks.
source_quote: Waka Kotahi will incorporate adaptation in the Investment Decision Making Framework, its structured approach to decisions on investment in land transport. This will include business case development and risk assessment.
section_header: Action 4.7: Integrate adaptation into Waka Kotahi decision-making
extraction_rationale: This is a specific institutional decision-making change for transport investment adaptation.

policy_statement: Amend the Environmental Reporting Act 2015 to improve measurement and reporting of environmental change.
source_quote: This work seeks to improve how the Ministry for the Environment (MfE) monitors, manages, accesses and reports on the environment. The amendments will extend the Environmental Reporting Act's functionality and breadth so that environmental reports have more impact.
section_header: Action 4.8: Amend the Environmental Reporting Act 2015 to allow better measurement of environmental change
extraction_rationale: This is a legislative amendment with climate-adaptation relevance through environmental monitoring, but the climate link is indirect.

policy_statement: Pass Climate Adaptation Act legislation to establish a managed retreat framework.
source_quote: The Government will develop legislation to address the complex technical, legal and financial issues associated with managed retreat as described by the Resource Management Review Panel. This legislation is being progressed through the development of the Climate Adaptation Act.
section_header: Action 5.1: Pass legislation to support managed retreat
extraction_rationale: This is a binding legislative action to enable retreat from climate and natural hazard risk.

policy_statement: Review the future of local government, including funding and financing arrangements for adaptation challenges.
source_quote: Adaptation will bring new challenges and opportunities to local governance. The system must be equipped for agile, sustainable and proactive decision-makin g and implementation.
section_header: Action 5.2: The Future for Local Government review
extraction_rationale: This is a formal review addressing governance, funding and financing for climate adaptation.

policy_statement: Complete a Westport case study to explore co-investment options for flood resilience.
source_quote: The Department of Internal Affairs (DIA) is working with the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA), the West Coast Regional Council, the Buller District Council and local iwi to explore options to increase flood resilience in Westport. This case stud y will focus on the challenges facing small local authorities and vulnerable communities in funding flood risk management.
section_header: Action 5.3: Complete case study to explore co-investment for flood resilience
extraction_rationale: This is a specific case study and co-investment exploration for named flood resilience needs.
