policy_statement: Develop options to maintain an appropriate role for home flood insurance in community resilience.
source_quote: Work is underway to increase understanding of the scale and timing of changes to the insurance market arising from greater use of risk-based pricing by insurers and flooding exacerbated by climate change . This work includes exploring options to support access and affordability of flood insurance.
section_header: Action 5.4: Develop options for home flood insurance
extraction_rationale: This is a specific financial risk-transfer policy work programme for flood resilience.

policy_statement: Publish a programme of work on how New Zealand meets climate costs and invests in resilience.
source_quote: Additional investment from public and private sources must also be facilitated where necessary to respond to the growing risks from climate change. There are many processes underway that c ould change how New Zealanders currently share the costs of climate change.
section_header: Action 5.5: Publish the programme of work on how Aotearoa meets the costs of climate change and invests in resilience
extraction_rationale: This is a coordinated public work programme on adaptation financing and cost allocation.

policy_statement: Scope a resilience standard or code for infrastructure to encourage risk reduction and resilience planning.
source_quote: Te Waihanga will scope the impact (including of costs, benefits and regulations) of a standard or code for resilient infrastructure. This action will focus on: how a standard or code would encourage risk reduction and resilience planning in existing and new assets
section_header: Action 5.6: Scope a resilience standard or code for infrastructure
extraction_rationale: This is a specific regulatory/standards scoping action for infrastructure resilience.

policy_statement: Reduce and manage climate-hazard impacts on homes and buildings through information, research, guidance, assessment frameworks and incentives.
source_quote: This action includes five components that build off one another and are necessary to inform regulatory change and other actions in this chapter . These five components are :
section_header: Action 5.7: Reduce and manage the impacts of climate hazards on homes and buildings
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete multi-component action to support property-level climate adaptation and future regulation.

policy_statement: Support kaitiaki communities to adapt and conserve taonga and cultural assets threatened by climate change.
source_quote: Work across government to ensure hapū, iwi and Māori and communities have access to information so they can plan for a changing climate and adapt their cultural assets. Support includes advice, wānanga (conferences, forums, seminars), expert assistance, information sharing and funding advice for kaitiaki to self -determine adaptation pathways.
section_header: Action 5.8: Support kaitiaki communities to adapt and conserve taonga/cultural assets
extraction_rationale: This is a named cross-government support action for cultural-asset climate adaptation.

policy_statement: Prioritise nature-based solutions in planning and regulations for carbon removals and climate adaptation.
source_quote: To address the climate and biodiversity crises together, the Government will prioritise nature -based solutions in planning and regulations, where possible, for both carbon removals and climate change adaptation. It will also investigate how to best ensure that climate change policy and planning use a biodiversity lens to prioritise nature-based solutions.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete planning and regulatory prioritisation for nature-based solutions.

policy_statement: Develop and implement Transpower's Adaptation Plan for the national grid.
source_quote: The Transpower Adaptation Plan will outline how Transpower will adapt to climate change through the design, delivery and operation of the national grid. It will address exposed assets and new investment in infrastructure, and consider adaptation in maintenance and development programmes.
section_header: Action 5.10: Develop and implement the Transpower Adaptation Plan
extraction_rationale: This is a named infrastructure adaptation plan with specified asset and investment coverage.

policy_statement: Encourage and support evaluation of climate risks to landfills and contaminated sites.
source_quote: Coastal inundation and flooding could be a significant risk to existing and closed landfills and contaminated sites across the country. At least 110 closed landfills are vulnerable to sea-level rise.
section_header: Action 5.11: Encourage and support the evaluation of climate risks to landfills and contaminated sites
extraction_rationale: This is a specific risk-evaluation support action for named climate hazards and vulnerable assets.

policy_statement: Explore funding options for investigating and remediating contaminated sites and landfills vulnerable to climate impacts.
source_quote: Considering this, the Government has agreed to consider how best to support the funding of remediation. Access to funding will help to turn risk assessment into risk reduction, and ensure remediation occurs before inundation risks become a reality.
section_header: Action 5.12: Explore funding options to support the investigation and remediation of contaminated sites and landfills vulnerable to the effects of climate change
extraction_rationale: This is a specific funding-options work programme for climate-vulnerable contaminated sites and landfills.

policy_statement: Connect communities to wider disaster response and recovery support through locally led, regionally coordinated and nationally supported networks.
source_quote: This action will continue work with central and local government, communities (including rural communities), iwi, organisations and others to support effective, integrated disaster response and recovery. Communities affected by disasters will be assisted by networks that are locally led, regionally coordinated and nationally supported.
section_header: Action 5.13: Connect communities to wider response and recovery support
extraction_rationale: This is a continuing disaster response and recovery support action relevant to climate-related disruption.

policy_statement: Support development of a green taxonomy to define climate- and nature-positive investments.
source_quote: This will support the development of a 'green' taxonomy to identify a common definition of climate and naturepositive investments. This could help guide businesses that are investing in both adaptation and mitigation to protect against greenwashing.
section_header: Action 5.14: Support the development of definitional tools to encourage greater investment in 'green' projects
extraction_rationale: This is a specific financial-market classification tool to support adaptation and mitigation investment.

policy_statement: Use the Climate Emergency Response Fund and Sovereign Green Bond programme to support climate change initiatives.
source_quote: The Government is supporting climate change objectives through its approach to the public finance system. This includes the establishment of the Climate Emergency Response F und (CERF) and the Sovereign Green Bond (Green Bond) programme.
section_header: Action 5.15: Public investment in climate change initiatives
extraction_rationale: This is a public finance and investment policy, including named fund and bond instruments.

policy_statement: Identify options to integrate nature-based solutions into urban form to reduce flooding and heatwave impacts.
source_quote: This work will build on indigenous knowledge and new research to produce new data and insights on nature-based solutions such as vegetation (eg, street trees and green roofs) and water elements (eg, open canals and waterways). This action will help reduce the impact of climate events, such as flooding and heatwaves, in our urban areas to improve outcomes for people, communities and biodiversity.
section_header: Action 5.16: Identify options to increase the integration of nature-based solutions into urban form
extraction_rationale: This is a specific nature-based urban adaptation work programme naming heatwaves and flooding.

policy_statement: Implement the Department of Conservation Climate Change Adaptation Action Plan for public conservation land, waters and threatened species.
source_quote: The Department of Conservation (DOC) Climate Change Adaptation Action Plan (CCAAP) is a medium-term plan, which applies to public conservation land and waters managed by DOC, as well as threatened native species and systems. The plan aims to assess ecosystem and species vulnerability to climate impacts, and the adaptation actions to enhance their resilience.
section_header: Action 6.1: Implement the Department of Conservation Climate Change Adaptation Action Plan
extraction_rationale: This is a named implementation plan for ecosystem and species climate adaptation.

policy_statement: Engage with councils to implement the New Zealand Coastal Policy Statement for coastal ecosystem and hazard management.
source_quote: The NZCPS provides the policy mechanism for protecting indi genous biodiversity in the coastal environment, and for managing risks to coastal ecosystems (policies 11, and 24-27 NZCPS). The NZCPS's coastal hazard management mechanisms include managed retreat and nature - based solutions.
section_header: Action 6.2: Engage with councils to implement the New Zealand Coastal Policy Statement
extraction_rationale: This is a policy implementation action for coastal ecosystem protection and climate hazard management.

policy_statement: Implement Te Mana o te Taiao to protect, restore and sustainably use biodiversity and align biodiversity and climate action.
source_quote: Te Mana o te Taiao - Aotearoa New Zealand Biodiversity Strategy 2020 (ANZBS) is a strategic document for the protection, restoration and sustainable use of biodiversity in Aotearoa from 2020 to 2050. A priority of ANZBS is to ensure efforts to tackle biodiversity loss and climate change are reciprocal.
section_header: Action 6.3: Implement Te Mana o te Taiao - Aotearoa New Zealand Biodiversity Strategy 2020
extraction_rationale: This is a named national biodiversity strategy with climate resilience and nature-based solution goals.

policy_statement: Implement the National Policy Statement on Indigenous Biodiversity to protect, maintain and restore indigenous biodiversity and ecological corridors.
source_quote: The objective of the NPS -IB is to protect, maintain and restore indigenous biodiversity. The NPS -IB plays a part in building the resilience of biodiversity to climate change through its role in protecting, maintaining and restoring biodiversity, including requiring councils and landowners to consider creating ecological corridors.
section_header: Action 6.4: Implement the proposed National Policy Statement on Indigenous Biodiversity
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory biodiversity policy statement with specific climate resilience relevance.

policy_statement: Implement the Water Availability and Security programme to help rural communities and food and fibre businesses adapt to variable freshwater availability.
source_quote: The Water A vailability and Security programme will help food and fibre businesses and rural communities adapt to increasingly variable natural water availability through a range of complementary activities to both reduce demand and make best use of available water. It will help restore and maintain the health of waterways, taking its lead from the National Policy Statement on Freshwater Management.
section_header: Action 6.6: Implement the Water Availability and Security programme
extraction_rationale: This is a named water programme using demand reduction and better water use to adapt to climate variability.

policy_statement: Implement the National Policy Statement on Freshwater Management 2020 to protect freshwater ecosystem health and support adaptation.
source_quote: The National Policy Statement on Freshwater Management 2020 (NPS-FM 2020) applies to all freshwater, including groundwater, and will require management of freshwater in both rural and urban areas. It requires councils to give effect to Te Mana o te Wai, which prioriti ses the health and wellbeing of water bodies and freshwater ecosystems.
section_header: Action 6.7: Implement the National Policy Statement on Freshwater Management 2020
extraction_rationale: This is a binding national policy statement regulating freshwater management and ecosystem resilience.

policy_statement: Deliver Biosecurity New Zealand actions to reduce invasive species risks to indigenous ecosystems and build climate resilience.
source_quote: The following actions address risks to indigenous ecosystems and species that result from the greater spread, survival and establishment of invasive species. They also help build climate resilience of ecosystems generally.
section_header: Action 6.8: Deliver a collection of actions run by Biosecurity New Zealand
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella action followed by numbered biosecurity sub-actions 6.8.1 through 6.8.8.

parent_statement: Action 6.8: Deliver a collection of actions run by Biosecurity New Zealand
policy_statement: Implement an on-farm biosecurity programme to improve voluntary biosecurity practices and resilience.
source_quote: This programme aims to improve biosecurity on dairy and sheep and beef farms and create a more resilient biosecurity system. It is responsible for developing and implementing an action plan to overcome barriers and increase voluntary on-farm biosecurity practices.
section_header: Action 6.8.1: Implement an on-farm biosecurity programme
extraction_rationale: This is a specific biosecurity programme supporting ecosystem and agricultural resilience.

parent_statement: Action 6.8: Deliver a collection of actions run by Biosecurity New Zealand
policy_statement: Invest in border biosecurity projects for mail and sea cargo pathways to protect biodiversity from pest species.
source_quote: Two significant projects (Sea Cargo Programme and Mail Pathways Project) delivered by Biosecurity New Zealand will improve how we address the biosecurity risk from mail and sea cargo pathways. They will also protect biodiversity by identifying pest species that arrive through our international borders.
section_header: Action 6.8.2: Invest in strengthening border biosecurity
extraction_rationale: This is a named investment in border biosecurity projects relevant to climate-amplified invasive species risk.

parent_statement: Action 6.8: Deliver a collection of actions run by Biosecurity New Zealand
policy_statement: Continue the Freshwater Biosecurity Partnership Programme and Check Clean Dry campaign to prevent freshwater pest spread.
source_quote: The programme's vision is to take collaborative action to protect Aotearoa New Zealand's freshwater from the impacts of freshwater pests. A changing climate could make more waterways vulnerable to freshwater p est establishment.
section_header: Action 6.8.3: Continue the Freshwater Biosecurity Partnership Programme
extraction_rationale: This is a named collaborative programme responding to climate-amplified freshwater pest risk.

parent_statement: Action 6.8: Deliver a collection of actions run by Biosecurity New Zealand
policy_statement: Implement the Clean Hull programme to reduce marine pest spread through domestic vessel movements.
source_quote: This involves implementing a behaviour change programme to address the risks of marine pest spread via domestic vessel movements. This will build on existing marine biosecurity partnerships in the upper North Island, upper South Island and Fiordland.
section_header: Action 6.8.4: Reduce the spread and impacts of marine pest species through the Clean Hull programme
extraction_rationale: This is a specific behavioural biosecurity programme to protect marine ecosystems.

parent_statement: Action 6.8: Deliver a collection of actions run by Biosecurity New Zealand
policy_statement: Prevent, contain or eradicate wilding conifers by 2030 to reduce fire risk, improve water availability and protect biodiversity.
source_quote: Established in 2016, this programme ensures a collaborative, coordinated and effective national approach to wilding conifer control. This reduces fire risk, improves water availability (including for hydropower generation), prevents the loss of productive land and preserves the biodiversity of indigenous ecosystems.
section_header: Action 6.8.5: Prevent the spread of wilding conifers, and contain or eradicate established areas of wilding conifers by 2030
extraction_rationale: This is a quantifiable pest-control target with climate adaptation benefits for fire and water risks.

parent_statement: Action 6.8: Deliver a collection of actions run by Biosecurity New Zealand
policy_statement: Continue the National Interest Pest Responses programme to eradicate or reduce harmful weed infestations.
source_quote: Nine harmful weeds are managed under the National Interest Pest Responses (NIPR) programme, with the aim of eradicating them or significantly reducing infestations. These weeds could cause serious harm to Aotearoa's environment and economy if allowed to spread.
section_header: Action 6.8.6: Continue the National Interest Pest Responses programme
extraction_rationale: This is a named pest-response programme with a defined eradication/reduction objective.

parent_statement: Action 6.8: Deliver a collection of actions run by Biosecurity New Zealand
policy_statement: Invest in a plant health and environmental capability facility to support plant-sector resilience to pests and diseases.
source_quote: Significant investment in Ministry for Primary Industry (MPI) plant health and environment work (currently in Tāmaki, Auckland) will support growth and development in the arable, forestry and horticulture sectors. Faster access to genetic material can support innovation and bring benefits such as higher yields and resilience to pests and diseases.
section_header: Action 6.8.7: Invest in plant health and environmental capability facility
extraction_rationale: This is a significant investment in plant health capability relevant to climate-resilient primary sectors.

parent_statement: Action 6.8: Deliver a collection of actions run by Biosecurity New Zealand
policy_statement: Use animal and plant health laboratories to improve diagnosis and management of emerging pests and diseases likely in a changing climate.
source_quote: The Animal Health Laboratory (AHL) and Plant Health Environment Laboratory (PHEL) are national reference laboratories that identify and validate suspected exotic and endemic pests and diseases affecting farm and aquatic animals. They bring a better understanding of new and emerging pests and diseases that are likely to establish in a changing climate.
section_header: Action 6.8.8: Use the Animal Health Laboratory and Plant Health and Environment Laboratory
extraction_rationale: This is a laboratory capability action tied to climate-driven pest and disease emergence.

policy_statement: Deliver Jobs for Nature projects to restore ecosystems, control pests and mobilise community action.
source_quote: This action support s more than 200 projects to restore ecosystems, control pests and mobilise community action across the country. Biodiversity can be strengthened by restoring ecosystems and reducing pests.
section_header: Action 6.9: Deliver Jobs for Nature to restore indigenous ecosystems
extraction_rationale: This is a funded programme supporting over 200 ecosystem restoration projects.

policy_statement: Implement Revitalising the Gulf actions including new marine protection areas and habitat restoration.
source_quote: This initiative includes establishing 19 new areas of marine protection and an area-based fisheries plan in the Hauraki Gulf Marine Park. Other elements include restricting trawling to specified trawl corridors, protected species initiatives, active habitat restoration, marine biosecurity, aquaculture and Ahu Moana (local marine management by mana whenua and communities).
section_header: Action 6.10: Implement Revitalising the Gulf: Government action on the Sea Change Plan
extraction_rationale: This is a named marine ecosystem programme with quantified protected areas and restoration actions.

policy_statement: Implement the South-east Marine Protection Initiative to establish new protected marine areas and improve ecosystem resilience.
source_quote: This initiative may result in 12 new areas of marine protection in the southeast waters of the South Island, comanaged by the Crown and Ngāi Tahu . It will improve the health of the marine ecosystem (and therefore its resilience) by managing impacts, and will inform future management through science, mātauranga Māori and monitoring.
section_header: Action 6.11: Implement the South-east Marine Protection Initiative
extraction_rationale: This is a specific marine protection initiative with quantified potential protected areas.

policy_statement: Implement the Sustainable Land Management Hill Country Erosion Programme to treat erosion-prone land and support afforestation.
source_quote: Th e Sustainable Land Management Hill Country Erosion Programme will support regional planning for, and treatment of, erosion-prone land and, in turn, contribute to afforestation. Afforestation can reduce soil loss and other effects from the increasing scale and magnitude of storms.
section_header: Action 6.12: Implement the Sustainable Land Management Hill Country Erosion Programme
extraction_rationale: This is a named programme using afforestation and land treatment to reduce storm and erosion impacts.

policy_statement: Research how cultural heritage contributes to community wellbeing and climate change adaptation.
source_quote: This research will look at the value of cultural heritage in building and sustaining communities, and how this links to community resilience and wellbeing.
section_header: Action 7.1: Research how cultural heritage contributes to community wellbeing and climate change adaptation
extraction_rationale: This is a proposed research action explicitly linked to community resilience and adaptation.

policy_statement: Partner with Māori landowners to develop resources and tools increasing resilience of Māori-owned land, homes and cultural sites.
source_quote: This work will be progressed in partnership with Māori landowners to produce resources and tools to improve understanding of climate-related risks and increase the resilience of housing on Māori land. It will promote mātauranga Māori and increase the resilience of Māori -owned land, homes and cultural sites.
section_header: Action 7.2: Partner with Māori landowners to increase the resilience of Māori -owned land, homes and cul tural sites
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete partnership and tool-development action for Māori land and housing adaptation.

policy_statement: Partner with Māori to support Māori-led adaptation planning and solutions using mātauranga Māori and Māori urban design principles.
source_quote: This work will be progressed in partnership with Māori to support Māori -led adaptation planning for example, in the new resource management system. This will support Māori -led adaptation solutions and the use of mātauranga Māori and Māori urban design principles in response to climate hazards.
section_header: Action 7.3: Partner with Māori to support Māori -led approaches to adaptation planning
extraction_rationale: This is a specific partnership action for Māori-led climate adaptation planning.

policy_statement: Update building regulatory requirements so buildings withstand more extreme climate hazards.
source_quote: Updated forward-looking climate data and modelling (action 3.2: Design and develop risk and resilience and climate adaptation information portals) will be used to: update Building Code performance requirements. This action will improve the quality of buildings and make them more resilient to future climate impacts.
section_header: Action 7.4: Update regulatory requirements to ensure buildings are designed and constructed to withstand more extreme climate hazards
extraction_rationale: This is a proposed regulatory update to the Building Code and climate hazard requirements.

policy_statement: Review and update housing and urban strategies, programmes and regulations for climate fitness.
source_quote: Current strategies, programmes and regulations will be reviewed to ensure housing and urban environments are fit for the changing climate. For example, this could lead to updated requirements for homeowners and landlords, or for public and community housing.
section_header: Action 7.5: Update housing and urban settings
extraction_rationale: This is a proposed review of regulatory and programme settings for climate-resilient housing and urban environments.

policy_statement: Monitor and manage adverse impacts of adaptation-related building regulatory changes on vulnerable communities.
source_quote: Vulnerable communities, such as those living along the coast or those with low incomes, may require additional support to adapt their homes and buildings. The Government will monitor the effects of action 5.7: Reduce and manage the impacts of climate hazards on homes and buildings and action 7.4: Update regulatory requirements to ensure buildings are designed and constructed to withstand more extreme climate hazards to identify who these regulatory changes may adversely affect.
section_header: Action 7.6: Manage potential impacts of adaptation related to regulatory change
extraction_rationale: This is a proposed equity safeguard and monitoring policy tied to adaptation regulations.

policy_statement: Develop and implement the Waka Kotahi Climate Adaptation Plan for land transport assets, investments and maintenance.
source_quote: In 2022, Waka Kotahi will publish and begin applyin g an adaptation plan. This will outline how Waka Kotahi will adapt to climate change through the design, delivery, operation and use of the land transport system.
section_header: Action 8.1: Develop and implement the Waka Kotahi Climate Adaptation Plan
extraction_rationale: This is a named adaptation plan for transport infrastructure with implementation and reporting commitments.

policy_statement: Develop a National Energy Strategy to support a net-zero, secure, reliable and affordable energy system.
source_quote: The Government has committed to developing an energy strategy by the end of 2024, fully collaborating and engaging with Māori and working with energy system stakeholders. The vision is for a net-zero economy in 2050, where energy is accessible and affordable, secure and reliable, and supports New Zealanders' wellbeing.
section_header: Action 8.2: Develop the National Energy Strategy
extraction_rationale: This is a named national strategy with a 2050 net-zero energy vision and sector pathways.

policy_statement: Manage dry-year electricity risk through the New Zealand Battery Project, including pumped hydro feasibility.
source_quote: The New Zealand Battery Project will assess the options for managing dry-year risk in a highly renewable electricity system. The current focus is on the feasibility of pumped hydroelectricity at Lake Onslow.
section_header: Action 8.3: Manage dry-year risk through the New Zealand Battery Project
extraction_rationale: This is a named energy resilience project addressing hydro low-inflow/dry-year risk.

policy_statement: Allow regulated network revenue settings to reflect prudent and efficient resilience costs.
source_quote: In the Commerce Commission's next reviews of regulated price-quality paths - from 2025 for electricity networks and from 2026 for gas networks - it will consider the extent to which revenue limits should provide for differe nt expenditure levels from the current period. This will include if expenditure levels need to change due to any increased costs of resilience to climate change, where these are based on robust forecasts.
section_header: Action 8.4: Provide for regulated network revenues to reflect the prudent and efficient costs of resilience
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory financial mechanism allowing climate resilience costs in utility revenue limits.

policy_statement: Progress the Rail Network Investment Programme to restore the rail network to a resilient and reliable state.
source_quote: KiwiRail's Rail Network Investment Programme (RNIP) is a 10-year programme of investment in Aotearoa New Zealand's rail network, to restore it to a resilient and reliable state. Mitigating climate change is a key focus within the RNIP when considering resilience projects for investment.
section_header: Action 8.5: Progress the Rail Network Investment Programme
extraction_rationale: This is a 10-year public investment programme for resilient rail infrastructure with climate mitigation relevance.

policy_statement: Invest in public and active transport to increase transport-system resilience and reduce private-vehicle reliance.
source_quote: Investment in multi-modal infrastructure can increase the resilience of the transport system and help manage the vulnerability of existing assets. More use of public transport and active modes will help reduce reliance on private vehicles.
section_header: Action 8.6: Invest in public transport and active transport
extraction_rationale: This is a public infrastructure investment action for multimodal and resilient transport.

policy_statement: Embed nature-based solutions in transport policy and investment to reduce emissions and improve adaptation and biodiversity outcomes.
source_quote: At a local, regional and national scale these measures can reduce transport emissions and improve climate adaptation as well as biodiversity. Key initiatives include: considering the role of nature-based solutions in reducing transport emissions and contributing to other benefits
section_header: Action 8.7: Embed nature-based solutions as part of the response to reducing transport emissions and improving climate adaptation and biodiversity outcomes
extraction_rationale: This is a specific commitment to integrate nature-based solutions into transport policy and investment.

policy_statement: Support infrastructure-sector knowledge sharing and implementation of adaptation actions.
source_quote: Te Waihanga will convene a regular event for local government, central government and private sector asset owners to share information on the implementation of actions in the national adaptation plan and to support alignment across the sector. Initially, the focus may be on the scope and content of the actions on adaptation guidance that Te Waihanga has committed to in the national adaptation plan, but may also provide a forum for updates on other policy matters relevant to infrastructure asset owners.
section_header: Action 8.8: Support knowledge sharing and the implementation of adaptation actions across the sector
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete sector coordination and knowledge-sharing mechanism for infrastructure adaptation.

policy_statement: Modernise the emergency management system through legislative reform, clearer roles, community work and stronger Māori partnership.
source_quote: The National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) plans to modernise emergency management, including through legislative reforms, working with communities and organisations, clearer roles and responsibilities, and a strengthened partnership with Māori. By 2024, new emergency management legislation will be adopted, and a national emergency management plan and improved guidance will be provided across the emergency management system.
section_header: Action 9.1: Modernise the emergency management system
extraction_rationale: This is a binding and operational reform programme for emergency resilience under increasing climate hazards.

policy_statement: Develop the Health National Adaptation Plan and regional climate health action plans.
source_quote: The Health National Adaptation Plan (HNAP) will complement the national adaptation plan and be supported by regional climate health action plans developed by the health sector. The aim of the HNAP is to prepare the health sector to meet the needs of communities in terms of the effects of climate change, including physical, mental and cultural health and wellbeing.
section_header: Action 9.2: Develop the Health National Adaptation Plan
extraction_rationale: This is a named sectoral adaptation plan for health, with regional implementation plans.

policy_statement: Develop the emergency management workforce to address increased frequency and severity of natural hazards.
source_quote: Work is ongoing to expand the operational capacity and capability of the emergency management workforce at the national, regional and local levels. This will position Aotearoa better to address the increased frequency and severity of natural hazards and support all people in response and recovery.
section_header: Action 9.3: Develop the emergency management workforce
extraction_rationale: This is a workforce capacity-building action for climate-amplified hazard response.

policy_statement: Implement the Climate Migration Action Plan for Pacific climate displacement and migration.
source_quote: Key values of the Climate Migration Action Plan include retaining social and cultural identity for Pacific communities, and supporting Pacific peoples to live in their own countries where possible. This work aims to support these communities to grow and th rive despite the challenges of climate-related displacement and migration .
section_header: Action: 9.4: Implement the Climate Migration Action Plan
extraction_rationale: This is a named action plan addressing climate-related displacement and migration.

policy_statement: Continue health and disability system reforms to strengthen local, equitable and environmentally informed public health services.
source_quote: The structure of the health and disability system and the delivery of health services are undergoing a period of reform. The new system will be simpler and more coordinated, allowing for better and more consistent care, shaped by the voices of consumers, communities and whānau.
section_header: Action 9.5: Continue with the reform of the health and disability system
extraction_rationale: This is a major system reform that supports adaptation capacity but is not primarily climate-specific.

policy_statement: Build community resilience through social cohesion, inclusion and participation.
source_quote: This work will improve inclusion and participation in society and build community resilience to lessen instability and isolation caused by climate change. The aim is to support the understanding of diversity within and across communities to allow everyone to feel safe and belong, and to access opportunities.
section_header: Action 9.6: Build community resilience through social cohesion
extraction_rationale: This is a specific social-cohesion programme tied to climate-related instability and isolation.

policy_statement: Strengthen climate change teaching and learning in schools, kura and early learning services.
source_quote: This work will improve community resilience by addressing inequities in learning outcomes that impact on lifelong wellbeing. It will support early learning services, schools and kura to include understanding of, and responses to, climate change in their local curricula and marau ā -kura (living, breathing curriculum), as well as learning that is important for social cohesion .
section_header: Action 9.7: Strengthen teaching and learning related to climate change
extraction_rationale: This is a specific education action to build climate literacy and community resilience.

policy_statement: Continue welfare system overhaul to improve income, employment, health and community support for vulnerable people.
source_quote: This action will make ongoing improvements in support - such as for employment, health and communities - and in incomes for those interacting with the welfare system. This aims to achieve the Government's vision of a welfare system that ensures people have an adequate income and standard of living; are treated with, and can live in, dignity; and can participate meaningfully in their communities.
section_header: Action 9.8: Continue to overhaul the welfare system
extraction_rationale: This supports adaptive capacity of vulnerable groups, though it is a broader welfare reform not solely climate-focused.

policy_statement: Expand funding for proactive Māori and community resilience through Whānau Ora.
source_quote: This will seek to expand funding for Māori to build their community resilience through the COVID-19 pandemic, and plug funding gaps for communities to carry out their long-term resilience plans. Funding would be decentralised by expanding the scope of funds provided through Whānau Ora .
section_header: Action 9.9: Expand current funding for proactive community resilience
extraction_rationale: This is a proposed funding expansion for community resilience and long-term adaptation capacity.

policy_statement: Implement an income insurance scheme to support workers and communities affected by economic disruption, including climate-related disruption.
source_quote: To better protect workers, whānau, households, communities and the wider economy, the Government is developing a proposal for a New Zealand income insurance scheme, which would support workers with a proportion of income replacement for up to seven months if they lose their job through no fault of their own due to a redundancy or a health condition or disability. This policy would reduce the economic impacts of a changing climate on workers and communities by, for example, cushioning the impact of a large employer closing or resizing in a small town or region, and enabling workers to transition to new job opportunities afforded by changes in the economy.
section_header: Action 9.10: Implement an income insurance scheme to support adaptive capacity of communities and the economy
extraction_rationale: This is a proposed insurance financial instrument explicitly linked to adaptive capacity and climate economic impacts.

policy_statement: Develop and deliver Defence climate crisis implementation initiatives covering mitigation, adaptation, infrastructure, capability and response operations.
source_quote: The plan identifies actions Defence will take as part of a broader government programme on climate change and sustainability. It sets out initiatives for mitigation and adaptation of Defence Force infrastructure, capability and response operations that protect the security of New Zealanders and the region.
section_header: Action 9.11: Develop and deliver initiatives in Responding to the Climate Crisis: An Implementation Plan (2019)
extraction_rationale: This is a named Defence implementation plan with climate mitigation and adaptation initiatives.

policy_statement: Produce guidance and tools for monitoring and evaluating adaptation initiatives.
source_quote: This will help ensure adaptation actions effectively increase our resilience and manage the risks we face. Monitoring is essential for an effective plan, and this guidance will help users identify signals that an action is no longer meeting its objectives.
section_header: Action 9.12: Produce guidance and tools for monitoring and evaluating the impact of adaptation initiatives
extraction_rationale: This is a specific monitoring and evaluation guidance/tool commitment for adaptation policy.

policy_statement: Review and expand active labour market programmes to help workers adapt to climate-driven economic change.
source_quote: Active labour market programmes (ALMPs) assist people into employment (including removing barriers to their ability to get or retain a job, or to move between jobs), increase earning capacity and improve the functioning of the labour market. It has committed to expanding existing, and introducing new, ALMPs to support people into work, or back to work, and to take up new job opportunities arising from changes in the economy.
section_header: Action 9.13: Review of active labour market programmes
extraction_rationale: This is a labour-market support programme with explicit adaptation relevance to changing climate impacts on workers and communities.

policy_statement: Deliver the New Zealand Freight and Supply Chain Strategy to improve resilience, reliability and disruption preparedness.
source_quote: This strategy will present a long -term and system-wide view of the freight system. Climate adaptation is being considered through the resilience outcome, to ensure Aotearoa New Zealand's freight and supply chain system is resilient, reliable and prepared for disruption.
section_header: Action 10.1: Deliver the New Zealand Freight and Supply Chain strategy
extraction_rationale: This is a named strategy with a specific climate adaptation resilience outcome for freight and supply chains.

policy_statement: Strengthen fisheries rules through the Fisheries Amendment Bill to make fisheries management more responsive to climate-driven stock changes.
source_quote: The Government is progressing work on the Fisheries Amendment Bill , which includes several legislative changes to the Fisheries Act 1996 . The aim is to strengthen and modernise Aotearoa New Zealand 's fisheries management system.
extraction_rationale: This is a legislative fisheries management reform with climate responsiveness for fish-stock abundance.

policy_statement: Deliver the Aquaculture Strategy to support sustainable, innovative aquaculture and industry adaptation to climate change.
source_quote: The Government's Aquaculture Strategy sets objectives and actions to support Aotearoa in becoming a world leader in sustainable and innovative aquaculture. One of the strategy's objectives is to support the industry to adapt to climate change.
extraction_rationale: This is a named sector strategy with explicit climate adaptation objectives and implementation plans.

policy_statement: Integrate climate risk into Reserve Bank supervision, stress-testing and guidance for financial entities.
source_quote: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) is taking action to help regulated financial entities identify and manage climate risks better . This includes: introducing climate-related stress tests that model the effect of severe but plausible scenarios on the balance sheets of regulated financial institutions
section_header: Action 10.4: Reserve Bank of New Zealand supports the stability of the financial system
extraction_rationale: This is a financial-regulatory supervisory action addressing climate-risk management and stability.

policy_statement: Deliver a Māori agribusiness extension programme supporting intergenerational planning for climate impacts on whenua Māori.
source_quote: This action will deliver a tailored extension programme for whenua Māori . As part of the programme, landowners will consider how best to plan intergenerationally for the impacts of climate change on their whenua.
section_header: Action 10.5: Deliver the Māori agribusiness extension programme
extraction_rationale: This is a tailored sector extension programme for Māori landowners and climate adaptation.

policy_statement: Continue Sustainable Land Management and Climate Change and Greenhouse Gas Inventory research programmes.
source_quote: This work will fund research and develop tools to support the agriculture sector to adapt to climate change better, measure emissions and mitigate land-use impacts on freshwater. It includes science extension and policy research and the ability to respond to the social impacts of climate change.
section_header: Action 10.6: Continue delivering the Sustainable Land Management and Climate Change and Greenhouse Gas Inventory research programmes
extraction_rationale: This is a research funding and tool-development programme for agricultural adaptation and emissions measurement.

policy_statement: Continue delivering the Sustainable Food and Fibre Futures Fund to co-invest in primary-sector climate innovation.
source_quote: The Sustainable Food and Fibre (SFF) Futures Fund supports innovative projects that design and test new approaches and solutions to risks such as climate change in the primary sector. The fund supports innovation in Aotearoa New Zealand's food and fibre sector by co-investing in initiatives that bring economic, environmental and social benefits for all New Zealanders.
section_header: Action 10.7: Continue delivering the Sustainable Food and Fibre Futures Fund
extraction_rationale: This is a named co-investment fund supporting climate-related primary-sector innovation.

policy_statement: Establish innovation grants to boost private-sector research and development for adaptation and low-emissions transition.
source_quote: These grants will boost investment in private sector research and development and support innovation. They will share the risk with Aotearoa companies.
extraction_rationale: This is a grant instrument for climate-focused innovation and adaptation.

policy_statement: Model and identify climate change impacts on regional economies to guide local risk assessments and investments.
source_quote: This work will involve modelling the economic impacts of a changing climate on regional economies and providing guidance for assessing climate impacts in local economic decisions. This will help to identify likely impacts and determine where our vulnerable communities are by exploring the distribution of economic impacts across different parts of Aotearoa.
section_header: Action 10.9: Identify the impacts of climate change on regional economies
extraction_rationale: This is a specific modelling and guidance action for regional economic climate adaptation.

policy_statement: Monitor residential insurance premiums and uptake to understand insurance availability and affordability shifts.
source_quote: Monitoring residential premiums and uptake of insurance gives a better understanding of the scale of shifts in insurance availability and affordability.
extraction_rationale: This is a monitoring action for climate-related insurance market shifts; it is not itself an insurance instrument.

policy_statement: Consider climate risk in Treasury economic and fiscal monitoring and forecasting.
source_quote: Treasury's six -monthly economic updates are a core way to monitor and forecast the economic and fiscal environment. The updates highlight known quantifiable and unquantifiable climate adaptation risks as a tool in fiscal and economic management.
section_header: Action 10.11: Consider climate risk in economic and fiscal monitoring and forecasting
extraction_rationale: This is a recurring fiscal-monitoring commitment to incorporate climate adaptation risks.

policy_statement: Implement the government response to the Prime Minister's Chief Science Advisor's commercial fishing report.
source_quote: This report makes several recommendations for the fisheries management system and for commercial fishers. The Government's response is underway and includes actions that support innovation across the system, progress an ecosystem approach to fisheries management and protect habitats of significance to fisheries management.
section_header: Action 10.12: Implement the Government response to the Prime Minister's Chief Science Advisor's report on commercial fishing
extraction_rationale: This is a specific fisheries-management implementation action supporting ecosystem-based resilience.

policy_statement: Support implementation of the Aotearoa Circle Seafood Sector Adaptation Strategy.
source_quote: This is an early example of a sector working together with Government, iwi and stakeholders to produce an adaptation strategy, including an implementation roadmap. It is an opportunity to adapt in ways that bring lasting co-benefits to habitats, ecosystems, communities and businesses.
section_header: CASE STUDY Seafood Sector Adaptation Strategy, 2021 -2030
extraction_rationale: The action title appears in cross-references, and the case study describes an implementation roadmap for sector adaptation.

policy_statement: Deliver the Tourism Industry Transformation Plan using tourism adaptation work to minimise climate impacts on tourism workers, businesses and communities.
source_quote: The Tourism Adaptation Roadmap developed by the Aotearoa Circle will be an input for the environmental phase of the Tourism Industry Transformation Plan. This allows for a sector-wide assessment of risks and actions.
section_header: Action 10.14: Deliver the Tourism Industry Transformation Plan
extraction_rationale: This is a named tourism-sector plan incorporating adaptation roadmap inputs.

policy_statement: Review the International Visitor Conservation and Tourism Levy to support resilient infrastructure and natural environments used by visitors.
source_quote: The Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), directed by the Minister of Tourism, is reviewing the International Visitor Conservation and Tourism Levy (IVL). This includes ensuring international visitors contribute to resilient, adaptable infrastructure and the natural environment they use during their visit.
section_header: Action 10.15: Review the settings for the International Visitor Conservation and Tourism Levy
extraction_rationale: This is a levy review with explicit climate resilience and adaptation spending relevance.

policy_statement: Leverage government procurement to enable mitigation and adaptation in public investments, especially construction.
source_quote: This action w ill check the current government's procurement policy framework enables mitigation and adaptation in government investments. The greatest opportunity will likely be in construction contracts, making buildings and infrastructure resilient to a changing climate, and reducing carbon emissions and waste.
section_header: Action 10.16: Leverage government procurement for climate outcomes
extraction_rationale: This is a procurement policy review to incorporate climate adaptation and mitigation outcomes.

policy_statement: Support Māori small and medium enterprises to develop low-emissions growth strategies and climate resilience.
source_quote: The aim of this work is to support Māori small and medium enterprises to develop low -emissions growth strategies, respond to climate-related risks and opportunities, and adopt resilient ways of working. Businesses would commit to reducing their emissions or improving their resilience to physical climate events.
section_header: Action 10.17: Support Māori small business resilience and transitions
extraction_rationale: This is a proposed support programme for Māori SMEs with explicit emissions and resilience commitments.

policy_statement: Research business adaptation preparedness and provide targeted guidance for small businesses to reduce climate risks.
source_quote: This will help small businesses reduce their climate risks through targeted guidance and information. The guidance will be based on research that will increase understanding of what businesses are doing to adapt, and the pain points for business owners.
section_header: Action 10.18: Research business adaptation preparedness and provide guidance for small businesses to adapt
extraction_rationale: This is a proposed research and guidance programme for small-business climate adaptation.

policy_statement: Enhance industry partnership networks to pool knowledge and resources for climate adaptation and innovation.
source_quote: This action will pool knowledge and resources to solve sector problems. The partnerships will recognise the complexity and interrelatedness of issues, such as climate adaptation, and the need for sophisticated networks to test, scale up and spread innovation to help address challenges facing Aotearoa.
extraction_rationale: This is a proposed sector partnership network action with explicit climate adaptation purpose.

policy_statement: Establish central government oversight and coordination for implementation of the national adaptation plan.
source_quote: This will provide transparency of implementation of the plan across government, improve coordination within central government and enable accountability. Annual reporting requirements by agencies will be completed each year, commencing in 2023.
section_header: Action 11.1: Establish central government oversight and coordination for implementing the national adaptation plan
extraction_rationale: This is a governance implementation policy with annual reporting requirements and cross-government coordination.

policy_statement: Italy commits to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 6.5% below 1990 levels under the Kyoto Protocol burden-sharing agreement.
source_quote: Italy  has  ratified  the  Kyoto  Protocol  on  1 st June 2002. The ratification law prescribes that: 1. Italy's greenhouse gas emissions should be reduced by 6.5%, compared to 1990 levels, as agreed under the European 'burden sharing' adopted by the European Union on 4 th March 2002;
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified national emissions-reduction target established by ratification law; it is a core mitigation policy.

policy_statement: Italy allocates 25 million Euro per year for 2002-2004 to pilot projects for energy efficiency, clean fuels and engines, and carbon sinks.
source_quote: 3. 25  millions  Euro/year  have  been  allocated,for the period 2002-2004, to support pilot projects to enhance energy efficiency, to promote clean fuels and engines, to increase carbon sinks; 4. 68  millions  Euro/year  have  been  allocated,  by 2003,  to  support  projects  in  the  developing countries aimed to reduce greenhouse gas emissions reduce, and to promote the adaptation to the adverse effects of climate change.
extraction_rationale: This is a committed public funding allocation for named climate mitigation interventions and carbon sinks.

policy_statement: Italy allocates 68 million Euro per year by 2003 for developing-country projects to reduce GHG emissions and support adaptation.
source_quote: 3. 25  millions  Euro/year  have  been  allocated,for the period 2002-2004, to support pilot projects to enhance energy efficiency, to promote clean fuels and engines, to increase carbon sinks; 4. 68  millions  Euro/year  have  been  allocated,  by 2003,  to  support  projects  in  the  developing countries aimed to reduce greenhouse gas emissions reduce, and to promote the adaptation to the adverse effects of climate change.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific climate finance commitment with mitigation and adaptation objectives.

policy_statement: The Regions and Autonomous Provinces commit to coordinate policies aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
source_quote: AGREEMENT PROTOCOL OF THE CONFERENCE OF THE PRESIDENTS OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENTS AND OF AUTONOMOUS PROVINCES FOR THE COORDINATION OF POLICIES AIMED AT REDUCING EMISSIONS OF GREENHOUSE GASES INTO THE ATMOSPHERE. The Regions and Autonomous Provinces, having taken note: - -that it would appear necessary to arrive at a reduction in greenhouse gases, so as to contribute to maintaining the commitment made by the Italian State under the obligations of the EU stipulated in international  accords  and  formalised  in  Resolution  137/98  of  the  Inter-Ministerial  Committee  on Economic Planning on 19 November 1998;
section_header: Conference of the Presidents of Regional Governments and of Autonomous Provinces
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella intergovernmental protocol with specific sub-commitments listed beneath it.

parent_statement: Agreement Protocol of the Conference of the Presidents of Regional Governments and Autonomous Provinces for the coordination of policies aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions
policy_statement: Regional and autonomous provincial policies shall be oriented as far as possible toward reducing greenhouse gases.
source_quote: undertake to guarantee: that their various policies shall be oriented, to the greatest extent possible, towards the reduction of greenhouse gases; that initiatives and financing, both Central-State and local, shall be coordinated for the priority objective of sustainability;
section_header: Conference of the Presidents of Regional Governments and of Autonomous Provinces
extraction_rationale: This is a stated governance commitment to orient regional policies toward GHG reduction, though broad.

parent_statement: Agreement Protocol of the Conference of the Presidents of Regional Governments and Autonomous Provinces for the coordination of policies aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions
policy_statement: Central and local initiatives and financing shall be coordinated toward sustainability.
source_quote: undertake to guarantee: that their various policies shall be oriented, to the greatest extent possible, towards the reduction of greenhouse gases; that initiatives and financing, both Central-State and local, shall be coordinated for the priority objective of sustainability;
section_header: Conference of the Presidents of Regional Governments and of Autonomous Provinces
extraction_rationale: This is a coordination commitment involving financing; the climate link is through the GHG-reduction protocol but the statement itself is sustainability-oriented.

parent_statement: Agreement Protocol of the Conference of the Presidents of Regional Governments and Autonomous Provinces for the coordination of policies aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions
policy_statement: Regions shall formulate optimal GHG-reduction strategies within air quality safeguarding and reclamation plans.
source_quote: that initiatives and financing, both Central-State and local, shall be coordinated for the priority objective of sustainability; that optimal strategies for the reduction of greenhouse gases shall be formulated as part of the Plans for the Safeguarding and Reclamation of Air Quality;
section_header: Conference of the Presidents of Regional Governments and of Autonomous Provinces
extraction_rationale: This is a planning mandate to integrate GHG reduction into air quality plans.

parent_statement: Agreement Protocol of the Conference of the Presidents of Regional Governments and Autonomous Provinces for the coordination of policies aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions
policy_statement: Each region shall draw up an Environmental Energy Plan by the end of 2002 favoring renewables, technological innovation, rationalized electricity production, consumption rationalization, energy certification, planning integration, and eco-efficiency.
source_quote: that an Environmental Energy Plan shall be drawn up by the end of the year 2002, based on the individual energy balances and favouring: renewable sources and technological innovation; rationalisation of the production of electricity; rationalisation of energy consumption, in particular with regard to the civil sector, with measures eventually to include the introduction of energy certification;
section_header: Conference of the Presidents of Regional Governments and of Autonomous Provinces
extraction_rationale: This is a time-bound planning commitment with named mitigation and efficiency mechanisms.

policy_statement: Italy’s National Action Plan identifies approved and planned measures to meet the Kyoto target through sectoral mitigation policies, sinks, and flexible mechanisms.
source_quote: These additional policies have been arranged after a study on the emission trends quantified the surplus of emissions compared to the Kyoto targets - see chapter 5. Part of these policies, listed in table 4.1, have already been approved and they are included in the reference scenario. Another set of policies, still under discussion,  is  listed    in  table  4.2.
section_header: 4.1 Summary of planned aimed measures almed at  of  achieving  the  objectives  of  the  Kyoto Protocol
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella national climate plan with multiple listed sub-measures; individual measures are extracted below.

parent_statement: National Action Plan approved/reference scenario measures
policy_statement: Italy will expand combined-cycle electricity generation by 3,200 MW to reduce emissions by 8.9 Mt CO2.
source_quote: In the reference scenario, a higher capacity  of  new  combined  cycles  is  assumed  for additional 3,200 MW, implying an emission reduction equal to 8.9 Mt. The  investment analysis presents a positive current net value of investment, implying that such option does not require additional incentives.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific electricity-sector intervention with quantified capacity and emissions reduction.

parent_statement: National Action Plan approved/reference scenario measures
policy_statement: Italy will expand electricity import capacity by 2,300 MW to reduce domestic emissions by 10.6 Mt.
source_quote: Another measure included in the reference scenario is the additional expansion of 2.300 MW enabling: - a remarkable emission reduction of 10.6 Mt, considering  that  the  entire  import  capacity  from abroad,  supposedly  from  under-exploited  plants, would cause a reduction in domestic emissions. - an economic advantage on account of low wholesale prices of electric power abroad .
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified infrastructure measure included in the reference scenario for emissions reduction; emissions may be displaced outside Italy, but the document treats it as mitigation.

parent_statement: National Action Plan approved/reference scenario measures
policy_statement: Italy will expand renewable electricity to about 75 TWh by 2010, including 5,478 MW of additional renewable capacity.
source_quote: The result of approximately 75 TWh anticipated in the reference scenario is also the objective indicated  by  the  Italian  Government  upon  approval  of Directive  2001/77/CE  on  Renewable  Sources.  The table  4.4  shows  the  hypotheses  of  expansion  for each renewable source.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified renewable-energy target, a direct mitigation policy.

parent_statement: National Action Plan approved/reference scenario measures
policy_statement: Italy will require an annual 0.3 percentage point increase in the renewable obligation from 2005 to 2012 to support the additional 11 TWh renewable expansion.
source_quote: The  policy  aiming  at  spurring  the  expansion  of renewable sources still further indicates as feasible an additional expansion by 2010,  of 11 TWh, mainly  on  account  of    increased  biomass,  waste  and wind  contribution.  This    additional  expansion requires    an  increase  of  0.3%  each  year  of  the mandatory  2%  obligation,  from  2005  to  2012..
extraction_rationale: This is a binding-style renewable obligation increase with dates and quantified annual increments.

parent_statement: National Action Plan approved/reference scenario measures
policy_statement: Italy will implement end-use energy efficiency decrees for electricity and gas distributors, expected to reduce 7-8 Mt CO2.
source_quote: Legislative Decrees of 24 April 2001 provide for the  reduction  of  electricity  and  gas  consumptions through the implementation of measures adopted by distribution companies; these measures are expected to  be  fully  adopted  since  non-compliance    would incur  financial  penalties.  The  overall  effect  of  such Decrees is expected to entail a reduction from 7 to 8 MtCO2.
section_header: 4.2.1 Measures implemented in the electric sector, including renewable sources
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory efficiency obligation with financial penalties and quantified expected emissions reductions.

parent_statement: National Action Plan approved/reference scenario measures
policy_statement: Italy will implement a 10,000 photovoltaic roofs programme, expected to reduce about 0.12 Mt CO2 per year.
source_quote: The  programme  of 10,000  photovoltaic  roofs is expected to be partially implemented and, according to  rough  estimates,  emission  reduction  should  be around 0.12 MtCO2 year. As  concerns  electricity  generated  from waste  by 2010 it is assumed that the burning capacity of the existing incinerators will increase by 220,000 tonnes every year, entailing a reduction of 1.6 MtCO 2 .
section_header: 4.2.1 Measures implemented in the electric sector, including renewable sources
extraction_rationale: This is a named renewable-energy deployment programme with a quantified expected GHG effect.

parent_statement: National Action Plan approved/reference scenario measures
policy_statement: Italy will increase electricity generation from waste by expanding incinerator capacity by 220,000 tonnes per year by 2010, reducing 1.6 Mt CO2.
source_quote: The  programme  of 10,000  photovoltaic  roofs is expected to be partially implemented and, according to  rough  estimates,  emission  reduction  should  be around 0.12 MtCO2 year. As  concerns  electricity  generated  from waste  by 2010 it is assumed that the burning capacity of the existing incinerators will increase by 220,000 tonnes every year, entailing a reduction of 1.6 MtCO 2 .
section_header: 4.2.1 Measures implemented in the electric sector, including renewable sources
extraction_rationale: This is a specific energy-from-waste intervention with quantified capacity expansion and emissions reduction; it is primarily energy substitution.

parent_statement: National Action Plan approved/reference scenario measures
policy_statement: Italy will promote replacement of liquid and solid fossil fuels with natural gas to mitigate CO2 and overall GHG emissions.
source_quote: The replacement of liquid and solid fossil fuels with natural  gas    is  an  option  aimed  at  mitigating  CO 2 emissions  and  overall  greenhouse-gas  emissions, given that the increase in methane leaks from networks, especially the distribution networks, and from end  users  seems  to  be  negligible.  Natural  gas  will continue to play a major role in the frame of national energy requirements.
section_header: 4.2.1 Measures implemented in the electric sector, including renewable sources
extraction_rationale: This is an explicit fuel-switching mitigation measure; its details are less quantified here but it is a named intervention.

parent_statement: National Action Plan additional measures not established
policy_statement: Italy plans to further increase renewable-source electricity by 500-1,200 MW beyond the reference scenario.
source_quote: Increase  in  the  production  of  energy  from renewable sources for 500-1.200 MW. This is an option which, in any case, must take into account the strong development already hypothesised in the reference scenario, where the achievement of 75 TWh of renewable energy by 2010 is taken for granted, as indicated in the White Paper of  1999.
section_header: 4.2.4 Additional measures for the electric energy sector
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified proposed renewable-energy expansion measure.

parent_statement: National Action Plan additional measures not established
policy_statement: Italy plans photovoltaic R&D and niche deployment of about 150 MW, requiring 1.125 billion Euro investment and reducing 0.1 Mt CO2.
source_quote: Research and development in the photovoltaic sector. This is a more expensive option than other renewable sources since it entails higher investment costs, that is  to  say,  in  the  order  of  7500  Euro/kW.  The possibility of an additional expansion of about 150 MW with an investment of 1.125 million Euros and a  negative  NPV  of  220  million  Euros  is  identified.
section_header: 4.2.4 Additional measures for the electric energy sector
extraction_rationale: This is a named R&D and deployment measure with capacity and cost figures; it is direct mitigation through solar power.

policy_statement: Italy will pursue high-efficiency industrial electric motors through co-financing, regulation from 2007, tax credits for replacement, and an information campaign, saving 2-7.2 TWh and reducing 1-3.6 Mt CO2.
source_quote: To the end of the application of this policy the following measures are necessary: -  co-financing  for  research  and  re-conversation activities  for  the  production  of  last-generation engines  (F1,  high  efficiency, including  a  total amount  of  investment  of  about  300-350  million Euros),  to  be  determined  in  the  voluntary  agreement with ANIE; -  regulations  establishing  that  all  electric  engines introduced on the market are of the F1 (high efficiency) type as from 2007. These  measures  are  associated  to  energy  savings between 2 and 7.2 TWh and to CO2 emission reductions in a range between 1 and 3.6 Mt.
section_header: 4.3.3.1 Increase in the efficiency of electric motors
extraction_rationale: This is a package of specific regulatory, fiscal, and informational measures for industrial motor efficiency with quantified energy and emissions savings.

policy_statement: Italy will restrict sale of inefficient transformers from 2008, requiring compliance with CEI 14.13 leakage standards.
source_quote: In  order  to  increase  the  average  efficiency  of  the Italian stock of transformers currently in operation (about 430,000), it is expected that, as from 2008, all transformers with leaks exceeding the standard indicated in the rules CEI 14.13. will not be allowed to  be  sold.  It  must  be  noted  that  the  additional investment return of a substitution producing efficiency  recovery  is  of  about  2  years,  with  evident advantages for end users.
section_header: 4.3.3.2 Increase in the efficiency of the transformers stock
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory sales restriction based on efficiency standards; emissions effect is indirect but included in climate plan.

policy_statement: Italy plans to raise the industrial COS standard from 0.9 to 0.95, saving 1 TWh and abating 0.5 Mt CO2.
source_quote: The raising of the COS standard is envisaged from 0.9  to  0.95  (the  same  as  the  European  average), with an aggravation of the tariff component connection to the reactive power. The CO2 abatement is 0.5 Mt and energy saving is 1 TWh.
section_header: 4.3.3.3 Raising of the COS j standard
extraction_rationale: This is a specific technical efficiency standard with quantified savings and CO2 abatement.

policy_statement: Italy plans to expand medium-size industrial cogeneration by 10-20 TWh, reducing CO2 by 0.8-1.5 Mt.
source_quote: A  potential  additional  expansion  of  medium-size cogeneration plants in the industrial sector is estimated in the range of 10-20 TWh with a reduction in CO2 emissions between 0.8 and 1.5 Mt. The evaluation of the investments, between 1,1002,100  million  Euros,  assumes  that  the  transfer  of electric  power  should  be  carried  out  taking  into account wholesale prices, estimated around 5 eurocents/kWh; this implies a negative NPV in a range between 48 and 90 million Euros.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified industrial energy-efficiency and emissions-reduction measure.

policy_statement: Italy plans to promote energy recovery from waste, including use of waste in cement works, to reduce 1.8-3 Mt CO2.
source_quote: In order to undertake the investments necessary to achieve this objective, a series of adequate resolutions,  authorizing  the  employment  of  wastes  in cement works, should be established to overcome the difficulties  arising  at  local  level.  Altogether, the investments on the use of heat from wastes both in the industry sector and for the production of electric energy are estimated in a range between 1.100 and 2.400 million Euros, with a NPV near to zero, proportionate to the tariffs of waste disposal  which  should  be  established  in  order  to enable  the  investment  return.  Potential  emission savings are estimated between 1.8 and 3 Mt.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific waste-to-energy and industrial fuel-substitution measure with investment and emissions-savings estimates.

policy_statement: The voluntary agreement with Fiat and European car producer agreements will reduce specific car emissions from 164 gCO2/km to 145 gCO2/km, reducing 6.8 MtCO2 by 2010.
source_quote: The voluntary  agreement  with  Fiat (integrated with agreement between the European Commis-sion and the car producers) foresee a reduction in specific car emissions from 164 gCO2/Km to 145 gCO2/km. This measure is estimated to enable a reduction of 6.8 MtCO2 by 2010.
section_header: 4.4.1 Measures implemented in the transport sector
extraction_rationale: This is a voluntary agreement with quantified vehicle emissions-performance targets and expected reductions.

policy_statement: Italy will increase use of methane, LPG, and biodiesel vehicles to reduce transport emissions by an additional 1 MtCO2.
source_quote: The increasing diffusion of methane, LPG and biodiesel vehicles will  enable  an  additional  reduction of 1 MtCO2. The direct effects of the measures promoting the use of collective  transport  means is  limited  to  0.5 MtCO2.
section_header: 4.4.1 Measures implemented in the transport sector
extraction_rationale: This is a named low-carbon fuels transport measure with quantified expected reduction.

policy_statement: Italy will promote collective transport measures expected to reduce transport emissions by 0.5 MtCO2.
source_quote: The increasing diffusion of methane, LPG and biodiesel vehicles will  enable  an  additional  reduction of 1 MtCO2. The direct effects of the measures promoting the use of collective  transport  means is  limited  to  0.5 MtCO2.
section_header: 4.4.1 Measures implemented in the transport sector
extraction_rationale: This is a specific transport demand-management measure with quantified emissions effect.

policy_statement: Italy will shift 12 Gt-km of freight from road to rail and sea, reducing about 1 MtCO2.
source_quote: A  series  of  measures  aim  at  increasing  the efficiency  of  goods  transport :    the  reduction achievable    through  the  shift  of  12  Gt/km  from road to rail/sea traffic, is of about 1 MtCO 2 ; assuming that all  other  anticipated  measures  are achieved,  the  emission  reduction  will  be  in  the range of 2.6 and 3.2 MtCO2.
section_header: 4.4.1 Measures implemented in the transport sector
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified freight modal-shift policy aimed at emissions reduction.

policy_statement: Italy’s established transport-sector reference scenario measures include low-carbon fuels, private transport optimization, and infrastructure measures.
source_quote: The established measures incorporated in the reference scenario are described and classified into three categories as follows: - -measures aimed toward the shift to low-carbon fuels; - -optimisation  of private transport systems  and car pooling; - -infrastructures.
section_header: 4.4.3 New initiatives already established for the transport sector
extraction_rationale: This is a parent grouping of transport climate policies with specific sub-measures listed beneath it.

parent_statement: Established transport-sector reference scenario measures
policy_statement: Italy will shift buses and private cars to low-carbon fuels such as LPG and methane, reducing 1.5 Mt CO2 by 2010.
source_quote: These measures should enable a reduction of 1.5 Mt of  CO 2 by 2010 (standard value 2,0 Mt), and total investment  up  to  880  million  Euros,  530  of  which charged to the public sector. The duration of the investment is supposed to be 15 years, implying a unit cost of 39 Euro/t.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified low-carbon vehicle fuel-shift measure with specified investment and emissions effect.

parent_statement: Established transport-sector reference scenario measures
policy_statement: Italy will promote natural gas use in vehicles through the Ministry of Environment-Fiat-Oil Industries protocol and development of a larger natural gas vehicle fleet.
source_quote: The Protocol potentialities are only partly exploited for the time being. The development of natural gas - which, in any case, gives positive results since it reduces  CO2 emissions  -  will  produce  the  best results when 'dedicated' engines will be available, that is to say, engines purposely devised and optimised  for  fuelling  vehicles  with  natural  gases.
section_header: Promotion of natural gas use. Protocol of the Ministry of Environment - Fiat - Oil Industries board
extraction_rationale: This is a named voluntary protocol promoting low-carbon transport fuel and dedicated engines.

parent_statement: Established transport-sector reference scenario measures
policy_statement: Italy will spur local transport companies to replace buses older than 10 years with gas-driven or hybrid buses.
source_quote: Having  considered  the  reassuring  results  of  Law no.194/98 and following developments (MD 25 May 1999), a proposal is made to spur the local transport companies  to  replace,  by  means  of  Programme Agreements  and  local  regulations,  their  outdated buses  (registered  more  than  10  years  before)  with gas-driven buses or hybrids. Promotion  of  LPG  use  Protocol  of  the  Ministry  of Industry- Fiat - LPG Consortium.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific public transport fleet-replacement intervention using local regulations and programme agreements.

parent_statement: Established transport-sector reference scenario measures
policy_statement: Italy will promote LPG vehicles through a protocol and financial incentives for acquisition or conversion of vehicles.
source_quote: The  protocol  was  signed  recently  and  it  includes  a series  of  financial  incentives  for  the  acquisition  of LPG-fuelled vehicles or in favour of those subject who are willing to convert their vehicles into LPG-fuelled cars within 36 months from the registration date. A series  of  mutual  commitments are also foreseen to the aim of improving the diffusion of this fuel.
section_header: Promotion  of  LPG  use  Protocol  of  the  Ministry  of Industry- Fiat - LPG Consortium
extraction_rationale: This is a specific incentive scheme for low-carbon transport fuel deployment.

parent_statement: Established transport-sector reference scenario measures
policy_statement: Italy will implement car pooling, car sharing, collective taxis, telematic freight systems, and fuel-tax reform to optimize private transport, reducing 2.1 Mt CO2 by 2010.
source_quote: These measures should enable a reduction of 2.1 Mt of  CO2 by  2010  (4.6  Mt  when  completed),  energy saving equal to 0.8 Mtoe (2 at completion ) and total investments amounting up to 60 million Euros, 49 of which charged to the public sector. The unit cost for the  reduction  of  emissions  is  estimated  around  3 euro/t.
section_header: 4.4.3.2  Systems  aimed  toward  the  optimisation  of the private transport sector
extraction_rationale: This is a package of named transport optimization interventions with quantified emissions and energy savings.

parent_statement: Established transport-sector reference scenario measures
policy_statement: Italy will implement the 'Highway of the Sea' maritime transport project to shift freight to coastal shipping.
