source_quote: In light of Law no. 27/2000, as well as the voluntary agreement with the Confitarma, plus the impetus in this direction on the European-Community level, the investments made for the restructuring and modernisation of port structures will prepare Italy (which sits at the centre of the transport flows in the Mediterranean basin) to meet the growing demand for coastal shipping, making that mode of transport competitive even for voyages of less than 500 km . Maritime transport. Reactivation and development of inland waterways.
section_header: Maritime transport. Implementation of the 'Highway of the Sea' project
extraction_rationale: This is a named infrastructure and modal-shift project to reduce road transport emissions; the quote is more transport-efficiency oriented than explicitly climate, but it sits within the climate measures section.

parent_statement: Established transport-sector reference scenario measures
policy_statement: Italy will complete high-speed railway lines and extend local railway networks, including intermodal rail/road and rail/ship connections.
source_quote: Completion  of  high-speed  railway  lines.  Railway transportation  -  Extension  of  the  local  railway  network. Extension  of  the  network  is  a  measure  needed  to ensure balanced and sustained development. Particular attention  is  paid  to  the  rail/road  and rail/ship  inter-modal  connections,  as  well  as  to  the reinforcement  of  passenger  transportation  on  the commuter routes.
section_header: Completion  of  high-speed  railway  lines.  Railway transportation  -  Extension  of  the  local  railway  network.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific transport infrastructure policy supporting modal shift and efficient mobility.

parent_statement: National Action Plan additional transport measures
policy_statement: Italy plans to incentivize replacement of existing vehicles with cars emitting 120 gCO2/km or less, reducing 3.5-6 Mt CO2.
source_quote: supplement  to  the  Fiat-Acea  agreement  for  the development of vehicles producing lower emissions of CO2 and incentives in the form of subsidies for the replacement of existing automobiles with new vehicles providing consumption rates lower than 5 lt/100 km (average CO2 emissions equal to or lower than 120 g/Km); it is expected that a directive on the subject  will  be  issued  before  the  end  of  this  year. Estimates  show  that  this  measure,    should  lead  to reductions in CO 2 from 3.5 to 6 Mt, with energy savings of between 1.5 and 2.5 Mtoe following investments of from 1.4 billion and 2.4 billion euro and a decrease in external costs of approximately 1 billion euro.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific subsidy and vehicle emissions performance measure with quantified CO2 and energy savings.

parent_statement: National Action Plan additional transport measures
policy_statement: Italy plans stricter registration rules and a voluntary agreement to improve heavy-transport energy efficiency, reducing 0.3-0.8 Mt CO2.
source_quote: Improvement  in  the  energy  efficiency  of  heavy transport vehicles . The measure would make registration of vehicles used for transport dependent on compliance with more restrictive rules in terms of both consumption and emissions. At the same time, a  voluntary  agreement  is  to  be  reached  with  the industry involved.
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory vehicle efficiency and emissions measure for heavy transport.

parent_statement: National Action Plan additional transport measures
policy_statement: Italy plans to blend up to 5% biodiesel into diesel motor fuel, reducing 4 Mt CO2.
source_quote: Bio-fuels. There  are  plans  for  the  blending  of diesel  fuel  used  in  engines  with  bio-diesel  (produced through the esterification of rape oil) up to a level of 5%. Within 4-6 years, the national industry  could  be  capable  of  turning  out  an  annual quantity of bio-diesel of between 1 and 1.3 Mt..
extraction_rationale: This is a specific fuel-content measure with an explicit 5% blending target and mitigation objective.

parent_statement: National Action Plan additional transport measures
policy_statement: Italy plans to revise vehicle owner tax to account for vehicle weight and inspections, encouraging lower-weight vehicles and reducing 1.3 Mt CO2.
source_quote: Revision of the method for calculating the owner's tax on vehicles so that it no longer reflects only the maximum horsepower of the vehicle,  but  also:  a) the weight of the vehicle, in this way pointing users towards  lower-weight  vehicles,  with  significant advantages in terms of CO2 emissions, lower consumption and less pervasive pollution; b) a return to annual vehicle inspections (see further on). It is estimated that this measure, in combination with the one that follows, would lead to a CO 2 reduction of 1.3 Mt and energy savings of 0.6 Mtoe, with a negligible  overall  cost  and  a  reduction  of  200  million euro in external costs.
extraction_rationale: This is a fiscal instrument and inspection policy tied to quantified emissions and energy savings.

parent_statement: National Action Plan additional transport measures
policy_statement: Italy plans annual vehicle inspections including engine and exhaust-reduction device efficiency checks.
source_quote: Annual frequency of vehicle inspections, including an inspection of the efficiency of the engine and the exhaust reduction devices. Improvement of quality and standardisation of fuels beginning in 2004:
extraction_rationale: This is a specific operational/regulatory measure to improve vehicle efficiency and emissions performance.

parent_statement: National Action Plan additional transport measures
policy_statement: Italy plans to reduce maximum sulphur in gasoline and set commercial standards for LPG and natural gas to enable low-consumption and dedicated-engine vehicles.
source_quote: Improvement of quality and standardisation of fuels beginning in 2004: - -Reduction  of  the  maximum  level  of  sulphur allowed  in  gasolines : this  measures  is  an  irreplaceable  precondition  to  the  development  of vehicles with low or extremely low levels of consumption. - -Setting of Lpg commercial standards: a normalised product that is free - or almost - of olefins is a precondition to the development of dedicated engine systems,  as  well  as  to  the  continued  progress  of today's most widely used post-conversion systems.
extraction_rationale: This is a fuel-quality standards policy enabling cleaner and more efficient transport technologies.

parent_statement: National Action Plan additional transport measures
policy_statement: Italy plans campaigns to promote fuel-efficient driving, reducing 0.2 Mt CO2 and saving 0.1 Mtoe.
source_quote: promotion of campaigns to heighten awareness regarding methods of driving vehicles. Given that no small percentage of wasted fuel and excess emissions is the result of the ways in which vehicles  of  individual  transport  are  driven  on  a daily  basis,  campaigns  designed  to  heighten awareness among roadway users would be able, even  in  relatively  brief  periods  of  time,  to  have extremely positive consequences on emission levels (and not only those of CO2 ), as well as on fuel consumption and roadway safety.
extraction_rationale: This is a behavior-change measure with specific transport energy and emissions focus.

policy_statement: Italy will promote natural gas use in residential and service sectors, with estimated 8 Mt CO2 reduction by 2010.
source_quote: The measures implemented can be classified under three  categories:  use  of  fuels  with  a  lower  carbon content, increased building insulation and promotion of more efficient equipment, both electric and thermal. A list of the measures adopted and their estimated effects on emissions is found on table 4.9. The use of natural gas in residential units registered significant increases in the years following 1990 and is  expected  to  continue  growing  in  the  years  to come; this remains the most economical measure for reducing  emissions.
section_header: 4.5.1 Measures implemented in the residential and tertiary sector
extraction_rationale: This is a residential/service fuel-switching mitigation measure; the estimated reduction appears in the referenced table.

policy_statement: Italy will apply Law 10/91 building energy rules to reduce heat consumption in new and renovated buildings.
source_quote: The legislation  developed  for  the implementation of Law 10/91 , and in particular art. 4C, points 1 and 2, has reduced energy consumption in new buildings by 10% within the last two years, compared to the 1990 levels. It has been estimated that annual residential and service-industry emissions, which total to 100 Mt CO2, could be reduced by 3% through application of this law.
section_header: 4.5.1 Measures implemented in the residential and tertiary sector
extraction_rationale: This is a binding building efficiency policy with quantified energy and emissions effects.

policy_statement: Italy provides a 41% income tax deduction for building restructuring expenses, including renewable-energy plants.
source_quote: Implementation of law 449/97, concerning deducibility  of  41% of building retrofitting expenses, including renewable-energy based plants; exemption from excise duties of 300,000 t/year of bio-diesel, as set forth in art. 21 of law 388/2000.
extraction_rationale: This is a tax incentive for building retrofits and renewable-energy installations.

policy_statement: Italy exempts 300,000 tonnes per year of biodiesel from excise duties.
source_quote: Implementation of law 449/97, concerning deducibility  of  41% of building retrofitting expenses, including renewable-energy based plants; exemption from excise duties of 300,000 t/year of bio-diesel, as set forth in art. 21 of law 388/2000.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified tax exemption for biofuel, a financial instrument supporting transport fuel decarbonization.

policy_statement: Italy will extend end-use efficiency decrees beyond 2006, reducing an additional 3.8-6.5 Mt CO2 by 2010.
source_quote: There are plans for the ministerial decrees of April 2001 to remain in effect beyond 2006, with the same annual increases as those set for the period 2002-2006: the result would be a further reduction  -  in  addition  to  that  estimated  for  the  year 2006 - of from 3.8 to 6.5 Mt CO2 from an investment  that,  as  of  2010,  would  total  between  19 and 33 million euro. The instrument of implementation  and  incentives  would  be  the  same  as  that proposed by the Authority for Electric Energy and Gas for the initial period of 2002-2006.
section_header: 4.5.4.1 Extension of effect of decrees on the efficiency of final uses
extraction_rationale: This is a proposed extension of existing efficiency obligations with quantified CO2 and investment estimates.

policy_statement: Italy plans broader use of thermal solar energy for low-temperature heat, saving 70,000 toe and reducing about 0.2 Mt CO2.
source_quote: It  is  predicted  that  investments  can  be  made  for potential  energy  savings  of  70,000  t.o.e.,  which would result in reductions of approximately 0.2 Mt in  CO 2 investments.  Overall  investments  are  estimated at 800 million euro, with a negative VAN of 160  million  euro  and  a  unit  cost,  assuming  the investment will last for 20 years, of 40 million euro.
section_header: 4.5.4.2 More extensive use of thermal solar energy
extraction_rationale: This is a named renewable heat measure with quantified energy savings, emissions reduction, and investment cost.

policy_statement: Italy’s carbon tax law reformulates fossil-energy taxation and dedicates revenues to emission reduction, energy efficiency, and renewable-energy development.
source_quote: Law  448/98 ,  which  introduced  the  carbon  tax, mentioned that the Government would be able to draw on a portion of the resulting revenues for use as compensation for the measures taken in the different sectors and as subsidies for the reduction of emissions, for the promotion of energy efficiency and for the development of renewable sources. The carbon-tax, for that matter, was supposed to have been gradually increased between 1999 and 2005;  instead, on account of the high price of oil, it was frozen at the 1999 levels.
extraction_rationale: This is a broad climate fiscal instrument; implementation was limited by freezing at 1999 levels but the policy exists.

policy_statement: Italy establishes a fund for reducing CO2 emissions and increasing energy efficiency under Law 388/2000.
source_quote: Law 388/00 proposes a number of different procedures for the reduction of emissions:  specifically, lower taxation on products that permit decreas- es in emissions, such as bio-diesel, together with the promotion of energy efficiency and renewable sources. Law 388/2000                                                                  | Art 22: products that contribute to environmental protection exempted from taxes. Art 23: tax reductions for some sectors Art 110: fund for measures geared towards reducing emissions of CO 2 and increasing energy effi- ciency.
extraction_rationale: This is a financial instrument and tax policy explicitly targeting CO2 reduction and energy efficiency.

policy_statement: Italy plans voluntary agreements to install thermal or catalytic abatement on adipic acid production and SCR on nitric acid production to reduce N2O emissions.
source_quote: In  the  case  of  adipic  acid,  the  planned  course  of action calls for the adoption in Italy of the devices (thermal  or  catalytic)  already  used  in  the  other European countries for the treatment of effluent gases. The measure referred to consists of a voluntary agreement with the only enterprise involved. As for nitric acid, the most advanced technology calls  for  installation  of  SCR  (selective  catalytic reduction)  systems  for  the  treatment  of  process gases.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific industrial process abatement policy targeting a non-CO2 greenhouse gas.

policy_statement: Italy promotes organic agriculture to reduce agricultural energy consumption, avoiding up to 0.28-0.337 Mt CO2.
source_quote: Organic agriculture is experiencing rapid growth, primarily  as  a  result  of  the  incentives  provided under EU Regulations no. 2078/92; the agricultural surface area on which the methods of organic agriculture are practiced, equal to 91,500 hectares in 1993, had already reached 1,069,339 hectares in the year 2000. Assuming that the specific level of energy consumption of organic agriculture is 30% lower than that of traditional agriculture, a projection through 2010 of current growth trends in the sector shows that the emissions avoided could total 0.337 Mt CO2.
extraction_rationale: This is an incentive-driven agricultural practice shift with quantified energy-related CO2 effects.

policy_statement: Italy will rationalize fertilizer use through awareness and codes of good agricultural practice to reduce N2O emissions from agricultural soils by about 0.46 MtCO2e.
source_quote: The emission reductions in question can result from a rationalisation of the use of fertilisers, with a subsequent limitation of the consumption and related emissions of nitrous oxide from agricultural soils. Of essential importance to achieving the above objective are: - ongoing efforts to increase awareness of the practice, plus -  the adoption of codes of good agricultural practice.
extraction_rationale: This is a named agricultural practice and regulatory/guidance intervention for N2O mitigation.

policy_statement: Italy will cover liquid animal waste storage tanks and convey biogas to combustion or cogeneration plants to reduce methane emissions by 7-39 kt CH4 per year.
source_quote: The proposed initiative involves covering the holding  tanks  used  to  store  liquid  animal  waste  and then conveying the resulting biogas to combustion or  cogeneration plants. The primary focus of the activities would be pigs (between 10% and 40% of the animals) and, to a relatively limited degree, cattle,  with  a  reduction  in  methane  emissions  of between 7 and 39 kt of methane per year, at an overall  cost  of  from  6.2  to  33.2  million  Euro  per year.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific manure-management methane mitigation intervention with quantified emissions and cost.

policy_statement: Italy will reduce biodegradable municipal waste sent to landfills by 50% by 2010 compared with 1995, reducing methane emissions by 0.64 MtCO2e.
source_quote: fulfilment of the deadlines set for the reduction of  the  biodegradable  fraction  of  the  municipal waste  in  landfills,  as  stipulated  under  Directive 99/31/EC, which calls for a reduction of 50% as early as 2010, compared to the 1995 level, in the quantity of biodegradable municipal waste to be placed in landfills, making for a forecast decrease of 0,64 Mt; substantial respect of the objectives of Legislative Decree 22/97, in particular as regards the recovery of energy from waste:
section_header: 4.7.3 Waste: Stabilisation of the organic fraction and energy recovery
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory waste-management target with quantified methane/GHG reduction.

policy_statement: Italy will send 30% of municipal waste to energy-recovery treatments by 2010, adding 500 MWe of electricity capacity from municipal waste and reducing 0.33 MtCO2e.
source_quote: substantial respect of the objectives of Legislative Decree 22/97, in particular as regards the recovery of energy from waste: it is assumed that, by 2010, the  portion  of  municipal  waste  sent  to  energyrecovery treatments shall be 30% (in line with the indications  of  the  'White  Book  on  the  Energy Optimisation  of  Renewable  Sources',  ENEA, 1999),  making  for  an  additional  increase  of  500 MWe  municipal  electrical  capacity  from  waste, compared to 2000, with a decrease in equivalent CO2 of 0.33 Mt. The measures and incentives that shall hopefully be established are similar to those contemplated  above  for  the  renewable  sources, and in particular for the energy use of waste.
section_header: 4.7.3 Waste: Stabilisation of the organic fraction and energy recovery
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified waste-to-energy recovery target and infrastructure expansion measure.

policy_statement: Italy plans to increase aluminium recycling to about 80% of total consumption by 2010 to reduce PFC emissions.
source_quote: Aluminium. The recycling of aluminium not only generates the economic benefits due to reduced imports of the raw material and lower energy consumption, but also makes it possible to avoid emissions of PFCs from the processing of the raw mineral.  We  have  assumed  that,  on  the quantity  of recycled aluminium will grow, between now and the  year  2010,  up  to  approximately  80%  of  the total consumption of this metal.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified material-recycling target explicitly linked to avoiding PFC emissions.

policy_statement: Italy supports semiconductor-sector abatement devices and lower-GWP etching fluids, aligned with a European voluntary commitment to reduce 2010 emissions 10% below 1995 levels.
source_quote: Production of semi-conductors. A limited initiative  consisting  of  the  installation  of  abatement devices and the use in the etching process of fluids  with  a  lower  level  of  GWP  is  currently  being studied.  The  European  industry  has  voluntarily agreed  to  limit  its  emissions  in  2010  to  a  figure 10% lower than 1995 levels.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific fluorinated-gas mitigation measure with a quantified industry emissions target.

policy_statement: Italy plans to reduce HFC leak rates from mobile air conditioners from 10% to 5% through design and maintenance adjustments.
source_quote: Mobile air conditioners. Reduction of from 10% to 5% in the rate of leaks from mobile air conditioners, to be obtained through adjustments made during the design phase of the systems and during the  maintenance phase. These initiatives shall be promoted  under  the  European  framework-directive currently up for discussion.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific HFC leak-reduction measure with a quantified leak-rate target.

policy_statement: Italy plans to reduce SF6 leakage from electrical equipment to 0.45% for installed equipment and 1% for end-of-life equipment by 2010.
source_quote: In the case of the sulphur hexafluoride contained in electrical equipment, consideration was given to the effects of a scenario in which the leakage rate of  installed  equipment  is  reduced,  by  the  year 2010, from 0.9 to 0.45%, while the leakage rate for equipment at the end of its life cycle falls from 3 to 1%. A  brief  description  is  also  given  for  each  of  the activities listed.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified fluorinated-gas leak reduction policy for electrical equipment.

policy_statement: Italy’s land use, land-use change and forestry measures will generate and certify carbon credits from forest management, afforestation, reforestation, farmland, pastures, and revegetation.
source_quote: The  measures  contemplated  in  the  sector  'land use, land use change and forestry' for the generation and certification of carbon credits during the period 2008-2012 are summarised on table 4.14. Table 4.14 - Maximum national potential for carbon removal
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella carbon-sink programme with multiple listed forestry and land-use sub-measures.

parent_statement: Forestry sector land-use carbon removal measures
policy_statement: Italy will count and seek revision of credits for forest management under Kyoto article 3.4, requiring a National Forestry Inventory of Carbon by 2005 and updates every five years.
source_quote: The  figure  assigned  to  Italy  can  be  modified, though, for this to be done, new and significant amounts of inventory data must be supplied to the Secretariat of the UNFCCC by June 2005, so that the figure can be corrected by 31 December 2006. From a technical perspective, the National Forestry Inventory of Carbon (INFOCARB) should be created by 2005.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific forest carbon accounting and management measure supporting carbon-removal credits.

parent_statement: Forestry sector land-use carbon removal measures
policy_statement: Italy will certify carbon credits from 117,428 hectares of old afforestation/reforestation plantings under EEC Regulation 2080/92, estimated at 1.0 Mt CO2 in 2008-2012.
source_quote: the plantings performed (old plantings) under EEC  Regulation  2080/92,  which  total  117,428 hectares. The carbon level for the  first  period  of  the  commitment  (2008-2012)  is estimated at approximately 1.0 Mt CO 2 ;
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified afforestation/reforestation carbon-credit measure.

parent_statement: Forestry sector land-use carbon removal measures
policy_statement: Italy will certify carbon credits from natural reforestation due to agricultural-environmental policies, estimated at 3 Mt CO2 for 2008-2012.
source_quote: so-called  'natural  reforestation',  which  includes the natural expansion of the forested area as a result of policies for the reduction of farming-pasture surface area and for the protection of the environment. Eligibility for carbon certification for the period 20082012 is tied to providing proof that these areas were the  result  of  agricultural-environmental  policies (human induced).
extraction_rationale: This is a nature-based carbon-removal policy relying on natural forest expansion and certification.

parent_statement: Forestry sector land-use carbon removal measures
policy_statement: Italy will establish 40,000 hectares of new afforestation/reforestation plantings during 2003-2008, removing about 1 Mt CO2 during 2008-2012 and 20 Mt CO2 at maturity.
source_quote: the new plantings to be made during the period 2003-2008,  forecast  at  40,000  hectares,  for  an average  removal  of  1  Mt  CO 2 during  the  period 2008-2012 and of 20 Mt CO2 at the maturity. These domestic plantings offer major advantages in term of the certification of carbon credits, and especially as  regards reaping the full fall-out of the benefits generated by reforestations on Italy's economic and environmental  systems.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified reforestation programme with dates, area, and carbon-removal estimates.

parent_statement: Forestry sector land-use carbon removal measures
policy_statement: Italy will plant 60,000 hectares in hydrogeologically unstable areas under Law 183/89, removing about 1 Mt CO2 during 2008-2012 and reducing hydrogeological risks.
source_quote: New plantings carried out in areas subject to hydrogeological imbalance (Law no. 183 of 18 May 1989) will present major advantages in terms of defence of the territory, prevention of hydro-geological risks and the reduction of damage due to imbalances. The operating capacity of the Basin Authorities is approximately 6,000 hectares of reforestation per year for the period of 2003-2012, making for a total of 60,000 hectares.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified reforestation measure with carbon-removal and named hazard-risk reduction benefits.

parent_statement: Forestry sector land-use carbon removal measures
policy_statement: Italy will study and account carbon absorbed or emitted from agricultural land, pastures, and revegetation, with estimated average removal of 0.1 MtCO2 per year.
source_quote: The costs currently forecast for this activity involve the preparation of a special study-plan designed to estimate the quantities of carbon absorbed/emitted by these activities, given the complete lack of data in  the  literature.  This  study-plan  is  necessary  in order  to  arrive  at  a  proper  reporting  within  the framework of the Kyoto Protocol. Average removal of 0.1 MtCO2/year is estimated.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific carbon accounting/removal measure for land management; more preparatory than implementation, but tied to quantified removals.

parent_statement: Forestry sector land-use carbon removal measures
policy_statement: Italy will establish a National Register of Agro-Forestry Carbon Storage Pools to certify carbon removed by agricultural and forestry systems.
source_quote: The  National  Register  of  Agro-Forestry  Carbon Storage Pools  is the tool for certifying the quantities  of  carbon  removed  by  Italian  agricultural  and forestry system. The registry provides an overview of the use made of Italian soil, placing within this picture the statistical data on the carbon contents of the different catgories of agricultural and forestry activities.
section_header: 4.8.4  National  Register  of  Agro-Forestry  Carbon Storage Pools
extraction_rationale: This is a specific institutional mechanism for certifying land-sector carbon removals.

policy_statement: Italy will use Kyoto flexible mechanisms—Emissions Trading, Clean Development Mechanism, and Joint Implementation—to complement domestic policies.
source_quote: The  present  section  addresses  the  use  of  flexible mechanisms: Emissions Trading, Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) and Joint Implementation (JI) project. These mechanisms complement internal policies, often  on  account  of  their  greater  convenience  in terms of the unit cost for reducing emissions.
extraction_rationale: This is a commitment to use market/project-based Kyoto mechanisms for mitigation; it is a broad financial/market instrument.

policy_statement: Italy will establish public-sector programmes or an agency to assist CDM and JI projects by providing guidelines, partnership, consulting, information, and preferential procedures.
source_quote: It is extremely important that the public sector adopt specific programs to assist the CDM and JI projects, eventually  under  the  coordination  of  a  specific agency. These programs (or the agency) can  provide guidelines, serve as a partner or provide consulting to companies  in  order  to  spread  information  on  the projects  and  facilitate  their  performance,  especially internationally,  through  international  initiatives  formulated on an ad hoc basis - taking advantage of the  existing  networks  operated  by  the  Ministry  of Foreign Affairs and the Institute of Foreign Trade for the CDM and JI projects.
extraction_rationale: This is an implementation-support policy for international emissions-reduction mechanisms.

policy_statement: Italy will implement coastal adaptation measures including drainage, pumping, well closure/regulation, sand feeding, and saline-wedge management.
source_quote: Among the others, the following measures should be adopted to thwart the negative effects of the relative sea level rise in Italy, such as: 1.  Channelling  and  pumping  works  with  draining pumps  of  depressed  areas  following  reclamation works; 2.  Dismantling  of  wells  for  gas-hydrocarbons  and water; 3. Sand feeding; 4. Saline wedge.
extraction_rationale: This is a list of specific adaptation interventions to address sea-level rise and coastal impacts.

policy_statement: Italy’s National Action Plan to Combat Desertification identifies vulnerable areas and prevention, mitigation, and adaptation strategies with Regions and Basin Authorities.
source_quote: After having acknowledged the significance of the desertification issue, and having adhered to the UN Convention  to  Combat  Desertification,  the  Italian Government  has  arranged  a  National  Action  Plan (MATT, 1999). The Plan, approved upon deliberation of the Interministerial Committee for Economic Planning of 21.12.1999, outlines  an  information and awareness path  addressed to the Regions and the  Basin  Authorities  to  spot  the  most  vulnerable areas and define prevention, mitigation and adaptation  strategies.
extraction_rationale: This is a national adaptation plan focused on desertification vulnerability and response strategies.

policy_statement: Italy will adapt agriculture through land-use planning, diversified climate-compatible production, biodiversity conservation, efficient energy use, and water-resource planning.
source_quote: The Italian actions aimed at thwarting the undesired effects  of  climate  change  in  the  agricultural  sector follow the indications provided in the Agenda 21 of the United Nations.  They consist in: - the arrangement of an attentive territorial and landuse  planning  according  to  a  multifunctional  view, taking into consideration both present and expected global changes; -  the  creation of diversified agricultural productions compatible with local territorial peculiarities and with the climatic region where the farmland is to be established;
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete set of agricultural adaptation actions; some items are broad but include named interventions.

policy_statement: Italy will protect forests from climate impacts by increasing forest biodiversity, creating new poly-specific forest plants, creating wooded areas in agro-industrial and urban landscapes, and implementing fire-prevention and extinction policies.
source_quote: The actions to protect the Italian forests  also contribute  to  prevent  degradation  and  desertification phenomena.  The following measures need particular attention: - the increase of specific and structural forest biodiversity  improving  resistance  and  resilience  to disturbances. This measure would enable forests to adapt at the ever-changing climate conditions ensuring  tree  coverage,  both  in  terms  of  space and time, even if this would imply the formation of different tree species;
extraction_rationale: This is a set of forest ecosystem adaptation measures using ecological mechanisms.

policy_statement: Italy’s 1998 National Research Plan for Climate Protection prioritizes response-measure analysis and research for technologies to reduce climate effects and emissions, including feasibility and cost-benefit analyses.
source_quote: In  1998,  the  Ministry  of  the  Environment  set  the guidelines of the National Research Plan for Climate Protection.  The  objectives  of  the  plan  include  the strengthening and analysis of response measures and research  activities  aimed  at  developing  new  technologies to reduce the effects and/or the emissions of harmful  components  that  may  jeopardise  climate, evolution,  including  feasibility  studies,  cost-benefit and cost-efficiency analysis to evaluate the response to efficient strategies.
section_header: 6.5.1 1998 Guidelines of the National Research Plan for Climate Protection
extraction_rationale: This is a named research policy supporting both mitigation and adaptation; it is included because it sets concrete research objectives.

policy_statement: Italy’s National Research Programme on Climate prioritizes research on Mediterranean climate impacts and Italian vulnerability, including ecosystems, water resources, food and timber, and public health.
source_quote: On December 21 1999, the Interministerial Committee  for  Economic  Planning  approved  the priority research  themes  of  the  National  Research Programme  on  Climate  for  the  three-year  period 1999-2001. Among  the  identified  themes,  the study of climate change impacts in the Mediterranean  area  and  of  vulnerability  in  Italy  is included,  in  the  frame  of  the  Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) indications, with the purpose to evaluate the effects on:
section_header: 6.5.2 Deliberation of the Interministerial Committee for Economic Planning on the priority  research  themes  of  the  National  Research Programme on Climate, 21 December 1999
extraction_rationale: This is a time-bound research programme directed at climate vulnerability and impacts; it supports adaptation planning.

policy_statement: Italy contributes to the Global Environment Facility as a financial mechanism for the Climate Change and Biodiversity Conventions, including 90.5 million US dollars for GEF-2.
source_quote: An important, new and additional resource to solve global environmental issues is certainly the Italian contribution to the Global Environment Facility GEF. Italy, which had contributed to GEF-1 with 128 US million dollars, supported the second replenishment of GEF with 90.5 US million dollars.  With a 4.39% share of total contribution, Italy stands out as the sixth leading contributor of GEF, immediately after USA, Japan, Germany, France and Great Britain.
extraction_rationale: This is a major multilateral climate finance contribution, though GEF covers multiple global environmental objectives.

policy_statement: Italy’s Carbon Tax resources fund international technology transfer and environmental cooperation projects supporting UNFCCC commitments and Kyoto mechanisms.
source_quote: The  aforementioned  financial  resources  are  provided for by the so-called 'Carbon Tax', or ecological  tax  no. 448/1998  'aimed  at  the  reduction  of carbon dioxide emissions'. Furthermore, the Italian Interministerial  Committee  for  Economic  Planning (CIPE),  in  its  'Guidelines  for  National  Policies  and Measures to Reduce Greenhouse Gas Emissions' of 19  November  1998,  established  that  national actions aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions must also be accompanied by international co-operation programmes.
extraction_rationale: This is a financial and cooperation instrument explicitly linked to CO2 reduction and Kyoto mechanisms.

policy_statement: Italy’s environmental cooperation programme with China invests about 14.5 million Euros in pilot projects and feasibility studies for renewable energy, energy efficiency, low-emission transport, sustainable agriculture, and reforestation.
source_quote: The Italian Ministry for the Environment and Territory is particularly active, both qualitatively and quantitatively, with a programme promoting environmental co-operation with China.  With a total amount of about 14.5 Million Euros, the programme aims to the implementation of  pilot projects and feasibility studies for the development of scientific and industrial projects for environmental protection and the development and use of renewable energy sources. Among such activities, particularly relevant to climate change are the following:
section_header: THE ENVIRONMENTAL CO-OPERATION PROGRAMME WITH CHINA TOWARDS SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT: AN EXAMPLE OF PARTNERSHIP
extraction_rationale: This is a funded international climate cooperation programme with concrete mitigation and adaptation-related project areas.

policy_statement: Italy supports a climate information action plan under CIPE Deliberation 218/99 to disseminate IPCC, Kyoto, vulnerability, energy efficiency, and local best-practice information.
source_quote: The deliberation of the Interministerial  Committee for Economic Planning (no. 218/99 of 21 December 1999)  contains  the  program  for  environmental information on climate change. The deliberation of the Interministerial  Committee for  Economic  Planning ,  in  particular,  identifies  the priority initiatives of the National Information Program on Climate Change for the three-year period 1999-2001:
section_header: 9.2.1. The Deliberation of 21 st December 1999 by the Interministerial Committee for Economic Planning
extraction_rationale: This is a named climate information programme with specific priority initiatives; education policies are climate-relevant but not directly emissions-reducing.

policy_statement: Italy will establish a Permanent Observatory on Climate Change to provide reliable climate information, media monitoring, negotiation updates, literature reviews, and local awareness support.
source_quote: The first step to be taken, as a direct result of the deliberation of the Interministerial Committee for Economic Planning, addressed in the first part of this  Text,  is  the  establishment  of  a  Permanent Observatory on Climate Change aimed to serve as the central source of reliable information for people who are working on climate issues and other professionally interested operators such as journalists. The Observatory should: - Collect  informations  in  national  and  international media on the issue; - Supply information on the activities of the central  government and local government bodies regarding climate change;
extraction_rationale: This is a specific institutional public-awareness and information policy; climate category assignment is indirect but climate relevance is explicit.

policy_statement: The National Action Plan annex approves maximum sectoral GHG emission levels for 2008-2012 and requires additional measures to meet Law 120/2002.
source_quote: The National Action Plan preparedby the Ministry of the Environment and Territory, in compliance with art. 2 of law 120 of 1 June 2002 aimed at reducing greenhouse-gas emissions and improving their removalis approved and it is annexed to thisDeliberation. Maximum emission levels assigned to each sector for the period 2008-2012, calculated as average yearly emissions as of Table 8, are established in conformity with the reference scenario, that is to say, on the basis of the results attainable through the implementation of the measures established on 30 June 2002 and through the implementation of actions, programmes and initiatives in the sectors of electricitygeneration, transportation, energy consumption in the residential and tertiary sector as well as in the international co-operation  sector.
section_header: Annex 1: Revised guidelines for national policies and measures regarding the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions (Law 120/2002)
extraction_rationale: This is a binding plan approval and sectoral emissions cap framework for Kyoto compliance.

policy_statement: Italy will organize ministerial offices to coordinate JI, CDM and emissions trading, census initiatives by 31 May 2003, register projects by 30 June 2003, and prepare companies for emissions trading.
source_quote: In order to ensure the promotion and the co-ordination of the projects carried out in the frame of the JI and CDM mechanisms as well as the Italian participation to the international and Community emissions trading (ET), the Ministry of the Environment and Territory, will have to take measures to organize, using ordinary human and instrumental resources, its own offices in such a way as to enable, in agreement with the Ministries of Production Activities, Agricultural and Forestry Policies, Foreign Affairs and Economics and Finance: - the arrangement, within 31 May 2003, of the census of the Italian public and private initiatives, already accomplished or under execution, in the 'Annex I' countries and in the Developing Countries, capable of generating emission credits, according to the decisions taken at Community and international level; - the starting, before 30 June 2003, of registration procedures at the competent institutions stipulated under the Framework Convention on Climate Change, of the projects that have already been implemented or are in progress, with the aim of issuing the emission credits;
section_header: Annex 1: Revised guidelines for national policies and measures regarding the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions (Law 120/2002)
extraction_rationale: This is a time-bound implementation policy for emissions-credit mechanisms and trading.

policy_statement: Portugal established the National Energy and Climate Plan 2021-2030 (PNEC 2030) as the primary national energy and climate policy instrument for the decade, with political coordination and target monitoring by the Ministerial Commission for Climate Action.
source_quote: The National Energy and Climate Plan 2021-2030 (PNEC 2030) is this decade's primary national energy and climate policy instrument and it was approved through the Council of Ministers Resolution n.º 53/2020, of 10 th of July. The Ministerial Commission for Climate Action (CAC) is responsible for the political coordination of PNEC 2030, in charge of supervising and monitoring its implementation and the achievement of the established targets.
section_header: Legal and policy frameworks and regulations
extraction_rationale: This is an approved national policy instrument with a binding resolution and implementation-monitoring structure. It qualifies as a policy framework rather than a single project.

policy_statement: Portugal adopted the Carbon Neutrality Roadmap 2050 as its long-term mitigation strategy to guide the country toward carbon neutrality by 2050.
source_quote: The Portuguese long-term vision for mitigation has been set in the Carbon Neutrality Roadmap 2050  (RNC2050),  approved  by  the  Council  of  Ministers  nº.  107/2019,  of  1 st of  July,  which constituted the Portuguese Long-Term Strategy submitted to the European Commission and to United Nations Framework Convention for Climate Change (UNFCCC). It shall be stressed that the Portuguese carbon neutrality goal in 2050 has been established in the  Resolution  of  the  Council  of  Ministers  n.º  107/2019,  which  as  above  mentioned  it  also approved the  Carbon  Neutrality  Roadmap  2050  (RNC2050)  that  constituted  the  Portuguese Long-Term Strategy submitted to the European Commission and to United Nations Framework Convention for Climate Change (UNFCCC).
section_header: Summaries of national strategies, policies, plans and efforts
extraction_rationale: The roadmap is an approved long-term strategy with a quantified 2050 carbon-neutrality goal. It is directly climate-related mitigation policy.

policy_statement: Portugal adopted the National Adaptation Strategy 2020 (ENAAC 2020) as its umbrella national strategy for climate change adaptation, structured around knowledge, implementation of adaptation measures, and mainstreaming adaptation into sectoral policies.
source_quote: Portugal also has a revised NAS - National Adaptation Strategy (ENAAC 2020, approved by the Council of Ministers Resolution n.º 56/2015, of 30 th of July) (English version in Annex 1), focusing on improving the articulation between domains (particularly those of transversal nature), on the integration in sectoral policies, and the implementation of adaptation measures. To achieve its vision for Portugal, ENAAC 2020 assumes three objectives that seek to continue the rationale of the previous phase by seeking a more operational orientation and its implementation.
extraction_rationale: The strategy is an approved umbrella initiative with named sub-objectives listed beneath it. It qualifies as a parent policy because the document specifies subordinate objectives and work areas.

parent_statement: National Adaptation Strategy 2020 (ENAAC 2020)
policy_statement: Improve Portugal’s level of knowledge on climate change by updating, developing, and promoting understanding of climate risks, impacts, and consequences, including extreme weather events.
source_quote: The objectives of ENAAC 2020 are: - I. Improving the level of knowledge about climate change. This objective aims to update, develop, and promote understanding of climate change and assess its potential risks 11 , impacts and consequences, including those related to extreme weather events.
extraction_rationale: This is a stated strategic objective under ENAAC 2020. It has a concrete knowledge and assessment function tied to climate risks, though it is enabling rather than a physical intervention.

parent_statement: National Adaptation Strategy 2020 (ENAAC 2020)
policy_statement: Implement adaptation measures by assessing adaptive capacity and prioritising measures that moderate future climate impacts or exploit opportunities from climate change.
source_quote: The objectives of ENAAC 2020 are: - I. Improving the level of knowledge about climate change. - II. Implement adaptation measures. Under this objective, it is intended to assess the current adaptive capacity and prioritise the implementation of adaptation options and measures that moderate future negative impacts and/or help seize opportunities arising from climate change.
extraction_rationale: This is a formal objective of the approved strategy and commits to prioritising and implementing adaptation measures. It is broad but anchored in a named strategy.

parent_statement: National Adaptation Strategy 2020 (ENAAC 2020)
policy_statement: Promote mainstreaming of climate change adaptation into public and sectoral policies, spatial planning, sustainable urban development, and territorial management instruments.
source_quote: The objectives of ENAAC 2020 are: - III. Promote the integration of adaptation into sectoral policies. This objective aims to promote the integration and monitoring of the climate change adaptation component (' mainstreaming ') in the most relevant public and sectoral policies, including spatial planning and sustainable urban development policies and their territorial planning and management instruments.
extraction_rationale: This is a formal strategic objective with a specific mainstreaming mechanism across policy and planning instruments. It qualifies as policy despite being institutional rather than project-based.

parent_statement: National Adaptation Strategy 2020 (ENAAC 2020)
policy_statement: Develop a National Adaptation Platform to centralise adaptation information, progress tracking, and stakeholder interaction in Portugal.
source_quote: The thematic area is dedicated to the promotion and dissemination of knowledge on Adaptation. It will support the development, systematisation, and dissemination of information necessary for decision-making. Without prejudice to other priorities that are agreed upon during the work of the Strategy, this area may: - i) Develop  a  National  Adaptation  Platform  that  centralises  information,  progress,  and stakeholder interaction on climate change adaptation in Portugal, taking into account the possible connection to similar platforms in Europe and the rest of the world 16 .
section_header: d) Communication and Dissemination (National Adaptation Platform)
extraction_rationale: The strategy names a specific intervention: a National Adaptation Platform. The wording uses 'may,' so implementation strength is somewhat soft, but the platform is a concrete action under an approved strategy.

policy_statement: Portugal requires environmental assessment procedures to consider current and future climate vulnerabilities, climate scenarios, climate risks, resilient alternatives, and adaptation measures.
source_quote: The Environmental Assessment procedures consider national and territorial adaptation planning instruments; current and future climatic vulnerabilities through historical data on the climate and the occurrences of extreme weather events; environmental, social and economic impacts and consequences, considering CC scenarios; key risks/impacts of CC in the project; assessment if  pre-existing vulnerabilities to CC will be exacerbated; alternatives more resilient to climate pressures and/or allowing a more significant climate vulnerability reduction; critical thresholds that compromise the project or the environment, forcing the adoption of adaptation measures; minimisation measures based on NAP for the relevant vulnerabilities or impacts.
section_header: Integration of climate change impacts and resilience into environmental assessment procedures
extraction_rationale: This describes a procedural requirement for environmental assessments to integrate climate risk and resilience considerations. It qualifies as regulatory/planning policy.

policy_statement: Portugal integrated climate change impacts and scenarios into the National Risk Assessment used for disaster management and risk reduction.
source_quote: In  addition, the National Risk Assessment was prepared in 2014 and reviewed later in 2019, following the "Risk Assessment and Mapping Guidelines for Disaster Management" issued by the  European  Commission  (document  SEC  (2010)  1626  final,  21.12.2010),  which  aims  to promote the better application of the precautionary principle, contributing to the adoption of measures  to  reduce  the  risk  of  major  accident  or  disaster  inherent  in  each  activity.  In  this assessment, the natural, technological, or mixed hazards that may affect the national territory were identified and characterised. The National Risk Assessment took into consideration, for the applicable risks, the impact of climate change and the resulting scenarios, indicating tendencies to worsen or mitigate risks.
section_header: Integration of climate change impacts and adaptation planning into disaster risk management frameworks and vice versa
extraction_rationale: The reviewed National Risk Assessment is a named risk-management instrument that incorporates climate scenarios. It is a planning policy for adaptation and disaster risk reduction.

policy_statement: Portugal approved the Adaptation to Climate Change Action Programme (P-3AC/NAP) to operationalise implementation of adaptation measures through priority lines of action for territory and infrastructure.
source_quote: The Adaptation to Climate Change Action Programme, approved by the Resolution of the Council of  Ministers  Nº.  130/2019,  of  2 nd of  August  (English  version  in  Annex  2),  complements  and systematises  the  work  carried  out  in  the  context  of  ENAAC  2020,  focusing  on  its  second objective: to implement adaptation measures. NAP  elects  eight  direct  intervention  lines  in  the territory and infrastructures, complemented by an additional line of action of transversal nature, seeking to respond to Portugal's significant impacts and vulnerabilities.
section_header: Summaries of national strategies, policies, plans and efforts
extraction_rationale: P-3AC is an approved action programme with specific subordinate lines of action, so it is a parent policy. It has direct adaptation objectives and funding/programming implications.

parent_statement: Adaptation to Climate Change Action Programme (P-3AC)
policy_statement: Implement rural fire prevention through structural interventions in agricultural and forestry areas, including fuel reduction, fire-spread reduction, forest resilience, and safety measures.
source_quote: Line of Action #1 - Rural fire prevention - structural interventions in agricultural and forestry areas. Main objectives: • Reducing biomass fuel • Reducing the speed at which fires spread • Increasing the forest's resilience to fire • Ensuring the safety of people and property. Goals: - 2020: make an additional EUR 129 million of public investment (PDR 2020: EUR 122 million; POSEUR: EUR 7 million; other funds: EUR 0.1 million)
section_header: Line of Action #1 - Rural fire prevention - structural interventions in agricultural and forestry areas
extraction_rationale: This is a named P-3AC line of action with defined objectives, interventions, and public investment. It directly addresses climate-related rural fire risk.

parent_statement: Adaptation to Climate Change Action Programme (P-3AC)
policy_statement: Implement soil conservation and fertility improvement techniques to minimise erosion, improve soil organic matter and water retention, reduce runoff, and strengthen ecosystem resilience.
source_quote: Line of Action #2 - Implementation of soil conservation and fertility improvement techniques. Main objectives: • Minimising soil erosion • Increase the levels of organic matter in the soil • Improve the soil's water retention capacity • Reduce runoff from extreme rainfall events • Increasing biodiversity in soils • To decrease the vulnerability of ecosystems, species, and habitats to the effects of climate change. Goals: - 2020: make an additional €1.4 million in public investment ( PDR 2020: €1.4 million)
section_header: Line of Action #2 - Implementation of soil conservation and fertility improvement techniques
extraction_rationale: This is a specific adaptation line of action with named land and soil interventions and funding. It explicitly addresses erosion, runoff, biodiversity, and vulnerability to climate impacts.

parent_statement: Adaptation to Climate Change Action Programme (P-3AC)
policy_statement: Implement good water management practices in agriculture, aquaculture, industry, and urban areas to reduce consumption, increase water efficiency, and prevent drought and scarcity impacts.
source_quote: Line of Action #3 - Implementation of good water management practices in agriculture, aquaculture, industry and the urban sector to prevent impacts resulting from drought and scarcity phenomena. Main objectives: • Reduce water consumption in the various sectors • Increasing water efficiency in the various sectors • Improving the resilience and productivity of species and varieties • Increasing the resilience of water supply infrastructure (agricultural, industrial, tourism, domestic). Goals: - 2020: 124 million of public investment (PDR 2020: €21 million; OP SEUR: EUR 100 million; other funds: EUR 3
section_header: Line of Action #3 - Implementation of good water management practices in agriculture, aquaculture, industry and the urban sector to prevent impacts resulting from drought and scarcity phenomena
extraction_rationale: This line has specific named water-efficiency interventions and a public investment commitment. It is primarily resource-efficiency because the main mechanism is reducing water use, with explicit drought and scarcity adaptation motivation.

parent_statement: Adaptation to Climate Change Action Programme (P-3AC)
policy_statement: Increase the resilience of ecosystems, species, and habitats to climate change through riparian restoration, ecological corridors, environmental flows, wildlife passages, and conservation of vulnerable species.
source_quote: Line of Action #4 - Increasing the resilience of ecosystems, species, and habitats to the effects of climate change. Main objectives: • Maintain or restore riparian galleries • Minimise barrier effects and reduce obstacles in the hydrographic network • Implementing environmental flow regimes • Conserving and managing temporary pond systems • Encourage the creation of refuges and ecological corridors for vulnerable fauna species. Goals: • 2020: make an additional €30 million of public investment ( PDR 2020: €24 million; POSEUR OP: €5 million; other funds: €1 million)
section_header: Line of Action #4 - Increasing the resilience of ecosystems, species, and habitats to the effects of climate change
extraction_rationale: This line is a concrete ecosystem-based adaptation programme with named interventions and funding. The primary mechanism is ecosystem and habitat management.

parent_statement: Adaptation to Climate Change Action Programme (P-3AC)
policy_statement: Reduce urban vulnerability to heatwaves and rising maximum temperatures through green infrastructure, shading, cooling equipment, ventilation corridors, public fountains, and public warning systems.
source_quote: Line of Action #5 - Reducing the vulnerability of urban areas to heatwaves and increasing maximum temperatures. Main objectives: • Regulating temperature in urban spaces • Minimising the adverse effects of intense heat on the health of populations in general and risk groups in particular Measures/concretization • Measures that counter the heat island effect, particularly during heatwave events: • Implementation of green infrastructure (including urban gardens with smart irrigation systems), including the use of natural materials as building material (e.g. green roofs and facades) and renaturalisation and restoration of pavement permeability.
section_header: Line of Action #5 - Reducing the vulnerability of urban areas to heatwaves and increasing maximum temperatures
extraction_rationale: This is a specific adaptation line addressing named hazards: heatwaves and rising maximum temperatures. It includes concrete interventions such as green infrastructure, shading, cooling, and alert systems.

parent_statement: Adaptation to Climate Change Action Programme (P-3AC)
policy_statement: Prevent the establishment and spread of invasive alien species, vector-borne diseases, and agricultural and forestry pests through surveillance, mapping, warning systems, control, eradication, and genetic-material measures.
source_quote: Line of Action #6 - Preventing the establishment and spread of invasive alien species, vector-borne diseases, and agricultural and forestry diseases and pests. Main objectives: • Monitor the vectors that potentially health to implement contingency plans • Control and eradicate invasive alien • Controlling emerging pests and diseases • Recover species and habitats affected. Goals: • 2020: 21 million of public investment (PDR 2020: 20 M€; SEUR OP: 1 M€)
section_header: Line of Action #6 - Preventing the establishment and spread of invasive alien species, vector-borne diseases, and agricultural and forestry diseases and pests
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete adaptation line addressing climate-sensitive health, agricultural, forestry, and biodiversity risks. The wording in the table is somewhat corrupted, but the line title and measures are clear.

parent_statement: Adaptation to Climate Change Action Programme (P-3AC)
policy_statement: Reduce or minimise flood risks by implementing flood-risk management plans, infiltration areas, restored river profiles, protective infrastructure, hydrometric stations, modelling, warning systems, and stormwater drainage upgrades.
source_quote: Line of Action #7 - Reducing or minimising the risks associated with flooding phenomena. Main objectives: • Reduce the risk of river and urban flooding • Increasing the resilience of infrastructure • Implementing Flood Risk Management Plans Measures/concretization: • Creating infiltration areas through: - Construction and/or rehabilitation of retention basins (excavation and dyke) - Reconversion of impermeable surface areas (e. g. renaturalisation of riverside ecosystems, installation of drainage paving).
section_header: Line of Action #7 - Reducing or minimising the risks associated with flooding phenomena
extraction_rationale: This is a named P-3AC line with concrete interventions and a named climate hazard: river and urban flooding. It includes both grey and ecosystem-based measures.

parent_statement: Adaptation to Climate Change Action Programme (P-3AC)
policy_statement: Increase coastal resilience and protection in high-risk areas from coastal erosion, overtopping, and flooding through sediment restoration, dune and coastal-system interventions, defence structures, planned retreat, and infrastructure relocation.
source_quote: Line of Action #8 - Increasing resilience and coastal protection in areas at high risk from coastal erosion, overtopping and flooding. Main objectives: • Reducing the risk of coastal flooding • To guarantee a coastline more resilient to erosion, overtopping and coastal flooding, particularly in built-up areas or urban centres • To guarantee sediment re-establishment, including large-scale artificial feeding operations and the operationalisation of processes promoting the natural re- establishment of sediment transport from river basins. Goals: • 2020: make an additional €47 million of public investment (POSEUR: €47 million) • 2030: make €560 million of public investment in coastal protection
section_header: Line of Action #8 - Increasing resilience and coastal protection in areas at high risk from coastal erosion, overtopping and flooding
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete adaptation investment line with named coastal hazards, interventions, and 2020/2030 public investment goals. It includes both engineered and nature-based coastal protection.

parent_statement: Adaptation to Climate Change Action Programme (P-3AC)
policy_statement: Develop decision-support tools, capacity building, awareness-raising, climate-risk mapping, adaptation plans, forecasting, warning and response systems, and monitoring and evaluation arrangements for adaptation.
source_quote: Line of Action #9 - Development of decision support tools, capacity building and awareness-raising actions. Main objectives: • Improving the level of knowledge on climate change • Systematising information and facilitating access to it • To sensitise, mobilise and raise awareness among citizens, communities, policymakers, administration technicians (central, regional, and local) and stakeholders • Build capacity of key public and private stakeholders for adaptive Demonstrate and monitor impacts of climate change Measures/concretization: • Communication, dissemination, education and awareness-raising actions climate change risks and adaptation measures.
section_header: Line of Action #9 - Development of decision support tools, capacity building and awareness-raising actions
extraction_rationale: This is a cross-cutting P-3AC line of action with specific capacity-building, information, planning, warning, and monitoring interventions. It is enabling adaptation policy rather than a direct physical measure.

policy_statement: Portugal is preparing the National Adaptation Roadmap 2100 to update climate projections, assess impacts in key sectors, establish regional adaptation narratives and spatial-planning guidelines, and identify investment needs and strategic adaptation measures.
source_quote: Following a similar approach, the National Adaptation Roadmap 2100 (RNA 2100) is being drawn up and is expected to be completed in 2023. The RNA 2100 will update the knowledge of climate projections for Portugal and respective impacts in key sectors, for different Greenhouse Gases (GHG) concentration scenarios. RNA 2100 will result in regional adaptation narratives, with a view  to  stablish  climate  change  adaptation  guidelines  for  spatial  planning  and  programmes, including at sub-national level.
section_header: Summaries of national strategies, policies, plans and efforts
extraction_rationale: This is a named planned national roadmap with a deadline and specific outputs for adaptation planning and investment identification. It is directly relevant to adaptation.

policy_statement: Portugal established the Portuguese Environmental Fund to support environmental policies, including climate change, water resources, waste, nature conservation, biodiversity, and international climate cooperation.
source_quote: The Portuguese Environmental Fund was established in 2017. The purpose of this instrument is to  support  national  environmental  policies  for  the  pursuit  of  Sustainable  Development Objectives,  contributing  to  the  achievement  of  national  and  international  objectives  and commitments, in particular those related to climate change, water resources, waste and nature conservation and biodiversity. One of  the  domains  that  is  clearly  identified  as  action  domain  of  this  Fund  is  international cooperation in the field of climate change, in accordance with the compliance of international commitments.
section_header: 4.5. Provision of new and additional resources
extraction_rationale: This is a named financial instrument established to fund environmental and climate objectives. It qualifies as a broad financial instrument.

policy_statement: Portugal committed, as an EU Member State, to mobilise 0.15% to 0.20% of its GNI as ODA for Least Developed Countries by 2030 and to focus support on countries most in need.
source_quote: As an EU Member State, Portugal made the commitment to mobilise 0.15% to 0.20% of its GNI as ODA allocated to Least Developed Countries (LDC) by 2030. It also endorsed the commitment derived  from  the  2014  ministerial-level  meeting  of  the  Development  Assistance  Committee (OECD/DAC) to focus the support from member countries on countries most in need (which includes Fragile States, LDC and Small Island Developing States (SIDS)).
section_header: 4.5. Provision of new and additional resources
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified financial commitment with a 2030 deadline. Its climate relevance is indirect because the quoted commitment is broader ODA, although placed within climate support and development assistance context.

policy_statement: Portugal provides bilateral climate adaptation cooperation finance, treating Portuguese Environmental Fund support for developing-country climate adaptation as new and additional to conventional ODA.
source_quote: Bearing in mind that financing ODA projects is not a core objective of Portuguese Environmental Fund and that this financing resources is complementary to conventional ODA flows, Portugal considers that the financing provided by the Portuguese Environmental Fund to activities that aim to promote the sustainable development and welfare of developing countries, consequently,  is  new  and  additional  to  the  current  sources  of  ODA  flows. Hence,  regarding climate change adaptation bilateral cooperation of a total amount of 6.6 million USD, 5.3 million USD is new and additional.
section_header: 4.5. Provision of new and additional resources
extraction_rationale: This is a climate finance allocation for adaptation cooperation and specifies the amount considered new and additional. It is financial and directly climate-related.

policy_statement: The Rural Development Programme (PDR 2020) supported adaptation of agriculture and forests to climate change with €1,746.5 million.
source_quote: In  the  case  of  the  agriculture  and  food/rural  development  sector,  the  Rural  Development Programme (PDR 2020) supported with €1746.5 million the adaptation of agriculture/forest to Climate Change (54.5% of total funding to agriculture and forests). This amount was distributed as follows: 0.5% (Knowledge); 12.2% (Investments); 1.6% (agricultural risks); 13.4% (forestry); 48.8% (agro-environmental measures and climate); 23.5% (Areas with constraints).
section_header: 5.1.1. State of play of the implementation of measures planned under 'Strategies and Plans', including an overview of the subnational level and the disbursement of funding to increase climate resilience
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete funding allocation to agriculture and forestry adaptation. It qualifies as a financial instrument/public investment support line.

policy_statement: The Operational Programme for Sustainability and Efficiency in the Use of Resources (POSEUR) funded climate adaptation and risk prevention/management through Priority Axis 2, including adaptation investment and disaster resilience systems.
source_quote: The Operational Programme for Sustainability and Efficiency in the Use of Resources (POSEUR) was partially funded by the EU Structural and Cohesion Funds and its Thematic Objective 5 aims to strengthen national adaptive capacity. Its Priority Axis 2 - Adaptation to climate change and risk  prevention  and  management,  includes  two  investment  priorities  (IP):  5.1.  Support  for investment for adaptation to climate change; 5.2. Promoting investments to address specific risks, ensure disaster resilience and develop disaster management systems.
section_header: 5.1.2. State of play of the implementation of measures planned under 'Strategies and Plans': spending earmarked for climate adaptation including in disaster risk management
extraction_rationale: This is a named financial programme with specified investment priorities for adaptation and disaster resilience. It qualifies as a financial instrument.

policy_statement: The Environmental Fund finances adaptation operations implementing local or regional measures to reduce flood risks and increase resilience of infrastructure, ecosystems, species, and habitats.
source_quote: The  Environmental  Fund  finances  adaptation  operations  aimed  at  implementing  material measures recommended in local or regional planning exercises, namely that reduce or minimise climate  risks  associated  with  flood  events  and  increase  the  resilience  of  infrastructures  and ecosystems, species, and habitats.
section_header: 5.1.2. State of play of the implementation of measures planned under 'Strategies and Plans': spending earmarked for climate adaptation including in disaster risk management
extraction_rationale: This is a funding policy for adaptation operations tied to local/regional planning and concrete outcomes. It is directly climate-relevant and financial.

policy_statement: Portugal created the More Sustainable Buildings support programme in 2020 to finance energy and water performance improvements in buildings, funding 890 applications worth €1.75 million.
source_quote: With the specific objective  of  rehabilitating  and  improving  buildings'  concerning  energy  and water  performance  it  was  created  the  support  programme  "More  Sustainable  Buildings",  in 2020, and it has been financing 890 applications, amounting to €1.75 million.
section_header: 5.1.3. State of play of the implementation of measures planned under 'Strategies and Plans': the share of spending used to support climate adaptation in each sector
extraction_rationale: This is a named support programme with funding and a specific resource-efficiency objective. Climate relevance is indirect in this adaptation communication, because the measure improves building energy and water performance rather than explicitly targeting emissions or a named hazard in the quoted text.

policy_statement: Portugal financed Village Condominium applications to manage fuels around high-forest-density settlements and dispersed rural villages, reducing wildfire risk.
source_quote: In  2020,  the  Environmental  Fund  financed  applications  with  the  objective  to  implement adaptation measures that guarantee the improvement of the adaptive capacity and increase the territory's resilience to the impacts of climate change and applications made under the "Village Condominium", the Integrated Support Programme for Villages located in forest territories, to ensure  the  management  of  fuels  around  settlements  in  areas  of  high  forest  density  and increased number and dispersion of small rural settlements.
section_header: 5.1.3. State of play of the implementation of measures planned under 'Strategies and Plans': the share of spending used to support climate adaptation in each sector
extraction_rationale: This is a named support programme for fuel management around vulnerable settlements. It is a concrete adaptation intervention aimed at wildfire risk and resilience.

policy_statement: The Autonomous Region of the Azores approved the Regional Programme for Climate Change (PRAC), covering mitigation and adaptation, vulnerability studies, and adaptation measures for relevant sectors.
source_quote: The Autonomous Region of the Azores proceeded with the Regional Programme for Climate Change  (PRAC -Portuguese  acronym),  approved  by  the  Regional  Legislative  Decree  Nº. 30/2019/A, 28 th of  November, which encompasses mitigation and adaptation. PRAC allowed improving the level of knowledge on climate change in the Region through the studies of current and  future  vulnerabilities  and  the  definition  of  adaptation  measures  for  the  most  relevant sectors.
section_header: 5.1.1. State of play of the implementation of measures planned under 'Strategies and Plans', including an overview of the subnational level and the disbursement of funding to increase climate resilience
extraction_rationale: This is a regional climate programme approved by legislative decree with adaptation and mitigation scope. It qualifies as a policy framework at subnational level.

policy_statement: Portugal expanded municipal and intermunicipal adaptation planning so that 271 municipalities, or 88% of Portuguese municipalities, were covered by climate change adaptation plans or strategies by the end of 2020.
source_quote: Until 2015 only three municipalities had  elaborated  adaptation  plans  and  strategies.  Since  then,  this  coverage  has  expanded considerably,  first  as  a  result  of  the  ClimAdaPT.Local  project  funded  by  EEA  Grants  and  the Environmental  Fund,  followed  by  the  European  Regional  Development  Fund  (ERDF)  funding provided  by  the  Operational  Programme  for  Sustainability  and  Efficiency  in  the  Use  of Resources, along with strategies and plans funded by the municipalities themselves. At the end of 2020, the number of municipalities covered by climate change adaptation plans or strategies (of municipal and/or inter-municipal or metropolitan scope) was 271, corresponding to 88% of Portuguese municipalities.
extraction_rationale: This describes a concrete funded planning rollout with a quantified coverage outcome. It is adaptation planning rather than a single regulatory mandate.

policy_statement: Portugal uses the National Programme for Spatial Planning Policy (PNPOT) to mainstream climate change across territorial planning and to promote knowledge and risk management considering climate adaptation.
source_quote: for 'Mainstreaming Adaptation', the publication of the PNPOT - National Programme for Spatial  Planning  Policy,  a  territorial  development  instrument  of  strategic  nature  that establishes the great options with relevance to the organization of the national territory, consubstantiates the framework of reference to be considered in the elaboration of other Territorial Management Instruments, and constitutes an instrument of cooperation with the other MS. Climate change was taken as a transversal theme and integrated into the different themes diagnosed, in the environmental, social and economic areas, assessing the impact of global scenarios applied to the national territory, and seeking to indicate the direction that some variables take in the region.
extraction_rationale: PNPOT is a named territorial planning instrument that integrates climate change as a transversal theme. It qualifies as mainstreaming adaptation policy.

policy_statement: Portugal’s National Irrigation Programme promotes sustainable and efficient irrigation, including rehabilitation and modernisation of hydro-agricultural facilities to improve agricultural water-use efficiency and combat desertification.
source_quote: Reference should also be made to the climate change adaptation measures framed within the National Irrigation Programme ( Programa Nacional de Regadios ) to promote irrigation from a perspective of sustainability and efficiency of water resources and combat desertification 30 . This programme provides for interventions in hydro-agricultural facilities aimed at the rehabilitation and modernisation of existing irrigation schemes, contributing to water consumption efficiency in the agricultural sector, thus constituting an adaptation measure.
section_header: 3. Progress in the design and implementation of adaptation policies in Portugal
extraction_rationale: This is a named programme with specific irrigation modernisation interventions and explicit adaptation framing. The main mechanism is water-use efficiency, with explicit desertification adaptation.

policy_statement: Portugal’s National Plan for Integrated Management of Rural Fires combines prevention and firefighting to reduce ignitions and support lower atmospheric pollutant emissions through improved plant fuel management.
source_quote: National Plan for Integrated Management of Rural Fires ( Plano Nacional de Gestão Integrada de Fogos Rurais ), which establishes the relationship between climate variability and rural fires, becoming a strategic document in bringing together prevention and firefighting, instituting a cyclical value chain, from planning to continuous improvement, in which one of the main aims is to reduce ignitions and, as a corollary, result in lower emissions of pollutants into the atmosphere, promoting, instead, plant fuel management practices that are more compatible with national commitments to GHG emissions. This Plan also aims to harmonise sectoral public policies.
section_header: 3. Progress in the design and implementation of adaptation policies in Portugal
extraction_rationale: This is a named strategic plan with specific wildfire-prevention and fuel-management mechanisms. It is primarily adaptation to wildfire risk, with explicit emissions co-benefit.

policy_statement: Portugal’s Litoral XXI Action Plan and Coastal Zone Programmes prioritise coastal interventions and safeguard regimes that account for climate-change-driven coastal risks.
source_quote: Litoral  XXI  Action  Plan 24 ( Plano  de  Ação  Litoral  XXI ),  which  is  the  reference  instrument  for  active management of the coastal zone for a horizon beyond 2020, reflecting the major policy lines and strategic options for the coast, prioritizes the interventions of each stretch of the coast taking into account the global processes arising from climate change. Additionally, the Coastal Zone 25  Programmes ( Programas de Orla Costeira ), as territorial management instruments, establish safeguard regimes of the values to be preserved and, taking into account the risk arising from climate scenarios, identify a set of interventions with territorial incidence to minimise the impacts.
section_header: 3. Progress in the design and implementation of adaptation policies in Portugal
extraction_rationale: This is a named coastal planning and intervention framework incorporating climate scenarios. It qualifies as adaptation policy for coastal risk.

policy_statement: Portugal’s National Forestry Strategy and Regional Forestry Management Plans integrate climate change risks and identify measures to increase forestry-sector resilience.
