source_quote: National Forestry Strategy 26 ( Estratégia Nacional para as Florestas ) and Regional Forestry Management  Plans ( Planos  Regionais  de  Ordenamento  Florestal  -  PROF ),  which  integrate  the  critical challenges that climate change raises for the forestry sector, highlighting as critical impacts the worsening of risks associated with harmful biotic agents and forest fires, also contributing to the conditioning of the productivity of stands, and identifying the general lines for increasing the resilience of the sector to these impacts.
section_header: 3. Progress in the design and implementation of adaptation policies in Portugal
extraction_rationale: This is a named forest policy framework that explicitly addresses climate-driven fire and biotic risks and forestry resilience. It is adaptation-focused with ecosystem/forest-management mechanisms.

policy_statement: Portugal’s National Strategy for Nature Conservation and Biodiversity 2030 treats climate change as a major pressure on ecosystems and establishes targets for action to protect biodiversity.
source_quote: National  Strategy  for  Nature  Conservation  and  Biodiversity  2030 27 ( Estratégia Nacional de Conservação da Natureza e Biodiversidade 2030 ), which considers the impacts of climate change as one of the main factors of pressure on ecosystems and, in this sense, a threat to biodiversity, both because of what it may represent in terms of loss of habitat and by creating conditions for non-native species to find in the country conditions for their development, creating imbalances in natural systems and, for these reasons, establishes its own targets for action.
section_header: 3. Progress in the design and implementation of adaptation policies in Portugal
extraction_rationale: This is a named 2030 strategy with targets responding to climate pressures on biodiversity. It is ecosystem-based adaptation/nature policy.

policy_statement: Portugal’s National Strategy for a Preventive Civil Protection integrates climate risks into all strategic objectives and promotes climate adaptation in safety-of-people-and-property mechanisms.
source_quote: National  Strategy  for  a  Preventive  Civil  Protection 28 ( Estratégia  Nacional  para  uma  Proteção  Civil Preventiva ), highlights the importance of promoting the integration of climate change adaptation in the mechanisms and strategies aimed at the safety of people and property and integrates climate risks in all strategic objectives.
section_header: 3. Progress in the design and implementation of adaptation policies in Portugal
extraction_rationale: This is a named civil-protection strategy that integrates climate risks across objectives. It is a policy for climate-resilient disaster risk management.

policy_statement: P-3AC establishes result indicators and 2020/2030 targets to track Portugal’s adaptation outcomes across planning coverage, water efficiency, infrastructure contingency planning, coastal erosion, floods, invasive species, and vector-borne disease.
source_quote: Table 1. Result indicators and targets defined under the NAP (Adaptation to Climate Change Action Programme - P-3AC). The results indicators associated with the identified materialise objectives of the adaptation process primarily derive from current sectoral planning instruments and intend to measure the programme's contribution, directly or indirectly, within the different areas of intervention (Annex II).
section_header: MRE methodology related to the implementation of adaptation actions
extraction_rationale: The table establishes quantified targets under P-3AC; because it contains multiple subordinate targets, it is treated as a parent policy set. These targets operationalise adaptation outcomes.

parent_statement: P-3AC result indicators and targets
policy_statement: Increase coverage of municipalities by adaptation plans from 60% in 2020 to 100% in 2030.
source_quote: Municipalities covered by adaptation plans (municipal, inter-municipal or regional) | 60% | 100%. The results indicators associated with the identified materialise objectives of the adaptation process primarily derive from current sectoral planning instruments and intend to measure the programme's contribution, directly or indirectly, within the different areas of intervention (Annex II).
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified adaptation planning target with a 2030 deadline. It is a planning commitment rather than physical infrastructure.

parent_statement: P-3AC result indicators and targets
policy_statement: Increase municipalities with forest fire defence plans integrating future climate vulnerability assessments and adaptation measures from 2% in 2020 to 100% in 2030.
source_quote: Municipalities with forest fire defence plans that integrate future climate vulnerability assessments and adaptation measures | 2% | 100%. The results indicators associated with the identified materialise objectives of the adaptation process primarily derive from current sectoral planning instruments and intend to measure the programme's contribution, directly or indirectly, within the different areas of intervention (Annex II).
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified target requiring municipal fire defence plans to integrate climate vulnerability and adaptation. It directly addresses climate-related wildfire risk.

parent_statement: P-3AC result indicators and targets
policy_statement: Achieve water-efficiency targets by 2030 of 85% for urban consumption, 90% for industrial consumption, and 80% for agricultural water use.
source_quote: Water efficiency in urban consumption | 80% | 85%. Water efficiency in industrial consumption | 85% | 90%. Water use efficiency in agriculture | 65% | 80%.
extraction_rationale: These are quantified water-efficiency targets with 2020 baselines and 2030 targets. The primary mechanism is resource efficiency; in the P-3AC context it supports adaptation to drought and scarcity.

parent_statement: P-3AC result indicators and targets
policy_statement: Increase the target population reached by awareness or dissemination campaigns on climate change impacts and adaptation measures from 5% in 2020 to 25% in 2030.
source_quote: Target population of awareness or dissemination campaigns related to climate change impacts and adaptation measures | 5% | 25%. The results indicators associated with the identified materialise objectives of the adaptation process primarily derive from current sectoral planning instruments and intend to measure the programme's contribution, directly or indirectly, within the different areas of intervention (Annex II).
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified awareness-raising target for adaptation. It is an enabling measure rather than direct hazard reduction.

parent_statement: P-3AC result indicators and targets
policy_statement: Increase the share of infrastructure and utility operators with adaptation or extreme-event contingency plans by 2030: transport to 50%, energy to 100%, water/wastewater to 100%, and telecommunications to 100%.
source_quote: Transport infrastructure managing entities that have adaptation plans or contingency plans for extreme events | 10% | 50%. Energy production, transmission and distribution companies that have adaptation plans or contingency plans for extreme events | 25% | 100%. Water supply and wastewater treatment companies that have adaptation plans or contingency plans for extreme events | 50% | 100%. Telecommunications companies that have adaptation plans or contingency plans for extreme events | 25% | 100%.
extraction_rationale: These are quantified sectoral adaptation and contingency planning targets for critical infrastructure and utilities. They directly address resilience to extreme events.

parent_statement: P-3AC result indicators and targets
policy_statement: Reduce the share of Portugal’s continental coastline in a critical state of erosion from 16.5% in 2020 to 10% in 2030.
source_quote: Continental coastline in a critical state of erosion | 16,5% | 10%. The results indicators associated with the identified materialise objectives of the adaptation process primarily derive from current sectoral planning instruments and intend to measure the programme's contribution, directly or indirectly, within the different areas of intervention (Annex II).
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified coastal adaptation outcome target. It directly addresses climate-related erosion and coastal vulnerability.

parent_statement: P-3AC result indicators and targets
policy_statement: Increase the irrigated infrastructure area using precision technologies that promote efficient water use from 10% in 2020 to 50% in 2030.
source_quote: Irrigated infrastructure area with precision technologies that promote efficient water use | 10% | 50%. The results indicators associated with the identified materialise objectives of the adaptation process primarily derive from current sectoral planning instruments and intend to measure the programme's contribution, directly or indirectly, within the different areas of intervention (Annex II).
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified target for precision irrigation technology and efficient water use. The primary mechanism is water resource efficiency, supporting adaptation to drought and scarcity.

parent_statement: P-3AC result indicators and targets
policy_statement: Reduce by 25% by 2030 the number of people affected by floods in risk areas identified in Flood Risk Management Plans, compared with the previous planning cycle.
source_quote: Reduction in the number of people affected by floods in risk areas identified in the Flood Risk Management Plans (compared with the previous cycle of the PGRI) | - | 25%. The results indicators associated with the identified materialise objectives of the adaptation process primarily derive from current sectoral planning instruments and intend to measure the programme's contribution, directly or indirectly, within the different areas of intervention (Annex II).
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified flood-risk reduction target. It is directly adaptation-relevant because floods are a named climate-related hazard.

parent_statement: P-3AC result indicators and targets
policy_statement: Reduce the geographical distribution area of invasive alien species by 10% by 2030 compared to the reference year.
source_quote: Reduction in the geographical distribution area of invasive alien species (compared to the reference year) | - | 10%. The results indicators associated with the identified materialise objectives of the adaptation process primarily derive from current sectoral planning instruments and intend to measure the programme's contribution, directly or indirectly, within the different areas of intervention (Annex II).
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified ecosystem management target linked to climate-sensitive invasive species risk under P-3AC. It primarily uses ecosystem management.

parent_statement: P-3AC result indicators and targets
policy_statement: Reduce by 10% by 2030 the decadal average number of human vector-borne disease cases associated with climate change.
source_quote: Reduction in the number of cases of human vector-borne diseases associated with climate change (decadal average) | - | 10%. The results indicators associated with the identified materialise objectives of the adaptation process primarily derive from current sectoral planning instruments and intend to measure the programme's contribution, directly or indirectly, within the different areas of intervention (Annex II).
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified health adaptation target addressing climate-associated vector-borne disease. It directly reduces climate-health vulnerability.

policy_statement: Qatar intends to reduce national GHG emissions by 25% by 2030 relative to a business-as-usual baseline.
source_quote: This current communication reflects an enhanced ambition by the State of Qatar towards reducing its overall emissions in response to the guidance set forth in Article 4.4 of the Paris Agreement. Qatar intends to reduce 25% of its GHG emissions by the year 2030, relative to baseline scenario {BusinessAs-Usual (BAU)}.
extraction_rationale: This is the headline quantified national mitigation target, with a specific percentage reduction, target year, and baseline scenario.

policy_statement: Qatar implements the Al-Shaheen Oil Field Gas Recovery and Utilization Project to reduce CO2 emissions by approximately 1.2 million tons annually during 2014-2021.
source_quote: The Al-Shaheen Oil Field Gas Recovery and Utilization Project has been registered as a Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) project since 2007 for 21 years within the framework of the Kyoto Protocol. The project received approval from the UNFCCC for the seven-year crediting period from 2014 to 2021, and it is expected to abate approximately 1.2 million tons of CO2 each year during this period.
extraction_rationale: This is a named emissions-reduction project with quantified annual abatement and an approved crediting period.

policy_statement: Qatar Petroleum is committed to zero routine flaring by 2030 and minimizing technically feasible non-routine flaring.
source_quote: The national oil company, Qatar Petroleum (QP), is committed to zero routine flaring by 2030, with a long-term goal to reduce flaring in onshore facilities to the absolute minimum. Technically feasible non-routine flaring is also covered.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear sectoral mitigation commitment with a deadline and specific operational intervention: ending routine flaring.

policy_statement: Qatar will use carbon capture and storage in the oil and gas sector, including a 2.2 MTPA CO2 capture and storage facility and CCS for new LNG facilities.
source_quote: Carbon capture storage (CCS) will be another pivotal measure for reducing the GHG emissions from the sector. Qatar commissioned the largest CO2 recovery and sequestration facility in the MENA region at Ras Laffan in 2019 with a design capacity of 2.2 MTPA of CO2 capture and storage. CCS is included for new LNG facilities and concepts, for remaining LNG facilities will be developed and implemented considering the economic, safety and environmental concerns.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific mitigation technology deployment commitment, including a quantified design capacity and planned inclusion in LNG facilities.

policy_statement: Qatar Petroleum will reduce methane emissions through methane guiding principles, leak detection and repair, and integrated fugitive methane monitoring and repair across assets.
source_quote: QP signed a set of Guiding Principles on 22 March 2018 that aim to reduce methane emissions across the natural gas value chain stretching from production to the final consumer. The principles aim to continuously curb methane emissions, stimulate strong performance across gas value chains, enhance the accuracy of methane emissions data, advance sound policies and regulations on methane emissions, and to increase transparency. In 2019, Qatar Petroleum introduced the smart leak detection and repair program (LDAR) in all upstream and downstream facilities of the oil & gas industry.
extraction_rationale: This is a named methane-reduction policy package using specific monitoring and repair interventions; the text explicitly targets methane emissions.

policy_statement: Qatar will implement oil and gas energy-efficiency projects by 2025, including turbine and boiler optimization, fuel gas and steam measurement, HRSG reliability, waste heat recovery, and recycling excess fuel gas.
source_quote: Qatar is enhancing energy efficiency in the oil & gas sector as a key measure to reduce GHG emissions. The energy efficiency program includes several projects that are allocated in upstream facilities as well as gas-to-liquid and downstream facilities. Amongst the variety of measures in energy efficiency, certain initiatives are aimed to be implemented by 2025, e.g., seasonal optimization of gas turbine generators and boilers, improved measurement / balancing for fuel gas / steam, and improved reliability of heat recovery steam generator (HRSGs).
extraction_rationale: This is a defined sectoral efficiency program with specific technical measures and a 2025 implementation timeframe.

policy_statement: Qatar plans to optimize and share electrical generation capacity across upstream and GTL facilities to reduce gas consumption and GHG emissions.
source_quote: Qatar also plans to efficiently utilize its power plant capacities by usage in other upstream facilities or feed-in from GTL (gas-to-liquid) facilities to its utility distribution / transmission grid. Electrical generation capacity shall be shared and optimized across all upstream facilities. This would allow more efficient dispatch of generating capacity and keep the units closer to their most efficient operating levels, thereby reducing gas consumption and GHG emissions.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific operational efficiency commitment in the oil and gas sector, with explicit intended reductions in gas consumption and emissions.

policy_statement: Qatar is introducing an 800 MW solar power plant and aims to expand renewable energy as a key national energy source.
source_quote: Nevertheless, recently Qatar has made significant progress in reducing the emissions from the power & water sector, by introducing its first 800 MW solar power plant, which shall be operational soon. It is the goal of the State of Qatar to expand these efforts and transform renewable energy into a key driver for ecological and commercial benefits.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified renewable-energy deployment measure and broader commitment to expand renewable energy.

policy_statement: Qatar will continue the Tarsheed national program to reduce per-capita electricity and water consumption.
source_quote: The National Program for Conservative & Efficient use of Water & Electricity (Tarsheed) has been successful in generating a lasting awareness over the issue of water and energy wastage, especially among the youth, and in reducing consumption of electricity & water per capita. It has ambitious aims for further reductions.
extraction_rationale: This is a named national conservation program with an ongoing commitment to further reduce water and electricity consumption.

policy_statement: Qatar Foundation, Education City, and Qatar Green Building Council are promoting demand-side energy efficiency, energy savings, and rooftop solar generation.
source_quote: Led by Qatar Foundation, Education City and the Qatar Green Building Council, efforts are being made to enhance the demand-side energy efficiency, energy savings, and local energy generation through rooftops solar panels. So far, the Tarsheed program has been successful in optimizing consumption of electricity & water and has ambitious aims for further reductions.
extraction_rationale: This includes specific interventions: demand-side energy efficiency and rooftop solar panels. It is somewhat broad but tied to named institutions and concrete measures.

policy_statement: Qatar is deploying district cooling and energy labeling for electronic devices to reduce energy intensity and household and SME GHG emissions.
source_quote: Energy efficiency measures such as district cooling and energy labeling for all electronic devices are systematically being deployed and play a growing role in the national economic diversification strategy by reducing energy intensity and the need for energy subsidies, while also mitigating the overall GHG emissions of households and small & medium enterprises. Qatar has implemented several specification improvement standards for electrical and electronic equipment such as air conditioners resulting in significant savings in electricity consumption.
extraction_rationale: This is a set of named efficiency interventions, including labeling and equipment standards, with explicit energy and emissions benefits.

policy_statement: Qatar is phasing out incandescent lamps and adopting energy-efficient lighting to conserve energy and reduce GHG emissions.
source_quote: The initiative to phase out incandescent lamps and adoption of Energy Efficient lighting has contributed in a major way for conservation of Energy and thereby GHG emissions reduction in the State of Qatar. Qatar is considered a pioneer in the field of district cooling (DC).
extraction_rationale: This is a specific lighting efficiency intervention with explicit GHG reduction relevance.

policy_statement: Qatar is expanding district cooling systems to save energy, water, and infrastructure resources in buildings.
source_quote: District cooling relies on largescale centralized cooling that provides a wide spectrum of savings in energy consumption and infrastructure. It consequently reduces impact on the environment. The DC system operations are essentially linked to the electricity and water consumption.
extraction_rationale: District cooling is a named infrastructure efficiency measure that reduces electricity and water use; the climate link is through resource efficiency and reduced environmental impact.

policy_statement: Qatar is upgrading sewage treatment plants to produce treated effluent for landscaping, irrigation, district cooling, and construction uses.
source_quote: Lastly, Qatar has continuously strived to upgrade its sewage treatment plants to produce treated effluents suitable for purposes such as landscaping, fodder crops irrigation, district cooling, construction industry use, etc. The transportation sector in Qatar has been earmarked for rapid modernization.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific water-reuse infrastructure intervention that improves water resource efficiency.

policy_statement: Qatar is developing public transport through the Doha Metro and Lusail Tram to reduce transport-sector emissions.
source_quote: The transportation sector in Qatar has been earmarked for rapid modernization. The Doha Metro and Lusail Tram are major milestones in the development of public transportation and subsequent reduction of emissions from this sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a named public-transport infrastructure intervention linked to transport emissions reduction.

policy_statement: Qatar is committing to electrify its public transport system and install EV charging infrastructure nationwide.
source_quote: The country has also taken significant strides to adopt electrification of on-road vehicles by committing to electrify its public transport system and investing in installation of charging infrastructure across the country. Transition from ICE vehicles to EV and providing necessary infrastructure for EV chargers will contribute in a major way for GHG reduction and thereby NDC goals.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific transport electrification commitment with infrastructure investment and explicit GHG reduction relevance.

policy_statement: Qatar is electrifying port operations, including use of electric tractors at Hamad Port, to reduce emissions.
source_quote: Electrification has also been adopted in port operations e.g. reducing emissions at Hamad port using electric tractors. Going forward, gradual adoption of Euro 6 emission standards for vehicles and promoting a shift towards electric vehicles for private use shall constitute key initiatives to reduce emissions from the transportation sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific operational electrification measure for port equipment, explicitly tied to emissions reduction.

policy_statement: Qatar will gradually adopt Euro 6 vehicle emission standards and promote private electric vehicle use.
source_quote: Electrification has also been adopted in port operations e.g. reducing emissions at Hamad port using electric tractors. Going forward, gradual adoption of Euro 6 emission standards for vehicles and promoting a shift towards electric vehicles for private use shall constitute key initiatives to reduce emissions from the transportation sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific regulatory and market-shift commitment for vehicles, with explicit emissions-reduction purpose.

policy_statement: Qatar is adopting GSAS green building standards and higher hotel sustainability standards for energy and water savings.
source_quote: Qatar has been transforming its building standards towards higher sustainability levels through the adoption of the Global Sustainability Assessment System (GSAS) standards. The number of projects registered for GSAS certifications has been rapidly increasing thereby facilitating the transition towards green buildings. The Qatar Green Building Council has been advising hotels on higher environmental standards for energy and water savings, and has certified an increasing number of hotels, in line with the new hotel classification system implemented by the Qatar Tourism Authority (QTA) which has set new and higher sustainability standard.
extraction_rationale: This is a named building standards and certification policy, with explicit energy and water savings in buildings and hotels.

policy_statement: Hamad International Airport’s second expansion terminal will achieve a 4-star GSAS rating and LEED Silver certification with energy-efficiency measures.
source_quote: In its plans for the second expansion phase, the terminal building will be the first airport in the MENA region to achieve a 4-star Global Sustainability Assessment System (GSAS) rating, which is the first performance-based system in the MENA region, developed for rating the green buildings and infrastructures. The terminal will also be a LEED Silver certified building with innovative measures of energy efficiency across the entire building.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific green-building certification commitment for a named infrastructure project, including energy-efficiency measures.

policy_statement: Qatar plans to promote decentralized renewable energy production and more efficient energy consumption in buildings.
source_quote: A steadily growing number of projects to install solar panels on residential buildings are being undertaken by the private sector. Qatar plans to promote decentralized renewable energy production and use in buildings while also making more efficient their energy consumption. The ongoing development of Lusail city is Qatar's main initiative concerning smart and sustainable cities with centralized water, cooling, waste, and transport systems as well as solar energy production.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete building-sector policy combining rooftop solar and building energy efficiency.

policy_statement: Qatar is developing Lusail City as a smart and sustainable city with centralized water, cooling, waste, transport systems, and solar energy production.
source_quote: Qatar plans to promote decentralized renewable energy production and use in buildings while also making more efficient their energy consumption. The ongoing development of Lusail city is Qatar's main initiative concerning smart and sustainable cities with centralized water, cooling, waste, and transport systems as well as solar energy production. Qatar has been making a steady progress towards attaining circular economy in the construction sector by implementing recycling and re-using construction waste and the government further plans to explore the use of environment friendly battery-powered generators for construction activities.
extraction_rationale: This is a named sustainable urban development initiative with specific centralized infrastructure systems and solar generation.

policy_statement: Qatar is implementing recycling and reuse of construction waste to advance a circular economy in the construction sector.
source_quote: The ongoing development of Lusail city is Qatar's main initiative concerning smart and sustainable cities with centralized water, cooling, waste, and transport systems as well as solar energy production. Qatar has been making a steady progress towards attaining circular economy in the construction sector by implementing recycling and re-using construction waste and the government further plans to explore the use of environment friendly battery-powered generators for construction activities.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific circular-economy resource-efficiency intervention in the construction sector.

policy_statement: QEERI released the Qatar Solar Atlas to support accelerated solar energy deployment across the country.
source_quote: Similar research activities are also conducted at Hamad Bin Khalifa University & its affiliated research institute, Qatar Environment and Energy Research Institute (QEERI), has released the first Qatar Solar Atlas, a tool that quantifies the country's solar resource and geographical distribution as a first step towards accelerating the use of more solar energy across the country. In addition, the recent Air Quality Index and Inhalable Particulates Index to provide the local population with information on gas and particulate emissions in Qatar.
extraction_rationale: This is an enabling research and information tool for renewable-energy deployment; it is specific, but its emissions impact is indirect.

policy_statement: The Qatar National Research Fund is funding research for an efficient national-scale carbon management system.
source_quote: The Qatar Research, Development and Innovation Council (QRDI) focuses on key topics of sustainability in Qatar's energy sector and in management of environmental, food and water resources. Meanwhile, the Qatar National Research Fund (QNRF) is funding research for an efficient carbon management system at the national scale.
extraction_rationale: This is a funding commitment for carbon-management research; it qualifies as a financial instrument supporting mitigation capacity.

policy_statement: Qatar’s Ministry of Education and Higher Education implements Eco School programs and a sustainable development committee to address climate change through education.
source_quote: Since 1994, the Ministry of Education and Higher Education has introduced the 'Eco School programs' initiative which promotes environmental education and awareness in primary and secondary levels. This is realized through parts of the curriculum covering climate change in combination with extracurricular activities. Building upon this legacy, the Ministry has also established a committee for sustainable development to enhance all activities in this sphere and address climate change through education.
extraction_rationale: This is a named climate education and awareness initiative. Its direct mitigation or adaptation effect is indirect and enabling, but it is explicitly about climate change education.

policy_statement: Qatar plans to enhance teacher training on climate change to support sustainability education and long-term behavioral change.
source_quote: On a more applied level, the state of Qatar is eager to foster climate change education throughout the daily routines of educational institutions. This is illustrated by the plan for enhancing teachers' training on climate change topics in order to enable educators to present the topics of sustainability and environmental development in an appealing manner to students, and to foster behavioral changes in the long-term.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific climate education capacity-building intervention, though its climate impact is indirect and behavioral.

policy_statement: Major university campuses in Qatar use rooftop solar panels and policies to reduce energy consumption.
source_quote: Also, all major university campuses in Qatar feature solar panels on building rooftops and policies to reduce energy consumption. Qatar Foundation (QF) is developing green campus and housing facilities which have a direct impact on the ecological footprint of facilities and additionally increases awareness and consciousness of students.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific institutional sustainability intervention combining rooftop solar and energy-consumption reduction policies.

policy_statement: Qatar Foundation is developing green campus and housing facilities to reduce ecological footprints and raise student awareness.
source_quote: Qatar Foundation (QF) is developing green campus and housing facilities which have a direct impact on the ecological footprint of facilities and additionally increases awareness and consciousness of students. Further projects include initiatives such as awareness campaigns advocating for banning single-use plastics in society and annual collection campaigns.
extraction_rationale: This is a named institutional green-facilities development commitment. The climate mechanism is resource efficiency, though the text frames impacts broadly as ecological footprint.

policy_statement: Education City operates an 11.5 km tram system with 24 stations using hybrid energy storage.
source_quote: Also, the Education City in QF, which is an extensive campus with a world class national library, several branches of leading international universities, schools and research centers, has been developing a strategy to implement solutions for a more sustainable educational complex. The Education City tram, for instance, now connects 24 designated tram stations across 11.5 km and runs on hybrid energy storage (HES).
extraction_rationale: This is a specific low-emission transport intervention within a campus, with quantified route and station details.

policy_statement: Qatar’s tourism strategy promotes sustainable tourism and reduces dependence on hydrocarbon resources for economic growth.
source_quote: The development of the country's first eco-resorts and major events like the FIFA World Cup 2022 and the Asian Games 2030 are set to further enhance the touristic appeal of the country while driving its socio-economic growth in a sustainable manner. Qatar's tourism strategy promotes sustainable tourism and aims to reduce dependence on hydrocarbon resources for economic growth.
extraction_rationale: This is an economic diversification strategy with sustainability aims. It is climate-relevant mainly through reduced hydrocarbon dependence, but the mitigation pathway is broad and not quantified.

policy_statement: Qatar has introduced water-conservation measures to reduce power and water consumption per capita and improve the ecological footprint of the water sector.
source_quote: Qatar depends mostly on seawater desalination for urban water supply, often using energy-intensive technologies. In the future, it is essential to reduce the consumption of both power and water per capita and use less energy-intensive technologies throughout the entire value stream. Qatar has also introduced several water-conservation measures which will significantly improve the ecological footprint of the sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a water and energy conservation commitment in an adaptation section; it responds to water scarcity while using efficiency as the mechanism.

policy_statement: Qatar is implementing water conservation regulation, high-consumption customer messages, aerator retrofits, TSE irrigation, and recycled water use in district cooling and construction.
source_quote: Besides the implementation of a new and ambitious water conservation regulation, several other measures have been started, e.g., increasing awareness via messages to residential customers with high consumption, retrofitting and replacing aerators in governmental facilities and switching to treated sewage effluent (TSE) for irrigation in parks. Additionally, savings are increasingly made by using recycled water in district cooling, the construction industry, and for a growing number of other usages.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete package of regulatory and operational water-conservation measures, including specific technologies and reuse applications.

policy_statement: Qatar has invested in treated sewage effluent reuse for agriculture, landscape irrigation, public parks, and aquifer injection as an adaptation measure.
source_quote: Efficient water management is a key adaptation measure. Therefore, Qatar has also invested significantly in this field. As a result, treated sewage effluent (TSE) volume in 2015 amounted to 194 million cubic meters or around 98.2% of total wastewater.
extraction_rationale: This is a resource-allocation and implementation measure for water reuse, with quantified wastewater treatment and reuse volumes.

policy_statement: Qatar has developed a National Water Policy, draft National Water Law, executive by-law, and draft law regulating groundwater well drilling.
source_quote: Moreover, as part of the development of Qatar's Water Plan and Strategy, the National Water Policy was developed as the draft of the National Water Law and its executive by-law have been finalized. Furthermore, a draft law to regulate groundwater wells drilling has been completed.
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory water-management policy package supporting adaptation to water scarcity and climate vulnerability.

policy_statement: Qatar is restoring marine habitats, growing mangrove trees, and planting indigenous urban trees to increase carbon sequestration.
source_quote: On biodiversity, Qatar is restoring marine habitats, particularly growing mangrove trees, and planting indigenous trees in urban areas and hence increasing the potential for carbon sequestration. Qatar has committed itself to formulating a comprehensive urban development plan and a sustainable urbanization and population distribution policy.
extraction_rationale: This is an ecosystem-based intervention using mangroves, marine habitat restoration, and indigenous trees, with explicit carbon sequestration benefits.

policy_statement: Qatar is formulating a comprehensive urban development plan and sustainable urbanization and population distribution policy.
source_quote: Qatar has committed itself to formulating a comprehensive urban development plan and a sustainable urbanization and population distribution policy. The plan, which comprises detailed strategies and operational aspects, is guided by the National Vision 2030 as a general framework.
extraction_rationale: This is a planning commitment for urban development and sustainable population distribution. Its climate relevance is somewhat indirect but appears in the adaptation infrastructure section.

policy_statement: Qatar is studying coastal climate impacts, including sea level rise, flooding, erosion, port operations, structural reliability, and coral bleaching for 2040 and 2100 horizons.
source_quote: The potential impacts of climate change on the Qatari coastal zone areas is currently being studied. A detailed analysis is carried out combining climate information based on historical trends for shortterm time horizons and projections of mean sea level rise by the end of the century. Sea level rise is considered the main driver of change but not the only one in the analysis.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific adaptation planning study addressing named climate hazards and coastal impact indicators, though it is primarily analytical rather than an implementation measure.

policy_statement: Qatar will use media campaigns and broad engagement initiatives to raise climate change awareness across society.
source_quote: Raising awareness is important for the creation of a shared understanding which is required to effectively rally resources and stakeholders for joint problem-solving. Traditional methods such as media campaigns will be used to spark attention and broad engagement initiatives will be applied to anchor the topic of climate change deeper in society.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific public awareness intervention for climate change. Its climate effect is enabling and behavioral, so classification is an edge case.

policy_statement: Qatar Foundation runs workplace campaigns such as 'think before you print,' 'save at your desk,' and 'Paperless office' to reduce waste and energy consumption.
source_quote: To target behavioral changes in the community by raising awareness about climate change, institutions like Qatar Foundation, for example, are initiating regular practices that encourage the adoption of more sustainable habits. The Foundation has established campaigns like, the 'think before you print,' 'save at your desk,' and 'Paperless office,' that encourage employees on changing printers' settings to minimize waste and incentivize users to further reduce the energy consumption.
extraction_rationale: This is a named set of behavioral resource-efficiency campaigns with explicit waste and energy consumption reduction aims.

policy_statement: TARSHEED community awareness activities provide conservation campaigns, school training, and KAHRAMAA awareness park programming for sustainable development behavior change.
source_quote: The TARSHEED Community awareness activities focuses on various conservation campaigns and basic training at school level, along with the KAHRAMAA awareness park for general public, is aimed to illustrate to the community the importance of sustainable development, and for inception of ideas for younger generation for behavioral changes. Other organizations like the Qatar Green Building Council (QGBC) has established a project under the name of 'no paper day' in 2013, that aims to encourage the local community to adopt eco-friendly initiatives geared at reducing waste nationwide and to remind the public that reducing the use of Qatar's resources not only can improve business efficiency, but also help to preserve the environment's long-term health.
extraction_rationale: This is a named conservation awareness program with specific outreach channels. It is resource-efficiency oriented and climate-relevant indirectly through consumption reduction.

policy_statement: The Qatar Green Building Council’s 'no paper day' project encourages schools, companies, and institutions to reduce paper, plastic, and metal consumption nationwide.
source_quote: Other organizations like the Qatar Green Building Council (QGBC) has established a project under the name of 'no paper day' in 2013, that aims to encourage the local community to adopt eco-friendly initiatives geared at reducing waste nationwide and to remind the public that reducing the use of Qatar's resources not only can improve business efficiency, but also help to preserve the environment's long-term health. The initiative is part of QGBC's efforts to help schools, companies, and institutions, find ways to reduce paper, plastic and metal consumption, engage the wider community in environmentally friendly practices, and raise sustainability awareness.
extraction_rationale: This is a named waste-reduction and resource-consumption initiative. Its climate relevance is indirect rather than a direct GHG or resilience policy.

policy_statement: Qatar has launched a national food security strategy to optimize agricultural land and water resources and protect domestic food needs from external and weather-related shocks.
source_quote: Qatar has launched a robust national food security strategy to optimize the use of the country's agricultural land and water resources and insulate domestic food needs from external shocks. This is increasingly important especially as rising weather-related disasters could disrupt the yields and provision of major crops, impacting Qatar's already challenging agriculture landscape. The strategy focuses on four pillars of enhancing international trade and logistics, increasing domestic selfsufficiency in some niches, building strategic reserves and enhancing domestic markets.
extraction_rationale: This is a named umbrella adaptation strategy with four stated pillars, so it is extracted as a parent policy.

parent_statement: National food security strategy
policy_statement: Qatar will diversify trade partners for critical commodities and use contingency plans to reduce exposure to trade shocks and disruptions.
source_quote: Under the first pillar of international trade and logistics, Qatar is geographically diversifying trade partners for critical commodities to reduce exposure to external shocks. In addition, Qatar has also proactively put in place contingency plans to limit impacts of trade shocks or other exogenous disruptions.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific sub-action under the national food security strategy, focused on resilience to external supply shocks.

parent_statement: National food security strategy
policy_statement: Qatar will increase domestic self-sufficiency in vegetables, red meat, and fisheries while reducing groundwater-based fodder production.
source_quote: Qatar has also made huge strides to increase the domestic self-sufficiency of its vegetables, red meat and fisheries production, as well as reducing groundwater-based fodder production. For vegetables production, it has plans to develop its hydroponics greenhouse cluster to reach 70% self-sufficiency on greenhouse vegetables and has launched multiple programs and subsidies towards greenhouse production.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete food-security sub-policy with sectoral targets and resource-management implications. It is primarily adaptation because it addresses food supply resilience.

parent_statement: National food security strategy
policy_statement: Qatar will develop hydroponic greenhouse clusters to reach 70% self-sufficiency in greenhouse vegetables, supported by programs and subsidies.
source_quote: For vegetables production, it has plans to develop its hydroponics greenhouse cluster to reach 70% self-sufficiency on greenhouse vegetables and has launched multiple programs and subsidies towards greenhouse production. Such initiatives will not only ensure that the country is well adapted to potential shocks, but also contribute towards more sustainable agriculture practices including better optimization of agrochemicals usage and water efficiency. This should also help decrease the transportation CO2 footprint of the food offered in the country.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified domestic food-production target with named technology and subsidies. The subsidy component makes it a financial instrument; the policy also explicitly mentions water efficiency.

parent_statement: National food security strategy
policy_statement: Qatar will build reserves of perishables, selected non-perishables, potable water, and groundwater to buffer against production disruptions.
source_quote: Qatar also plans to put in place adequate reserves, including perishables, selected non-perishables, potable water and groundwater reserves to buffer against potential production disruptions. Lastly, it is also building transparency and efficiency in its domestic market through farmer support programs, food waste programs and food standards governance initiatives.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific resilience measure under the food security strategy, designed to buffer against supply or production disruptions.

parent_statement: National food security strategy
policy_statement: Qatar will improve domestic food market transparency and efficiency through farmer support programs, food waste programs, and food standards governance initiatives.
source_quote: Qatar also plans to put in place adequate reserves, including perishables, selected non-perishables, potable water and groundwater reserves to buffer against potential production disruptions. Lastly, it is also building transparency and efficiency in its domestic market through farmer support programs, food waste programs and food standards governance initiatives.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific food-system governance and waste-reduction sub-action. It has indirect climate relevance through food system efficiency and resilience.

policy_statement: Qatar will design a National Measurement, Reporting and Verification system to measure and validate progress toward NDC commitments using verified sector-specific communications.
source_quote: Governed by the MME Climate Change Department, the National Measurement, Reporting and Verification (MRV) System will be designed to measure and validate progress towards the commitments made in this NDC, using verified sector specific MRV communications prepared by the national stakeholders. Effective MRV processes are key to guarantee best practice accounting, transparency, precision and comparability on climate change information.
extraction_rationale: This is a named climate governance system for tracking NDC implementation. It is included as a policy because it is a concrete institutional mechanism, though it enables rather than directly reduces emissions.
